# Rashi on Isaiah

רש"י על ישעיהו

Link: [https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah)

הפירוש הנפוץ והמוכר ביותר לתורה, המבאר את פשטי המקראות בתוספת הרחבות פרשניות; חובר במאה ה-11.

Most widely-read biblical commentary, compiled in the 11th-century, explaining the simple meaning of the text with interpretive elaborations.

## Chapter 1


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:1:1)


**חֲזוֹן יְשַׁעְיָהוּ בֶן אָמוֹץ וְגוֹ׳.** אָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי (מגילה י:): דָּבָר זֶה מָסֹרֶת בְּיָדֵינוּ מֵאֲבוֹתֵינוּ: אָמוֹץ וַאֲמַצְיָה מֶלֶךְ יְהוּדָה אַחִים הָיוּ:


**the vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz** Said Rabbi Levi: We have a tradition from our ancestors that Amoz and Amaziah, king of Judah, were brothers.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:1:2)


**אֲשֶׁר חָזָה עַל יְהוּדָה וִירוּשָׁלִָם.** וַהֲלֹא עַל כַּמָּה אֻמּוֹת נִתְנַבֵּא: מַשָּׂא בָּבֶל (ישעיהו יג:א), מַשָּׂא מוֹאָב (ישעיהו טו:א)? הָא לָמַדְתָּ שֶׁאֵין זֶה תְּחִלַּת הַסֵּפֶר וְלֹא נִקְרָא הַסֵּפֶר עַל שֵׁם הֶחָזוֹן הַזֶּה. וְכֵן שָׁנִינוּ בִּבְרַיְתָא דִּמְכִילְתָּא, ״בִּשְׁנַת מוֹת הַמֶּלֶךְ עֻזִּיָּהוּ״ (ישעיהו ו:א) תְּחִלַּת הַסֵּפֶר, אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין מֻקְדָּם וּמְאֻחָר בַּסֵּדֶר. וְהַדְּבָרִים מוֹכִיחִים, שֶׁהֲרֵי בְּיוֹם הָרַעַשׁ, יוֹם שֶׁנִּצְטָרַע עֻזִּיָּהוּ, נֶאֱמַר ״וָאֶשְׁמַע אֶת קוֹל ה׳ אוֹמֵר אֶת מִי אֶשְׁלַח וּמִי יֵלֶךְ לָנוּ״ (ישעיהו ו:ח), וְאָמַר ״הִנְנִי שְׁלָחֵנִי״. לָמַדְנוּ שֶׁהוּא תְּחִלַּת שְׁלִיחוּתוֹ, וּנְבוּאָה זוֹ נֶאֶמְרָה אַחַר כָּךְ. וְעַל זוֹ לְבַדָּהּ נֶאֱמַר ״אֲשֶׁר חָזָה עַל יְהוּדָה וִירוּשָׁלִָם״, כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאָמַר עַל מַשָּׂא כָּל אֻמָּה וְאֻמָּה ״מַשָּׂא אֻמָּה פְּלוֹנִי״, אַף כָּאן כָּתַב חָזוֹן זֶה חָזָה עַל יְהוּדָה וִירוּשָׁלִָם. וּלְפִי שֶׁהֵם תּוֹכְחוֹת קֹשִׁי, קְרָאָם חָזוֹן, שֶׁהוּא קָשֶׁה מֵעֲשָׂרָה לְשׁוֹנוֹת שֶׁנִּקְרֵאת נְבוּאָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (בראשית רבה מד:), וּרְאָיָה לַדָּבָר ״חָזוּת קָשָׁה הֻגַּד לִי״ (ישעיהו כא:ב):


**which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem** Now, did he not prophesy concerning many nations, viz. the prophecy of Babylonia (ch. 13), the prophecy of Moab (ch. 15)? Thus you learn that this is not the beginning of the Book, and that the Book is not given its name for this prophecy. So we learned in the Baraitha of the Mechilta (Exod. 15: 9,10): “In the year of King Uzziah’s death” (6:1) is the beginning of the Book, but there is no early and late in the order [i.e., the order of the chapters is no indication of the chronological order. (Others read: There is no early and late in the Book—Parshandatha.] The context proves this point, for, on the day of the earthquake (see Zech. 14:5), the day Uzziah became a metzora (see 2 Chron. 26:19), it was said: “Whom shall I send and who will go for us?” And I said, “Here I am; send me” (6:8). We learn that this was the beginning of his mission, and this prophecy was said afterwards. And concerning this alone, it is stated: which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem, just as Scripture says concerning each nation, “the prophecy of such and such a nation.” Here too, Scripture writes: “which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.” Since they are harsh reproofs, he calls them “chazon,” which is the harshest of the ten expressions by which prophecy is called, as is stated in Gen. Rabbah (44:7), and proof of this is the verse (infra 21:2), “A harsh prophecy (חָזוּת) was told to me.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:1:3)


**בִּימֵי עֻזִּיָּהוּ וְגוֹ׳.** מַלְכֵי יְהוּדָה – אַרְבָּעָה מְלָכִים הַלָּלוּ קִפֵּחַ בְּיָמָיו. בְּיוֹם שֶׁנִּצְטָרַע עֻזִּיָּהוּ שָׁרְתָה שְׁכִינָה עָלָיו, וְנִתְנַבֵּא כָּל יְמֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַלָּלוּ, עַד שֶׁעָמַד מְנַשֶּׁה וַהֲרָגוֹ (וּנְבוּאָה זוֹ נֶאֶמְרָה בִּימֵי חִזְקִיָּהוּ אַחַר שֶׁגָּלוּ עֲשֶׂרֶת הַשְּׁבָטִים כְּתַרְגּוּם יוֹנָתָן):


**in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, [and] Hezekiah, kings of Judah.** These four kings he buried, [i.e. he outlived,] in his lifetime. On the day Uzziah became a metzora, the Shechinah rested upon him, and he prophesied all the days of these kings, until Manasseh arose and killed him. (And this prophecy was said in the days of Hezekiah after the ten tribes were exiled.)



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:2:1)


**שִׁמְעוּ שָׁמַיִם וְהַאֲזִינִי אֶרֶץ.** מֹשֶׁה אָמַר ״הַאֲזִינוּ הַשָּׁמַיִם וְתִשְׁמַע הָאָרֶץ״ (דברים לב:א), לָמָּה שִׁנָּה יְשַׁעְיָה אֶת הַלָּשׁוֹן? שָׁנוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ בְּדָבָר זֶה וּמִדְרָשׁוֹת רַבִּים בְּפָרָשַׁת הַאֲזִינוּ בְּסִפְרִי, וְנֶחְלְקוּ חֲכָמִים עֲלֵיהֶם וְאָמְרוּ: אֵין הַדָּבָר כֵּן, אֶלָּא בִּזְמַן שֶׁהָעֵדִים בָּאִים וּמְעִידִים וְנִמְצְאוּ דִבְרֵיהֶם מְכֻוָּנִים – עֵדוּתָן קַיֶּמֶת, וְאִם לָאו – אֵין עֵדוּתָן קַיֶּמֶת. אִלּוּ לֹא בָּא יְשַׁעְיָה וְנָתַן שְׁמִיעָה לַשָּׁמַיִם וְהַאֲזָנָה לָאָרֶץ, הָיוּ שָׁמַיִם מְעִידִים וְאוֹמְרִים: כְּשֶׁנִּקְרָאנוּ לְעֵדוּת זוֹ בִּימֵי מֹשֶׁה, שֶׁאָמַר ״הַעִידֹתִי בָכֶם הַיּוֹם״ (דברים ל:יט), בְּהַאֲזָנָה שָׁמַעְנוּ, וְהָאָרֶץ מְעִידָה: אֲנִי נִקְרֵאתִי בִּלְשׁוֹן שְׁמִיעָה, וְאֵין עֵדוּתָן מְכֻוֶּנֶת. בָּא יְשַׁעְיָה וְחִלֵּף אֶת הַדָּבָר, נִמְצְאוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם מְעִידִים בִּלְשׁוֹן הַאֲזָנָה וּבִלְשׁוֹן שְׁמִיעָה:


**Hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth** And Moses said, “Give ear, O heavens,...and may the earth hear” (Deut. 32:1). Why did Isaiah change the wording? Our masters taught concerning this matter, [and] many midrashim [are] in the section entitled “Ha’azinu” in Sifrei, but the Sages disagreed with them and said: A matter is not so unless witnesses come and testify. If their words coincide, their testimony is fulfilled; if not, their testimony is not fulfilled. Had Isaiah not addressed the heavens with giving ear and the earth with hearing, the heavens would testify and say, ‘When we were called to this testimony in Moses’ time, when he said, (Deut. 30:19) “I call heaven and earth to witness against you,” we heard with an expression of giving ear,’ and the earth would testify, ‘I was called with an expression of hearing,’ hence their testimony would not coincide. [Therefore,] Isaiah came and reversed the matter. Consequently, both are found to testify with an expression of giving ear and with an expression of hearing.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:2:2)


**כִּי ה׳ דִּבֵּר.** שֶׁתִּהְיוּ עֵדִים בַּדָּבָר כְּשֶׁהִתְרֵיתִי בָּם בִּימֵי מֹשֶׁה. לָכֵן בֹּאוּ וְשִׁמְעוּ שֶׁאֲנִי מִתְוַכֵּחַ עִמָּם, שֶׁעָבְרוּ עַל הַהַתְרָאָה. אֲנִי לֹא סָרַחְתִּי בָּהֶם, אֶלָּא גִּדַּלְתִּים וְרוֹמַמְתִּים וְהֵם פָּשְׁעוּ בִי (סֵפָרִים אֲחֵרִים). שֶׁתִּהְיוּ עֵדִים לַדָּבָר, וְהֵיכָן דִּבֵּר? ״הַאֲזִינוּ הַשָּׁמַיִם וַאֲדַבֵּרָה״ (דברים לב:א) בַּמְכִילְתָּא (בא יב):


**for the Lord has spoken** That you should be witnesses in this matter, when I warned them in Moses’ time. Therefore, come and hear what I reason with them, for they transgressed the warning, I did not sin against them, but I raised them and exalted them, yet they rebelled against me. [Another version reads:] That you should be witnesses in this matter. Now, where did He speak? “Give ear, O heavens and I will speak” (ibid. 32:1). [So this was taught] in Mechilta (Bo 12).



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:3:1)


**קֹנֵהוּ.** מְתַקְּנוֹ בַּחֲרִישָׁה בַּיּוֹם, וּמֵאַחַר שֶׁהִרְגִּילוֹ בְּכָךְ יוֹדֵעַ בּוֹ. אֲבָל חֲמוֹר אָטוּם אֵינוֹ מֵבִין בְּעָלָיו עַד שֶׁיַּאֲכִילֶנּוּ. וְיִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא נִתְפַּקַּח לֵידַע כְּשׁוֹר, כְּשֶׁקְּרָאתִיו ״יִשְׂרָאֵל יִהְיֶה שְׁמֶךָ״ (בראשית לה:י), וְהוֹדַעְתִּיו קְצָת חֻקּוֹתַי וְהֵם עֲזָבוּנִי, כִּדְמְפוֹרָשׁ (יחזקאל כ:לט) וְאוֹמֵר ״אִישׁ אֶת גִּלּוּלֵי וְגוֹ׳״. וְאַף לְאַחַר שֶׁהוֹצֵאתִים מִמִּצְרַיִם וְהֶאֱכַלְתִּים אֶת הַמָּן וְקָרָאתִי אוֹתָם ״עַמִּי בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״, לֹא הִתְבּוֹנְנוּ כַּחֲמוֹר (סא"א). דָּבָר אַחֵר: **יָדַע שׁוֹר קֹנֵהוּ.** מַכִּיר הַשּׁוֹר קוֹנֵהוּ לִהְיוֹת מוֹרָאוֹ עָלָיו, לֹא שִׁנָּה מַה שֶׁגָּזַרְתִּי עָלָיו לוֹמַר אֵינִי חוֹרֵשׁ הַיּוֹם, וַחֲמוֹר לֹא אָמַר לִבְעָלָיו אֵינִי טוֹעֵן הַיּוֹם. וּמָה אֵלּוּ שֶׁנִּבְרְאוּ לְשַׁמֶּשְׁכֶם, וְאֵינָם לֹא לְקִבּוּל שָׂכָר אִם יִזְכּוּ וְלֹא לְשִׁלּוּם פֻּרְעָנוּת אִם חוֹטְאִים, לֹא שִׁנּוּ אֶת מִדָּתָם שֶׁגָּזַרְתִּי עֲלֵיהֶם, וְיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁאִם זוֹכִים מְקַבְּלִים שָׂכָר וְאִם חוֹטְאִים מְקַבְּלִים פֻּרְעָנוּת:


**his owner** Heb. קֹנֵהוּ [is] like מְתַקְּנוֹ, the one who affixes him to the plowshare for plowing by day, and since he has accustomed him to this, he knows him. The dull donkey, however, does not recognize his master until he feeds him. Israel was not intelligent like the ox, to know, when I called him and said, “Israel will be your name” (Gen. 35:10), and I informed them of several of My statutes, yet they deserted Me, as is related in Ezekiel (20:39): “Let each one go and worship his idols.” Even after I took them out of Egypt and fed them the manna and called them, “My people, the children of Israel,” they did not consider even as a donkey. Another explanation is: **An ox knows its owner** An ox recognizes his owner so that his fear is upon him. He did not deviate from what I decreed upon him, by saying, I will not plow today. Neither did a donkey say to his owner, I will not bear burdens today. Now, these [creatures,] who were created to serve you, and are not destined to receive reward if they merit, or to be punished if they sin, did not change their manner, which I decreed upon them. Israel, however, who, if they merit receive reward, and if they sin are punished.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:3:2)


**לֹא יָדַע.** לֹא אָבוּ לֵידַע, וְיָדְעוּ וְדָשׁוּ בְּעָקֵב, וְעַמִּי לֹא נָתַן לֵב לְהִתְבּוֹנֵן:


**does not know** i.e., did not want to know; they knew but trod with their heels, and my people did not take heart to consider.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:4:1)


**הוֹי.** כָּל הוֹי שֶׁבַּמִּקְרָא לְשׁוֹן קֹבֶל וְקִינָה, כְּאָדָם הַגּוֹנֵחַ מִלִּבּוֹ וְצוֹעֵק ״אֲהָה״, אֶלָּא שֶׁיֵּשׁ מֵהֶם מוּעָטִין שֶׁהֵם לְשׁוֹן צַעֲקַת קְרִיאַת קוֹל, כְּמוֹ ״הוֹי הוֹי וְנֻסוּ מֵאֶרֶץ צָפוֹן״ (זכריה ב:י), וְתַרְגּוּמוֹ ״אַכְלוּ״ לְשׁוֹן הַכְרָזָה. הוֹי יֵשׁ לִזְעוֹק עַל גּוֹי קָדוֹשׁ הַנֶּהְפַּךְ לִהְיוֹת גּוֹי חוֹטֵא, וְעַם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ ״כִּי עַם קָדוֹשׁ אַתָּה״ (דברים ז:ו) נֶהְפַּךְ לִהְיוֹת עַם כֶּבֶד עָוֹן:


**Woe** Every instance of הוֹי in Scripture is an expression of complaining and lamenting, like a person who sighs from his heart and cries, “Alas!” There are, however, several, which are an expression of a cry, the vocative voice, e.g., “Ho, ho, flee from the land of the north” (Zech. 2:10), which the Targum renders, אַכְלוּ, an expression of announcing. **Woe** There is a reason to cry about a holy nation that turned into a sinful nation, and a people referred to by the expression, “for you are a holy people” (Deut. 7:6), turned into a people with iniquity.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:4:2)


**עַם כֶּבֶד עָוֹן.** כְּבֵדוּת עָוֹן. כָּבֵד אָדָם שֶׁהוּא כָּבֵד, פישנ״ט בְּלַעַ״ז. כֶּבֶד שֵׁם דָּבָר שֶׁל כְּבֵדוּת, פישנטומ״א בְּלַעַ״ז, וְדָבוּק עִם תֵּיבַת עָוֹן:


**a people heavy with iniquity** The heaviness of iniquity. The word denotes a person who is heavy, pesant in French, ponderous. The word כֶבֶד is a substantive of heaviness, pesantoma in French, and is in the construct state, and is connected with the word עָוֹן, iniquity.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:4:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:4:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:4:3)


**זֶרַע מְרֵעִים.** וְהֵם הָיוּ ״זֶרַע בֵּרַךְ ה׳״ (ישעיהו סא:ט), בָּנִים הָיוּ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נֶהֶפְכוּ לְמַשְׁחִיתִים:


**evildoing seed** And they were seed whom the Lord blessed (Isa. 61:9). Similarly, they were children of the Holy One, blessed be He, and they became corrupt.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:4:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:4:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:4:4)


**נִאֲצוּ.** הִרְגִּיזוּ:


**they provoked** Heb. נִאֲצוּ, they angered.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:4:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:4:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:4:5)


**נָזֹרוּ אָחוֹר.** אֵין נְזִירָה בְּכָל מָקוֹם אֶלָּא לְשׁוֹן פְּרִישׁוּת, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר ״וְיִנָּזְרוּ מִקָּדְשֵׁי בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״ (ויקרא כב:ב), ״נְזִיר אֶחָיו״ (בראשית מט:כו). אַף כָּאן נָזוֹרוּ – נְסוֹגוּ לַאֲחוֹרֵיהֶם מֵאֵצֶל הַמָּקוֹם:


**they drew backwards** [The root נְזִירָה,] wherever it appears, is only an expression of separation. Similarly, Scripture states: “And they shall separate (וְיִנָּזְרוּ) from the holy things of the children of Israel” (Lev. 22:2), “the one separated (נְזִיר) from his brothers” (Gen. 49:26). Here too, they drew away from being near the Omnipresent.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:5:1)


**עַל מֶה תֻכּוּ וְגוֹ׳.** אָדָם שֶׁלָּקָה וְחוֹזֵר עַל סִרְחוֹנוֹ, חֲבֵרוֹ מוֹכִיחוֹ וְאוֹמֵר לוֹ: ״עַל זֶה לָקִיתָ, וְאֵינְךָ נוֹתֵן לֵב לוֹמַר ׳עַל סֻרְחָן זֶה לָקִיתִי, לֹא אָשׁוּב לַעֲשׂוֹת עוֹד׳?״ אַף כָּאן ״עַל מֶה תֻּכּוּ״ מֵאַחַר שֶׁעֲדַיִן אַתֶּם מוֹסִיפִים סָרָה, לָסוּר מֵאַחֲרֵי הַמָּקוֹם? הֲלֹא כְּבָר כָּל רֹאשׁ לָחֳלִי, וְלָמָּה לֹא תָבִינוּ?


**Why are you beaten...** A person who was punished (lit. beaten) and repeats his sinhis friend admonishes him and says to him, For this you have been punished, yet you do not take heart to say, ‘For this I have been punished. I will not repeat it again.’ Here too, why are you beaten since you continue disobedience, to turn away from following the Omnipresent? Is not every head afflicted with illness and every heart with malaise? Why then do you not understand?



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:6:1)


**מְתֹם.** לְשׁוֹן תְּמִימוּת, שָׁלֵם מֵאֵין מַכְאוֹב:


**soundness** An expression of perfection, sound without pain.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:6:2)


**פֶּצַע.** מַכַּת חֶרֶב:


**wounds** Heb. פֶּצַע, i.e., a wound of a sword.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:6:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:6:3)


**חַבּוּרָה.** לְשׁוֹן חַבָּלָה:


**contusions** Heb. חַבּוּרָה, an expression of a bruise. [Some editions read:] Other bruises.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:6:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:6:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:6:4)


**וּמַכָּה טְרִיָּה.** תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״מְרַסְסָא״, כְּתוּתָה וּמְרוּסֶסֶת:


**and lacerated sores** Jonathan renders: מְרַסְסָא, lacerated and crushed.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:6:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:6:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:6:5)


**טְרִיָּה.** דמיצייד״א בְּלַעַ״ז, וּבִלְשׁוֹן גְּמָרָא יֵשׁ ״טַרְיֵה לְרֵישֵׁיהּ״ (חולין מה:). מְנַחֵם פֵּירֵשׁ לְשׁוֹן לַחוּת, כְּלוֹמַר: לַחָה וְרְטוּבָה, תָּמִיד נוֹבַעַת, מוישט״א בְּלַעַ״ז:


**and lacerated sores** demarcejjre, in O.F., and in the language of the Talmud, we find, “he bumped (טַרְיֵה) his head” (Chullin 45b). Menahem explained it as an expression of moisture, i.e., moist and wet, always oozing [muyte in O.F.].


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:6:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:6:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:6:6)


**לֹא זֹרוּ.** הַנְּגָעִים הָאֵלֶּה לֹא זוֹרוּ עַל יְדֵי רוֹפְאִים אַבְקַת סַמָּנֵי תַחְבּוֹשֶׁת, לָשׁוֹן ״יְזֹרֶה עַל נָוֵהוּ גָפְרִית״ (איוב יח:טו). וּמְנַחֵם פֵּרֵשׁ לְשׁוֹן רְפוּאָה, כְּמוֹ ״אֵין דָּן דִּינֵךְ לְמָזוֹר״ (ירמיהו ל:יג). **וְלֹא חֻבָּשׁוּ.** לְשׁוֹן רְפוּאָה:


**they have not been sprinkled** These lesions were not sprinkled with medicinal powders by physicians. This is an expression of: (Job 18:15) “Sulphur shall be sprinkled (יְזֹרֶה) on his dwelling.” Menahem explained it as an expression of healing, as in (Jeremiah 30:13): “No one pronounced your judgment for healing (לְמָזוֹר).”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:6:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:6:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:6:7)


**וְלֹא רֻכְּכָה בַּשָּׁמֶן.** לֹא רֻכְּכָה מַכָּתָם בַּשֶּׁמֶן כְּמִשְׁפַּט שְׁאָר מַכּוֹת, וְאֵין נוֹפֵל כָּאן לוֹמַר ׳לֹא רֻכְּכוּ בַּשֶּׁמֶן׳, שֶׁאֵין מְרַכְּכִין אֶלָּא בִּמְקוֹם הַמַּכָּה, אֲבָל הַמָּזוֹר וְהַחֲבִישָׁה נוֹפֵל לְשׁוֹנָם עַל כָּל הַגּוּף, לְפִיכָךְ נוֹפֵל בָּם לְשׁוֹן רַבִּים: ״לֹא זֹרוּ״ הַנְּגָעִים ״וְלֹא חֻבָּשׁוּ״. וְיוֹנָתָן פָּתַר כָּל הַמִּקְרָא בִּלְשׁוֹן דּוּגְמָא, עַל שֶׁהֵם מְלוּכְלָכִים וּמְנוּגָּעִים בֶּעָוֹן, וְתִרְגֵּם ״מִכַּף רֶגֶל וְעַד רֹאשׁ״ מִקְּטַנִּים וְעַד גְּדוֹלִים (ירמיהו ו:ג), ״אֵין בּוֹ מְתֹם״ אֵין טוֹב בּוֹ, ״פֶּצַע וְחַבּוּרָה״ פֶּשַׁע וַעֲוֹנוֹת וְחַטָּאִים. **לֹא זֹרוּ וְגוֹ׳** כְּלוֹמַר לֹא נִתְרַפְּאוּ לָשׁוּב בִּתְשׁוּבָה שְׁלֵמָה, וְלֹא רֻכְּכָה בַּשָּׁמֶן אֲפִלּוּ צַד הִרְהוּר תְּשׁוּבָה אֵין בְּלִבָּם:


**neither was it softened with oil** Their wound was not softened with oil, as is customary with other wounds. It would be inappropriate to say here, “They were not softened with oil,” for they soften only the place of the sore, not the wound and the contusion but the sprinkling and the bandaging applies to all three, [i.e., the wound, the contusion, and the lacerated sore.] Therefore, the plural number applies to them; the lesions were not sprinkled and not bandaged. Jonathan interprets the entire verse figuratively, referring to the fact that they were soiled and afflicted with iniquity. Accordingly, he rendered, “From the sole of the foot until the head,” from the smallest to the greatest, there is no soundness. There is none good among them, wounds and contusions, rebellious deeds, iniquities, and inadvertent sins. **they have not been sprinkled...** i.e., they have not been healed by repenting wholeheartedly, nor has it been softened with oil, not even a trace of repentant thought has entered their heart.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:7:1)


**לְנֶגְדְּכֶם זָרִים אֹכְלִים אֹתָהּ.** לְעֵינֵיכֶם יֹאכְלוּהָ אוֹיְבֵיכֶם:


**in your presence, strangers devour it** Before your eyes, your enemies will devour it.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:7:2)


**וּשְׁמָמָה.** מִכֶּם, כְּנַחֲלָה הַנֶּהְפֶּכֶת לְזָרִים וְהִיא שְׁמָמָה מִבְּעָלֶיהָ; כָּךְ תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן:


**and desolate** of you as a heritage turned over to strangers, which is desolate of its owners. Jonathan renders in this manner.



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:8:1)


**וְנוֹתְרָה בַת צִיּוֹן.** רֵיקָנִית מִיּוֹשְׁבֶיהָ, כִּי יִגְלוּ מִתּוֹכָהּ, כַּאֲשֶׁר תִּוָּתֵר סֻכַּת הַכֶּרֶם שֶׁעֲשָׂאָהּ נוֹצֵר, וּבְעֵת יִבְצֹר הַכֶּרֶם מַנִּיחַ סֻכָּתוֹ וְהוֹלֵךְ, ״בָּתַר דִּקְטָפוּהִי״ (תרגום יונתן) – לְאַחַר שֶׁבָּצְרוּ אוֹתָהּ:


**And the daughter of Zion shall be left** devoid of its inhabitants, for they will be exiled from its midst, as a hut in a vineyard, made by a watchman, and when the produce of the vineyard is gathered, he leaves his hut and goes away, after they gather it.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:8:2)


**כִּמְלוּנָה בְמִקְשָׁה.** ״כַּאֲשֶׁר תֵּעָזֵב הַמְּלוּנָה שֶׁעָשָׂה נוֹצֵר בְּרֹאשׁ הַמִּקְשָׁה לִשְׁמֹר קִישּׁוּאִין שֶׁלָּהּ, וּמִשֶּׁתִּלָּקֵט מַנִּיחָהּ וְהוֹלֵךְ. זוֹ שֶׁבַּכֶּרֶם קְרוּיָה סֻכָּה, לְפִי שֶׁהוּא גָּר שָׁם יוֹמָם וָלַיְלָה, בַּיּוֹם שׁוֹמְרָהּ מִן הָעוֹפוֹת וּבַלַּיְלָה מִן הַגַּנָּבִים. אֲבָל הַקִּישּׁוּאִין קָשִׁין הֵם וְאֵין לִירָא מִן הָעוֹפוֹת וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לְשָׁמְרָהּ בַּיּוֹם, לְפִיכָךְ נִקְרֵאת מְלוּנָה עַל שֶׁהִיא לִינַת הַלֵּילוֹת. ״כְּעַרְסַל מְבָתוּתָא״ – כְּמִשְׁכַּב הַמְּלוּנָה, ״בְּמִקְשָׁיָא בָּתַר דְּאַבְעִיוּהִי״ – לְאַחַר שֶׁלִּקְּטוּהוּ, לְשׁוֹן הַמִּשְׁנָה (פאה ד:): ״שָׁלֹשׁ אַבְעָיוֹת בַּיּוֹם:


**like a lodge in a cucumber field** As the lodge, which the watchman made at the end of a cucumber field, to watch its cucumber, is left, for after it is gathered, he leaves it and goes away; the one in the vineyard is called a hut since he lives in it day and night; by day, he guards it from the birds and by night from the thieves, b ut cucumbers are hard, and there is no fear of the birds, and one need not watch them by day. It is, therefore, called a lodge since it is a place of lodging at night. Jonathan renders: Like a bed in a lodge (again repeated in Hebrew), [in] a cucumber field, in a cucumber field after it has been picked (בָּתַר דְאַבְעָיוּהִי), after it has been picked. [This is the expression of the Mishnah] (Peah 4:5): “There are three gatherings (אַבְעָיוֹת) a day.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:8:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:8:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:8:3)


**כְּעִיר נְצוּרָה.** כְּעִיר שֶׁצָּרוּ עָלֶיהָ, וְעוֹשִׂים סֻכּוֹת סָבִיב לָהּ לְהִסְתַּתֵּר שָׁם הַחֲיָלוֹת, וּכְשֶׁמִּסְתַּלְּקִים מֵעָלֶיהָ מַנִּיחִין אוֹתָם וְהוֹלְכִין. כָּל זֶה תַּרְגּוּם יוֹנָתָן:


**like a besieged city** Like a city which was besieged, and they make huts around it to hide the troops, and when they give up the siege [lit., when they go away from it], they leave them and go away. All this is Jonathan’s translation.



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:9:1)


**לוּלֵי וְגוֹ׳ הוֹתִיר לָנוּ שָׂרִיד.** מֵאֵלָיו וּבְרַחֲמָיו, וְלֹא בְּצִדְקוֹתֵינוּ:


**Had not the Lord of Hosts left us a remnant** by His own volition and with His mercy, not because of our merits.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:9:2)


**כִּמְעָט כִּסְדֹם הָיִינוּ.** כֻּלָּנוּ כָּלִים:


**we would soon be like Sodom** All of us would be destroyed.



### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:10:1)


**קְצִינֵי סְדֹם.** שָׂרִים שֶׁמַּעֲשֵׂיהֶם כִּסְדוֹם. מִכָּאן אָמְרוּ (ברכות יט.): אַל יִפְתַּח אָדָם פִּיו לַשָּׂטָן:


**rulers of Sodom** Princes whose deeds are like those of Sodom. From here, [the Rabbis] deduced that a person should not open his mouth to Satan.

**I am sated with the burnt-offerings of rams** This is similar to: “Lest he have too much of you and hate you,” (Proverbs 25:18).

###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:11:3

**I do not want** Since you transgress My Torah, the sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination [from Prov. 21:27].

### Verse 13

###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:13:1)


**לֹא תוֹסִיפוּ הָבִיא מִנְחַת שָׁוְא.** מַתְרֶה אֲנִי בָּכֶם: לֹא תָּבִיאוּ לִי מִנְחַת שָׁוְא שֶׁלָּכֶם, שֶׁהֶעָשָׁן עוֹלֶה מִמֶּנָּה קִיטוֹר שֶׁל תִּיעוּב הוּא לִי, וְלֹא לְנַחַת הָרוּחַ:


**You shall bring no more vain meal-offerings** I warn you, you shall not bring Me your vain meal- offering, for the smoke that rises from it is smoke of abomination to Me, and not for My satisfaction.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:13:2)


**חֹדֶשׁ וְשַׁבָּת קְרֹא מִקְרָא לֹא אוּכַל וְגוֹ׳.** וְלִקְרוֹא מִקְרָא חֹדֶשׁ וְשַׁבָּת שֶׁאַתֶּם נֶאֱסָפִים לִקְרֹא עֲצָרָה וַאֲסִיפָה בָּהֶם, לֹא אוּכַל לִסְבּוֹל אָוֶן שֶׁבִּלְבַבְכֶם הַנּוֹטֶה לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְהָעֲצָרָה עִמּוֹ, שֶׁאֵין שְׁנֵי הַדְּבָרִים כָּאֵלּוּ רְאוּיִין יַחַד: לִקְרוֹא עֲצָרָה לֵיאָסֵף לְפָנַי, וְהָאָוֶן שֶׁבִּלְבַבְכֶם לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, וְאֵין אַתֶּם מוֹצִיאִין אוֹתוֹ מִתּוֹךְ לְבַבְכֶם:


**New moons and Sabbaths, calling, convocations, I cannot...** and [sic, does not appear in Parshandatha] to call convocations, i.e., New Moons and Sabbaths when you gather to call a convocation and an assembly on them, I cannot bear the iniquity in your hearts that is inclined to paganism, and the convocation with it, for these two things are incompatible: to call a convocation to gather before Me, and the iniquity that is in your hearts for paganism, and you do not take it out of your hearts.

### Verse 16

###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:16:1)


**רַחֲצוּ הִזַּכּוּ.** פַּתַּח הוּא, לְשׁוֹן צִוּוּי, לְפִי שֶׁהוּא מִגִּזְרַת רְחַץ, אֲבָל רָחֲצוּ קָמַץ לְשׁוֹן עָבַר שֶׁהוּא מִגִּזְרַת רָחַץ:


**Wash, cleanse yourselves** Voweled with a ‘patach,’ the imperative form, since it is derived from רְחַץ, but רָחֲצוּ, [in the past tense, is voweled with a ‘kamatz’ because it is derived from רָחַץ].


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:16:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:16:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:16:2)


**רַחֲצוּ, הִזַּכּוּ, הָסִירוּ, חִדְלוּ, לִמְדוּ, דִּרְשׁוּ, אַשְּׁרוּ, שִׁפְטוּ, רִיבוּ, לְכוּ.** עֶשֶׂר אַזְהָרוֹת שֶׁל לְשׁוֹן תְּשׁוּבָה יֵשׁ כָּאן, כְּנֶגֶד עֲשֶׂרֶת יְמֵי תְּשׁוּבָה וּכְנֶגֶד עֲשָׂרָה מַלְכֻיּוֹת זִכְרוֹנוֹת וְשׁוֹפָרוֹת:


**Wash, cleanse yourselves, remove, learn, seek, strengthen, perform justice, plead, go** Ten exhortations of the expression of repentance are [listed] here, corresponding to the Ten Days of Penitence and to the ten verses of Kingship, Remembrances, and Shofaroth [in the musaf service of Rosh Hashanah].


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:16:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:16:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:16:3)


**חִדְלוּ הָרֵעַ.** חִדְלוּ מִמַּעֲשִׂים הָרָעִים:


**cease to do evil** Desist from your evil deeds.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:16:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:16:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:16:4)


**הָרֵעַ.** כְּמוֹ לְהָרֵעַ, אֵין צָרִיךְ לִכְתּוֹב מֵהָרֵעַ, שֶׁכֵּן לְשׁוֹן הַמִּקְרָא נוֹפֵל עַל לְשׁוֹן חֲדָלָה, ״וְחָדַל לַעֲשׂוֹת הַפֶּסַח״ (במדבר ט:ג), ״עַד כִּי חָדַל לִסְפֹּר״ (בראשית מא:ט), כְּלוֹמַר: חָדְלָה הַסְּפִירָה, חָדְלָה הָעֲשִׂיָּה, אַף כָּאן תַּחְדְּלוּ הָרָעָה:


**to do evil** Heb. הרע, like לְהָרֵעַ, to do evil. [Rashi explains this because the preposition is absent in Hebrew.] Scripture does not have to write מֵהָרֵעַ, desist from doing evil, for so does the Biblical language treat the expression of חֲדָלָה, stopping, [e.g.,] “and he failed to make (לַעֲשׂוֹת) the Pesach” (Num. 9:13); “until he stopped counting (לִסְפֹּר)” (Gen. 41:49). That is to say, the counting stopped, the making failed, here too, stop the evildoing.



### Verse 17

###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:17:1)


**לִמְדוּ.** רָפֵי נָקוּד, וְהוּא מִגִּזְרַת ״לָמוֹד״ – הָיוּ לְמֵדִין לְהֵיטִיב. הַמְּלַמֵּד לְעַצְמוֹ הוּא מִמִּשְׁקוֹלֶת לָשׁוֹן קַל, לְפִיכָךְ צִוּוּי לָשׁוֹן רַבִּים שֶׁלּוֹ נָקוּד בְּחִירִק כְּמוֹ ״אִמְרוּ״, ״שִׁמְעוּ״, אֲבָל הַמְּלַמֵּד לַאֲחֵרִים הוּא מִמִּשְׁקוֹלֶת לָשׁוֹן כָּבֵד הַמַּדְגִּישׁ, וְאִם בָּא לְצַוּוֹת אֶת הָרַבִּים הוּא נָקוּד ״לַמְּדוּ״. וְכֵן ״דִּרְשׁוּ״ מִגִּזְרַת ״דָּרוֹשׁ״, אֲבָל ״אַשְּׁרוּ״ שֶׁהַשִּׁי״ן מֻדְגֶּשֶׁת מִמִּשְׁקוֹלֶת לָשׁוֹן כָּבֵד וּמִגִּזְרַת ״אַשֵּׁר״, לְפִיכָךְ לָשׁוֹן צִוּוּי לְרַבִּים נָקוּד פַּתַּח כְּמוֹ ״דַּבְּרוּ״, ״סַפְּרוּ״, ״בַּשְּׂרוּ״:


**Learn** It is punctuated ‘raphe,’ weak, without a dagesh. This is from the form לָמֹד, learn to do good. One who teaches himself is of the ‘kal’ form. Therefore, its imperative plural is voweled with a ‘chirik’ like אִמְרוּ, שִׁמְעוּ, but one who teaches others is of the form of the ‘heavy conjugation’ (pi’el) with a ‘dagesh,’ and if one comes to command a number of people, the word is voweled לַמְּדוּ. And so, דִּרְשׁוּ, from the form דְרשׁ, but אַשְּׁרוּ in which the ‘shin’ has a ‘dagesh,’ is from the ‘heavy conjugation,’ and from the form אַשֵּׁר ; therefore, the imperative plural is voweled with a ‘patach’ like בַּשְּׂרוּ, סַפְּרוּ, דַּבְּרוּ.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:17:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:17:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:17:2)


**אַשְּׁרוּ חָמוֹץ.** הַחֲזִיקוּ אֶת הַגָּזוּל, וְהוּא לְשׁוֹן מִשְׁנָה: ״אֲשַׁרְנוּהִי״ (כתובות כא.), ״אִי אֲיַשֵּׁר חֵילִי״ (גיטין ל:), ״יִישַׁר כֹּחֲךָ״ (שבת פז.). לָשׁוֹן אַחֵר: הַדְרִיכוּהוּ בִּנְתִיב אֱמֶת לִזְכּוֹת בְּשֶׁלּוֹ, לְשׁוֹן ״בַּאֲשׁוּרוֹ אָחֲזָה רַגְלִי״ (איוב כג:א), ״וְאַשֵּׁר בְּדֶרֶךְ לִבֶּךָ״ (משלי כג:ט):


**strengthen the robbed** Heb. אַשְּׁרוּ חָמוֹץ. This is a Mishnaic term, אֲשַׁרְנוּהִי, “we have verified it” (Ketuboth 21a); “if I had strength (אֲיַשֵּׁר)” (Gittin 30b); “May your strength be strengthened (יִישַׁר)” (Shabbath 87a). Another explanation is: Lead him in the path of truth to acquire what rightfully belongs to him. An expression of: (Job 23:11) “My foot held its path (בֲּאֲשׁוּרוֹ)”; (Prov. 23:19) “And go (וְאַשֵׁר) in the way of your heart.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:17:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:17:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:17:3)


**שִׁפְטוּ יָתוֹם.** פְּלוֹנִי זַכַּאי, פְּלוֹנִי חַיָּב:


(**perform justice** So-and-so is innocent and so-and- so is guilty.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:17:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:17:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:17:4)


**רִיבוּ אַלְמָנָה.** הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּ בְּרִיבָהּ לְהִתְוַכֵּחַ בַּעֲדָהּ, שֶׁאֵינָהּ יוֹצֵאת לַחֲזוֹר אַחֲרֵי בַּעֲלֵי דִינָהּ (סא"א):


**plead the case of the widow** Endeavor in their quarrel to plead for her, for she cannot go out to pursue her opponents.)


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:17:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:17:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:17:5)


**חָמוֹץ.** גָּזוּל, וְדוֹמֶה לוֹ ״מִכַּף מְעַוֵּל וְחוֹמֵץ״ (תהלים עא:ד):


**the robbed** Heb. חָמוֹץ, similar to (Ps. 71:4) “from the hand of the unrighteous and the robber (וּמְחַמֵּץ).”



### Verse 18

###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:18:1)


**לְכוּ נָא וְנִוָּכְחָה** יַחַד, אֲנִי וְאַתֶּם, וְנֵדַע מִי סָרַח עַל מִי; וְאִם אַתֶּם סְרַחְתֶּם עָלַי, עוֹדֶנִּי נוֹתֵן לָכֶם תִּקְוָה לָשׁוּב:


**Come now, let us debate** together, I and you, and we will know who offended whom, and if you offended Me, I still give you hope to repent.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:18:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:18:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:18:2)


**אִם־יִהְיוּ חֲטָאֵיכֶם כַּשָּׁנִים.** כְּתוּמִים לְפָנַי כְּאוֹדֶם שָׁנִים, אַלְבִּינֵם כַּשֶּׁלֶג:


**If your sins prove to be like crimson** Stained before Me like crimson red, I will make them as white as snow.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:18:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:18:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:18:3)


**יֹאמַר ה׳.** תָּמִיד הוּא אוֹמֵר לָכֶם כֵּן, כְּמוֹ ״עַל פִּי ה׳ יַחֲנוּ״ (במדבר ט:). דָּבָר אַחֵר: לְכוּ נָא וְנִוָּכְחָה – מַה כָּתוּב לְמַעְלָה מִמֶּנּוּ? ״חִדְלוּ הָרֵעַ לִמְדוּ הֵיטֵב״ (ישעיהו א:ז-יז), וְאַחַר שֶׁתָּשׁוּבוּ אֵלַי לְכוּ וְנִוָּכְחָה יַחַד לְהוֹדִיעֵנִי: ״עָשִׂינוּ מַה שֶׁעָלֵינוּ, עֲשֵׂה מַה שֶׁעָלֶיךָ״, וַאֲנִי אוֹמֵר ״אִם יִהְיוּ חֲטָאֵיכֶם כַּשָּׁנִים כַּשֶּׁלֶג״ וְגוֹ׳:


**says the Lord** [The verb is in the future form to denote that] He always says this to you, like: (Num. 9:20) “By the word of the Lord they would camp (יַחֲנוּ),” also a future form. Another explanation is: Come now, let us debate. What is written above this? “Cease to do evil; learn to do good.” And after you return to Me, come now, and let us debate together, to notify Me, “We have done what is incumbent upon us; You do what is incumbent upon You;” and I say, “If your sins prove to be like crimson, they will become white as snow...”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:18:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:18:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:18:4)


**כַתּוֹלָע.** צֶבַע שֶׁצּוֹבְעִים בּוֹ אָדוֹם, גַּרְעִינִים הֵם, וְיֵשׁ תּוֹלָעִים בְּכָל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד:


**as crimson dye** Heb. תּוֹלָע, lit. a worm. Dye with which they dye fabrics red. They are kernels, each one of which has a worm inside it. Hence the name תּוֹלָע.



### Verse 20

###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:20:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:20:1)


**כִּי פִּי ה׳ דִּבֵּר.** וְהֵיכָן דִּבֵּר? ״וְהֵבֵאתִי עֲלֵיכֶם חֶרֶב״ (ויקרא כו:ה):


**for the mouth of the Lord spoke** Where did He speak? (Lev. 26:25) “And I will bring upon you a sword.”



### Verse 21

###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:21:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:21:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:21:1)


**לְזוֹנָה.** תּוֹעָה מֵעַל אֱלֹהֶיהָ:


**a harlot** Astray from her God.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:21:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:21:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:21:2)


**קִרְיָה.** שֶׁהָיְתָה נֶאֱמָנָה וּמְלֵאָה מִשְׁפָּט, וְצֶדֶק הָיָה לָן בָּהּ, וְעַתָּה מְרַצְּחִים:


**city** which was faithful and full of justice, and righteousness would lodge therein, but now murderers.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:21:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:21:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:21:3)


**מְלֵאֲתִי מִשְׁפָּט.** כְּגוֹן ״רַבָּתִי עָם״ (איכה א:):


**full of justice** Heb. מְלֵאֲתִי מִשְׁפָּט [equivalent to מְלֵאַתמִשְׁפָּט, the ‘yud’ being superfluous,] as in (Lamentations 1:1) רַבָּתִי עָם, “great in population” [equivalent to רַבַּתעָם].


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:21:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:21:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:21:4)


**צֶדֶק יָלִין בָּהּ.** תָּמִיד שֶׁל שַׁחַר הָיָה מְכַפֵּר עַל עֲבֵירוֹת שֶׁל הַלַּיְלָה, וְשֶׁל בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם מְכַפֵּר עַל שֶׁל הַיּוֹם. דָּבָר אַחֵר: שֶׁהָיוּ מְלִינִים בָּהּ דִּינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת, כְּשֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ מוֹצְאִין לוֹ זְכוּת בַּיּוֹם הָרִאשׁוֹן לֹא הָיוּ גּוֹמְרִין אֶת דִּינוֹ עַד לְמָחָר, אוּלַי יִמְצְאוּ לוֹ זְכוּת, וְעַתָּה נַעֲשׂוּ רוֹצְחִין. וּמָצִינוּ בִּפְסִיקְתָּא (פרק טו:ז): רַבִּי מְנַחֵם בַּר אוֹשַׁעְיָא אָמַר: תפ״א (אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת וּשְׁמוֹנִים וְאַחַת) בָּתֵּי כְנֵסִיּוֹת הָיוּ בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם כְּמִנְיַן מְלֵאֲתִי בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא:


**in which righteousness would lodge** The daily dawn sacrifice would atone for the sins [committed] at night, and the daily afternoon [sacrifice] would atone for those of the day. Another explanation is that they would allow capital cases to rest overnight when they could find no merit for him, [i.e., for the defendant;] they would not conclude his verdict until the morrow, perhaps they would find a merit for him, and now they have become murderers. [We find in] Pesikta [d’Rav Kahana p. 121a]: Rabbi Menahem bar Oshia [according to Parshandatha,] Rabbi Phinehas in the name of Rabbi Oshia said: Four hundred eighty-one synagogues were in Jerusalem, corresponding to the numerical value of מְלֵאֲתִי.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:21:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:21:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:21:5)


**וְעַתָּה מְרַצְּחִים.** הָרְגוּ אֶת אוּרִיָּה, הָרְגוּ אֶת זְכַרְיָה:


**and now murderers** They killed Uriah; they killed Zechariah.



### Verse 22

###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:22:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:22:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:22:1)


**כַּסְפֵּךְ הָיָה לְסִיגִים.** שֶׁהָיוּ עוֹשִׂין מָעוֹת נְחֹשֶׁת וּמְצַפִּין אוֹתָן בְּכֶסֶף לְהוֹנוֹת בָּהֶם:


**Your silver has become dross** They would make copper coins and plate them with silver, in order to cheat with them.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:22:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:22:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:22:2)


**סָבְאֵךְ מָהוּל בַּמָּיִם.** מַשְׁקִים שֶׁלָּכֶם מְעוֹרָבִים בַּמַּיִם, כְּדְאִיתָא בִּפְסִיקְתָּא (פסיקתא רבתי טו:). מָהוּל – מְעוֹרָב, וְאֵין לוֹ דִּמְיוֹן בַּמִּקְרָא; וּמִדְרָשׁ אַגָּדָה פּוֹתֵר ״לִשְׂחוֹק אָמַרְתִּי מְהוֹלָל״ (קהלת ב:) – מְעוֹרְבָּב:


**your wine is diluted with water** Your drinks are mixed with water, as is stated in Pesikta (122b). [The word] means ‘mixed,’ although there is no similar word in Scripture to prove it, but the Midrash Aggadah explains (Ecc. 2:2): “Of laughter I said, it makes one mad (מְהוֹלָל)” to mean that it is confused, or mixed up.



### Verse 23

###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:23:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:23:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:23:1)


**סוֹרְרִים.** סָרִים מִן הַדֶּרֶךְ הַיְשָׁרָה:


**rebellious** Deviating from the straight path.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:23:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:23:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:23:2)


**וְרֹדֵף שַׁלְמוֹנִים.** תַּשְׁלוּמִין. תַּרְגּוּם יוֹנָתָן: ״אָמְרִין גְּבַר לְחַבְרֵיהּ עֲבִיד לִי טַב בְּדִינִי וַאֲשַׁלֵּם לָךְ בְּדִינָךְ״. שׁוֹפֵט שֶׁהָיָה גַּזְלָן, וְהַנִּגְזָל צוֹעֵק עָלָיו בִּפְנֵי שׁוֹפֵט אַחֵר, זֶה אוֹמֵר לוֹ: צַדְּקֵנִי הַיּוֹם וַאֲנִי אֲשַׁלֵּם גְּמוּלְךָ כְּשֶׁיִּצְעֲקוּ עָלֶיךָ בְּפָנַי. הֲוֵי רוֹדֵף תַּשְׁלוּם גְּמוּלוֹת:


**and runs after payments** This word is similar to the Talmudic תַּשְׁלוּמִין. Jonathan paraphrases: One man says to another, Do me a favor in my case, and I will repay you in your case. This refers to a judge who was a robber, and the robbery victim complains about him before another judge. This one says to him, Declare me innocent today, and I will repay you when they complain about you before me. This is the meaning of running after payments.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:23:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:23:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:23:3)


**וְרִיב אַלְמָנָה לֹא־יָבוֹא אֲלֵיהֶם.** הָאַלְמָנָה בָּאָה לִצְעוֹק, וְהַיָּתוֹם יוֹצֵא, וְזוֹ פּוֹגַעַת בּוֹ וְשׁוֹאַלְתּוֹ: ״מַה הוֹעַלְתָּ בִּצְעָקָתְךָ לִפְנֵי הַשּׁוֹפֵט?״ וְהוּא אוֹמֵר: ״כָּל הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה יָגַעְתִּי לוֹ בִּמְלָאכָה, וְסוֹפוֹ לֹא הוֹעַלְתִּי.״ וְזוֹ חוֹזֶרֶת לַאֲחוֹרֶיהָ וְאוֹמֶרֶת: ״וּמַה זֶּה שֶׁהוּא אִישׁ לֹא הוֹעִיל, אֲנִי לֹא כָּל שֶׁכֵּן?״ הֲוֵי ״יָתוֹם לֹא יִשְׁפֹּטוּ וְרִיב אַלְמָנָה לֹא יָבוֹא אֲלֵיהֶם״ כְּלָל:


**and the quarrel of the widow does not come to them** The widow comes to complain, and the orphan is coming out, when this one meets him and asks him, What did you accomplish in your case? He replies, All day long I toiled at work, but I did not accomplish anything. And this one turns around and says, If this one, who is a man, did not accomplish anything, surely I will not. This is the meaning of, “the orphan they do not judge, and the quarrel of the widow does not come to them” at all.



### Verse 24

###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:24:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:24:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:24:1)


**נְאֻם הָאָדוֹן.** שֶׁהַכֹּל שֶׁלּוֹ, וּבְיָדוֹ לַעֲקוֹר אֶתְכֶם מֵאַרְצְכֶם וְלִנְטוֹעַ בָּהּ אֲחֵרִים:


**says the Master** Who possesses everything, and in Whose power it is to uproot you from your land and to settle others in it.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:24:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:24:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:24:2)


**אֲבִיר יִשְׂרָאֵל.** תָּקְפּוֹ שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל:


**the Mighty One of Israel** the strength of Israel.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:24:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:24:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:24:3)


**הוֹי.** לְשׁוֹן הַזְמָנָה וְהַכְרָזָה, וְדוֹמֶה לוֹ ״הוֹי וְנֻסוּ מֵאֶרֶץ צָפוֹן״ (זכריה ב:), וְיֵדְעוּ הַכֹּל כִּי אֶנָּחֵם מִצָּרַי שֶׁהִכְעִיסוּנִי בְּמַעֲשֵׂיהֶם:


**Oh** Heb. הוי. An expression of preparation and announcement, and similar to this is (Zech. 2:10): “Ho, ho, (הוי הוי) flee from the land of the north.” And let all know that I will console Myself of My adversaries, who angered Me with their deeds.



### Verse 25

###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:25:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:25:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:25:1)


**וְאָשִׁיבָה יָדִי עָלַיִךְ.** מַכָּה אַחַר מַכָּה, עַד כְּלוֹת הַפּוֹשְׁעִים:


**And I will return My hand upon you** One blow after another, until the transgressors have been completely destroyed.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:25:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:25:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:25:2)


**כַּבֹּר.** לְשׁוֹן בּוֹרִית, סבו״ן בְּלַעַ״ז, וּלְשׁוֹנוֹ לְשׁוֹן נִקָּיוֹן, כְּמוֹ ״וּבַר לֵבָב״ (תהילים כד:), עַל שֵׁם שֶׁהוּא מְנַקֶּה הַבֶּגֶד מִכְּתָמָיו:


**as with lye** This is an expression meaning soap [sbon in O.F., savon (in modern French)]. Its deviation is an expression of cleanliness, similar to (Ps. 24:4): “and pure (בַּר) of heart,” since it cleanses the garment of its stains.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:25:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:25:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:25:3)


**סִיגָיִךְ.** הָאָמוּר לְמַעְלָה כְּמוֹ ״כַּסְפֵּךְ הָיָה לְסִיגִים״ (ישעיהו א:כב), תַּעֲרוֹבֶת נְחֹשֶׁת בְּכֶסֶף קָרוּי סִיג, אַף כָּאן תַּעֲרוֹבֶת רְשָׁעִים עִם הַכְּשֵׁרִים. אֲנִי אֲכַלֶּה הַפּוֹשְׁעִים שֶׁהֵם הַסִּיג:


**your dross** mentioned above, as: “Your silver has become dross”; a mixture of silver with copper is called dross. Here too, a mixture of the wicked with the righteous. I will destroy the transgressors, who are all dross.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:25:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:25:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:25:4)


**כָּל־בְּדִילָיִךְ.** בְּדִיל הַמְעוֹרָב בַּכֶּסֶף, כְּלוֹמַר: הָרְשָׁעִים שֶׁבָּךְ. בְּדִיל אשטיי״ס בְּלַעַ״ז:


**all your tin** The tin mixed with silver, that is to say, the wicked among you. בְדִיל is called estejjn [etain] in O.F. [tin].



### Verse 26

###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:26:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:26:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:26:1)


**כְּבָרִאשֹׁנָה.** אַעֲמִיד לָכֶם שׁוֹפְטִים כְּשֵׁרִים:


**as at first** I will appoint for you pious judges.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:26:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:26:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:26:2)


**עִיר הַצֶּדֶק.** כְּבַתְּחִלָּה ״צֶדֶק יָלִין בָּהּ״ (ישעיהו א:כא):


**City of Righteousness** As in the beginning, righteousness will lodge therein.



### Verse 27

###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:27:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:27:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:27:1)


**בְּמִשְׁפָּט תִּפָּדֶה.** עַל יְדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיוּ בָּהּ עוֹשֵׂה מִשְׁפָּט:


**shall be redeemed through justice** Since there will be in it people who practice justice.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:27:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:27:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:27:2)


**תִּפָּדֶה.** מֵעֲוֹנוֹתֶיהָ:


**shall be redeemed** from her iniquities.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:27:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:27:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:27:3)


**וְשָׁבֶיהָ.** עוֹשֵׂי תְשׁוּבָה שֶׁבְּתוֹכָהּ. (בִּצְדָקָה – בְּמַצְדִּיקִים עַצְמָם בְּמִשְׁפָּט וּבִצְדָקָה שֶׁבְּתוֹכָהּ):


**and her penitent** those penitent among them. (**through righteousness** through those who make themselves righteousthrough justice and through righteousness—that are in her midst [or,] among them.)



### Verse 28

###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:28:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:28:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:28:1)


**וְשֶׁבֶר פֹּשְׁעִים וגו׳.** שֶׁבְּכֻלָּן הוֹכִיחָן לְמַעְלָה: ״וְהֵם פָּשְׁעוּ בִי״ (ישעיהו א:ב), ״גּוֹי חוֹטֵא״, ״עָזְבוּ אֶת ה׳״ (ישעיהו א:ד):


**And destruction shall come upon rebels...** For with all these expressions he reproved them above: and they rebelled against Me (verse 2), sinful nation; they forsook the Lord (verse 4).


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:28:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:28:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:28:2)


**פֹּשְׁעִים.** מוֹרְדִים וְהָעוֹבְדִים לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה:


**rebels** Rebels and sectarians and those who worship idols.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:28:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:28:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:28:3)


**וְחַטָּאִים.** אֵלּוּ עַבְרְיָינִים הָעוֹבְרִים עַל שְׁאָר אִסּוּרִין:


**and sinners** Apostates guilty of other sins.



### Verse 29

###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:29:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:29:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:29:1)


**מֵאֵילִים.** לְשׁוֹן אֵלָה, מִין אִילָן שֶׁקּוֹרִין אולמ״א בְּלַעַ״ז:


**of the elms** Heb. מֵאֵלִים, an expression derived from אֵלָה, a species of tree called olme in O.F. [orme in modern French, an elm].


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:29:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:29:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:29:2)


**אֲשֶׁר חֲמַדְתֶּם.** לַעֲבוֹד תַּחְתֵּיהֶם עֲבוֹדַת כּוֹכָבִים, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״תַּחַת אַלּוֹן וְלִבְנֶה וְאֵלָה כִּי טוֹב צִלָּהּ״ (הושע ד:ג):


**that you desired** to worship idols under them, similar to what is stated (Hosea 4:13): “Under the oak and the aspen, and the elm, for its shade is good.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:29:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:29:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:29:3)


**מֵהַגַּנּוֹת.** שָׁם הָיוּ עוֹבְדִים כּוֹכָבִים, כְּמָה דְאַתְּ אָמַר ״הַמִּתְקַדְּשִׁים וְהַמִּטַּהֲרִים אֶל הַגַּנּוֹת״ (ישעיהו סו:יז):


**because of the gardens** There they would worship idols, as it is stated (infra 66:17): “Those who prepare themselves and purify themselves for the gardens.”



### Verse 30

###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:30:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:30:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:30:1)


**נֹבֶלֶת עָלֶה.** הֶעָלֶה שֶׁלָּהּ נוֹבֶלֶת, כָּמוּשׁ, פלישטיישנ״ט בְּלַעַ״ז. בְּבֹא עָלָיו שָׁרָב אוֹ קֶרַח הוּא כָּמֵשׁ, וְלִחְלוּחוֹ אָבַד וְכָלֶה. וְאֵין ׳נוֹבֵל׳ לְשׁוֹן רִקָּבוֹן כְּמוֹ ׳בָּלֶה׳ (איכה ג:), שֶׁאֵין נוּ״ן נוֹפֶלֶת בְּאוֹתוֹ לָשׁוֹן, אֶלָּא ׳נוֹבֵל׳ לְשׁוֹן דָּבָר הַנִּלְאֶה וְכָלֶה, כְּמוֹ מִגִּזְרַת ״נָבֹל תִּבֹּל״ (שמות יח:ח), כְּמוֹ ׳תִּנְבּוֹל׳, וּמְתַרְגְּמִינָן: מֵילָאָה תֵּילָאָה:


**whose leaves wilt** Its leaf ([Other editions read:] whose leaf) wilts, becomes wilted [flatisant in O. F.]. When heat or cold comes upon it, it wilts and its moisture is lost and destroyed. [The word] נבל is not an expression of decay like בלה, for no ‘nun’ is found in that expression, but נבל [is an expression of something that becomes fatigued and its strength is curtailed, from the root of] נָבֹל תִּבֹּל (Exod. 18: 18), which Onkelos renders: You will surely be exhausted.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:30:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:30:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:30:2)


**אֲשֶׁר־מַיִם אֵין לָהּ.** לְהַשְׁקוֹת זְרָעֶיהָ; בְּדָבָר שֶׁחוֹטְאִים בּוֹ מַשְׁוֶה פֻּרְעָנוּתָם:


**that has no water** to water its seeds; to the thing with which they sin, he compares their punishment.



### Verse 31

###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:31:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:31:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:31:1)


**הֶחָסֹן.** הַתֹּקֶף, שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹנְסִין אֶת הָעֲנִיִּים וְגוֹזְלִין אוֹתָן וּמִתְחַסְּנִין בַּמָּמוֹן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר לְמַעְלָה (ישעיהו א:כג) ״וְחַבְרֵי גַנָּבִים״, יִהְיֶה אוֹתוֹ מָמוֹן לִנְעוֹרֶת שֶׁמְּנַעֲרִין מִן הַפִּשְׁתָּן (שבת כ:), שֶׁהוּא קַל וְנוֹחַ לִשָּׂרֵף:


**the[ir] strength** with which they take from the poor by force and rob them and strengthen themselves with the money. That money will become as tow, which is shaken out of the flax, which is light and easily ignited.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:31:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:31:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:31:2)


**וּפֹעֲלוֹ.** וְהָעוֹשֶׂה אוֹתוֹ תֹּקֶף יִהְיֶה לְנִיצוֹץ אֵשׁ, וּבָעֲרוּ זֶה בָּזֶה. **נִיצוֹץ** אישטנציל״א בְּלַעַ״ז. תַּרְגּוּם יוֹנָתָן: ״וּפֹעֲלוֹ״ – ״וְעוֹבַד יְדֵיהוֹן״, וְאֵין זֶה אַחַר לְשׁוֹן הָעִבְרִית, שֶׁאִם כֵּן הָיָה לוֹ לִנָּקֵד וּפָעֳלוֹ חֲטַף קָמַץ, וִיהֵא נִבְאָר לְשׁוֹן פָּעוּל. עַכְשָׁיו שֶׁהוּא נָקוּד מְלֹא פוּם (רוֹצֶה לוֹמַר חוֹלָם), נִבְאָר לְשׁוֹן פּוֹעֵל:


**and its perpetrator** The one who amasses this power will become as a spark of fire, and they will burn, one with the other. **as a spark** Heb. וּפֹעֲלוֹ לְנִיצוֹץ, estencele in O.F. [etincelle in modern French], a spark. Jonathan renders וְעוֹבַד יְדֵיהוֹן, and the work of their hands. This does not follow the Hebrew, however, for, were it so, it would have to be voweled וּפָעֳלוּ with a ‘kamatz- chatuf,’ a hurried ‘kamatz,’ and it would be explained as an expression of work. Now, that it is voweled with a ‘cholam,’ it is an expression of a worker, or perpetrator.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 1:31:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:31:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/1:31:3)


**וְאֵין מְכַבֶּה.** תַּרְגּוּם יוֹנָתָן: ״וְלָא יְהֵא עֲלֵיהוֹן חַיִּיס״:


**with no one to extinguish** Jonathan renders: And no one will pity them.



## Chapter 2


### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:2:1)


**בְּאַחֲרִית הַיָּמִים.** לְאַחַר שֶׁיִּכְלוּ הַפּוֹשְׁעִים (ישעיהו א:לא):


**At the end of the days** after the rebels perish.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:2:2)


**נָכוֹן.** מְתֻקָּן:


**firmly established** fixed.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:2:3)


**בְּרֹאשׁ הֶהָרִים.** בָּהָר שֶׁהוּא רֹאשׁ לְכָל הֶהָרִים, בַּחֲשִׁיבוּת הֶהָרִים:


**at the top of the mountains** On a mountain that is the head of all the mountains in the importance of the mountains.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:2:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:2:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:2:4)


**וְנִשָּׂא מִגְּבָעוֹת.** יִגְדַּל נֵס שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה בּוֹ, מִנִּסֵּי סִינַי וְכַרְמֶל וְתָבוֹר:


**and it shall be raised above the hills** The miracle performed on it, will be greater than the miracles of Sinai, Carmel, and Tabor.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:2:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:2:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:2:5)


**וְנָהֲרוּ.** יִתְקַבְּצוּ, יִמָּשְׁכוּ אֵלָיו כַּנְּהָרוֹת:


**will stream** will gather and stream to it like rivers.



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:3:1)


**אֶל בֵּית אֱלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב.** לְפִי שֶׁהוּא קְרָאוֹ ״בֵּית אֵל״ (בראשית כח:יט), לְפִיכָךְ יִקָּרֵא עַל שְׁמוֹ, אֲבָל אַבְרָהָם קְרָאוֹ ״בְּהַר ה׳ יֵרָאֶה״ (בראשית כב:יד), יִצְחָק קְרָאוֹ שָׂדֶה – ״לָשׂוּחַ בַּשָּׂדֶה״ (בראשית כד:סג):


**to the house of the God of Jacob** Since he [Jacob] called it [the Temple site] Beth El [the house of God], therefore, it will be called on his name, but Abraham called it a mount, “On God’s mount shall He appear” (Gen. 22:14); Isaac called it a field, “to meditate in the field” (ibid. 24:63).



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:4:1)


**לְאִתִּים.** קולטר״ש בלע״ז:


**into plowshares** koltres in O.F.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:4:2)


**לְמַזְמֵרוֹת.** שרפ״ש בְּלַעַ״ז, שֶׁזּוֹמְרִין בָּהֶן הַכְּרָמִים:


**pruning hooks** sarpes in O.F. [serpes in modern French], with which they prune the vineyards.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:5:1)


**בֵּית יַעֲקֹב וְגוֹ׳.** הָאֻמּוֹת יֹאמְרוּ לָהֶם כֵּן, וְהַמִּקְרָא הַזֶּה הוּא מוּסָב עַל ״וְהָלְכוּ עַמִּים רַבִּים וְגוֹ׳״ (ישעיהו ב:ג):


**O house of Jacob...** The nations will say this to them, and this verse refers back to the verse [commencing with], “And many peoples shall go...”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:5:2)


**לְכוּ וְנֵלְכָה בְּאוֹר ה׳.** יֹאמְרוּ לָהֶם כֵּן. וְיוֹנָתָן תִּרְגֵּם: ״יֵימְרוּן דְּבֵית יַעֲקֹב אֵיתוֹ וְגוֹ׳״:


**come and let us go in the light of the Lord** They will say this to them. Jonathan, however, renders: And those of the house of Jacob will say, [“Come and let us go in the teaching of the Law of the Lord”].



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:6:1)


**כִּי נָטַשְׁתָּה עַמְּךָ בֵּית יַעֲקֹב.** הַנָּבִיא מֵסֵב הַדִּבּוּר אֶל הַשְּׁכִינָה וְאוֹמֵר, כִּי עַד הֵנָּה עָזַבְתָּ אֶת עַמְּךָ בִּשְׁבִיל עֲוֹנָם. (דָּבָר אַחֵר: הַנָּבִיא מוֹכִיחָן וְאָמַר לָהֶם כֵּן, **כִּי נָטַשְׁתָּה עַמְּךָ בֵּית יַעֲקֹב וְכוּ׳**, עָזַבְתָּ אֶת מַעֲשֵׂה הַטּוֹב אֲשֶׁר עַל יָדוֹ נִהְיֵיתָ לְעַם, אַתֶּם בֵּית יַעֲקֹב):


**For You have forsaken Your people, the house of Jacob** The prophet addresses the Shechinah and says, “For until now You have forsaken Your People because of their iniquity.” [Other editions read:] “...that which You have forsaken Your people was because of their iniquity, for they are full of [witchcraft] from the East,” and the entire section, and all the chapters follow one another, until (ch. 5) “I will sing now...” Therefore, in the end of days, when the sinners perish, it will be good for them(Parshandatha). (Another explanation is: The prophet admonishes them and says this to them, “For you have forsaken your people, O house of Jacob...” You have forgotten [the deed of your people—Parshandatha] the good deed through which you became a people, you house of Jacob.)


###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:6:2)


**כִּי מָלְאוּ מִקֶּדֶם.** נִתְמַלְּאוּ צִבְאוֹתָם מִמַּעֲשֵׂי אֲרַמִּיִּים שֶׁהָיוּ יוֹשְׁבִים בַּמִּזְרָח, שֶׁהָיוּ מְכַשְּׁפִים וּמִשְׁתַּמְּשִׁים בְּשֵׁם עֲבוֹדַת כּוֹכָבִים (סנהדרין צא א):


**for they are full...from the east** Their hosts have become full of the deeds of the Arameans who dwell in the East, who were sorcerers and used the name of pagan deities. [Other editions read:]...and used the name of defilement [sorcery and demonism—Rashi ad loc.], as we say in Ch. Chelek (Sanh. 91a): “Abraham gave gifts” (Gen. 25:6)He gave them the name of defilement and sent them away to the land of the East [as quoted by Parshandatha].


###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:6:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:6:3)


**וּבְיַלְדֵי נָכְרִים יַשְׂפִּיקוּ.** בּוֹעֲלִים בְּנוֹת עַכּוּ״ם וּמִתְעָרְבִים בָּהֶם, וְיוֹלְדוֹת לָהֶם יְלָדִים, וּבָהֶם הֵם מַסְפִּיקִים תָּמִיד וּמִתְעַסְּקִים וּמִתְרַפְּקִין וְנִטְרָחִים בָּהֶם. לְשׁוֹן ״פֶּן יְסִיתְךָ בְשֶׂפֶק״ (איוב לו:יח), דביטימנ״ט בלע״ז:


**and with children of gentiles they please themselves** They cohabit with the daughters of the heathens and mingle with them, and they would bear children to them, with whom they are always pleased, and they occupy themselves [with them] and long for them and bother with them. This is an expression similar to [that of] (Job 36:18) “lest he incite you because of abundance (בְּשֶׂפֶק)” [debatement in O.F].



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:7:1)


**וְאֵין קֵצֶה.** לְשׁוֹן קֵץ:


**end** Heb. קָצֶה, an expression derived from קץ.



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:8:1)


**יִשְׁתַּחֲווּ.** כְּמוֹ מִשְׁתַּחֲוִים:


**they prostrate themselves** Heb. ישתחוו. Although the form is future, it is to be rendered like מִשְׁתַּחֲוִים, they prostrate themselves.



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:9:1)


**וַיִּשַּׁח אָדָם.** הַקְּטַנִּים:


**And man has become bowed down** [This refers to] inferior [men].


###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:9:2)


**וַיִּשְׁפַּל אִישׁ.** הַגְּדוֹלִים וְהַגִּבּוֹרִים אַנְשֵׁי הַחַיִל:


**and man has become humble** [This refers to] great [men], heroes, and warriors.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:9:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:9:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:9:3)


**וְאַל תִּשָּׂא לָהֶם.** הַנָּבִיא אוֹמֵר לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: וְיָדַעְתִּי כִּי לֹא תִסְלַח לָהֶם מִלְּהִפָּרַע מֵהֶם:


**and You shall not forgive them** The prophet says to the Holy One, blessed be He: And I know that you shall not forgive them from punishing them.



### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:10:1)


**בּוֹא בַצּוּר.** לָבוֹא בַּצּוּר לִבְרֹחַ בְּנִקְרַת הַצּוּרִים:


**Come into the rock** To come into the rock to escape in the cracks of the rocks.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:10:2)


**וְהִטָּמֵן בֶּעָפָר.** וּלְהִטָּמֵן בֶּעָפָר:


**and hide in the dust** and to hide in the dust.



### Verse 11

###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:11:1)


**עֵינֵי גַּבְהוּת אָדָם.** גַּסּוּת הָרוּחַ, וְכֵן כָּל לְשׁוֹן גֹּבַהּ עֵינַיִם שֶׁבַּמִּקְרָא, כְּמָה דְאַתְּ אָמַר ״גְּבַהּ עֵינַיִם וּרְחַב לֵבָב״ (תהלים קא:ה):


**The haughty eyes of man** [This means] the haughty spirit, and so every expression of haughty eyes in the Scriptures, as it is said: “Whoever is haughty of eye, lustful in heart...” (Ps. 101:5).



### Verse 13

###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:13:1)


**אַרְזֵי הַלְּבָנוֹן.** דֻּגְמָא הוּא עַל הַגִּבּוֹרִים:


**the cedars of the Lebanon** This is symbolic of the heroes [var. the kings].


###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:13:2)


**אַלּוֹנֵי הַבָּשָׁן.** הַשַּׁלְטוֹנִין, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאַלּוֹנִים פְּחוּתִים מִן הָאֲרָזִים:


**the oaks of the Bashan** The governors, just as the oaks are inferior to the cedars.



### Verse 14

###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:14:1)


**וְעַל כָּל הֶהָרִים הָרָמִים.** עַל יוֹשְׁבֵיהֶם:


**And over all the high mountains** over their inhabitants.



### Verse 16

###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:16:1)


**וְעַל כָּל אֳנִיּוֹת.** תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״וְעַל כָּל דְּיָתְבִין בְּנִיסֵי יַמָּא״ בְּאִיֵּי הַיָּם, שֶׁמּוֹצָאָן וּמוּבָאָן בָּאֳנִיּוֹת:


**And over all the ships** Jonathan renders: And over all those who inhabit the islands of the sea, who go and come by ship.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:16:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:16:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:16:2)


**תַּרְשִׁישׁ.** שֵׁם יָם שֶׁשְּׁמוֹ תַּרְשִׁישׁ:


**Tarshish** The name of a sea called Tarshish.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:16:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:16:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:16:3)


**שְׂכִיּוֹת הַחֶמְדָּה.** פַּלְטֵרִין רְצוּפִין בְּמַשְׂכִּית, רִצְפַת שַׁיִשׁ, כְּמוֹ ״וְאֶבֶן מַשְׂכִּית״ (ויקרא כו:א), עַל שֵׁם שֶׁסוֹכְכִים בּוֹ אֶת הַקַּרְקַע:


**and over all coveted floors** Heb. שְׂכִיוֹת, palaces paved with coverings of marble floors, similar to: (Lev. 26:1) and a covering stone (וְְאֶבֶן מַשְׂכִּית), since they cover the ground with it.



### Verse 17

###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:17:1)


**בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא.** הוּא יוֹם הַדִּין:


**on that day** That is the Day of Judgment.



### Verse 18

###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:18:1)


**כָּלִיל יַחֲלֹף.** כֻּלּוֹ יַחֲלֹף, כֻּלָּם יֹאבֵדוּ:


**shall completely pass away** They will all pass away; they will all vanish.



### Verse 19

###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:19:1)


**וּבָאוּ.** יוֹשְׁבֵי הָאָרֶץ בִּמְעָרוֹת צוּרִים:


**And they shall come** [i.e.,] the inhabitants of the earth shall come into the caves of the rocks.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:19:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:19:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:19:2)


**מְחִלּוֹת.** הֵם הֵם מְעָרוֹת:


**and into the hollows** They are caves.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:19:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:19:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:19:3)


**בְּקוּמוֹ.** לְיוֹם הַדִּין:


**when He rises** for Judgment Day.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:19:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:19:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:19:4)


**לַעֲרֹץ הָאָרֶץ.** לִשְׁבּוֹר רִשְׁעֵי הָאָרֶץ:


**to break the earth** to break the wicked of the earth.



### Verse 20

###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:20:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:20:1)


**לְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֹת לַחְפֹּר פֵּרוֹת.** גִּלּוּלִים בִּדְמוּת חֲפַרְפָּרוֹת, מִינֵי שְׁרָצִים שֶׁחוֹפְרִין הָאָרֶץ, שֶׁקּוֹרִין טלפ״ש בלע״ז:


**to prostrate himself to moles** Heb. לַחְפֹּר פֵּרוֹת, idols in the likeness of moles, a species of rodents who dig in the earth, called talpes in O.F. [taupes in modern French].


###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:20:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:20:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:20:2)


**וְלָעֲטַלֵּפִים.** קלבא שורי״ץ בלע״ז. יֵשׁ לִפְתּוֹר עוֹד: אֶת אֱלִילָיו אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה לוֹ לְהִשְׁתַּחֲווֹת, יַשְׁלִיךְ הָאָדָם בַּחֲרִיצִים וּבַנְּעִיצִין שֶׁיִּמְצָא לְפָנָיו, כְּשֶׁהוֹלֵךְ לִבְרוֹחַ וּלְהִטָּמֵן:


**and to bats** kalbe soric [chauvesouris in modern French]. Alternatively, this may be interpreted to mean that man will cast his idols that he made for himself, before which to prostrate himself, into pits and ditches that he finds before him when he goes to escape and hide.



### Verse 22

###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:22:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:22:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:22:1)


**חִדְלוּ לָכֶם מִן הָאָדָם.** שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹעַ לְאוֹתָן הַמַּתְעִים אֶתְכֶם מֵאַחֲרַי וּלְהִשְׁתַּחֲווֹת לְמַעֲשֵׂה יָדָיו:


**Withdraw yourselves from man** not to heed those who cause you to stray from following Me and to prostrate yourselves to the work of his hands.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 2:22:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:22:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/2:22:2)


**אֲשֶׁר נְשָׁמָה בְּאַפּוֹ.** אֲשֶׁר כָּל חַיָּתוֹ וְכֹחוֹ תְּלוּיָה בְּנִשְׁמַת אַפּוֹ, שֶׁהוּא רוּחַ פּוֹרֵחַ, שֶׁהַיּוֹם יֶשְׁנָהּ בּוֹ וּמָחָר תֵּצֵא מִמֶּנּוּ, וְקַל וָחוֹמֶר לִדְמוּת חֲפַרְפָּרוֹת שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַמָּשׁ. דָּבָר אַחֵר: חִדְלוּ לָכֶם מִכָּל הַדְּרָכִים הָרָעִים, וְלִמְדוּ מִן הָאָדָם אֲשֶׁר נְשָׁמָה בְּאַפּוֹ, הַרְאִיתֶם לְמָה נֶחְשָׁב הוּא, וְקַל וָחוֹמֶר לַגְּלוּלִים שֶׁאֵינוֹ נֶחְשָׁב לִכְלוּם:


**whose breath is in his nostrils** Whose entire life and strength are dependent upon the breath of his nostrils, which is a fleeting spirit, in him today and leaving him tomorrow. Surely the image of the moles and the bats has no substance. Another explanation is: Withdraw yourselves from all the evil ways and learn from the man who has a soul in his nostrils. Have you seen to what he is esteemed? Surely the image of his handiwork is of no esteem.



## Chapter 3


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Isaiah 3:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:1:1)


**מֵסִיר מִירוּשָׁלִַם וגו׳.** כֻּלָּהּ מְפֹרֶשֶׁת בְּמַסֶּכֶת חֲגִיגָה (חגיגה יד א): שְׁמוֹנָה עֶשְׂרֵה קְלָלוֹת קִלֵּל יְשַׁעְיָה אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְלֹא נִתְקָרְרָה דַּעְתּוֹ עַד שֶׁאָמַר ״יִרְהֲבוּ הַנַּעַר בַּזָּקֵן וְהַנִּקְלֶה בַּנִּכְבָּד״ (ישעיהו ג:ה):


**removes from Jerusalem...** This entire section is explained in Tractate Chagigah (14a): Isaiah cursed Israel [i.e., prophesied tribulations for them] with eighteen curses, yet he was not satisfied until he said, (verse 5) “The youth shall behave haughtily against the old, and the base against the honorable.”



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Isaiah 3:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:2:1)


**וְקֹסֵם.** זֶה מֶלֶךְ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״קֶסֶם עַל שִׂפְתֵי מֶלֶךְ״ (משלי טז:י):


**soothsayer** This denotes the king, as it is stated: (Prov. 16:10) “[Like] soothsaying on the lips of a king.”



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Isaiah 3:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:3:1)


**יוֹעֵץ.** יוֹדֵעַ לְעַבֵּר שָׁנִים וְלִקְבּוֹעַ חֳדָשִׁים:


**counsellor** One who knows how to intercolate the years and fix the months.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 3:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:3:2)


**וַחֲכַם חֲרָשִׁים.** שֶׁכְּשֶׁפּוֹתֵחַ בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה נַעֲשׂוּ הַכֹּל כְּחֵרְשִׁים:


**skillful craftsman** [explained by the Talmud as “wise of the deaf,” meaning that] when he commences [to speak of] words of Torah, all become as deaf [i.e., unable to refute his statement].


###### Rashi on Isaiah 3:3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:3:3)


**וּנְבוֹן לָחַשׁ.** רָאוּי לִמְסוֹר לוֹ סִתְרֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּתְּנוּ בְּלַחַשׁ, כְּגוֹן מַעֲשֵׂה בְּרֵאשִׁית וּמַעֲשֵׂה מֶרְכָּבָה:


**one who understands secrets** [The Talmud separates this into two, explaining “understanding” as one capable of deducing a decision from an earlier premise. “Secret” is explained as] one fit to be entrusted with secrets of the Torah, given in whispers, such as the story of Creation and the account of the Celestial Chariot, related in Ezekiel 1.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Isaiah 3:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:4:1)


**וְנָתַתִּי נְעָרִים שָׂרֵיהֶם.** אֵלּוּ בְּנֵי אָדָם הַמְנֹעָרִים מִן הַמִּצְוֹת:


**And I will appoint youths as their princes** These are people devoid of any observance of the commandments.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 3:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:4:2)


**וְתַעֲלוּלִים יִמְשְׁלוּ בָם.** שׁוּעָלִים, בְּנֵי אָדָם חֲלָשִׁים. וַאֲנִי אוֹמֵר לְפִי פְּשׁוּטוֹ: תַּעֲלוּלִים לֵיצָנֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם הַמִּתְעוֹלְלִים בָּהֶן וּמְבַזִּין אוֹתָם, כְּמוֹ (איוב טז:טו) ״וְעוֹלַלְתִּי בֶּעָפָר קַרְנִי״, (שמות י:ב) ״אֶת אֲשֶׁר הִתְעַלַּלְתִּי״:


**and scorners will rule over them** Heb. וְתַעֲלוּלִים [related to the Aramaic תַּעֲלֵי] foxes, [i.e.,] weak people. But I say that according to the simple meaning, תַּעֲלוּלִים means scornful people, people who mock them, as (Job 16:15): “I soiled (וְעוֹלַלְתִּי) my radiance in the dust,” and (Exod. 10: 2): “how I mocked (הִתְעַלַּלְתִּי) the Egyptians.”



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Isaiah 3:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:5:1)


**וְנִגַּשׂ הָעָם.** יִהְיוּ דְחוּקִין וּנְגוּשִׁין זֶה עַל זֶה בְּתִיגוּר וְחִירוּם:


**And the people shall be oppressed** They shall be pressed and oppressing each other with competition and strife.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 3:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:5:2)


**יִרְהֲבוּ הַנַּעַר בַּזָּקֵן.** יִתְגַּדֵּל הַנַּעַר עַל הַזָּקֵן:


**they shall behave haughtily, the youth against the elder** The youth will raise himself over the elder.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 3:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:5:3)


**וְהַנִּקְלֶה בַּנִּכְבָּד.** כִּפְשׁוּטוֹ. וּמִדְרָשׁוֹ (חגיגה יד א): יָבֹא מִי שֶׁחֲמוּרוֹת דּוֹמוֹת עָלָיו כְּקַלּוֹת, וְיִרְהַב בְּמִי שֶׁהַקַּלּוֹת דּוֹמוֹת עָלָיו כִּכְבֵדוֹת:


**and the base against the honorable** [This is to be interpreted] according to its simple meaning. The exegetical meaning is as follows: Let one to whom grave interdicts seem light come and raise himself over one to whom light interdicts seem grave.



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Isaiah 3:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:6:1)


**כִּי יִתְפֹּשׂ אִישׁ בְּאָחִיו.** כַּאֲשֶׁר יִתְפֹּשׂ אִישׁ בְּאָחִיו בְּבֵית אָבִיו לֵאמֹר: ״עָשִׁיר אַתָּה בַּתּוֹרָה, וּמְחֻוֶּרֶת הִיא בְּיָדְךָ כַּשִּׂמְלָה״:


**When a man shall seize his brother** When a man shall seize his brother in his father’s house, saying, “You are wealthy in Torah, and it is as white to you as a garment.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 3:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:6:2)


**קָצִין תִּהְיֶה לָּנוּ.** וּתְלַמְּדֵנוּ:


**be an officer to us** and teach us.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 3:6:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:6:3)


**וְהַמַּכְשֵׁלָה הַזֹּאת.** שֶׁאָנוּ נִכְשָׁלִים בָּהּ בְּאִסּוּר אוֹ בְּהֶתֵּר, בְּטֻמְאָה אוֹ בְּטָהֳרָה, **תַּחַת יָדֶיךָ** הוּא, שֶׁאַתָּה יוֹדֵעַ לְהוֹרוֹת לָנוּ. דָּבָר אַחֵר: **שִׂמְלָה לְךָ** לְהַלְבִּישׁ עָרוֹם:


**and this obstacle** upon which we are stumbling, in prohibition or permissibility, in defilement or in purity, shall be under your hand, for you know how to instruct us. Another explanation is: You have a garment to clothe the naked.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 3:6:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:6:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:6:4)


**וְהַמַּכְשֵׁלָה.** (פיילנצ״א בלע״ז) מֶחְסְרוֹנִי שֶׁאֲנִי מְחֻסַּר לֶחֶם תַּחַת יָדֶךָ לְהַסְפִּיקֵנִי, וּלְכָךְ **קָצִין תִּהְיֶה לָּנוּ.** וְהוּא מֵשִׁיב: **בְּבֵיתִי אֵין לֶחֶם וְאֵין שִׂמְלָה**, וּמַה טִיבִי לְקָצִין?


**and this obstacle** fajjlejjnca in O.F. [faibless in modern French]. My want, that I lack bread, is under your hand to supply me. Therefore, you shall be to us as an officer. He replies, In my house there is neither bread nor clothing. What then are my qualifications as an officer?



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Isaiah 3:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:7:1)


**יִשָּׂא בַיּוֹם הַהוּא.** אֵין ״יִשָּׂא״ אֶלָּא לְשׁוֹן שְׁבוּעָה: הוּא יִשָּׁבַע לָהֶם, **לֹא אֶהְיֶה חוֹבֵשׁ** – לֹא אֶהְיֶה מֵחוֹבְשֵׁי בֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ, **וּבְבֵיתִי אֵין לֶחֶם וְשִׂמְלָה** – אֵין בְּיָדִי לֹא טַעַם מִשְׁנָה וְלֹא טַעַם אַגָּדָה. דָּבָר אַחֵר לְפִי פְּשׁוּטוֹ: **לֹא אֶהְיֶה חוֹבֵשׁ** – לֹא אֶהְיֶה שׁוֹפֵט, שֶׁהוּא חוֹבֵשׁ אֶת הַנִּדּוֹנִים בְּבֵית הַסֹּהַר:


**He shall swear on that day** [lit. he will raise. The word יִשָּׂא] is only an expression of swearing; he will swear to them, I will not be a ‘Chovesh.’ I will not be one of those confined to the study hall, since, in my house there is neither bread nor clothing; I have understanding neither of the Mishnah nor of the Aggadah. Another explanation according to the simple meaning is: I will not be a confiner; I will not be a judge, who confines the convicts to prison.



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Isaiah 3:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:8:1)


**כִּי כָשְׁלָה יְרוּשָׁלִַם.** כֻּלָּם חֲסֵרִים וּנְפוּלִים, וְאֵין עוֹזֵר זֶה לָזֶה. וְלָמָּה? כִּי מֵאֲנוּ לִשְׁמֹעַ, וְעַתָּה כֻּלָּם מַכְעִיסִים:


**For Jerusalem stumbled** They are all faulty and falling, and no one assists the next one. Why? Because they refused to obey, and now, they all provoke.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 3:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:8:2)


**כִּי לְשׁוֹנָם וּמַעַלְלֵיהֶם אֶל ה׳.** לְנֶגְדּוֹ, לְהַכְעִיסוֹ:


**for their tongue and their deeds are against the Lord** [lit. to the Lord;] against Him to provoke Him.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 3:8:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:8:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:8:3)


**לַמְרוֹת עֵינֵי כְבוֹדוֹ.** לְהַקְנִיט לִפְנֵי כְּבוֹדוֹ. דָּבָר אַחֵר: עִנְיְנֵי כְּבוֹדוֹ:


**to provoke the eyes of His glory** to provoke before His glory. Another explanation is: to provoke the matters of His glory.



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Isaiah 3:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:9:1)


**הַכָּרַת פְּנֵיהֶם.** עָוֹן שֶׁהֵם מַכִּירִים פָּנִים בַּדִּין, הִיא עָנְתָה בָּם לְפָנַי. לָשׁוֹן אַחֵר: הַכָּרַת פְּנֵיהֶם – נִכָּרִים הֵם בְּעַזּוּת פְּנֵיהֶם:


**The recognition of their faces** The sin that they recognize faces [i.e., show favoritism] in judgment testified against them before Me. Another version is: The recognition of their faces—They are recognizable by the boldness of their faces.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 3:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:9:2)


**כִּסְדֹם הִגִּידוּ. לֹא כִחֵדוּ,** בְּפַרְהֶסְיָא עָשׂוּ:


**like Sodom they told, they did not deny** They committed [sins] publicly.



### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Isaiah 3:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:10:1)


**אִמְרוּ** לְמִי שֶׁהוּא **צַדִּיק כִּי טוֹב** עָשָׂה:


**Praise the righteous man for he is good** Say to the righteous man that he did good.



### Verse 11

###### Rashi on Isaiah 3:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:11:1)


**אוֹי לְרָשָׁע רָע.** שֶׁהוּא רַע לְעַצְמוֹ וְרַע לַאֲחֵרִים; גּוֹרֵם רָעָה לוֹ וְלַאֲחֵרִים. בְּתַנְחוּמָא (תנחומא, אמור ה). וְהַמִּקְרָא מוּסָב עַל **אִמְרוּ צַדִּיק כִּי טוֹב** לוֹ, וְ**אוֹי** לוֹ **לְרָשָׁע רָע**:


**Woe to the wicked [who does] evil** For he is bad to himself and to others; he brings about harm to himself and to others. [This is found] in Tanchuma (Emor 5). This verse refers back to: Say to the righteous that he is good and woe is to the wicked [who does evil].



### Verse 12

###### Rashi on Isaiah 3:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:12:1)


**נֹגְשָׂיו מְעוֹלֵל.** לֵיצָנִים הֵם:


**their rulers are mockers** Heb. נֹגְשָׂיו מְעוֹלֵל, they are mockers.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 3:12:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:12:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:12:2)


**וְנָשִׁים מָשְׁלוּ בוֹ.** נָשִׁים נוֹאֲפוֹת מָשְׁלוּ בּוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר לְמַטָּה ״יַעַן כִּי גָבְהוּ בְּנוֹת צִיּוֹן״ (ישעיהו ג:טז), וְהִטּוּ לִבָּם לְרָעָה. (לְפִיכָךְ כָּל חַלָּשִׁים מָשְׁלוּ בוֹ). וְיוֹנָתָן תִּרְגֵּם לְשׁוֹן (נוֹשִׁים):


**and women govern them** Heb. נָשִׁים. Adulterous women govern them, as he states below (verse 16): “Since the daughters of Zion were haughty,” and they turned their hearts to evil; therefore, all weaklings governed them. Jonathan renders it as an expression of creditors (נוֹשִׁים) [rendering: and as creditors they govern them].


###### Rashi on Isaiah 3:12:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:12:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/3:12:3)


**מְאַשְּׁרֶיךָ.** מַדְרִיכֶיךָ, שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם לְאַשְּׁרֶךָ בְּדֶרֶךְ טוֹב, הֵם מַתְעִים אוֹתָם:


**Your leaders** Heb. מְאַשְּׁרֶיךָ. Your leaders, who should have led you on the good way, lead you astray.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 3:12:4
