Raising an ensign (נֵס) is like a long pole (כְּלוּנָס), at the end of which they attach a cloth, [i.e., a flag,] and they climb to the top of a lofty mountain and see it from afar; and that is the sign for people to gather. Comp. (infra 49:22) “And to peoples I will raise My ensign (נִסִּי)”; comp. also (Numbers 21:8), “And set it upon a pole (נֵס),” meaning a pole (כְּלוּנָס), perche in French, but since it is for a sign, it is called נֵס.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 5:26:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:26:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:26:2)


**וְשָׁרַק.** שיבלי״ר בְּלַעַ״ז, אַף הוּא סִימָן לְקִבּוּץ:


**And He will whistle** sibler in O.F. This too is a sign for gathering.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 5:26:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:26:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:26:3)


**מִקְצֵה הָאָרֶץ.** שֶׁיָּבוֹאוּ מֵרָחוֹק לָצוּר עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל:


**from the end of the earth** that they should come from afar to besiege Israel.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 5:26:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:26:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:26:4)


**קַל יָבוֹא.** הָאוֹיֵב עֲלֵיהֶם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּפָרֵשׁ וְהוֹלֵךְ:


**swiftly he will come** The enemy [will come] upon them [swiftly,] as Scripture proceeds to explain.



### Verse 27

###### Rashi on Isaiah 5:27:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:27:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:27:1)


**אֵין עָיֵף וְאֵין כּוֹשֵׁל בּוֹ.** לֹא יִיעַף וְלֹא יִכָּשֵׁל בִּמְרוּצָתוֹ, לְקַיֵּים ״יְמַהֵר יְחִישָׁה״ (ישעיהו ה:יט) שֶׁהֵם אוֹמְרִים לְפָנָיו:


**None is weary or stumbles among them** No one will be weary and no one will stumble in his running, to fulfill (supra v. 19), “Let Him hurry, let Him hasten,” that they say before Him.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 5:27:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:27:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:27:2)


**נִפְתַּח.** לְשׁוֹן נִתַּר, כְּמוֹ ״וַיְפַתַּח הַגְּמַלִּים״ (בראשית כד:לב):


**open up** Heb. נִפְתַּח, an expression of untying, as (Genesis 24:32): “And he untied (וַיְפַתַּח) the camels.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 5:27:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:27:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:27:3)


**וְלֹא נִתַּק.** וְלֹא יִרְאוּ שָׁם סִימָן כִּשָּׁלוֹן, לִירָא מִמֶּנִּי מִלָּבֹא:


**nor will...be torn** And they will not see any omen of defeat, because of which to fear to come.



### Verse 28

###### Rashi on Isaiah 5:28:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:28:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:28:1)


**כַּצַּר.** תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״כְּטִינְרָא״, כְּמוֹ צוּר:


**like flint** Jonathan renders: like a rock, similar to צור.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 5:28:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:28:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:28:2)


**וְגַלְגִּלָּיו.** אוֹפַנֵּי מַרְכְּבוֹתָיו:


**and his wheels** the wheels of his chariots.



### Verse 29

###### Rashi on Isaiah 5:29:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:29:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:29:1)


**שְׁאָגָה.** אֵימָה זוֹ תִּהְיֶה עֲלֵיכֶם כְּמוֹ לָבִיא:


**He has a roar like a lion** His fear will be upon you like a lion.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 5:29:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:29:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:29:2)


**וְיַפְלִיט.** יַצִּילֶנּוּ לְטַרְפּוֹ מִיַּד כָּל הַבָּאִים לְהַצִּילָהּ. **יַפְלִיט** – אישקמוצייר בלע״ז:


**and he will retrieve** He will save it from all those who try to save it. יַפְלִיט is esmoucer in O.F. [to seize].



### Verse 30

###### Rashi on Isaiah 5:30:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:30:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:30:1)


**וְיִנְהֹם.** אוֹתוֹ הָאוֹיֵב עַל עַם ה׳ הַנִּזְכָּר לְמַעְלָה:


**And he will growl** That enemy [will growl] at the people of the Lord, mentioned above.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 5:30:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:30:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:30:2)


**כְּנַהֲמַת יָם.** אֲשֶׁר יֶהֱמוּ גַּלָּיו, כֵּן יָבוֹא בַּחֲיָלוֹת הוֹמוֹת:


**like the growling of the sea** whose waves roar, so will he come with roaring armies.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 5:30:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:30:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:30:3)


**וְנִבַּט לָאָרֶץ.** לְשׁוֹן הַבָּטָה: יַבִּיטוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל וִיצַפּוּ שֶׁיַּעַזְרוּם מַלְכֵי אֶרֶץ שֶׁהֵם סוֹמְכִין עֲלֵיהֶם, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״הַיֹּרְדִים מִצְרַיִם לְעֶזְרָה״ (ישעיהו לא:א):


**and he will look to the land** Heb. וְנִבַּט, an expression of looking. Israel will look and hope that the kings of the land, upon whom they rely, will assist them, like the matter that is stated (infra 31:1): “Those who go down to Egypt for aid.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 5:30:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:30:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:30:4)


**וְהִנֵּה חֹשֶׁךְ.** שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא עוֹזֵר לָהֶם. **וְנִבַּט** לְשׁוֹן נִפְעַל, כְּמוֹ ״לֹא נִפְתַּח״ וְ״לֹא נִתַּק״ (ישעיהו ה:כז), וְהַוָּי״ו גּוֹרֶמֶת לוֹ לְהָסֵב הַדִּבּוּר לְהַבָּא, אייר״ט איסגרד״י בלע״ז:


**and behold darkness** for they will have no support. וְנִבַּט is in the passive voice (נִפְעַל) like וְלֹא נִפְתַּח, will not open up, וְלֹא נִתַּק, will not be torn, and the ‘vav’ causes the tense to be reversed to the future. Ediert esvuardeyd in O.F.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 5:30:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:30:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:30:5)


**צַר וָאוֹר חָשַׁךְ.** כְּמוֹ ״וְכָשַׁל עוֹזֵר וְנָפַל עָזוּר״ (ישעיהו לא:ג), מִי שֶׁצַּר לוֹ שֶׁבָּאת עָלָיו הַצָּרָה, וְזֶה שֶׁבָּא לְהָאִיר לוֹ – שְׁנֵיהֶם חָשְׁכוּ. וְיֵשׁ פּוֹתְרִין: צַר הִיא הַלְּבָנָה שֶׁנִּתְמַעֲטָה, וְאוֹר הִיא הַחַמָּה:


**the distressed one and the light shall darken** Comp. (infra 31:3) “And the helper shall stumble and the one who is helped shall fall.” He who is distressed, upon whom the trouble has come, as well as he who comes to bring light to him, both of them will darken. Some interpret צַר as the moon, whose light was diminished, צַר [meaning narrow,] and אוֹר as the sun, [meaning light].


###### Rashi on Isaiah 5:30:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:30:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:30:6)


**בַּעֲרִיפֶיהָ.** בְּבֹא מַאֲפֵלִיָּה שֶׁלָּהּ, לָשׁוֹן ״יַעֲרֹף כַּמָּטָר״ (דברים לב:ב), וְכֵן דֶּרֶךְ בַּעֲרוֹף מָטָר הָאוֹר מַאֲפִיל:


**in its eclipse** Heb. בַּעֲרִיפֶיהָ. When its darkening comes. An expression similar to (Deut. 32:2): “Shall drip (יַעֲרֹף) like rain,” for so is the nature that when rain falls, the light darkens.



## Chapter 6


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Isaiah 6:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:1:1)


**בִּשְׁנַת מוֹת.** כְּשֶׁנִּצְטָרַע (תנחומא צו יג):


**In the year of the death** i.e., when he was smitten with zaraath.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 6:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:1:2)


**וְשׁוּלָיו.** כְּמוֹ ״שׁוּלֵי הַמְּעִיל״ (שמות כח:לד), תַּחְתִּיתוֹ. רְאִיתִיו **יוֹשֵׁב עַל כִּסֵּא** בַּשָּׁמַיִם, וְרַגְלָיו בַּהֵיכָל, הֲדוֹם מַרְגְּלוֹתָיו בְּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, לָדוּן עַל עֻזִּיָּה שֶׁבָּא לִטּוֹל כֶּתֶר כְּהֻנָּה:


**and His lower extremity** Heb. וְשׁוּלָיו, comp. (Exodus 28:34) “On the hem (שׁוּלֵי) of the robe,” meaning its lower extremity. I saw Him sitting on His throne in heaven with His feet in the Temple, His footstool in the Sanctuary, to pass judgment on Uzziah, who came to usurp the crown of the priesthood.



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Isaiah 6:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:2:1)


**שְׂרָפִים עֹמְדִים מִמַּעַל.** בַּשָּׁמַיִם:


**Seraphim stood above** in heaven.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 6:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:2:2)


**לוֹ.** לְשַׁמְּשׁוֹ, כֵּן תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״שַׁמְּשִׁין קַדִּישִׁין בְּרוֹמָא קֳדָמוֹהִי״:


**for Him** i.e., to serve him, and so does Jonathan render: Holy servants are on high before Him.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 6:2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:2:3)


**בִּשְׁתַּיִם יְכַסֶּה פָנָיו.** שֶׁלֹּא יַבִּיט לְצַד הַשְּׁכִינָה:


**with two he would cover his face** so as not to look toward the Shechinah.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 6:2:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:2:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:2:4)


**וּבִשְׁתַּיִם יְכַסֶּה רַגְלָיו.** לִצְנִיעוּת, שֶׁלֹּא יֵרָאֶה כָּל גּוּפוֹ לִפְנֵי בּוֹרְאוֹ. וּבְתַנְחוּמָא (תנחומא, אמור ח) רָאִיתִי: כִּסּוּי הָרַגְלַיִם לְפִי שֶׁהֵם ״כְּכַף רֶגֶל עֵגֶל״ (יחזקאל א:ז), שֶׁלֹּא לְהַזְכִּיר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל עֲוֹן הָעֵגֶל:


**and with two he would cover his feet** for modesty, so as not to bare his entire body before his Creator. And in Tanhuma (Emor 8), I saw that the feet were covered because they are like the sole of the foot of a calf, in order not to remind Israel of the sin of the golden calf.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 6:2:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:2:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:2:5)


**וּבִשְׁתַּיִם יְעוֹפֵף.** וּבִתְרֵין מְשַׁמֵּשׁ:


**and with two he would fly** And with two he would serve [from Targum Jonathan].



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Isaiah 6:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:3:1)


**וְקָרָא זֶה אֶל זֶה.** נוֹטְלִין רְשׁוּת זֶה מִזֶּה, שֶׁלֹּא יַקְדִּים הָאֶחָד וְיַתְחִיל וְיִתְחַיֵּב שְׂרֵפָה, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן פָּתְחוּ כֻּלָּם כְּאֶחָד; וְזֶהוּ שֶׁיִּסַּד בְּיוֹצֵר אוֹר: ׳קְדוּשָׁה כֻּלָּם כְּאֶחָד עוֹנִים׳. וּמִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה מַעֲשֵׂה מֶרְכָּבָה הוּא; וְכֵן תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן:


**And one called to the other** They would take permission from one another so that one would not commence before [his fellows] and be guilty of [a sin punishable by] burning, unless they all commenced simultaneously. This is what was established in [the blessing commencing:] “...Who formed light,” “the declaration of holiness, they all respond as one...” This is a Midrash Aggadah of the account of the Merkavah. And so did Jonathan render this.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 6:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:3:2)


**קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ.** שָׁלוֹשׁ פְּעָמִים, כְּתַרְגּוּמוֹ:


**Holy, holy, holy** Three times, as the Targum renders.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Isaiah 6:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:4:1)


**וַיָּנֻעוּ אַמּוֹת הַסִּפִּים.** ״אֵילְוַת סִפֵּי״ (תרגום יונתן), הֵם מְזוּזוֹת הַפֶּתַח, שֶׁנִּמְדָּדִין בְּמִדּוֹת אַמּוֹת לְגֹבַהּ וּלְרֹחַב, וְהֵן מְזוּזוֹת הַהֵיכָל:


**And the doorposts quaked** [Jonathan renders:] אֵילְוַת סִפֵּי, they are the doorposts of the entrance, which are measured with the measurements of cubits in the height and in the width, and they are the doorposts of the Temple.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 6:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:4:2)


**מִקּוֹל הַקּוֹרֵא.** מִקּוֹל הַמַּלְאָכִים הַקּוֹרְאִים, וְהוּא הָיָה יוֹם הָרַעַשׁ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ ״וְנַסְתֶּם כַּאֲשֶׁר נַסְתֶּם מִפְּנֵי הָרַעַשׁ בִּימֵי עֻזִּיָּה״ (זכריה יד:ה). בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם עָמַד עֻזִּיָּה לְהַקְטִיר בַּהֵיכָל, רָעֲשׁוּ שָׁמַיִם לְשָׂרְפוֹ לוֹמַר: דִּינוֹ בִּשְׂרֵפָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וַתֹּאכַל אֵת הַחֲמִשִּׁים וּמָאתַיִם אִישׁ״ (במדבר טז:לה), וְזֶהוּ שֶׁקְּרָאָם שְׂרָפִים שֶׁבָּאוּ לְשָׂרְפוֹ. רָעֲשָׁה הָאָרֶץ לְבָלְעוֹ, כִּסְבוּרָה: דִּינוֹ לִבָּלַע כְּקֹרַח שֶׁעִרְעֵר עַל הַכְּהֻנָּה. יָצְתָה בַּת קוֹל וְאָמְרָה: ״זִכָּרוֹן לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹ׳״ (במדבר יז:ה), וְלֹא יִהְיֶה עוֹד אָדָם הַמְעוֹרֵר עַל הַכְּהֻנָּה כְּקֹרַח בִּבְלִיעָה וְכַעֲדָתוֹ בִּשְׂרֵפָה, אֶלָּא כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר ה׳ בְּיַד מֹשֶׁה בַּסְּנֶה ״הָבֵא נָא יָדְךָ בְּחֵיקֶךָ״ (שמות ד:ו), וְהוֹצִיאָהּ מְצֹרַעַת כַּשֶּׁלֶג; אַף כָּאן צָרַעַת פָּרְחָה בְּמִצְחוֹ:


**from the voice of him who called** [i.e.,] from the voice of the angels calling. This took place on the day of the earthquake, about which it is stated (Zechariah 14:5): “And you shall flee as you fled on the day of the earthquake in the days of Uzziah.” On the day that Uzziah stood, ready to burn incense in the Temple, the heavens quaked, [attempting] to burn him, as if to say that his punishment should be by burning, as it is said (Num. 16:35): “And it consumed the two hundred and fifty men.” For this reason, Scripture calls them seraphim, for they attempted to burn him. The earth quaked, attempting to swallow him up, thinking that his punishment should be that he be swallowed up like Korah, who contested the priesthood. Thereupon, a heavenly voice emanated and said (ibid. 17: 5), “And there shall not be” another man contesting the priesthood “like Korah” to be swallowed up, “and like his assembly” to be burnt, but, “as the Lord spoke by the hand of Moses,” in the thornbush (Exodus 4:6), “Now bring your hand into your bosom,” and he took it out, stricken with zaraath like snow, here too, the zaraath shone on his forehead.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 6:4:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:4:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:4:3)


**וְהַבַּיִת יִמָּלֵא עָשָׁן.** הָיָה נִמְלָא עָשָׁן:


**and the House became filled with smoke** Was filled with smoke [i.e., even though the future tense is used, the past is meant].



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Isaiah 6:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:5:1)


**כִּי נִדְמֵיתִי.** הֲרֵינִי מֵת, שֶׁלֹּא הָיִיתִי כְּדַאי שֶׁאֶרְאֶה פְּנֵי הַשְּׁכִינָה. וְדֻגְמָתוֹ מָצִינוּ בְּמָנוֹחַ ״מוֹת נָמוּת כִּי אֱלֹהִים רָאִינוּ״ (שופטים יג:כב):


**for I am lost** I will die, for I was not worthy of seeing the Countenance of the Shechinah. We find a similar statement made by Manoah (Judges 13:22): “We shall surely die, for we have seen God.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 6:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:5:2)


**נִדְמֵיתִי.** כְּמוֹ ״כִּי נִדְמָה כָּל עַם כְּנַעַן״ (צפניה א:יא):


**I am lost** Heb. נִדְמֵיתִי, comp. (Zephaniah 1:11): “The entire people of Canaan is broken (נִדְמֶה).”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 6:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:5:3)


**טְמֵא שְׂפָתַיִם.** ״דִּמְגָעַל בְּחוֹבִין״ (תרגום יונתן):


**people of unclean lips** that are defiled with sins [from Jonathan].



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Isaiah 6:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:6:1)


**רִצְפָּה.** גַּחֶלֶת, וְכֵן ״עֻגַת רְצָפִים״ (מלכים א יט:ו) כְּמוֹ ׳עֻגַּת רְשָׁפִים׳. וְנֶאֱמַר בִּישַׁעְיָהוּ וּבְאֵלִיָּהוּ בְּצָדִ״י ׳רִצְפָּה׳, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאָמְרוּ דִילָטוֹרְיָא עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל: זֶה קְרָאָם ״עַם טְמֵא שְׂפָתַיִם״, וְזֶה אָמַר ״כִּי עָזְבוּ בְרִיתֶךָ״ (מלכים א יט:י). אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לַמַּלְאָךְ: רְצוֹץ פֶּה שֶׁאָמַר דִילָטוֹרְיָא עַל בָּנַי (שיר השירים רבה א:ט):


**a glowing coal** Heb. רִצְפָּה, a coal, and similarly, (I Kings 19:6) “a cake baked on hot coals (עֻגַּת רְצָפִים),” like עֻגַּת רְשָׁפִים. In regards to Isaiah and Elijah, however, it is written with a ‘zadi,’ רִצְפָּה, because they spoke ill of Israel. This one [Isaiah] called them a people of unclean lips, and this one [Elijah] said, (ibid. 10) “For...have forsaken Your covenant.” Said the Holy One, blessed be He, to the angel, “Break the mouth (רְצוֹץ פֶּה) that spoke ill of My children.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 6:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:6:2)


**בְּמֶלְקָחַיִם.** בִּצְבָת:


**with tongs** Heb. (בְּמֶלְקֳחַיִם) with tongs.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 6:6:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:6:3)


**לָקַח מֵעַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ.** שֶׁבָּעֲזָרָה:


**he had taken it from upon the altar** that was in the forecourt.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Isaiah 6:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:7:1)


**וַיַּגַּע עַל פִּי וְגוֹ׳. וְסָר עֲוֺנֶךָ** – זֶה לְיַסְּרֶךָ, לְכַפֵּר עֲוֺנְךָ שֶׁחֵרַפְתָּ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל. וְגָדוֹל כֹּחוֹ, שֶׁהַמַּלְאָךְ יָרֵא לְקַחְתָּהּ כִּי אִם בְּמֶלְקָחַיִם, וְהִגִּיעָהּ עַל שִׂפְתֵי הַנָּבִיא וְלֹא הֻזַּק, בְּתַנְחוּמָא (תנחומא, וישלח ב). וְזֶהוּ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״כִּי רַב מְאֹד מַחֲנֵהוּ״ (יואל ב:יא) – אֵלּוּ מַלְאָכִים, וַעֲצוּמִים מֵהֶם ״עוֹשֵׂי דְבָרוֹ״ (שם) – הֵם הַנְּבִיאִים. וְיוֹנָתָן תִּרְגֵּם **וּבְיָדוֹ רִצְפָּה** – ״וּבְפוּמֵיהּ מְמַלֵּל״. לְשׁוֹן ״רִצְפָּה״ דִּבּוּר הָרָצוּף בַּפֶּה וּבַלָּשׁוֹן. **מֵעַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ** – קִבֵּל הַדִּבּוּר מִפִּי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, מִכִּסְאוֹ שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם, שֶׁהָיָה מְכֻוָּן כְּנֶגֶד הַמִּזְבֵּחַ שֶׁבַּהֵיכָל:


**And he caused it to touch my mouth... “...and your iniquity shall be removed”** This is to cause pain, to atone for your iniquity that you degraded Israel. And his strength was great, for the angel was afraid to take it without tongs, yet he caused it to touch the prophet’s lip, and he [the prophet] was not injured. [This is found] in Tanhuma (ibid.) This is [the meaning] of what Scripture states (Joel 2: 11): “For His camp is very great,” these are the angels; “and stronger” than they “are those who fulfill His word”these are the prophets (Tanhuma ibid.). Jonathan renders: “And in his hand was a glowing coal,” to mean, “And in his mouth was speech.” The expression רִצְפָּה: [means a thing refined in the mouth and with the tongue] (רָצוּף בְּפֶּה). “From upon the altar,” he received the speech from the mouth of the Holy One, blessed be he, from His throne in Heaven, which was directed opposite the altar that was in the Temple.



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Isaiah 6:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:8:1)


**אֶת מִי אֶשְׁלַח.** לְהוֹכִיחַ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל? שָׁלַחְתִּי אֶת עָמוֹס וְהָיוּ קוֹרִין אוֹתוֹ פְּסִילוּס, לְפִי שֶׁהָיָה כְּבַד לָשׁוֹן, וְהוּא נִתְנַבֵּא ״שְׁנָתַיִם לִפְנֵי הָרַעַשׁ״ (עמוס א:א), וְהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל אוֹמְרִים: הִנִּיחַ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶת הָעוֹלָם וְהִשְׁרָה שְׁכִינָתוֹ עַל הַדֵּין קְטִיעַ לִישְׁנָא וְכוּ׳, כִּדְאִיתָא בַּפְּסִיקְתָּא (פסיקתא דרב כהנא טז, ד):


**Whom shall I send** to admonish Israel? I sent Amos, and they called him, ‘Pesilus,’ because he was tongue tied, [’Pesilus’ being the Greek word for tongue-tied.] He prophesied two years before the earthquake, and the Israelites would say, The Holy One, blessed be He, left over the whole world and caused His Shechinah to rest on this tongue-tied one, as is stated in Pesikta.



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Isaiah 6:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:9:1)


**שִׁמְעוּ שָׁמוֹעַ.** אֲנִי אוֹמֵר לָכֶם **שִׁמְעוּ שָׁמוֹעַ**, וְאַתֶּם אֵין אַתֶּם נוֹתְנִים לֵב לְהָבִין, **וּרְאוּ** נִסִּים שֶׁעָשִׂיתִי לָכֶם, וְאֵינְכֶם נוֹתְנִים לֵב לָדַעַת אוֹתִי:


**Indeed you hear** I say to you, Indeed you hear, but you do not strive to understand, and indeed you see miracles that I have performed for you, yet you do not strive to know Me.



### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Isaiah 6:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:10:1)


**הַשְׁמֵן לֵב הָעָם הַזֶּה.** כְּמוֹ ״הַכְבֵּד אֶת לִבּוֹ״ (שמות ח:יא), לְשׁוֹן הָלוֹךְ, לְשׁוֹן פָּעוֹל: לִבָּם הוֹלֵךְ הָלוֹךְ וְהַשְׁמֵן (אנגריישנ״ט בְּלַעַ״ז), **וְאָזְנָיו** הוֹלְכִים הָלוֹךְ **וְהַכְבֵּד** מִשְּׁמוֹעַ:


**This people’s heart is becoming fat** [This structure] הַשְׁמֵן resembles (Exodus 8:11), “And making his heart heavy (הַכְבֵּד),” an expression of a continuous action. Their heart continuously becomes fatter, angrajjsant in O.F., and his ears are becoming heavier and heavier, [i.e., harder and harder] of hearing.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 6:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:10:2)


**וְעֵינָיו הָשַׁע.** טָחִים, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ישעיהו מד:יח) ״כִּי טַח מֵרְאוֹת עֵינֵיהֶם״, הַטּוֹחַ (ויקרא יד:מג) מְתַרְגְּמִינָן ״דְּאִתְשַׁע״:


**and his eyes are becoming sealed** Plastered, comp. (infra 44:18) “For their eyes are plastered from seeing.” הִטּוֹחַ (Leviticus 14:43) is translated into Aramaic as דְאִתְשַׁע. We, thereby, equate the two words הָשַׁע and טָח.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 6:10:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:10:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:10:3)


**פֶּן יִרְאֶה בְעֵינָיו** נָתְנוּ לִבָּם שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁמְעוּ דִּבְרֵי נְבִיאִים, שֶׁהֵם יְרֵאִים שֶׁמָּא יוּטְבוּ בְּעֵינֵיהֶם דְּבָרָיו, וְיָבִינוּ בְּלִבָּם וְיָשׁוּבוּ אֵלַי, וְהִיא רְפוּאָתָם:


**lest he see with his eyes** They intended not to hearken to the words of the prophets, for they fear lest His words please them, and they will understand with their heart, and return to Me, and this will be their cure.



### Verse 11

###### Rashi on Isaiah 6:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:11:1)


**עַד מָתַי** יַכְבִּידוּ אֶת לִבָּם וְלֹא יִשְׁמְעוּ?


**Until when** will they make their heart heavy and not listen?


###### Rashi on Isaiah 6:11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:11:2)


**וַיֹּאמֶר.** יָדַעְתִּי כִּי לֹא יָשִׁיבוּ עַד תָּבֹא פֻּרְעָנוּת עֲלֵיהֶם, וְיֵלְכוּ בַּגּוֹלָה, **וְשָׁאוּ** עָרֵיהֶם **מֵאֵין יוֹשֵׁב.**


**And He said** I know that they will not repent until retribution comes upon them and they go into exile, and the cities will be desolate without inhabitants.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 6:11:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:11:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:11:3)


**שָׁאוּ... תִּשָּׁאֶה** לְשׁוֹן גַּלְמוּד **מֵאֵין יוֹשֵׁב.**


**lies waste and desolate** an expression of solitude, without an inhabitant.



### Verse 12

###### Rashi on Isaiah 6:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:12:1)


**וְרַבָּה הָעֲזוּבָה.** שֶׁ״הָאָרֶץ תֵּעָזֵב מֵהֶם״ (ויקרא כו:מג), וְכָךְ הַלָּשׁוֹן: יִרְבּוּ מְקוֹמוֹת עֲזוּבִים **בְּקֶרֶב הָאָרֶץ.**


**and the deserted places be many** For the land will be abandoned by them, and this is the explanation of the language: Deserted places will increase in the midst of the land.



### Verse 13

###### Rashi on Isaiah 6:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:13:1)


**וְעוֹד בָּהּ עֲשִׂרִיָּה.** גַּם אוֹתָהּ הַשְּׁאֵרִית אָשִׁיב יָדִי עָלֶיהָ בְּצֵרוּף אַחַר צֵרוּף, **וְהָיְתָה לְבָעֵר** עַד שֶׁלֹּא יִשָּׁאֲרוּ אֶלָּא צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים שֶׁיָּשׁוּבוּ אֵלַי בְּכָל לִבָּם:


**And when there is yet a tenth** [And when they are diminished to one out of ten (Rashi ms.)] even upon this remnant will I return My hand as a purge after a purge, and it will be purged until only completely righteous men will remain, who will repent wholeheartedly.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 6:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:13:2)


**כָּאֵלָה וְכָאַלּוֹן.** אֲשֶׁר בְּעֵת זְמַן שַׁלֶּכֶת שֶׁלָּהֶן, מַשְׁלִיכִין עָלִין שֶׁלָּהֶן בִּימֵי הַסְּתָיו שִׁלּוּךְ אַחַר שִׁלּוּךְ, עַד שֶׁאֵין נוֹתָר בָּהּ זוּלָתִי הַמַּצֶּבֶת. אַף הֵם, זֶרַע הַקֹּדֶשׁ הַנִּמְצָאִין בָּהּ, עוֹמְדִים בִּקְדוּשָׁתוֹ, הֵם יִהְיוּ לָהּ לְמַצֶּבֶת. דָּבָר אַחֵר: מַצַּבְתָּהּ – נְטִיעָתָהּ, לְכָךְ אֵינִי מְכַלֶּה אוֹתָם, נְטַעְתִּים **זֶרַע קֹדֶשׁ.** וְיֵשׁ פּוֹתְרִים: שַׁעַר שַׁלֶּכֶת הָיְתָה בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר בְּעֶזְרָא (דברי הימים א כו:טז), וְהָיוּ שָׁם אֵלָה וְאַלּוֹן נְטוּעִים:


**like the terebinth and like the oak** which, at the time of their casting, when they cast off their leaves during the fall, one casting after another casting, until nothing is left in it except the trunk, they too, the holy seed found in its midst, adhering to their holiness, they will be to Me as the trunk; another explanation of מַצַּבְתָּהּ is: its planting. Therefore, I will not destroy them, for I planted them as holy seed. Some explain that there was a Shallecheth Gate in Jerusalem, as it is stated in Ezra (I Chron. 26:16, written by Ezra), and there, terebinths and oaks were planted.



## Chapter 7


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:1:1)


**וַיְהִי בִּימֵי אָחָז.** מָה רָאָה הַכָּתוּב לְיַחֲסוֹ? אֶלָּא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁסּוֹפוֹ שֶׁל הַכָּתוּב לוֹמַר **וְלֹא יָכֹל לְהִלָּחֵם עָלֶיהָ,** וּלְלַמֶּדְךָ שֶׁזְּכוּת אָבוֹת עָמְדָה לוֹ. אָמְרוּ מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: ״וַוי, מִי הוּא זֶה שֶׁמָּלַךְ רָשָׁע זֶה?״ אָמַר לָהֶם: ״**בֶּן יוֹתָם** הוּא, **בֶּן עֻזִּיָּהוּ** הוּא, אֲבוֹתָיו הָיוּ צַדִּיקִים, לְפִיכָךְ אִי אֶפְשִׁי לִפְשׁוֹט יָדִי בּוֹ״. הֲדָא הוּא **וְלֹא יָכֹל לְהִלָּחֵם עָלֶיהָ** מִפְּנֵי זְכוּת אֲבוֹתָיו (בראשית רבה סג, א):


**And it came to pass in the days of Ahaz** What did Scripture see to trace his lineage? But, since the end of the verse states: “And he could not wage war against it,” it teaches you that the merit of his forebears stood him in good stead. The ministering angels said before the Holy One, blessed be He, Woe! Who is this wicked man who has become king? He replied to them, He is the son of Jotham; he is the son of Uzziah. His forebears were righteous. I, therefore, do not wish to harm him. This is the meaning of the words, “and he could not wage war against it,” because of the merit of his forefathers. [This is found in Gen. Rabbah 63:1.]



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:2:1)


**וַיֻּגַּד לְבֵית דָּוִד.** לְפִי שֶׁרָשָׁע הָיָה, לֹא הִזְכִּיר שְׁמוֹ:


**And it was told to the House of David** Since he was wicked, Scripture did not mention his name.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:2:2)


**נָחָה אֲרָם עַל אֶפְרָיִם.** נִתְחַבֵּר מֶלֶךְ אֲרָם עַל מֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל לָבֹא עָלֶיךָ. ׳נָחָה׳ לְשׁוֹן נְקֵבָה, עַל שֶׁהַמַּלְכוּת נָחָה. פושי״ר בלע״ז, לְשׁוֹן ״וַיָּנַח בְּכָל גְּבוּל מִצְרָיִם״ (שמות י:יד):


**Aram has allied itself with Ephraim** lit. has rested upon Ephraim. The king of Aram has joined the king of Israel to attack you. נָחָה is the feminine gender, since the kingdom (מַלְכוּת) joined. Posad in O. F., lay, comp. (Exodus 10:14) “And it rested (וַיַָּנַח) in all the boundary of Egypt.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:2:3)


**וַיָּנַע לְבָבוֹ.** לְפִי שֶׁכְּבָר נִלְחַם בּוֹ כָּל אֶחָד מֵהֶם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ, וְיָכְלוּ לוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וַיִּתְּנֵהוּ ה׳ בְּיַד מֶלֶךְ אֲרָם וְגוֹ׳״ (דברי הימים ב כח:ה), אוֹמֵר ״וַיַּהֲרֹג פֶּקַח בֶּן רְמַלְיָה מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים אֶלֶף אִישׁ״, שְׁנֵיהֶם בְּדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים (דברי הימים ב כח:ו):


**and his heart... trembled** Since each one individually had already waged war with him and defeated him, as it is said (II Chron. 28:5): “And the Lord his God delivered into the hand of the king of Aram...,” and it states further (v. 6): “And Pekah son of Remaliah slew 120,000 men.” Both verses are in Chronicles.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:2:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:2:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:2:4)


**כְּנוֹעַ עֲצֵי יַעַר.** קוֹל אִילָנֵי סְרָק יִשָּׁמַע יוֹתֵר מִכָּל אִילָנֵי פֵּירֵי, כִּדְאִיתָא בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (בראשית רבה טז:):


**as the trees of the forest tremble** The sound of trees that do not produce fruit is heard more than that of all fruit trees [var. the sound of fruit trees], as is [found] in Gen. Rabbah (16:3).



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:3:1)


**וּשְׁאָר יָשׁוּב בְּנֶךָ.** שְׁאֵרִית מְעַט שֶׁיָּשׁוּבוּ אֵלַי עַל יָדְךָ, וְהֵם כְּבָנֶךָ:


**and Shear yashuv your son** The small remnant that will return to Me through you, and they are like your sons.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:3:2)


**אֶל קְצֵה תְּעָלַת.** שָׁם תִּמְצָאֵהוּ. **תְּעָלַת** – פושי״ר בלע״ז:


**to the edge of the conduit** There you will find him. תְּעָלַת is fosed [a ditch] in O.F.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:3:3)


**בְּרֵכָה.** כְּעֵין מִקְוֵה מַיִם שֶׁעוֹשִׂים לְדָגִים:


**the upper pool** A type of gathering of water that is made for fish.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:3:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:3:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:3:4)


**הָעֶלְיוֹנָה.** בְּמוֹרַד הָהָר, וְיֵשׁ בְּרֵכָה אַחֶרֶת לְמַטָּה הֵימֶנָּה בְּתַחְתִּיתוֹ:


**upper** On the incline of the mountain, and there is one below it at its base.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:3:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:3:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:3:5)


**שְׂדֵה כוֹבֵס.** שָׂדֶה שֶׁהַכּוֹבְסִים שׁוֹטְחִים שָׁם בְּגָדִים לְנַגְּבָם, כָּךְ תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן. וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ דָּרְשׁוּ (סנהדרין קד א): נִכְנַע אָחָז לִפְנֵי יְשַׁעְיָהוּ וְשָׂם עַל רֹאשׁוֹ אוֹכְלָא דְּקַצָּרֵי, כָּפָה עָלָיו כְּלִי, פֵּירוּשׁ כְּלִי מְנֻקָּב שֶׁל כּוֹבְסִים שֶׁמְּזַלְּפִין בּוֹ מַיִם עַל הַבְּגָדִים:


**the washer’s field** A field in which the washers spread out laundry to dry. So did Jonathan render this. Our Rabbis expounded that Ahaz humbled himself before Isaiah and placed on his head a washer’s utensil, i.e., he inverted a vessel on his head [i.e., a perforated vessel used by the washers, with which they sprinkle water on the clothing].



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:4:1)


**הִשָּׁמֵר.** שֵׁב בְּשָׁלוֹם כְּיַיִן עַל שְׁמָרָיו:


**Feel secure** Heb. הִשָּׁמֵר. Sit tranquilly like wine on its lees (שְׁמָרָיו).


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:4:2)


**זַנְבוֹת הָאוּדִים הָעֲשֵׁנִים.** יִהְיוּ בְעֵינֶיךָ כִּזְנָבוֹת אוּדִים שֶׁכָּבְתָה שַׁלְהֶבֶת שֶׁלָּהֶם. **אוּדִים** – טיצונ״ש בלע״ז:


**smoking stubs of firebrands** Consider them as stubs of firebrands whose flame has been extinguished. אוּדִים is tisons [embers] in French.



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:6:1)


**וּנְקִיצֶנָּה.** נְעוֹרְרָהּ בְּמִלְחָמָה:


**and provoke it** Let us provoke them to war.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:6:2)


**וְנַבְקִיעֶנָּה אֵלֵינוּ.** נְשַׁוֶּה אוֹתָהּ עִמָּנוּ כְּבִקְעָה זוֹ שֶׁהִיא שָׁוָה; וְכֵן תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״וּנְשַׁוִּינוּן עִמָּנָא״, שֶׁיִּהְיוּ שָׁוִין עִם עֲשֶׂרֶת הַשְּׁבָטִים בְּמֶלֶךְ אֶחָד:


**and annex it to us** Heb. וְנַבְקִיעֶנָּה. Let us even it out with us like a valley (בִּקְעָה) that is even. And so does Jonathan render: And let us even them with us, that they should be even with the ten tribes under one king.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:6:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:6:3)


**אֶת בֶּן טָבְאַל.** בֶּן הַטּוֹב אֵלֵינוּ, כֵּן תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן. וְיֵשׁ לְפָרֵשׁ ״טוֹב אֵל״ אֲשֶׁר לֹא טוֹב בְּעֵינֵי הַמָּקוֹם, וּבְגִימַטְרִיָּא שֶׁל אוֹתִיּוֹת אלב״ם: **טָבְאַל** הוּא רַמְלָא, ט״ר ב״ם א״ל, **בֶּן טָבְאַל** בֶּן רַמְלָא:


**one who is good for us** Heb. בֶּן טָבְאַל [a combination of the words: טוֹב אֶל,] good for us; so did Jonathan render it. It is also possible to interpret it as: טוֹב אַל, not good in the eyes of the Omnipresent, and according to the calculation of the letters of ‘al-bam,’ Tov’al is Ramla. ‘Teth’ equals ‘resh’; ‘beth’ equals ‘mem’; ‘aleph’ equals ‘lammed.’ Hence, “ben tov’al” equals ‘ben Ramla.’



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:7:1)


**לֹא תָקוּם.** עֲצָתָם זֹאת, שֶׁתְּהֵא יְהוּדָה כְּבוּשָׁה תַּחְתֵּיהֶם:


**Neither shall it succeed** This plan of theirs, that Judah should be subordinated under them.



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:8:1)


**כִּי רֹאשׁ אֲרָם.** הִיא דַּמֶּשֶׂק, וְאֵין לִירוּשָׁלַיִם עִמָּהֶם כְּלוּם:


**For the head of Aram** that is Damascus, and Jerusalem has nothing with them.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:8:2)


**וְרֹאשׁ דַּמֶּשֶׂק רְצִין** בְּדַמֶּשֶׂק יִהְיֶה רֹאשׁ, וְלֹא בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם, וְגַם פֶּקַח וַעֲשֶׂרֶת הַשְּׁבָטִים **בְּעוֹד שִׁשִּׁים וְחָמֵשׁ שָׁנָה** מִיּוֹם שֶׁנִּגְזַר בִּימֵי עָמוֹס ״וְיִשְׂרָאֵל גָּלֹה יִגְלֶה מֵעַל אַדְמָתוֹ״ (עמוס ז:יא):


**and the head of Damascus is Rezin** In Damascus he shall be head, but not in Jerusalem, and also as regards Pekah and the ten tribes in another sixty-five years from the day it was decreed in the days of Amos (7:11): “And Israel shall surely be exiled from upon its land.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:8:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:8:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:8:3)


**יֵחַת אֶפְרַיִם.** תְּרוֹצַץ אֶפְרַיִם מֵעָם, שֶׁיַּגְלֵם סַנְחֵרִיב עִם מַלְכָּם הוֹשֵׁעַ בֶּן אֵלָה. צֵא וַחֲשׁוֹב מִנְּבוּאַת עָמוֹס עַד שֶׁגָּלוּ עֲשֶׂרֶת הַשְּׁבָטִים, וְתִמְצָאֵם שִׁשִּׁים וְחָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים: נְבוּאַת עָמוֹס הָיְתָה שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים לִפְנֵי שֶׁנִּתְנַגַּע עֻזִּיָּה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (עמוס א:א) ״שְׁנָתַיִם לִפְנֵי הָרַעַשׁ״, וְעֻזִּיָּה נִתְנַגַּע עֶשְׂרִים וְחָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים, הֲרֵי עֶשְׂרִים וְשֶׁבַע, וְשֵׁשׁ עֶשְׁרֵה שֶׁל יוֹתָם, וְשֵׁשׁ עֶשְׁרֵה שֶׁל אָחָז, וְשֵׁשׁ שֶׁל חִזְקִיָּהוּ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (מלכים ב יח:י-יא) ״וַיִּלְכְּדֻהָ בִּשְׁנַת שֵׁשׁ לְחִזְקִיָּהוּ הִיא שְׁנַת תֵּשַׁע לְהוֹשֵׁעַ וַיִּגֶל אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל אַשּׁוּרָה״, הֲרֵי שִׁשִּׁים וְחָמֵשׁ. וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁיְּמֵי חֲלוּטוֹ שֶׁל עֻזִּיָּהוּ עֶשְׂרִים וְחָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים? שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (מלכים ב טו:א) ״בִּשְׁנַת עֶשְׂרִים וָשֶׁבַע לְיָרָבְעָם בֶּן יוֹאָשׁ מֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל מָלַךְ עֻזִּיָּה בֶן אֲמַצְיָה עַל יְהוּדָה״. אֶפְשָׁר לוֹמַר? וַהֲלֹא עֻזִּיָּה וְיָרָבְעָם מָלְכוּ כְּאַחַת, לְפִי חֶשְׁבּוֹן שֶׁתִּמְצָא בְּסֵפֶר מְלָכִים! אֶלָּא שֶׁמָּלַךְ מַלְכוּת מְנֻגַּעַת בִּשְׁנַת עֶשְׂרִים וְשֶׁבַע לְמָלְכוֹ נִתְנַגַּע, וְהוּא מָלַךְ חֲמִשִּׁים וּשְׁתַּיִם שָׁנָה. וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִמְנוֹת **בְּעוֹד שִׁשִּׁים וְחָמֵשׁ שָׁנָה** מִיּוֹם שֶׁאָמַר יְשַׁעְיָה נְבוּאָה זוֹ, שֶׁהֲרֵי בִּימֵי אָחָז אֲמָרָהּ, וְהֵם גָּלוּ בִּשְׁנַת שֵׁשׁ לְחִזְקִיָּהוּ. וְכָךְ מְפֹרָשׁ בְּסֵדֶר עוֹלָם (סדר עולם רבה כח), שֶׁמָּנָה הַכָּתוּב לִנְבוּאָתוֹ שֶׁל עָמוֹס:


**Ephraim shall be broken, no longer to be a people** Ephraim shall be shattered, no longer to be a people, for Sennacherib will exile them with their king, Hoshea son of Elah. Go out and calculate from Amos’ prophecy until the ten tribes were exiled, and you will find them to be sixty-five years. Amos’ prophecy was two years before Uzziah was stricken, as it is stated (Amos 1:1): “Two years before the earthquake.” And Uzziah was stricken for twenty-five years, plus these two years, giving us a total of twenty-seven years. Add the sixteen years of Jotham and the sixteen years of Ahaz and six years of Hezekiah, as it is stated (II Kings 18:10, 11): “And they captured it [at the end of three years]; in the sixth year of Hezekiah, which is the ninth year of Hoshea, king of Israel...And the king of Assyria exiled Israel to Assyria.” Here are sixty-five years. Now how do we know that the duration of Uzziah’s state as a confirmed metzora was twenty-five years? For it is stated (ibid. 15:1): “In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam the king of Israel, Azariah the son of Amaziah the king of Judah, became king.” Is it possible to say this? Did not Uzziah and Jeroboam reign simultaneously, according to the calculation you will find in the Book of Kings (See Rashi II Kings 14:22)? Rather he reigned a plagued kingship. In the twenty-seventh year he was stricken, and he reigned for fifty-two years. It is impossible, however, to count “and in another sixty-five years” from the day that Isaiah said this prophecy, for he said it in the days of Ahaz, and they were exiled in the sixth year of Hezekiah. In this manner it is explained in Seder Olam (ch. 28), that Scripture counted from the prophecy of Amos.

**Ask for yourself a sign** for this thing, for I know that you do not believe the words of the Holy One, blessed be He.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:11:2)


**הַעְמֵק שְׁאָלָה.** הַעֲמֵק וּשְׁאַל שְׁאָלָה, כְּמוֹ ״שְׁמָעָה סְלָחָה״ (דניאל ט:יט). שְׁאַל אוֹת בְּעִמְקֵי תְהוֹם לְהַחֲיוֹת לְךָ מֵת, **אוֹ הַגְבֵּהַּ לְמַעְלָה** לִשְׁאוֹל אוֹת בַּשָּׁמַיִם:


**ask it in the depths** Heb. הַעֲמֵק שְׁאָלָה. Go down to the depths and ask. שְׁאָלָה is like, “שְׁמָעָה, hear, סְלָחָה, forgive” (Daniel 9:19). Ask for a sign in the depths of the abyss, to resurrect a dead person for you, or go up to the heights above to ask for a sign in the heavens.

### Verse 14

###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:14:1)

**the Lord, of His own, shall give you a sign** He will give you a sign by Himself, against Your will.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:14:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:14:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:14:2)


**הָרָה.** לְשׁוֹן עָתִיד הוּא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בְּאֵשֶׁת מָנוֹחַ שֶׁאָמַר לָהּ הַמַּלְאָךְ ״וְהָרִית וְיָלַדְתְּ בֵּן״ (שופטים יג:ג), וּכְתִיב ״וַיֹּאמֶר לָהּ הִנָּךְ הָרָה וְגוֹ׳״ (שופטים יג:ה):


**is with child** This is actually the future, as we find concerning Manoah’s wife, that the angel said to her (Judges 13:3): “And you shall conceive and bear a son,” and it is written, “Behold, you are with child and shall bear a son.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:14:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:14:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:14:3)


**הָעַלְמָה.** אִשְׁתִּי הָרָה הַשָּׁנָה הַזֹּאת, וְהִיא הָיְתָה שְׁנַת אַרְבַּע לְאָחָז:


**the young woman** My wife will conceive this year. This was the fourth year of Ahaz.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:14:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:14:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:14:4)


**וְקָרָאת שְׁמוֹ.** רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ תִּשְׁרֶה עָלֶיהָ:


**and she shall call his name** Divine inspiration will rest upon her.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:14:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:14:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:14:5)


**עִמָּנוּ אֵל.** לוֹמַר שֶׁיְּהֵא צוּרֵנוּ עִמָּנוּ, וְזֶה הָאוֹת! שֶׁהֲרֵי נַעֲרָה הִיא וְלֹא נִתְנַבְּאָה מִיָּמֶיהָ, וּבָזוֹ תִּשְׁרֶה בָּהּ רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ; וְזֶהוּ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר לְמַטָּה ״וָאֶקְרַב אֶל הַנְּבִיאָה וְגוֹ׳״ (ישעיהו ח:ג), וְלֹא מָצִינוּ אֵשֶׁת נָבִיא שֶׁנִּקְרְאָה נְבִיאָה אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הִתְנַבְּאָה. וְיֵשׁ פּוֹתְרִין, שֶׁעַל חִזְקִיָּה נֶאֱמַר; וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר, שֶׁהֲרֵי כְּשֶׁאַתָּה מוֹנֶה שְׁנוֹתָיו תִּמְצָא, שֶׁנּוֹלַד חִזְקִיָּה לִפְנֵי מַלְכוּת אָבִיו תֵשַׁע שָׁנִים. וְיֵשׁ פּוֹתְרִין, שֶׁזֶּה הָאוֹת: שֶׁעַלְמָה הָיְתָה וְאֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה לְוָלָד:


**Immanuel** [lit. God is with us. That is] to say that our Rock shall be with us, and this is the sign, for she is a young girl, and she never prophesied, yet in this instance, Divine inspiration shall rest upon her. This is what is stated below (8:3): “And I was intimate with the prophetess, etc.,” and we do not find a prophet’s wife called a prophetess unless she prophesied. Some interpret this as being said about Hezekiah, but it is impossible, because, when you count his years, you find that Hezekiah was born nine years before his father’s reign. And some interpret that this is the sign, that she was a young girl and incapable of giving birth.



### Verse 15

###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:15:1)


**חֶמְאָה וּדְבַשׁ יֹאכֵל.** הַוָּלָד, שֶׁתְּהֵא אַרְצֵנוּ מְלֵאָה כָּל טוּב:


**Cream and honey he shall eat** [i.e.,] the child [shall eat,] for our land shall be replete with all good.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:15:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:15:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:15:2)


**לְדַעְתּוֹ מָאוֹס בָּרָע וּבָחוֹר בַּטּוֹב.** כְּשֶׁיֵּדַע לִמְאוֹס בָּרָע וְלִבְחוֹר בַּטּוֹב, וּמֵאַיִן לָנוּ הַטּוֹבָה הַזֹּאת? הֲלֹא עַתָּה הָאָרֶץ חֲרֵבָה בִּגְדוּדֵי מַלְכֵי אֲרָם וּפֶקַח בֶּן רְמַלְיָהוּ?


**when he knows to reject bad and choose good** Heb. לְדַעְתּוֹ [lit. to his knowledge], when he knows to reject bad and choose good. Now whence will we have this plenty? Is not our land desolate now from the troops of the kings of Aram and Pekah the son of Remaliah?



### Verse 16

###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:16:1)


**כִּי בְּטֶרֶם יֵדַע הַנַּעַר מָאֹס בָּרָע וּבָחֹר בַּטּוֹב, תֵּעָזֵב.** הָאָרֶץ מִיּוֹשְׁבֶיהָ, אַדְמַת רְצִין וְאַדְמַת פֶּקַח:


**For, when the lad does not yet know to reject bad and choose good** the land shall be abandoned by its inhabitants, [i.e.,] the land of Rezin and the land of Pekah.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:16:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:16:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:16:2)


**אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה קָץ.** וְיָגוּר מִפְּנֵי שְׁנֵי מְלָכֶיהָ, רְצִין וּפֶקַח. שֶׁבְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁנָה עָלָה מֶלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר עַל דַּמֶּשֶׂק, כִּי שְׂכָרוֹ אָחָז, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּסֵפֶר (מלכים ב טז:ט): ״וַיִּתְפְּשֶׂהָ וַיַּגְלֶהָ קִירָה וְאֶת רְצִין הֵמִית״, וְאוֹתָהּ שָׁנָה ״וַיִּקְשֹׁר קֶשֶׁר הוֹשֵׁעַ בֶּן אֵלָה עַל פֶּקַח בֶּן רְמַלְיָהוּ וַיַּכֵּהוּ וַיְמִיתֵהוּ בִּשְׁנַת עֶשְׂרִים לְיוֹתָם״ (מלכים ב טו:ל), שֶׁהִיא שְׁנַת אַרְבַּע לְאָחָז:


**you dread** and fear its two kings, Rezin and Pekah, for in that year the king of Assyria marched on Damascus since Ahaz hired him, as it is stated in the Book of II Kings (16:9): “And seized it and exiled its inhabitants to Kir, and he slew Rezin,” and in that very year (ibid. 15:30), “Hoshea the son of Elah revolted against Pekah the son of Remaliah, and he struck him and slew him...in the twentieth year of Jotham,” which was the fourth year of Ahaz.



### Verse 17

###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:17:1)


**יָבִיא ה׳ עָלֶיךָ וְעַל עַמְּךָ.** עַל חִזְקִיָּהוּ בִּנְךָ הַמּוֹלֵךְ אַחֲרֶיךָ, וּלְפִי שֶׁהוּא צַדִּיק לֹא קְרָאוֹ בְּנוֹ:


**The Lord shall bring upon you and upon your people** “And yet greater that this, the Lord shall bring upon you and upon your people [ms]. Upon Hezekiah your son, who will reign after you,” but since he was righteous, he did not call him his son.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:17:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:17:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:17:2)


**יָמִים אֲשֶׁר לֹא בָאוּ.** מִיּוֹם שֶׁנֶּחְלְקָה מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד וְסָר **אֶפְרַיִם מֵעַל יְהוּדָה.** וּמַה הֵם הַיָּמִים? יְמֵי חֵיל **מֶלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר,** וְאַף בָּהֶם יַעֲשֶׂה לִיהוּדָה, וְכֵן מָצִינוּ (דברי הימים ב כח:כ) שֶׁבָּא מִתְּחִלָּה עַל אָחָז, דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיָּבֹא עָלָיו תִּגְלַת פִּלְאֶסֶר וַיָּצַר לוֹ וְלֹא חֲזָקוֹ״, וּבִימֵי חִזְקִיָּהוּ בְּנוֹ נַעֲשָׂה הַנֵּס:


**days which have not come** since the day the kingdom of the House of David was divided, and Ephraim seceded from Judah. And what are the days? The days of the army of the king of Assyria, and even then [lit. in them], a miracle shall be performed for Judah, and so we find in II Chron. (28:20) that he came first upon Ahaz, for it is written: “And Tilgath-Pilnesser [not as in printed editions] came upon him and distressed him, but did not strengthen him.” And in the days of Hezekiah his son, the miracle was performed.



### Verse 18

###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:18:1)


**וְיִשְׁרֹק ה׳.** יִרְמוֹז לָהֶם שֶׁיִּתְקַבְּצוּ:


**the Lord shall whistle** Shall signal them that they assemble.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:18:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:18:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:18:2)


**לַזְּבוּב.** חֲיָלוֹת רַבּוֹת כַּזְּבוּבִים מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם יָבוֹאוּ עִם סַנְחֵרִיב:


**to the “fly”** Armies as numerous as flies, will come from Egypt with Sennacherib.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:18:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:18:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:18:3)


**יְאוֹרֵי מִצְרָיִם.** לְפִי שֶׁכָּל אֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם עֲשׂוּיָּה יְאוֹרִים, שֶׁאֵין הַגְּשָׁמִים יוֹרְדִים שָׁם, אֶלָּא נִילוּס עוֹלֶה וּמַשְׁקֶה:


**the canals of Egypt** Since all the land of Egypt is made into canals, for rain does not fall there, but the Nile rises and waters it.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:18:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:18:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:18:4)


**וְלַדְּבוֹרָה.** חֵיל גִּבּוֹרִים, עוֹקְצִים כַּדְּבוֹרִים:


**and to the “bee”** An army of heroes who sting like bees.



### Verse 19

###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:19:1)


**בְּנַחֲלֵי הַבַּתּוֹת.** נַחֲלֵי עֲמָקִים, שְׂדוֹת בּוּרִים:


**in the desolate valleys** Heb. נַחֲלֵי means valleys, i.e., fallow fields.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:19:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:19:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:19:2)


**וּבִנְקִיקֵי הַסְּלָעִים** לֶאֱרוֹב, **נְקִיקֵי** – נִקְרוֹת הַצּוּר:


**and in the clefts of the rocks** to ambush. נְקִיקֵי is synonymous with נִקְרוֹתהַצּוּר.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:19:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:19:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:19:3)


**וּבְכׇל הַנַּעֲצוּצִים.** מְקוֹם הַסִּירִים (שקורין ברוצ״ש בלע״ז), וְכֵן ״תַּחַת הַנַּעֲצוּץ יַעֲלֶה בְרוֹשׁ״ (ישעיהו נה:יג):


**and in the thornbushes** the places of the thorns called broces [briars]. And similarly (infra 55:13): “Instead of the thornbush (הנַּעֲצוּץ) the fir tree shall come up.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:19:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:19:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:19:4)


**הַנַּהֲלֹלִים.** ״בָּתֵּי תוּשְׁבַּחְתָּא״ (תרגום יונתן):


**the shrines** houses of praise [from Jonathan].



### Verse 20

###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:20:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:20:1)


**יְגַלַּח אֲדֹנָי בְּתַעַר הַשְּׂכִירָה.** הַגְּדוֹלָה, וְכֵן ״גַּם שְׂכִירֶיהָ בְּקִרְבָּהּ״ (ירמיהו מו:כא), תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״רַבְרְבָהָא יְגַלַּח״:


**the Lord shall shave with the great razor** Heb. (שְּׂכִירָה), comp. (Jer. 46:21) “Also its officers (שְׂכִירֶיהָ) in its midst,” which Jonathan renders: its great ones.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:20:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:20:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:20:2)


**בְּעֶבְרֵי נָהָר.** בְּיוֹשְׁבֵי עֵבֶר הַנָּהָר, וּבְמִי מִן הַיּוֹשְׁבִים? בְּמֶלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר. **אֶת הָרֹאשׁ** יְגַלַּח. **וְשַׂעַר הָרַגְלָיִם;** לְפִי שֶׁהוּא דָבוּק נִשְׁתַּנָּה לִנָּקֵד פַּתַּח:


**on the other side of the river** Of those who dwell on the other side of the river, and of which of those dwellers? The king of Assyria, the head He will shave and the hair of the legs. Since it is in the construct state, it is voweled with a ‘pattach,’ (שַׂעַר) instead of (שֵׂעָר).


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:20:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:20:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:20:3)


**תִּסְפֶּה.** תִּכְלֶה, וְהַתִּגְלַּחַת הִיא הַהֲרִיגָה, וְהַתַּעַר הִיא הַחֶרֶב:


**shall be entirely removed** Will be destroyed. The shaving is the slaying, and the razor is the sword.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:20:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:20:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:20:4)


**אֶת הָרֹאשׁ.** הוּא סַנְחֵרִיב:


**the head** This symbolizes the king.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:20:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:20:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:20:5)


**הָרַגְלָיִם.** ״מַשְׁרְיָיתֵיהּ״ (תרגום יונתן):


**the legs** [This symbolizes] his camps [from Jonathan].


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:20:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:20:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:20:6)


**הַזָּקָן.** ״שִׁלְטוֹנַיָּיא״ (תרגום יונתן), וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ אָמְרוּ: גִּלּוּחַ מַמָּשׁ, וְסָפַת הַזָּקָן חֲרִיכָתָהּ בָּאֵשׁ, **הַזָּקָן** זְקַן סַנְחֵרִיב, כִּדְאִיתָא בְּאַגָּדַת חֵלֶק (סנהדרין צה, ב):


**the beard** [This symbolizes] the governors [from Jonathan]. But our Rabbis said that this literally refers to shaving, and the removal of the beard is by singeing it with fire. “The beard” refers to the beard of Sennacherib, as is found in the Aggadah of the chapter entitled, ‘Chelek.’



### Verse 21

###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:21:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:21:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:21:1)


**יְחַיֶּה אִישׁ וגו׳.** וּלְפִי שֶׁתְּהֵא אַרְצָם רֵיקָנִית, שֶׁיָּבֹזּוּ הַחֲיָלוֹת אֶת הַבְּהֵמוֹת, וּבַמְּעַט הַנּוֹתָר אֶתֵּן בְּרָכָה:


**a man shall keep alive** and since the land will be empty, for the armies will pillage the livestock, and in the few that remain I will give a blessing.



### Verse 22

###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:22:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:22:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:22:1)


**וְהָיָה מֵרֹב.** חָלָב שֶׁיַּעֲשׂוּ **שְׁתֵּי הַצֹּאן** הַלָּלוּ, יָבֹזוּ בְּעֵינֵיהֶם **הֶחָלָב** וְיֹאכְלוּ **הַחֶמְאָה,** הוּא שׁוּמַן הֶחָלָב:


**And it shall be, because of the plentiful milk** that these two sheep will produce, they will despise the milk and eat the cream, which is the fat of the milk.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:22:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:22:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:22:2)


**כָּל הַנּוֹתָר.** הַצַּדִּיקִים הַפְּלֵטִים מֵחֶרֶב סַנְחֵרִיב, בְּשׂוֹרָה גְדוֹלָה הוּא מְבַשֵּׂר לָהֶם, שֶׁתִּזְדַּמֵּן לָהֶם פַּרְנָסָה אַחַר כָּל הַשִּׁמָּמוֹן הַהוּא:


**everyone left** The righteous who were saved from the sword of Sennacheribhe is bringing them good news, that sustenance will be prepared for them after that desolation.



### Verse 23

###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:23:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:23:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:23:1)


**וְהָיָה בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא.** אֲשֶׁר תִּהְיֶה הָאָרֶץ שְׁמָמָה, יִהְיֶה מָקוֹם שֶׁהָיוּ שָׁם לִפְנֵי בֹּא חֲיָלוֹת:


**And it shall come to pass on that day** that the land will be desolate, there will be a place where there were, before the coming of the armies.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:23:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:23:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:23:2)


**אֶלֶף גֶּפֶן.** שָׁווֹת **אֶלֶף כֶּסֶף,** יִהְיוּ **לַשָּׁמִיר וְלַשַּׁיִת,** כִּי יַנִּיחוּם בַּעֲלֵיהֶם וּבוֹרְחִין, וְהֵם מַעֲלוֹת קִמְשׁוֹנִים וְתוֹלָעִים וְעַקְרַבִּים:


**a thousand vines** worth a thousand pieces of silver will be for the worms and the thorns, for their owners will abandon them and flee, and they will be overgrown by thorns and worms and scorpions.



### Verse 24

###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:24:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:24:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:24:1)


**בַּחִצִּים וּבַקֶּשֶׁת יָבוֹא שָׁמָּה.** כָּל הָרוֹצֶה לִכָּנֵס לְתוֹכוֹ, יְהֵא צָרִיךְ קֶשֶׁת וְחִצִּים בְּיָדוֹ לְמַלֵּט עַצְמוֹ מֵחַיּוֹת רָעוֹת וּנְחָשִׁים וְעַקְרַבִּים:


**With arrows and with a bow shall one come there** Everyone who wishes to enter therein, will require a bow and arrows in his hand, to save himself from wild beasts, snakes, and scorpions.



### Verse 25

###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:25:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:25:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:25:1)


**וְכֹל הֶהָרִים** אֲשֶׁר שָׁם שְׂדוֹת לָבָן לִתְבוּאָה:


**And all the mountains** where there are wheat fields fit for grain.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:25:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:25:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:25:2)


**אֲשֶׁר בַּמַּעְדֵּר יֵעָדֵרוּן.** הִיא כְּמִין מָרִיש שֶׁקּוֹרִין פשויי״ר בלע״ז:


**that will be dug with a spade** It is a kind of shovel called fosojjr in O.F.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:25:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:25:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:25:3)


**לֹא תָבוֹא שָׁמָּה יִרְאַת שָׁמִיר וָשָׁיִת.** כִּי בָּהֶם יִתְעַסְּקוּ לִזְרֹעַ תְּבוּאָה לְמַאֲכָל, שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר בְּלֹא הַתְּבוּאָה, אֲבָל הַגְּפָנִים יִהְיוּ לָבַז, כִּי אוֹתוֹ הַדּוֹר שֶׁל יְחִזְקִיָּהוּ יָשׁוּבוּ אֵלַי לַעֲסֹק בַּתּוֹרָה וְלֹא לִשְׁתּוֹת יַיִן. וְכֵן הָיְתָה, כִּדְאִיתָא בְּחֵלֶק (סנהדרין צד ב): בָּדְקוּ מִדָּן וְעַד בְּאֵר שֶׁבַע וְלֹא מָצְאוּ אִישׁ שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בָּקִי בַּהֲלָכוֹת אִסּוּר וְהֶתֵּר וְטֻמְאָה וְטָהֳרָה. וְעַל אוֹתוֹ הַדּוֹר הוּא אוֹמֵר ״וְהָיָה כָל מָקוֹם וְגוֹ׳״, הוּא שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (משלי כה:א) ״אֲשֶׁר הֶעְתִּיקוּ אַנְשֵׁי חִזְקִיָּהוּ מֶלֶךְ יְהוּדָה״:


**the fear of worms and thorns** For in them they will engage to sow grain for food, for it is impossible without grain, but the vines will be neglected, for that generation of Hezekiah will return to Me to engage in the Torah, and not to drink wine, as it is [stated] in [the chapter of] “Chelek” (San. 94b): They searched from Dan to Beer-sheba, and did not find any man who was not well-versed in the laws of prohibition and permissibility and ritual defilement and purity. And concerning that generation, Scripture says: And it shall come to pass, that every place, etc. This is what is stated (Prov. 25:1): “Which the men of Hezekiah, king of Judah, strengthened.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 7:25:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:25:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:25:4)


**וְהָיָה לְמִשְׁלַח שׁוֹר.** שָׁם יִרְעוּ בְּהֵמוֹתֵיהֶם מִרְעֶה שָׁמֵן:


**and it shall be for the pasture of oxen** There their cattle will graze on fat pastureland.



## Chapter 8


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Isaiah 8:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:1:1)


**גִּלָּיוֹן.** מְגִלָּה:


**scroll** Heb. גִּלְיוֹן, like מְגִלָה. ([Mss. add:] Or a tablet.)


###### Rashi on Isaiah 8:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:1:2)


**בְּחֶרֶט אֱנוֹשׁ.** בְּמִכְתָּב כְּתָב אֲשֶׁר יָרוּץ כָּל אֱנוֹשׁ הַקּוֹרֵא בּוֹ, אֲפִילּוּ אֱנוֹשׁ כָּל שֶׁהוּא, וַאֲפִילּוּ אֵינוֹ חָכָם. וְכֵן תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״כְּתָב מְפָרַשׁ״:


**in common script** In script which any man who reads it can skim through quickly, even a very common man, even if he is not intelligent. In this manner Jonathan renders: in a distinct script.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 8:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:1:3)


**לְמַהֵר שָׁלָל** לָבֹא סַנְחֵרִיב וְלִשְׁלוֹל אֶת כָּל הוֹן עֲשֶׂרֶת הַשְּׁבָטִים, וּלְהָחִישׁ לָבוֹז נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר אַחֲרָיו אֶת צִדְקִיָּהוּ וְדוֹרוֹ:


**to hasten loot, speed the spoils** For Sennacherib to come and to loot all the possessions of the ten tribes and to speed Nebuchadnezzar to pillage Zedekiah and his generation.



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Isaiah 8:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:2:1)


**וְאָעִידָה לִּי.** גַּם בְּאוֹתָן הַיָּמִים, בִּימֵי יְהוֹיָקִים, עַל אוֹתוֹ פֻּרְעָנוּת, שְׁנֵי עֵדִים נֶאֱמָנִים: הָאֶחָד לְבַשְּׂרָם רָעָה הָעֲתִידָה לָבֹא עֲלֵיהֶם, **אוּרִיָּה הַכֹּהֵן,** שֶׁהֲרָגוֹ יְהוֹיָקִים, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ירמיהו כו:כ) ״וְגַם אִישׁ הָיָה מִתְנַבֵּא בְּשֵׁם ה׳ אוּרִיָּה בֶּן שְׁמַעְיָה מִקִּרְיַת הַיְּעָרִים וַיִּתְנַבֵּא עַל הָעִיר הַזֹּאת וְעַל הַמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה אֶת כָּל דִּבְרֵי יִרְמְיָהוּ״:


**And I will call to testify for Myself** also in those days, in the days of Jehoiakim, concerning that calamity, destined to befall them, two trustworthy witnesses, one to foretell for them the evil that was destined to come upon them, viz. Uriah the priest, whom Jehoiakim dispatched, as it is said (Jer. 26: 20): “And also a man was prophesying in the name of the Lord, Uriah the son of Shemaiah from Kiriath-jearim, and he prophesied concerning this city and concerning this land, according to all the words of Jeremiah.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 8:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:2:2)


**וְאֶת זְכַרְיָהוּ בֶּן יְבֶרֶכְיָהוּ.** בִּשְׁנַת שְׁתַּיִם לְדָרְיָוֶשׁ ״עוֹד יֵשְׁבוּ זְקֵנִים וּזְקֵנוֹת בִּרְחוֹבוֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָם״ (זכריה ח:ד). אוּרִיָּה סִימָן לִזְכַרְיָהוּ: אִם תִּרְאוּ שֶׁתִּתְקַיֵּם נְבוּאַת אוּרִיָּה, תִּהְיוּ מְצַפִּים שֶׁתִּתְקַיֵּם נְבוּאַת זְכַרְיָהוּ, כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהַעִידוֹתִי בְּשֶׁל סַנְחֵרִיב עָמוֹס וִישַׁעְיָה: עָמוֹס לְפֻרְעָנוּתָן שֶׁל עֲשֶׂרֶת הַשְּׁבָטִים ״וְיִשְׂרָאֵל גָּלֹה יִגְלֶה״ (עמוס ז:יא), וִישַׁעְיָה (ישעיהו לב:א) לְהַבְטָחָתוֹ שֶׁל חִזְקִיָּהוּ כְּשֶׁיִּמְלוֹךְ:


**and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah** who prophesied in the second year of Darius (Zech. 8:4): “Old men and old women will again sit in the streets of Jerusalem.” Uriah is a sign for Zechariah. If you see that Uriah’s prophecy is fulfilled, you can expect that Zechariah’s will likewise be fulfilled, just as I have called to testify concerning Sennacherib, Amos and Isaiah; Amos for the calamity of the ten tribes (Amos 7:11): “And Israel shall surely be exiled,” and Isaiah for his promise to Hezekiah (Isaiah 32,33) [when he would reign].



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Isaiah 8:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:3:1)


**וַתֵּלֶד בֵּן.** הוּא הַבֵּן עַצְמוֹ, שֶׁקָּרְאָה הַנְּבִיאָה ״עִמָּנוּ אֵל״, עַל שֵׁם שֶׁהָיָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעֵזֶר שֶׁל חִזְקִיָּה כְּשֶׁיִּמְלוֹךְ. וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹמַר שֶׁבֵּן שֵׁנִי הוּא, שֶׁהֲרֵי שָׁנִינוּ (סדר עולם רבה כב) בִּשְׁנַת אַרְבַּע לְאָחָז נֶאֶמְרָה נְבוּאָה זוֹ, וּבִשְׁנַת אַרְבַּע לְאָחָז נֶהֱרַג פֶּקַח, וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר שְׁנֵי בָּנִים לְהִוָּלֵד בְּשָׁנָה אַחַת בָּזֶה אַחַר זֶה. וִישַׁעְיָה אָבִיו קָרָא שְׁמוֹ ״מַהֵר שָׁלָל״ עַל שֵׁם פֻּרְעָנוּת הָעֲתִידָה לָבֹא עַל רְצִין וּבֶן רְמַלְיָהוּ, שֶׁהָיוּ בָּאִין לִטּוֹל מְלוּכָה מִבֵּית דָּוִד, וְתֻשְׁבַּת מַלְכוּתוֹ שֶׁל חִזְקִיָּהוּ:


**and she bore a son** He is the very son whom the prophetess called Immanuel, since the Holy One, blessed be He, would be at the aid of Hezekiah when he would reign. [It is impossible to say that it was another son, for we learned [in Seder Olam ch. 22] that in the fourth year of Ahaz, this prophecy was said, and in the fourth year of Ahaz, Pekah was assassinated, and it is impossible for two children to be born in one year, one after the other.] And Isaiah his father called him Maher-shalal-hash-baz, because of the calamity destined to befall Rezin and the son of Remaliah, who were coming to wrest the kingdom from the House of David and to curtail the kingdom of Hezekiah.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Isaiah 8:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:4:1)


**יִשָּׂא אֶת חֵיל דַּמֶּשֶׂק.** ״וַיַּעַל דַּמֶּשֶׂק וַיִּתְפְּשֶׂהָ״ (מלכים ב טז:ט):


**the wealth of Damascus...shall be carried off** And [the] king of Assyria went up to Damascus and seized it (II Kings 16:9).


###### Rashi on Isaiah 8:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:4:2)


**וְאֵת שְׁלַל שֹׁמְרוֹן.** לְאַחַר שֶׁנֶּהֱרַג פֶּקַח וּמָלַךְ הוֹשֵׁעַ, ״עָלָיו עָלָה שַׁלְמַנְאֶסֶר מֶלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר וַיְהִי לוֹ הוֹשֵׁעַ עֶבֶד״ (מלכים ב יז:ג), וְנָתַן לוֹ מִנְחָה וְשֹׁחַד. הוּא **שְׁלַל שׁוֹמְרוֹן.** כָּל אֵלֶּה הָיָה בִּשְׁנַת אַרְבַּע לְאָחָז:


**and the plunder of Samaria** After Pekah was assassinated, and Hoshea reigned, Shalmaneser, king of Assyria, went up against him, and Hoshea became his vassal, and gave him tribute and a bribe (ibid. 17:3). That is the plunder of Samaria. All this took place in the fourth year of Ahaz.



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Isaiah 8:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:6:1)


**אֶת מֵי הַשִּׁלֹחַ הַהֹלְכִים לְאַט.** ״בְּמַלְכוּתָא דְּבֵית דָּוִד דִּמְדַבַּר לְהוֹן בְּנִיחַ כְּמֵי שִׁלוֹחָא דְּנַגְדִין בְּנִיחַ״. **שִׁלוֹחַ** מַעְיָן הוּא וּשְׁמוֹ גִּיחוֹן וְשִׁילוֹחַ, שֶׁרָצוּ לְהָסִיר אֶת מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד בִּימֵי אָחָז לְפֶקַח בֶּן רְמַלְיָהוּ. וְכָאן נִבָּא עַל שֶׁבְנָא וְסִיעָתוֹ שֶׁרָצוּ לִמְרוֹד בְּחִזְקִיָּהוּ, שֶׁמָּאֲסוּ בּוֹ עַל שֶׁרָאוּהוּ שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בּוֹחֵר בְּשֻׁלְחַן מְלָכִים, אֶלָּא אוֹכֵל לִטְרָא יָרָק וְעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה. עָלָיו נֶאֱמַר ״צַדִּיק אוֹכֵל לְשׂוֹבַע נַפְשׁוֹ״ (משלי יג:כה). וְרָאוּ אֶת פֶּקַח בֶּן רְמַלְיָה אוֹכֵל אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה גוֹזָלוֹת בְּקִנּוּחַ סְעוּדָה, וְהָיוּ מְלִיזִין עַל חִזְקִיָּהוּ וְאוֹמְרִין: זֶה הָגוּן לִהְיוֹת מֶלֶךְ? אֵין זֶה מֶלֶךְ אֶלָּא רְצִין וּבֶן רְמַלְיָהוּ הָיוּ רְאוּיִין לִמְלוֹךְ בְּחַיֵּיהֶן, וְזֶהוּ **וּמְשׂוֹשׂ אֶת רְצִין וְגוֹ׳.** אָמַר לָהֶם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: אוֹכְלִין אַתֶּם מִתְאַוִּים, אֲנִי מֵבִיא עֲלֵיכֶם אוֹכְלִין הַרְבֵּה. **הִנֵּה ה׳ מַעֲלֶה עֲלֵיכֶם וְגוֹ׳ אֶת מֵי הַנָּהָר הָעֲצוּמִים** תַּחַת מֵי הַשִּׁילוֹחַ חֲלָשִׁים וְהַנּוֹחִים:


**the waters of the Shiloah that flow gently** [i.e., they rejected] the kingdom of the House of David, which leads them gently, like the waters of the Shiloah that flow gently [Jonathan]. Shiloah is a spring, known as Gihon and Shiloah. Here he prophesied concerning Shebna and his company who wanted to rebel against Hezekiah, for they rejected him since they saw that he did not choose a regal table, but would eat a litre of vegetables and engage in the Torah. Concerning him, it is stated (Prov. 13:25): “A righteous man eats to satiate his body.” They saw Pekah son of Remaliah eat forty seahs of pigeons for dessert. They would ridicule Hezekiah and say, Is this one fit to be a king? There is no king but Rezin and the son of Remaliah. They were fit to rule in their lifetimes. And this is the meaning of: “And rejoice in Rezin and the son of Remaliah.” The Holy One, blessed be He, said to them, Do you desire eaters? I will bring many eaters upon you. “Behold the Lord brings upon them the mighty...waters of the river” instead of the weak and gentle waters of the Shiloah.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Isaiah 8:7:1
