###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:9:2)


**רְפָאִים.** עֲנָקִים הַשּׁוֹכְבִים שָׁם:


**giants** Heb. רְפָאִים, the giants lying there.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:9:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:9:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:9:3)


**כָּל עַתּוּדֵי אָרֶץ.** כָּל מַלְכֵי הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמָזָלוֹת, הַשָּׂרִים וְהַשָּׂרוֹת, הַכָּתוּב מוֹשְׁלָם לְפָרִים וְלִפְרוֹת וְלַעֲתוּדִים, כְּמוֹ (תהלים כב:יג) ״כִּי סְבָבוּנִי פָרִים״, וּכְמוֹ (עמוס ד:א) ״פָּרוֹת הַבָּשָׁן אֲשֶׁר בְּשׁוֹמְרוֹן״, וְכָאן מוֹשְׁלָם לַעֲתוּדִים:


**all the chiefs of the earth** [lit. the he-goats.] All the kings of the nations, the princes, and the princesses, are compared by Scripture, to bulls, to cows, and to he-goats. Comp. (Psalms 22:13) “Bulls surrounded me.” Also (Amos 4:1): “The cows of the Bashan that were on Mt. Shomron,” and here he compares them to he-goats.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:9:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:9:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:9:4)


**הֵקִים.** הִשְׁלִיךְ:


**he caused to rise** he threw


###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:9:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:9:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:9:5)


**מִכִּסְאוֹתָם.** שֶׁבַּגֵּיהִנֹּם כָּל מַלְכֵי גוֹיִם:


**from their thrones** [i.e.,] the messenger of Gehinnom caused all the kings of the nations [to rise] from their thrones. [according to mss. and Shem Ephraim]



### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:10:1)


**גַּם אַתָּה חֻלֵּיתָ כָמוֹנוּ.** תְּמֵהִים אָנוּ: אֵיךְ בָּאת עָלֶיךָ רָעָה, שֶׁגַּם אַתָּה נֶחֱלֵיתָ לִהְיוֹת **כָּמוֹנוּ** לָמוּת:


**Have you too become weak like us** We are amazed how the misfortune has fallen upon you, that you too have become weak, to be like us, to die.



### Verse 11

###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:11:1)


**הֶמְיַת נְבָלֶיךָ.** נְבָלִים וְכִנּוֹרוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ מְזַמְּרִים לְפָנֶיךָ. וְיֵשׁ לִפְתּוֹר **הֶמְיַת נְבָלֶיךָ** – הֶמְיַת בְּנֵי נָבָל, עוֹשֵׂי נְבָלָה שֶׁבַּחֲיָלוֹתֶיךָ. וּמְדֻמֶּה אֲנִי שֶׁבַּמְּסוֹרָה הַגְּדוֹלָה חִבֵּר אֶת זֶה וְאֶת ״זִמְרַת נְבָלִים״ (עמוס ה:כג) בְּאָלֶף בֵּית שֶׁל שְׁתֵּי לְשׁוֹנוֹת:


**the stirring of your psalteries** The psalteries and harps that used to play before you. It is also possible to interpret, הֶמְיַת נְבָלֶיךָ as, the stirring of the wanton ones, who commit wanton acts, of your armies, and it seems to me that in the great Masorah, this was combined with (Amos 5:21) “The song of your psalteries,” in the aleph-beth of two meanings.



### Verse 12

###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:12:1)


**הֵילֵל בֶּן שָׁחַר.** כּוֹכַב הַנֹּגַהּ הַמֵּאִיר אוֹר כְּכוֹכַב הַבֹּקֶר. זוֹ הַקִּינָה עַל שָׂרָהּ שֶׁל בָּבֶל נֶאֱמָרָה, שֶׁיִּפּוֹל **מִשָּׁמַיִם**:


**Lucifer, the morning star** This is Venus, which gives light as the morning star, הֵילֵל being derived from יהל, to shed light. This is the lamentation over the heavenly prince of Babylon, who will fall from heaven.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:12:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:12:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:12:2)


**נִגְדַּעְתָּ לָאָרֶץ.** אַתָּה, נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר, שֶׁהָיִיתָ **חוֹלֵשׁ עַל גּוֹיִם** מֵטִיל גּוֹרָל עֲלֵיהֶם, עַל הַמְּלָכִים, מִי מֵהֶם יְשָׁרֶתְךָ בְּיוֹם פְּלוֹנִי וּמִי בְּיוֹם פְּלוֹנִי. וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ דְּרָשׁוּהוּ (שבת קמט:-קנ.) שֶׁהָיָה מֵטִיל גּוֹרָל עַל הַמְּלָכִים וְכוּ׳:


**You have been cut down to earth** You, Nebuchadnezzar, who would cast lots on nations. You would cast lots on them, on the kings, who of them would serve you on such and such a day, and who on such and such a day. Our Rabbis, however, expounded this to mean that he would cast lots on the kings for purposes of pederasty.



### Verse 13

###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:13:1)


**מִמַּעַל לְכוֹכְבֵי אֵל.** יִשְׂרָאֵל:


**above the stars of God** Israel.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:13:2)


**בְּהַר מוֹעֵד.** הַר שֶׁהַכֹּל מִתְוַעֲדִים שָׁם, הוּא הַר צִיּוֹן:


**on the mount of the assembly** The mount where all assemble, i.e., Mount Zion.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:13:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:13:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:13:3)


**בְּיַרְכְּתֵי צָפוֹן.** בַּעֲזָרָה, מָקוֹם שֶׁנִּבְחַר בּוֹ יֶרֶךְ הַצְּפוֹנִי; כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ויקרא א:יא) ״עַל יֶרֶךְ הַמִּזְבֵּחַ צָפֹנָה״:


**in the farthest end of the north** In the forecourt, the chosen place, the north side, as the matter is stated (Lev. 1:11): “On the side of the altar to the north.”



### Verse 14

###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:14:1)


**אֶעֱלֶה עַל בָּמֳתֵי עָב.** אֵינִי כְּדַאי לָדוּר עִם בְּנֵי אָדָם, אֶעֱשֶׂה לִי עָב קְטַנָּה בָּאֲוִיר וְאֵשֵׁב בָּהּ. וְיוֹנָתָן תִּרְגֵּם: ״אֶסַּק עִלּוֹי כָּל עַמָּא״:


**I will ascend above the heights of the clouds** I am not fit to dwell with mortals. I will make myself a small cloud in the air and I will dwell there. Jonathan renders: I will ascend over all nations.



### Verse 16

###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:16:1)


**יַשְׁגִּיחוּ.** יַבִּיטוּ דֶּרֶךְ חוֹרִין וַחֲרָכִּין, אבוט״ר בלע״ז:


**shall look at you** They will look through holes and cracks [aboater in O.F.].


###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:16:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:16:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:16:2)


**יִתְבּוֹנָנוּ.** פורופנשי״ר בלע״ז:


**shall gaze earnestly** [Por panser in O.F.] To think of oneself.



### Verse 17

###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:17:1)


**לֹא פָתַח בָּיְתָה.** לֹא פָּתַח לָהֶם בֵּית אֲסוּרֵיהֶם לְהוֹצִיאָם כָּל יְמֵי חַיֵּיהֶם, לְפוֹטְרָם לָלֶכֶת לְבֵיתָם. כָּל תֵּיבָה שֶׁצְּרִיכָה לָמֶ״ד בִּתְחִלָּתָהּ הִטִּיל לָהּ הֵ״א בְּסוֹפָהּ (יבמות יג ב):


**he did not open the house** Heb. בָּיְתָה. He did not open their house of imprisonment to release them all the days of their lives, to allow them to go to their home. Every word that requires a ‘lammed’ at the beginning Scripture placed a ‘heh’ to it at the end.



### Verse 18

###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:18:1)


**אִישׁ בְּבֵיתוֹ.** בְּקִבְרוֹ, וְכֵן תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״בְּבֵית עָלְמֵיהּ״:


**each in his house** In his grave, and so did Jonathan render: In his eternal house.



### Verse 19

###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:19:1)


**כְּנֵצֶר נִתְעָב.** כְּיוֹנֵק אִילָן הַנִּתְעָב בְּעֵינֵי בְּעָלָיו, שֶׁחוֹפֵר וּמְשָׁרֵשׁ וּמוֹצִיאוֹ, כָּךְ הָשְׁלַכְתָּ מִקִּבְרְךָ. אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים (ויקרא רבה יח:): כְּשֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה בְּהֵמָה וְחַיָּה שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים, הִמְלִיכוּ עַם הָאָרֶץ אֶת אֱוִיל מְרוֹדַךְ; וּכְשֶׁחָזַר לְמַלְכוּתוֹ, נְטָלוֹ וַחֲבָשׁוֹ בְּבֵית הָאֲסוּרִין עַד יוֹם מוֹתוֹ. וּכְשֶׁמֵּת, הוֹצִיאוּ אֱוִיל מְרוֹדַךְ מִבֵּית הַסֹּהַר לְהַמְלִיכוֹ, וְלֹא קִבֵּל עָלָיו; אָמַר: אִם יָשׁוּב לְמַלְכוּתוֹ יַהַרְגֵנִי. אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מֵת וְנִקְבַּר; וְלֹא הֶאֱמִין, עַד שֶׁהוֹצִיאוּהוּ מִקִּבְרוֹ:


**like a despised sapling** Like a sapling of a tree, which is despised by its owner, who digs it up and uproots it and takes it out. So were you cast out of your grave. The Sages stated (Lev. Rabbah 18:2): When he became an animal and a wild beast for seven years, the populace crowned Evil-Merodach, and when he was restored to his kingdom, he took him and imprisoned him in the dungeon until the day of his death. When he died, they took Evil-Merodach out of prison to crown him king, but he did not accept it upon himself. He said, If he returns to his kingdom, he will kill me. They said to him, He is dead and buried. But he did not believe them until they took him out of his grave and dragged him.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:19:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:19:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:19:2)


**לְבוּשׁ הֲרֻגִים מְטֹעֲנֵי חָרֶב.** בִּלְבוּשׁ מְלֻכְלָךְ כְּמוֹ **לְבוּשׁ הֲרֻגִים.**


**[in] the garb of the slain** With filthy apparel, like that of the slain.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:19:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:19:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:19:3)


**מְטֹעֲנֵי חָרֶב.** מְדֻקְּרֵי רְמָחִים, ׳מְדֻקָּר׳ בִּלְשׁוֹן עֲרָבִי: מֻטְעָן:


**of those pierced by the sword** Heb. מְטֹעֲנֵי, pierced by spears (sic). “Pierced” in Arabic is ‘mut’an.’


###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:19:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:19:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:19:4)


**יוֹרְדֵי אֶל אַבְנֵי בוֹר.** אֶל עִמְקֵי בוֹר, מָקוֹם שֶׁהָאֲבָנִים צוֹלְלִים שָׁם, יָרַדְתָּ:


**who descend to the stones of the pit** to the depths of the pit, the place where stones sink there, you have descended.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:19:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:19:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:19:5)


**כְּפֶגֶר מוּבָס.** תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״מְדַשְׁדַּשׁ״, כְּמוֹ ״נָבוּס קָמֵינוּ״ (תהלים מד:ו), ״וְעַל הָרַי אֲבוּסֶנּוּ״ (ישעיהו כה:י), ״מִתְבּוֹסֶסֶת בְּדָמָיִךְ״ (יחזקאל טז:ו), הַנָּדוּשׁ כְּטִיט חוּצוֹת:


**like a trampled corpse** Heb. מוּבָס. Jonathan renders: trampled, like (Ps. 44:6), “We will trample (נָבוּס) those who rise up against us”; (infra verse 25) “And on my mountains I will trample him (אֲבוּסֶנוּ)”; (Ezekiel 16: 6) “Trampled (מִתְבּוֹסֶסֶת) in your blood,” trampled like the mud of the streets.



### Verse 20

###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:20:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:20:1)


**לֹא תֵחַד אִתָּם בִּקְבוּרָה.** לֹא תִשְׁוֶה לִשְׁאָר מְלָכִים לָנוּחַ בְּקִבְרְךָ:


**You shall not join them in burial** You shall not be equal to other kings, to rest in your grave.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:20:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:20:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:20:2)


**כִּי אַרְצְךָ שִׁחַתָּ** בְּרֹב עֲבוֹדָה, וְעַמְּךָ הָרַגְתָּ חִנָּם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּפוֹרָשׁ בְּדָנִיֵּאל: ״וְאָמַר לְהוֹבָדָא לְכָל חַכִּימֵי בָבֶל״ (דניאל ב:יב), לְכָךְ שְׂנָאוּךָ וְנָהֲגוּ בְּךָ בִּזָּיוֹן לְהַשְׁלִיכְךָ מִקִּבְרְךָ:


**for you have destroyed your land** with excessive labor, and you have slain your people groundlessly, as it is related in Daniel (2:12): “And he said to destroy all the wise men of Babylon.” Therefore, they hated you and treated you with contempt to throw you out of your grave.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:20:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:20:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:20:3)


**לֹא יִקָּרֵא לְעוֹלָם זֶרַע מְרֵעִים** וְאַף בָּנֶיךָ יִלְקוּ בַּעֲווֹנֶיךָ, וְלֹא יִתְקַיְּמוּ אַחֲרֶיךָ יָמִים רַבִּים, כִּי יִתְחַבְּרוּ עֲלֵיהֶם שׂוֹנְאֶיךָ וְיַשְׁחִיתוּם, וְיֹאמְרוּ זֶה לָזֶה:


**the seed of evil doers shall not be named forever** Even your children shall suffer for your iniquities, and they shall not endure long after you, for their enemies will unite against them and destroy them, and they shall say to each other.



### Verse 21

###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:21:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:21:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:21:1)


**הָכִינוּ לְבָנָיו מַטְבֵּחַ.** לְבַל יָקוּמוּ וְיִירְשׁוּ אָרֶץ, וְתִתְמַלֵּא הָאָרֶץ שׂוֹנְאִים וּמְצִיקִים. וְכֵן תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״בַּעֲלֵי דְבָבִין״, כְּמוֹ ״וַיְהִי עָרֶךָ״ (שמואל א כח:טז). וְעוֹד יֵשׁ לִפְתּוֹר **וּמָלְאוּ פְנֵי תֵבֵל עָרִים** כְּלַפֵּי שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ לְמַעְלָה ״שָׂם תֵּבֵל כַּמִּדְבָּר וְעָרָיו הָרָס״ (ישעיהו יד:יז), חָזַר וְאָמַר: וְיִכְלֶה זַרְעוֹ וְיַחְזְרוּ יוֹשְׁבֵי הֶעָרִים לִמְקוֹמָן **וּמָלְאוּ פְנֵי תֵבֵל** עֲיָרוֹת:


**Prepare a slaughter for his sons** lest they rise and inherit the land, and the land will be filled with enemies and oppressors. So did Jonathan render עַָרִים, enemies. Comp. (I Sam. 28:16) “And has become your adversary (עָרֶךְ).” It can also be interpreted: And fill the surface of the earth with cities. In contrast with what he said before (verse 17): “Who made the land like a desert and demolished his cities,” he says further: His seed shall perish, and the inhabitants of the cities shall return to their place, and the surface of the earth shall be filled with cities.



### Verse 22

###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:22:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:22:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:22:1)


**וּשְׁאָר.** שְׁאֵרִית:


**and a remnant** Heb. שְׁאָר, a remnant.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:22:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:22:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:22:2)


**נִין.** בֵּן מוֹשֵׁל בְּמַלְכוּת אָבִיו:


**and a son** Heb. וְנִין, a son ruling in the kingdom of his father.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:22:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:22:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:22:3)


**וָנֶכֶד.** בֶּן הַבֵּן. **נִין** – זֶה בֵּלְשַׁצַּר, **וָנֶכֶד** – זוֹ וַשְׁתִּי (מגילה י ב):


**and a grandson** The son of the son. The son is Belshazzar, and the grandson [or granddaughter in this case] was Vashti.



### Verse 23

###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:23:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:23:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:23:1)


**קִפֹּד.** הריצו״ן בלע״ז:


**hedgehog** Heb. קִפֹּד [hricon or hericon in O.F.] [In Modern French it is spelled herisson.]


###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:23:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:23:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:23:2)


**וְטֵאטֵאתִיהָ.** לְשׁוֹן ׳כִּבּוּד׳, אשקובי״ר בלע״ז, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ (מגילה יח א): ״לֹא הֲוֵי יָדְעִי רַבָּנָן מַאי וְטֵאטֵאתִיהָ עַד דְּשַׁמְעוּהָ כּוּ׳״:


**and I will sweep** Heb. וְטִאטֵאתִיהָ, an expression of sweeping [eskober in O.F.], as our Rabbis stated: The Rabbis did not know the meaning of וְטִאטֵאתִיהָ בְּמַטְאֲטֵא הַשְׁמֵד, until they heard [Rabbi’s (R. Judah Hanasi’s) maidservant say to her friend, “Take a broom (מַטְאֲטֵא) and sweep (וְטַאְטְאִי) the house.”]



### Verse 24

###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:24:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:24:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:24:1)


**כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּמִּיתִי** בְּאַשּׁוּר כֵּן הָיְתָה, אַתָּה נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר רָאִיתָ שֶׁנִּתְקַיְּמוּ דִּבְרֵי נְבִיאֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּסַנְחֵרִיב:


**as I thought** concerning Assyria, so it was. You, Nebuchadnezzar, saw that the words of the prophets of Israel about Sennacherib were fulfilled.



### Verse 25

###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:25:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:25:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:25:1)


**לִשְׁבֹּר אַשּׁוּר בְּאַרְצִי.** וּבְזֹאת תֵּדַע, כִּי אֶת **אֲשֶׁר יָעַצְתִּי** אֵלֶיךָ גַּם **הִיא תָּקוּם**:


**To break Assyria in My land** And with this you shall know that what I planned about you will remain as well.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:25:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:25:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:25:2)


**לִשְׁבֹּר אַשּׁוּר וְגוֹ׳.** מוּסָב עַל **כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּמִּיתִי כֵּן הָיְתָה**:


**“To break...”** is connected to “As I thought, so it was.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:25:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:25:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:25:3)


**אֲבוּסֶנּוּ.** אֲשֶׁר אָמַרְתִּי לְרוֹמְסוֹ וּלְבוֹסְסוֹ:


**will I trample him** Heb. אֲבוּסֶנוּ, which I said to tread upon him and trample him.



### Verse 26

###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:26:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:26:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:26:1)


**עַל כָּל הַגּוֹיִם.** עַל אַשּׁוּר בִּשְׁעָתוֹ וְעַל בָּבֶל בִּשְׁעָתָהּ:


**over all the nations** Over Assyria in its time and over Babylon in its time.



### Verse 28

###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:28:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:28:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:28:1)


**בִּשְׁנַת מוֹת הַמֶּלֶךְ אָחָז.** וּמָלַךְ חִזְקִיָּהוּ בְּנוֹ, הָיָה הַמַּשָּׂא הַזֶּה עַל פְּלִשְׁתִּים:


**In the year of King Ahaz’s death** and his son Hezekiah reigned, was this harsh prophecy concerning the Philistines given.



### Verse 29

###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:29:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:29:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:29:1)


**אַל תִּשְׂמְחִי פְלֶשֶׁת כֻּלֵּךְ.** שֶׁהֲרִימוֹת רֹאשׁ בִּימֵי אָחָז, שֶׁהָיָה רָשָׁע שֶׁגָּרַם לוֹ רִשְׁעוֹ שֶׁנִּמְסַר בְּיֶדְכֶם, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דברי הימים ב כח:יח) ״וּפְלִשְׁתִּים פָּשְׁטוּ בְּעָרֵי הַשְּׁפֵלָה וְגוֹ׳״:


**Rejoice not, Philistia, all of you** for you have lifted your head during the days of Ahaz, who was wicked, whose wickedness brought about that he was delivered into your hands, as the matter is stated in II Chron. 28:18: “And the Philistines raided the cities of the lowlands...”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:29:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:29:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:29:2)


**כִּי נִשְׁבַּר שֵׁבֶט מַכֵּךְ.** כִּי נֶחְלְשָׁה וְנִשְׁפְּלָה מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד, שֶׁהָיוּ לְמוּדִים לְהַכּוֹת בָּכֶם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בְּדָוִד; וְכֵן עֻזִּיָּהוּ מֶלֶךְ יְהוּדָה שֶׁהִכָּה אֶתְכֶם, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דברי הימים ב כו:ו): ״וַיֵּצֵא וַיִּלָּחֶם בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּים וַיִּפְרֹץ אֶת חוֹמַת גַּת״:


**that the rod that smote you has been broken** that the kingdom of the House of David, which was wont to smite you, has been weakened and humbled, as we find concerning David, and so, concerning Uzziah, king of Judah, who smote you, as the matter is stated (II Chron. 26:6): “And he went out and fought against the Philistines and breached the wall of Gath.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:29:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:29:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:29:3)


**כִּי מִשֹּׁרֶשׁ נָחָשׁ.** מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ אוֹתוֹ נָחָשׁ יֵצֵא צֶפַע, שֶׁהוּא קָשֶׁה מִנָּחָשׁ. וּמִי הָיָה זֶה? חִזְקִיָּה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ (מלכים ב יח:ח): ״הוּא הִכָּה אֶת הַפְּלִשְׁתִּים וְאֶת עַזָּה וְאֶת גְּבוּלֶיהָ מִמִּגְדַּל נוֹצְרִים עַד עִיר מִבְצָר״:


**for, from the root of a snake** From the root of that snake, shall emanate a venomous serpent, which is more formidable than a snake. Now who was this? This was Hezekiah, concerning whom it is stated (II Kings 18:8): “He slew the Philistines up to Gaza and its boundaries, from watchtower to fortified city.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:29:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:29:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:29:4)


**וּפִרְיוֹ שָׂרָף מְעוֹפֵף.** תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״וִיהוֹן עוֹבְדוֹהִי בְּכוֹן כְּחִיוֵי״:


**and his offspring is a fiery flying serpent** Jonathan renders: And his deeds against you will be like flying snakes.



### Verse 30

###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:30:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:30:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:30:1)


**וְרָעוּ בְּכוֹרֵי דַלִּים. וְרָעוּ** בִּימֵי שָׂרֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהֵן עַכְשָׁיו **דַּלִּים** מִפְּנֵיכֶם. **בְּכוֹרֵי** לְשׁוֹן ׳שָׂרִים׳, כְּמוֹ (תהלים פט:כח) ״גַּם אֲנִי בְּכוֹר אֶתְּנֵהוּ״:


**And the first born of the poor shall graze** In his days, the princes of Israel, who are now poor because of you, shall graze. “Firstborn,” is an expression of princes. Comp. (Ps. 89:28) “Also, I will appoint him My firstborn.”



### Verse 31

###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:31:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:31:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:31:1)


**כִּי מִצָּפוֹן עָשָׁן בָּא.** פֻּרְעָנוּת קָשָׁה כְּעָשָׁן תָּבֹא עֲלֵיהֶם **מִצָּפוֹן**. עַזָּה וּגְבוּלֶיהָ, שֶׁהִכָּה חִזְקִיָּה, הָיוּ בִּדְרוֹמָהּ שֶׁל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּמִקְצוֹעַ דְּרוֹמִית מַעֲרָבִית, נִמְצֵאת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל לָהּ מִצָּפוֹן. וְכֵן מָצִינוּ בְּסִפְרֵי בְּהַאֲזִינוּ (ספרי דברים שכב): בִּקְשׁוּ לִבְרוֹחַ כְּלַפֵּי דָּרוֹם, הָיוּ מַסְגִּירִין אוֹתָן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (עמוס א:ו) ״עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה פִּשְׁעֵי עַזָּה״; לָמַדְנוּ שֶׁעַזָּה בַּדָּרוֹם:


**for from the North smoke has come** Retribution harsh as smoke shall come upon them from the north. Gaza and its boundaries, which Hezekiah smote, were in the south of Eretz Israel in the southwestern corner. Eretz Israel is found to be north of it. And so we find in Sifrei in Ha’azinu 322: They attempted to flee through the south, and they turned them over, as it is stated (Amos 1:6): “For three transgressions of Gaza... [because of their exiling a complete exile to deliver to Edom.]” Hence, we learn that Gaza is on the south.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:31:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:31:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:31:2)


**וְאֵין בּוֹדֵד בְּמוֹעָדָיו.** תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״וְלֵית דְּמְאַחֵר בְּזִמְנוֹהִי״, בַּגְּדוּדִים שֶׁיִּעֵד לָבֹא עֲלֵיכֶם, וְאֵין מְאַחֵר פְּעָמָיו לִהְיוֹת בּוֹדֵד וּבָא בָּדָד לְבַדּוֹ, אֶלָּא כֻּלָּם כְּאֶחָד יָבוֹאוּ בְּחָזְקָה:


**and there is no straggler in his ranks** Jonathan renders: And there is no straggler among his appointed ones, i.e., in his ranks whom he appointed to come upon them, and no one delays his steps to be secluded and to come in seclusion alone, but all of them shall come as one, with strength.



### Verse 32

###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:32:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:32:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:32:1)


**וּמַה יַּעֲנֶה מַלְאֲכֵי גוֹי.** וּמַה יַגִּידוּ בִּימֵי חִזְקִיָּהוּ מַלְאֲכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הַהוֹלְכִים לְבַשֵּׂר בְּשׂוֹרוֹת? כֵּן יַגִּידוּ: **ה׳ יִסַּד בְּצִיּוֹן**, הֵקִים בָּהּ מֶלֶךְ הָגוּן וְחָזָק, וַה׳ עִמּוֹ:


**And what shall the messengers of a nation announce** What shall the messengers of Israel, who go to bring news, announce in the days of Hezekiah? This is what they shall announce: The Lord has founded in Zion; He has set up therein a fitting and powerful king; the Lord is with him.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 14:32:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:32:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/14:32:2)


**וּבָהּ יֶחֱסוּ עֲנִיֵּי עַמּוֹ.** אַף מֵעֲשֶׂרֶת הַשְּׁבָטִים בָּאִים שָׁם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּפוֹרָשׁ (דברי הימים ב ל:א-ו) שֶׁשָּׁלַח חִזְקִיָּהוּ מַלְאָכִים בְּכָל גְּבוּל יִשְׂרָאֵל לָשׁוּב לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:


**and therein shall the poor of His people shelter themselves** Even from the ten tribes they would come there, as is related in II Chron. (30:6), “Hezekiah sent messengers throughout the border of Israel, to return to the Holy One, blessed be He.



## Chapter 15


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Isaiah 15:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:1:1)


**מַשָּׂא מוֹאָב.** נִתְנַבֵּא יְשַׁעְיָה שֶׁיָּבוֹא סַנְחֵרִיב עַל מוֹאָב וְיַגְלֵם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ישעיהו טז:יד) ״בְּשָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים כִּשְׁנֵי שָׂכִיר וְנִקְלָה כְּבוֹד מוֹאָב״:


**The harsh prophecy concerning Moab** Isaiah prophesied that Sennacherib would come upon Moab and exile them, as it is said (infra 16:14): “In three years, like the years of a hireling, shall the glory of Moab be debased.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 15:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:1:2)


**כִּי בְּלֵיל שֻׁדַּד עָר מוֹאָב נִדְמָה.** נִדְמָה מוֹאָב כְּאִלּוּ יָשֵׁן דּוֹמֶה וְאֵין יָכוֹל לְהִלָּחֵם, וּבְלֵיל אַחֵר אֲשֶׁר שׁוּדַּד בּוֹ **קִיר מוֹאָב נִדְמָה**. תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״וְאִינּוּן רְדִימִין״. עָר וְקִיר שְׁתֵּי מְדִינוֹת מוֹאָב הֵם:


**for on the night that Ar of Moab was pillaged, it was as though they were sleeping silently** Moab was silent as though they were sleeping silently and were unable to wage war, and on another night when Kir of Moab was pillaged, it was as though they were sleeping silently. Jonathan renders: And they were sleeping. Ar and Kir were two provinces of Moab.



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Isaiah 15:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:2:1)


**עָלָה הַבַּיִת וְדִיבֹן.** עָלָה מוֹאָב הַבַּיִת, וְאַנְשֵׁי דִיבוֹן עַל הַבָּמוֹת:


**They went up to the temple, and Dibon** Moab went up to the temple, and the people of Dibon to the high places.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 15:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:2:2)


**לְבֶכִי.** אֵלּוּ בּוֹכִים בַּבַּיִת, וְאֵלּוּ בּוֹכִים בְּרָאשֵׁי בָּמוֹתֵיהֶם:


**to weep** These would weep in the temple, and these would weep atop their high places.



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Isaiah 15:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:3:1)


**יֹרֵד בַּבֶּכִי.** גּוֹנֵחַ וְנוֹהֵם בִּבְכִי, כְּמוֹ (שופטים יא:לז) ״וְיָרַדְתִּי עַל הֶהָרִים״, וְכֵן (איכה ג:יט) ״זְכָר עָנְיִי וּמְרוּדִי״:


**sighing** Heb. יֹרֵד, sighing and roaring with weeping. Comp. (Judges 11:37) “And I will cry, (וְיָרַדְתִּי) on the mountains,” and (Lam. 3:19) “Remember my affliction and my cry (וּמְרוּדִי).”



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Isaiah 15:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:4:1)


**עַל כֵּן חֲלֻצֵי מוֹאָב יָרִיעוּ.** עַל אֲשֶׁר מְזֻיָּנֵי מוֹאָב יָרִיעוּ לִקְרַאת הַמִּלְחָמָה, וְ**נַפְשׁוֹ** שֶׁל מוֹאָב **יָרְעָה לוֹ**, מִתְרוֹעֶעֶת כְּאָבֵל עַל עַצְמוֹ:


**because the armed men of Moab shall cry in alarm** Since the armed men of Moab shall cry out towards the battle, and the soul of Moab shall cry out for itself, like one mourning for himself.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Isaiah 15:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:5:1)


**לִבִּי לְמוֹאָב יִזְעָק.** נְבִיאֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵינָם כִּנְבִיאֵי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, בִּלְעָם הָיָה מְבַקֵּשׁ לַעֲקוֹר אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל לֹא דָבָר, וּנְבִיאֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִתְאוֹנְנִים עַל פֻּרְעָנוּת הַבָּאָה עַל הָאֻמּוֹת (תנחומא בלק א):


**My heart shall cry out for Moab** The Jewish prophets are not like the gentile prophets. Balaam sought to uproot Israel for no reason, whereas the prophets of Israel bewail the calamity that befalls the nations.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 15:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:5:2)


**בְּרִיחֶהָ עַד צֹעַר.** עַל כָּל חָזְקָה שֶׁל מוֹאָב יִזְעַק לִבִּי עַד צוֹעַר, שֶׁהִיא **עֶגְלָה שְׁלִישִׁיָּה** עִקַּר חֹזֶק שֶׁלָּהֶם, כְּעֶגְלָה שֶׁהִיא שְׁלִישִׁית לַבֶּטֶן. לָשׁוֹן אַחֵר: שְׁלִישִׁיָּה גִּבַּרְתָּנִית. וְיוֹנָתָן תִּרְגֵּם בְּרִיחֶהָ כְּמוֹ בּוֹרְחֶיהָ: הַבּוֹרְחִים יִבְרְחוּ מֵהֶם לְהִמָּלֵט עַד צוֹעַר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁעָשָׂה לוֹט אֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבָּרַח לְצוֹעַר:


**its bars as far as Zoar** Heb. בְּרִיחֶיהָ, bars. For the entire strength of Moab shall my heart cry, as far as Zoar, which is a third born heifer; it is their main strength, like a heifer born third to its mother. Alternatively, שְׁלִשִׁיָּה means a strong heifer. Jonathan, however, renders בְּרִיחֶיהָ like בּוֹרְחֶיהָ, those of her who flee. Those who flee shall flee from them to escape to Zoar, as Lot, their forebear, fled to Zoar.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 15:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:5:3)


**מַעֲלֵה הַלּוּחִית.** מְקוֹם מַעֲלוֹת הַר שֶׁשְּׁמוֹ מַעֲלֵה הַלּוּחִית, וְכֵן ״מוֹרַד חוֹרֹנַיִם״ (ירמיהו מח:ה), יִבְכּוּ הַבּוֹרְחִים דֶּרֶךְ שָׁם. וְכָל הַמְּקוֹמוֹת הָאֵלֶּה מִמּוֹאָב הֵם:


**the ascent of Haluhith** A place on the ascents of the mountain, named “the ascent of Haluhith,” and similarly (Jer. 48:5), “The descent of Horonaim.” Those who flee through them shall weep. All these locations are from Moab.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 15:5:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:5:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:5:4)


**יְעֹעֵרוּ.** יִצְעָקוּ, וְלָשׁוֹן אֲרָמִי הוּא, שֶׁתִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן ״לֹא יִדְרֹךְ הַדּוֹרֵךְ הֵידָד״ (ישעיהו טז:י): ״לָא יְעוֹעֲרוּן בְּקָלְהוֹן״:


**they shall raise** Heb. יְעֹעֵרוּ, they shall cry, and this is an Aramaic expression, for Jonathan renders (infra 16:10): “The treader shall not tread; I have abolished the cry,” as: “They shall not cry (יְעוֹעֲרוּן) with their voice.”



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Isaiah 15:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:6:1)


**מֵי נִמְרִים.** נָהָר שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ מָקוֹם:


**the waters of Nimrim** The river of that place.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 15:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:6:2)


**מְשַׁמּוֹת יִהְיוּ.** מִדַּם חָלָל הַמִּתְעָרֵב וְנוֹפֵל בָּהֶם:


**shall be a waste** from the blood of the fallen that was mixed and fell into it.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 15:6:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:6:3)


**כִּי יָבֵשׁ חָצִיר וגו׳.** כְּלוֹמַר, גִּבּוֹרֵיהֶם וּמַלְכֵיהֶם וְשַׁלִּיטֵיהֶם. וּלְפִי שֶׁשִּׁבְחָהּ שֶׁל אֶרֶץ מוֹאָב הוּא מִרְעֶה הַטּוֹב שֶׁבָּהּ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁנִינוּ (מנחות פז א): אֵילִים מִמּוֹאָב, לְפִיכָךְ מָשַׁל אֶת פֻּרְעָנוּת בְּחֻרְבַּן מִרְעֶה שֶׁלָּהּ:


**for the grass has dried up** meaning their heroes and their kings and their rulers, and since the land of Moab is noted for its good pastureland, as we learned (Menachoth 87a): “Rams from Moab,” he therefore compared its retribution to the destruction of its pastureland.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Isaiah 15:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:7:1)


**עַל כֵּן יִתְרָה עָשָׂה.** עַל אֲשֶׁר יִתְרָה עָשָׂה, תָּבֹא עָלָיו הַפֻּרְעָנוּת הַזֶּה; שֶׁהָיוּ כְּפוּיֵי טוֹבָה, שֶׁהֲרֵי בְּכַמָּה מְקוֹמוֹת עָמַד אַבְרָהָם לְלוֹט: בְּצֵאתוֹ מֵחָרָן, וּבְלֶכְתּוֹ לְמִצְרַיִם, וּבִזְכוּתוֹ שֻׁלַּח מִתּוֹךְ הַהֲפֵכָה, וְנִלְחַם עָלָיו עִם אַמְרָפֶל וַחֲבֵרָיו. וְהָיָה לָהֶם לִגְמוֹל טוֹבָה לְזַרְעוֹ, וְהֵם הָיוּ מוֹנִים אוֹתָם; כְּשֶׁהִגְלָה סַנְחֵרִיב לָראוּבֵנִי וְלַגָּדִי, וְהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בּוֹכִים וּמִתְאוֹנְנִים, וְהָיוּ אוֹמְרִים לָהֶם: עַל מָה אַתֶּם מִתְאוֹנְנִים, וַהֲלֹא לְבֵית אֲבִיכֶם אַתֶּם הוֹלְכִים? אַבְרָהָם אֲבִיכֶם לֹא מֵעֵבֶר הַנָּהָר בָּא? וְזֶהוּ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (צפניה ב:ח): ״שָׁמַעְתִּי חֶרְפַּת מוֹאָב וְגִדּוּפֵי בְּנֵי עַמּוֹן״. וְעוֹד: שֶׁסִּיְּעוּ אֶת סַנְחֵרִיב שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים שֶׁצָּר עַל שׁוֹמְרוֹן, הוּא שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ישעיהו טז:יד): ״בְּשָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים כִּשְׁנֵי שָׂכִיר וְנִקְלָה כָּל כְּבוֹד מוֹאָב״:


**Because of the many things they did** Because they did many things, this retribution shall come upon them, for they were unappreciative, for in many places Abraham stood up for Lot: when he left Haran, and when he went to Egypt, and in his merit he was sent out of the overturning of Sodom, and he fought for him with Amraphel and his allies. For this, they should have repaid his descendants with favors. Yet they taunted them when Sennacherib exiled the Reubenites and the Gadites, and the Israelites were weeping and lamenting, and they would say to them, ‘Why are you lamenting? Aren’t you going to your father’s house? Didn’t your father Abraham come from the other side of the river?’ And this is what is stated (Zephaniah 2:8): “I heard the insults of Moab and the jeers of the children of Ammon.” Moreover, they aided Sennacherib for three years when he besieged Samaria. This is what is stated (infra 16:14): “In three years, like the years of a hireling, the glory of Moab shall be debased.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 15:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:7:2)


**וּפְקֻדָּתָם.** תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״וְתְחוּמֵיהוֹן דְּעַל יַמָּא מַעֲרָבָא יִתְנְסִיב״, וְהוּא לְשׁוֹן מִנּוּי, כְּמוֹ ״וּפְקֻדַּת אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֵן״ (במדבר ד:טז), כְּלוֹמַר: אַרְצָם שֶׁפְּקֻדָּתָם עָלֶיהָ תִּלָּקַח מֵהֶם:


**and their appointed territory** Heb. וּפְקֻדָּתָם. Jonathan renders: and their boundaries that are on the western sea, shall be taken. This is an expression of appointment. Comp. (Num. 4:16) “And the appointment of Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest.” The land over which they were appointed, shall be taken from them.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 15:7:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:7:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:7:3)


**עַל נַחַל הָעֲרָבִים יִשָּׂאוּם.** יִקְחוּ הָאוֹיְבִים אוֹתָם אֶת הַגְּבוּלִין. וְעוֹד יֵשׁ לְפָרֵשׁ **וּפְקֻדָּתָם** – עֲלֵיהֶם זוֹ תִּהְיֶה נַחַל הָעֲרָבִים יִשָּׂאוּם, הָאוֹיְבִים יַגְלוּ אוֹתָם אֶל אֶרֶץ בָּבֶל שֶׁהוּא נַחַל עֲרָבִים, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (תהלים קלז:ב) ״עַל עֲרָבִים בְּתוֹכָהּ תָּלִינוּ כִּנֹּרוֹתֵינוּ״:


**by the western sea, they shall take them** The enemies shall take them, namely the boundaries. Alternatively, it may be interpreted as: and their visitation; i.e., their visitation that I will bring upon them will be, that to the valley of the willows they shall carry them off. The enemies shall exile them to the land of Babylon, which is the valley of the willows, as it is said (Ps. 137:2): “On willows in its midst we hung our harps.”

### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Isaiah 15:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:9:1)


**מֵי דִימוֹן.** שֵׁם הַנָּהָר:


**The waters of Dimon** The name of the river.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 15:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:9:2)


**מָלְאוּ דָם.** כְּשֵׁם הַנָּהָר:


**have been filled with blood** Like the name of the river. [The name דִּימוֹן resembles דַּם, blood.]


###### Rashi on Isaiah 15:9:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:9:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:9:3)


**כִּי אָשִׁית עַל דִּימוֹן נוֹסָפוֹת.** דָּם שְׁמוֹ, וְדָם חֲלָלִים אוֹסִיף עָלָיו לְמַלְּאוֹתוֹ, וְהוּא לְשׁוֹן ״סְפוּ שָׁנָה עַל שָׁנָה״ (ישעיהו כט:א), ״סְפוֹת הָרָוָה״ (דברים כט:יח). וְיוֹנָתָן תִּרְגֵּם **נוֹסָפוֹת**: ״כְּנִישַׁת מַשִׁירְיָן״, מַחֲנוֹת הַנֶּאֱסָפוֹת יַחַד:


**for I will place upon Dimon additions** Its name is blood, and I will add the blood of the fallen, to fill it. Jonathan renders, however: כְּנִישַׁת מַשַׁירְיָן, the gathering of the camps, the camps joined together. This is an expression of (infra 21:1) “Join (סְפוּ) year to year”; (Deut. 29:18) “to add (סְפוֹת) the inadvertent sins.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 15:9:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:9:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:9:4)


**לִפְלֵיטַת מוֹאָב אַרְיֵה.** פְּלֵיטָה שֶׁיַּשְׁאִיר סַנְחֵרִיב, יָבֹא נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר בְּעִתּוֹ וְיַשְׁחִיתֶהָ, וְהוּא נִקְרָא אַרְיֵה, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ירמיהו ד:ז) ״עָלָה אַרְיֵה מִסֻּבְּכוֹ״:


**for the survivors of Moab is the lion** The survivors which Sennacherib will leave over, Nebuchadnezzar will carry away in his time, and he will destroy them. And he is called “the lion,” as the matter is stated (Jer. 4:7): “The lion has come up out of his thicket.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 15:9:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:9:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:9:5)


**וְלִשְׁאֵרִית.** יִשְׂרָאֵל:


**and for the remnant** of Israel.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 15:9:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:9:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/15:9:6)


**אֲדָמָה.** אַדְמַתְכֶם:


**is the land** [i.e,] your land.



## Chapter 16


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:1:1)


**שִׁלְחוּ כַר מֹשֵׁל אֶרֶץ.** אַל תִּתְגָּאוּ בְּגַאֲוַתְכֶם, הֲלֹא יְדַעְתֶּם שֶׁמּוֹשֵׁל אֶרֶץ שֶׁלָּכֶם מֵישַׁע מֶלֶךְ מוֹאָב (מלכים ב ג:ד) ״הָיָה נוֹקֵד וְהֵשִׁיב לְמֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵאָה אֶלֶף כָּרִים״, שִׁלְחוּ אוֹתוֹ כַּר הַמּוֹשֵׁל שֶׁלָּכֶם **מִסֶּלַע מִדְבָּרָה אֶל הַר בַּת צִיּוֹן**:


**Send lambs of the ruler of the land** Be not proud. Do you not know that the ruler of your land, Mesha, king of Moab, (II Kings 3:4) was a sheepman; and he would repeatedly pay tribute to the king of Israel one hundred thousand lambs. Send those lambs of your ruler from Sela Midbarah to the mountain of the community of Zion.



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:2:1)


**כְּעוֹף נוֹדֵד.** מִקִּנּוֹ:


**like a wandering bird** from its nest.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:2:2)


**קֵן מְשֻׁלָּח.** כְּאֶפְרוֹחִים מְשֻׁלָּחִים מִקִּנָּם, שֶׁהוֹלְכִים מְטֻלְטָלִין, כֵּן **תִּהְיֶינָה בְּנוֹת מוֹאָב** לְמַעְבָּרוֹת אַרְנוֹן:


**driven from the nest** like young birds driven from their nest, who roam and wander, so shall the villages of Moab wander to the fords of the Arnon.



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:3:1)


**עֲשִׂי פְלִילָה.** הוּא לְשׁוֹן וִכּוּחַ מִשְׁפָּט, לִבְחוֹר לְךָ אֶת הַטּוֹב, כְּמוֹ (איוב לד:ד) ״מִשְׁפָּט נִבְחֲרָה לָּנוּ״:


**deliberate judgment** This is an expression of a debate of judgment, to choose for yourself what is good. Comp. (Job 34:4) “Let us choose for ourselves what is just.” [derajjsnement in O.F., discernment.]


###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:3:2)


**שִׁיתִי כַלַּיִל צִלֵּךְ.** שִׁיתִי לָךְ צֵל בַּצָהֳרַיִם שֶׁיַּחְשִׁיךְ צִלֵּךְ כַּלַּיְלָה, לְהִסָּתֵר בּוֹ מִפְּנֵי אוֹיְבֶיךָ:


**make like the night your shadow** Make yourself a shadow at noon that will darken your shadow like night, to hide therein from before your enemies.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:3:3)


**סַתְּרִי נִדָּחִים.** אִם יִבְרְחוּ עוֹד נִדְחֵי עַמִּי דֶּרֶךְ עֲלֵיכֶם בִּימֵי נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר, אַל תַּסְגִּירֵם אֶלָּא תַּסְתִּירֵם:


**conceal the exiles** If the exiles of My people flee again through your land in the days of Nebuchadnezzar, do not turn them over to the Chaldees but conceal them.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:4:1)


**יָגוּרוּ בָךְ נִדָּחַי.** בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הַבּוֹרְחִים:


**May My exiles sojourn among you** The fleeing children of Israel.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:4:2)


**הֱוִי סֵתֶר לָמוֹ.** כִּי גַם אַתְּ דְּעִי נֶפֶשׁ הַנּוֹדְדִים, מַה הִיא צָרָתָם:


**become a hiding place for them** for you too shall know the soul of the wanderers, what their distress is.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:4:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:4:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:4:3)


**כִּי אָפֵס הַמֵּץ.** הַמֵּץ שֶׁלָּךְ, עָשְׁרֵךָ וּכְבוֹדֵךָ, שֶׁהָיָה לָךְ עַל יְדֵי צֹאנֵךָ וּבְקָרֵךָ, שֶׁאַתְּ מוֹצֶצֶת מֵהֶם חָלָב וְחֶמְאָה:


**for the milking has come to an end** Your squeezing, your wealth and your glory, which you had through your flocks and your cattle, from which you would squeeze milk and cream.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:4:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:4:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:4:4)


**כָּלָה שֹׁד.** לְשׁוֹן ׳שָׁדַיִם׳, הַמַּסְפִּיקִין חָלָב, כְּמוֹ ״וְשֹׁד מְלָכִים תִּינָקִי״ (ישעיהו ס:טז):


**the udders have vanished** Heb. כָּלָה שֹׁד, an expression of breasts that supply milk. Comp. (infra 60:16) “And the breast of (וְשֹׁד) the kings you shall suck.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:4:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:4:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:4:5)


**תָּמּוּ רֹמֵס.** הַבְּהֵמוֹת שֶׁלְּךָ הָרוֹמְסוֹת בָּאָרֶץ:


**the tramplers have ceased** Your animals that trample [the earth] in your land.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:5:1)


**וְהוּכַן בַּחֶסֶד כִּסֵּא.** כְּשֶׁיָּבֹא עָלֶיךָ הַשֶּׁבֶר הַזֶּה, אָז יִכּוֹן כִּסֵּא דָּוִד וְיִגְדַּל, שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ הַפֶּרֶק יִפּוֹל סַנְחֵרִיב עַל יְדֵי חִזְקִיָּהוּ, וְיִהְיֶה נָכוֹן כִּסְאוֹ בַּחֶסֶד שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ שֶׁהָיָה גּוֹמֵל חֶסֶד, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים (דברי הימים ב ל:כד): ״כִּי חִזְקִיָּהוּ מֶלֶךְ יְהוּדָה הֵרִים לַקָּהָל אֶלֶף פָּרִים וְשִׁבְעַת אַלְפֵי צֹאן״:


**And the throne shall be established through lovingkindness** When this destruction comes upon you, then the throne of David shall be established and magnified, for at that time, Sennacherib shall meet his downfall through Hezekiah, whose throne shall be established through the lovingkindness that he shall perform, as we find that he bestowed lovingkindness, as it is stated in II Chron. (30:24): “For Hezekiah, king of Judah provided for the assembly a thousand bulls and seven thousand sheep.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:5:2)


**וְיָשַׁב עָלָיו וְגוֹ׳. שׁוֹפֵט וְדוֹרֵשׁ מִשְׁפָּט וּמְהִיר צֶדֶק**, תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״וְעָבִיד קְשׁוֹט״:


**and there shall sit...one who judges and demands justice and performs righteousness** Heb. וּמְהִר צֶדֶק. Jonathan renders: and performs justice.



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:6:1)


**גֵּא מְאֹד.** נִתְגָּאָה מְאֹד:


**they have become very proud** Heb. גֵּא מְאֹד, [lit.] he has become very proud.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:6:2)


**גַּאֲוָתוֹ וּגְאוֹנוֹ.** שֶׁלֹּא כַּדִּין הוּא, כִּי עִקַּר גִּדּוּלֵי בָּנָיו עַל יְדֵי מַמְזֵרוּת וְנִאוּף הַבָּנוֹת מֵאֲבִיהֶן:


**their pride and their haughtiness** are improper, for the source of the nurturing of their branches was through illegitimacy and the incest of the daughters from their father.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:6:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:6:3)


**עֶבְרָתוֹ.** עִבּוּרוֹ וְהֵרָיוֹן שֶׁלּוֹ. דָּבָר אַחֵר: **עֶבְרָתוֹ** – חֲמָתוֹ, שֶׁשָּׁמַר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל:


**and their conception** Heb. וְעֶבְרָתוֹ, their conception, [lit. his conception.] Alternatively, עֶבְרָתוֹ means “his anger,” the anger they bore for Israel.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:6:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:6:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:6:4)


**לֹא כֵן.** גִּבּוֹרָיו עָשׂוּ, שֶׁהָיוּ כְּפוּיֵי טוֹבָה:


**improper** Their heroes acted improperly, for they were unappreciative.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:7:1)


**יְיֵלִיל מוֹאָב לְמוֹאָב.** עַל מוֹאָב:


**Therefore, Moab shall wail for Moab** [lit. to Moab,] for Moab.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:7:2)


**לַאֲשִׁישֵׁי קִיר חֲרֶשֶׂת.** אֶל חוֹמוֹת קִיר חֲרֶשֶׂת. **אֲשִׁישֵׁי.** כְּמוֹ ״נָפְלוּ אָשְׁיוֹתֶיהָ״ (ירמיהו נ:טו):


**for the walls of Kir-hareseth** Heb. לַאֲשִׁישֵׁי, for the walls of Kir-hareseth. **for the walls** Comp. (Jer. 50:15) “Her walls (אָשְׁיוֹתֶיהָ) fell.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:7:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:7:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:7:3)


**תֶּהְגּוּ אַךְ נְכָאִים.** שְׁבָרִים:


**shall you lament, but broken-hearted** Heb. נְכָאִים, broken.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:7:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:7:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:7:4)


**תֶּהְגּוּ.** תְּקוֹנְנוּ:


**shall you lament** Heb. תֶּהֶגּוּ.



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:8:1)


**שַׁדְמוֹת.** שְׂדוֹת תְּבוּאָה:


**grain fields** Heb. שַׁדְמוֹת.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:8:2)


**גֶּפֶן שִׂבְמָה** יֵשׁ לִלְמֹד שֶׁחֶשְׁבּוֹן הָיְתָה מְקוֹם שָׂדוֹת וְשִׂבְמָה מְקוֹם כְּרָמִים. וְאִם תֹּאמַר: כָּל אֵלֶּה עָרֵי עֵבֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן הֵם וְיִשְׂרָאֵל לְקָחוּם מִיַּד סִיחוֹן, וְאֵימָתַי חָזְרוּ לְיַד מוֹאָב? כְּשֶׁהִגְלָה סַנְחֵרִיב לָראוּבֵנִי וְלַגָּדִי, בָּאוּ הַמּוֹאָבִים הַסְּמוּכִים לָהֶם וְיָשְׁבוּ בָּהֶם:


**the vine of Sibmah** We can deduce that Heshbon was a place of fields and Sibmah a place of vineyards. Now if you ask, All these are cities of the east side of the Jordan, and Israel took them from the hands of Sihon. Now when did they return to the hands of Moab? When Sennacherib exiled the Reubenites and the Gadites, the neighboring Moabites came and settled in them.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:8:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:8:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:8:3)


**אֻמְלָל.** חָרֵב:


**has become desolate** Heb. אֻמְלָל, has become desolate.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:8:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:8:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:8:4)


**שְׂרוּקֶּיהָ.** נְטִיעוֹת שׂוֹרֵק שֶׁלָּהּ:


**its saplings** its choice saplings.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:8:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:8:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:8:5)


**עַד יַעְזֵר נָגָעוּ.** שַׁדְמוֹת וְגֶפֶן וְשׂוֹרֵק הַנִּזְכָּרִים כָּאן אֵינָם אֶלָּא מָשָׁל, וְהֵם מַחֲנוֹת וְסִיעוֹת בִּימֵי הָעַמִּים הָאֵלֶּה, וְכֵן תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן:


**they reached as far as Jazer** The grain fields and the vine and the saplings mentioned here are merely an allegory. They represent camps, companies, and rulers [in the days of these peoples]. So did Jonathan paraphrase it.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:8:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:8:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:8:6)


**עַד יַעְזֵר נָגָעוּ.** הָלְכוּ בְּגוֹלָה:


**they reached as far as Jazer** they went into exile.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:8:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:8:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:8:7)


**תָּעוּ מִדְבָּר.** לַמִּדְבָּר:


**they strayed to the desert** lit. they strayed the desert.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:8:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:8:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:8:8)


**שְׁלֻחוֹתֶיהָ.** זְמוֹרוֹתֶיהָ, וְהֵם מָשָׁל גָּלִיּוֹתֶיהָ:


**its tendrils** its branches; and they are the symbol of its exiles.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:8:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:8:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:8:9)


**נִטְּשׁוּ.** נָפֹצוּ, כְּמוֹ ״וּנְטַשְׁתִּיךָ הַמִּדְבָּרָה״ (יחזקאל כט:ה), ״וְהִנָּם נְטוּשִׁים״ (שמואל א ל:טז), ״וַיִּנָּטְשׁוּ בְּעֵמֶק רְפָאִים״ (שמואל ב ה:כב):


**spread out** Heb. נִטְּשׁוּ, scattered. Comp. (Ezekiel 29:5) “And I will scatter you (וּנְטַשְׁתִּיךָ) in the desert”; (I Sam. 30: 16) “And behold, they were scattered (נְטוּשִׁים)”; (II Sam. 5:22) “And spread out (וַיִּנָּטְשׁוּ) in the valley of Rephaim.”



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:9:1)


**אֶבְכֶּה בִּבְכִי יַעְזֵר.** תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״כְּמָא דְאַיְיתִיתִי מַשְׁרְיָין עַל יַעְזֵר כֵּן אַיְיתִי קְטוֹלִין עַל שִׂבְמָה״, וּלְשׁוֹן הַמִּקְרָא הַנָּבִיא אוֹמֵר: כְּעֵין קִינוֹת יַעְזֵר יֵשׁ לִי לְקוֹנֵן עָלֶיךָ, אַתְּ הַגֶּפֶן שִׂבְמָה:


**I will weep with the weeping of Jazer** Jonathan paraphrases: As I brought camps upon Jazer, so will I bring killers upon Sibmah, and, according to the wording of the verse, the prophet states: Similar to the lamentations of Jazer, I have to lament over you, the vine of Sibmah.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:9:2)


**אֲרַיָּוֶךְ דִּמְעָתִי.** אֶתְרַוֶּה עָלֶיךָ דִּמְעָה. יֵשׁ תֵּיבָה מְשַׁמֶּשֶׁת כִּשְׁתֵּי תֵיבוֹת, כְּמוֹ ״בָּנַי יְצָאוּנִי״ (ירמיהו י:כ), ״אֶרֶץ הַנֶּגֶב נְתַתָּנִי״ (יהושע טו:יט), ״דַּבְּרוֹ לְשָׁלוֹם״ (בראשית לז:ד):


**I will be sated over you with my tears** Heb. אַרְיָוֶךְ, I will be sated over you. There are some words that serve as two words. Comp. (Jer. 10:20) “My children went out of me (יְצֵאוּנִי)”; (Jos. 15:19) “A dry land you have given to me (נְתַתָּנִי)”; (Gen. 37:4) “To speak to him (דַּבְּרוֹ) peacefully.”

**your figs** Heb. (קִיצֵךְ), the figs that are dried out in the summer.

### Verse 14

###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:14:1)


**וְעַתָּה דִּבֶּר ה׳.** לְקָרֵב אֶת הַפֻּרְעָנוּת לָהֶם:

###### Rashi on Isaiah 16:14:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:14:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/16:14:2)


**בְּשָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים כִּשְׁנֵי שָׂכִיר.** בִּשְׁבִיל שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים שֶׁסִּיְּעוּ אֶת סַנְחֵרִיב, כְּשֶׁצָּר עַל שׁוֹמְרוֹן, וַעֲזָרוּהוּ בְּלִי בֶּצַע כְּאִלּוּ הָיוּ לוֹ שְׂכִירִים, לְפִיכָךְ **וְנִקְלָה כְּבוֹד מוֹאָב** בֵּין כָּל שְׁאָר הֲמוֹנוֹ שֶׁל סַנְחֵרִיב שֶׁשִּׁטְּפָם בַּשְּׁבִי מִתּוֹךְ אוֹתוֹ הַחַיִל וַיֵּלֶךְ לוֹ. וְכֵן מְפֹרָשׁ בְּסֵדֶר עוֹלָם (סדר עולם רבה כג): שָׁטַף עַמּוֹנִים וּמוֹאָבִים שֶׁהָיוּ מְסַיְּעִין אוֹתָם כְּשֶׁצָּר עַל שׁוֹמְרוֹן שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים, לְקַיֵּם מַה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר **שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים כִּשְׁנֵי שָׂכִיר וְגוֹ׳**. וְעוֹד יֵשׁ לְפָרֵשׁ **שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים כִּשְׁנֵי שָׂכִיר**: שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים נִגְזְרוּ עֲלֵיכֶם לְאֹרֶךְ זְמַן, אֲבָל מְצֻמְצָמִין יִהְיוּ וְלֹא תְאַחֵר עוֹד הַפֻּרְעָנוּת, כַּאֲשֶׁר יְדַקְדֵּק הַשָּׂכִיר בִּשְׁנֵי שְׂכִירוּתוֹ לְצַמְצֵם:


**In three years like the years of a hireling** Because of three years that they aided Sennacherib when he besieged Samaria, and they aided him without compensation, as though they were his hirelings, the glory of Moab shall, therefore, be debased among the rest of Sennacherib’s multitudes, for he swept them away into captivity from the midst of that army and went away. And so it is related in Seder Olam (ch. 23): He swept away the Ammonites and the Moabites who aided him when he besieged Samaria three years, to fulfill what is said: “Three years like the years of a hireling, etc.” It can further be explained as follows: “Three years like the years of a hireling.” Three years were decreed upon you as a reprieve, but they will be exact, and the retribution will not be delayed further, as a hireling is exact with the years of his hire, to limit them.

## Chapter 17


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:1:1)

###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:1:2

###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:1:3

**מְעִי.** לְשׁוֹן שִׁפְלוּת וְעֹמֶק, כְּמוֹ ״מְעוֹת יָמִים״ (ישעיהו מח:יט):
