### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:2:1)


**עֲזֻבוֹת עָרֵי עֲרֹעֵר.** יוֹנָתָן תִּרְגֵּם לְשׁוֹן חוּרְבָּן, כְּמוֹ ״עַרְעֵר תִּתְעַרְעַר״ (ירמיהו נא:נח), וּפֵרְשׁוֹ עַל עָרֵי אֲרָם. וּמִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה מַתְמִיהַּ: לְפִי שֶׁעֲרוֹעֵר מֵאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיְתָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וְאֶת עֲרֹעֵר״ (במדבר לב:לד), עוֹמֵד בְּדַמֶּשֶׂק וּמַכְרִיז בַּעֲרוֹעֵר? אֶלָּא שֶׁהָיוּ בְּדַמֶּשֶׂק שְׁוָקִים כְּמִנְיַן יְמוֹת הַחַמָּה, וְכָל אַחַת יֵשׁ בָּהּ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְעוֹבְדִים לָהּ יוֹם אֶחָד בַּשָּׁנָה, וְיִשְׂרָאֵל עָשׂוּ אֶת כֻּלָּן קִבּוּץ אֶחָד וְהָיוּ עוֹבְדִין אֶת כֻּלָּם בְּכָל יוֹם, לְכָךְ הִזְכִּיר מַפֶּלֶת עֲרוֹעֵר אֵצֶל דַּמֶּשֶׂק. וַאֲנִי מְפָרְשׁוֹ לְפִי פְּשַׁט הַמִּקְרָא: עַל שֶׁנִּתְחַבְּרוּ רְצִין וּפֶקַח בֶּן רְמַלְיָהוּ יַחַד, וְהַנָּבִיא הָיָה מִתְנַבֵּא עַל מַפֶּלֶת דַּמֶּשֶׂק וְאָמַר **הִנֵּה דַמֶּשֶׂק מוּסָר מֵעִיר**, עָרֵי עֲרוֹעֵר שֶׁהָיוּ שֶׁל פֶּקַח כְּבָר הָיוּ עֲזוּבוֹת, שֶׁגָּלוּ הָראוּבֵנִי וְהַגָּדִי כְּבָר, וַהֲרֵי תָּמִיד לְעֶדְרֵי צֹאן הֵם נְתוּנוֹת וְרוֹבְצִים שָׁם צֹאן מוֹאָב **וְאֵין מַחֲרִיד**. עוֹד תְּהִי מַלְכוּת פֶּקַח הוֹלֶכֶת וְכָלָה, וְתִלָּכֵד גַּם שׁוֹמְרוֹן בִּימֵי הוֹשֵׁעַ, וְאָז **וְנִשְׁבַּת מִבְצָר מֵאֶפְרַיִם וּמַמְלָכָה מִדַּמֶּשֶׂק** שֶׁיֵּהָרֵג רְצִין:


**The cities of Aroer are abandoned** Jonathan renders this as an expression of destruction. Comp. (Jer. 51:58) “shall be destroyed (עַרְעֵר תִּתְעַרְעַר), and he explained it in reference to the cities of Aram, i. e., Jonathan renders it: Their cities are abandoned, they are destroyed. The Midrash Aggadah (introduction to Lam. Rabbah 10 [with variations], Yalkut Machin) asks in amazement, since Aroer was [part] of Eretz Israel, as it is said (Num. 32:34): “and Aroer.” He is dealing with Damascus and he announces matters concerning Aroer? But, since in Damascus there were streets as numerous as the days of the solar year, and in each one was a pagan deity, which they would worship one day in the year, and the Israelites made them all into one group and worshipped all of them every day, he, therefore, mentioned the downfall of Aroer juxtaposed to Damascus. I explain it, however, according to the simple meaning of the verse, as follows: Since Rezin and Pekah son of Remaliah joined together, and the prophet prophesying about the downfall of Damascus, and saying, “Behold, Damascus shall be removed from [being] a city,” and the cities of Aroer which belonged to Pekah were already abandoned, for the Reubenites and the Gadites had already been exiled, and they were always given to the flocks of sheep, and the sheep of Moab would lie there undisturbed, he continues to say that the kingdom of Pekah shall continue to be gradually terminated, and that Samaria, too, shall be captured in the days of Hoshea, and then (v. 3) And a fortress shall cease from Ephraim and a kingdom from Damascusfor Rezin shall be killed.



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:3:1)


**כִּכְבוֹד** עֲשֶׂרֶת הַשְּׁבָטִים יִהְיוּ, גַּם אֵלּוּ גָּלוּ לַחְלַח וְחָבוֹר וְאֵלּוּ יִגְלוּ לְקִיר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיִּגְלֶה קִירָה וְאֶת רְצִין הֵמִית״ (מלכים ב טז:ט):


**like the glory of** the ten tribes, shall these also be [var. Aram, too, shall be]. These shall be exiled to Halah and Habor, and these shall be exiled to Kir, as it is stated (II Kings 16:9): “And exiled its inhabitants to Kir, and he slew Rezin.”



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:4:1)


**וּמִשְׁמַן בְּשָׂרוֹ יֵרָזֶה.** ״וְעוּתַר יְקָרֵיהּ יִגְלֵי״ (תרגום יונתן):


**And the fatness of his flesh shall become emaciated** Jonathan [renders]: And the wealth of his glory shall be exiled.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:5:1)


**וְהָיָה כֶּאֱסֹף קָצִיר קָמָה.** כְּמוֹ שֶׁבְּעֵת קְצִירַת קָמָה אוֹסֵף הַקּוֹצֵר צְבַת הַקָּמָה בְּיָד אַחַת, וּזְרוֹעוֹ הַשֵּׁנִית שִׁבֳּלִים יִקְצוֹר בְּמַגָּל, כֵּן יַעֲקוֹר סַנְחֵרִיב וְיַגְלֶה הַכֹּל, וְאַף לֶקֶט הַנּוֹשֵׁר בִּשְׁעַת קְצִירָה יְלַקֵּט וְיִשָּׂאֶנּוּ, כְּלוֹמַר: אַף הַבּוֹרְחִים לֹא יִמָּלְטוּ מִיָּדוֹ וִילַקְּטוּם (כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּלַקֵּט שִׁבֳּלִים סא"א):


**And it shall be like gathering the harvest of the standing grain** Just as at the time of the harvest, the reaper gathers the bundle of the standing grain in his one hand and with his other arm he reaps the ears, so will Sennacherib uproot and exile everyone, and even the gleanings that fall at the time of harvest he will gather and carry it off. That is to say that even those who flee will not escape his hand, and they will gather them [var. and he will gather them] [like one who gathers ears].


###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:5:2)


**בְּעֵמֶק רְפָאִים.** הִיא הַגַּיְא אֲשֶׁר עַל פְּנֵי יְרוּשָׁלַיִם, בְּסֵפֶר יְהוֹשֻׁעַ (יהושע טו:ח, יח:טז) תִּמְצָא שֶׁעֵמֶק רְפָאִים סְמוּכָה לִירוּשָׁלַיִם:


**in the valley of Rephaim** That is the valley that is before Jerusalem. In the Book of Joshua (15:8, 18:16) you will find that the valley of Rephaim adjoins Jerusalem.



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:6:1)


**וְנִשְׁאַר בּוֹ.** חִזְקִיָּהוּ וְסִיעָתוֹ שֶׁהֵם תּוֹךְ יְרוּשָׁלַיִם, אֲנָשִׁים מְעַט כְּ**עֹלְלוֹת** כֶּרֶם וּ**כְנֹקֵף זַיִת** הַמַּשְׁאִיר **שְׁנַיִם שְׁלֹשָׁה גַּרְגְּרִים**:


**And...shall be left in it** Hezekiah and his company, who are inside Jerusalem. They are few people like the gleanings of a vineyard and like the cutter of an olive tree, who leaves over two or three berries.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:6:2)


**כְּנֹקֶף זַיִת.** קוֹצֵץ זֵיתִים לְלוֹקְטָן מִן הָאִילָן, וְכֵן ״וְנִקַּף בְּסִבְכֵי הַיַּעַר״ (ישעיהו י:לד). וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ דָּרְשׁוּ: **וְנִשְׁאַר בּוֹ** בַּהֲמוֹן סַנְחֵרִיב אֲנָשִׁים מְעַט **כְּנקֵף זַיִת**, כִּדְאִיתָא בְּאַגָּדַת חֵלֶק (סנהדרין צה ב):


**like the cutter of an olive tree** Heb. כְּנֹקֶף, like the one who cuts olives to pick them from the tree. Comp. (infra 10:34) “And the thickets of the forest shall be cut off (וְנִקַּף).” Our Rabbis expounded: “And...shall be left in it,” as referring to Sennacherib’s army; i.e., there shall be left in the multitude of Sennacherib a few people like the cutter of an olive tree, as it is stated in the Aggadah of ‘Chelek’ (95b).


###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:6:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:6:3)


**בְּרֹאשׁ אָמִיר.** בְּרֹאשׁ הֶעָנָף:


**at the end of the uppermost bough** at the end of the bough.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:6:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:6:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:6:4)


**בִּסְעִפֶיהָ.** בַּעֲנָפֶיהָ, וְכֵן ״וְכִלָּה סְעִיפֶיהָ״ (ישעיהו כז:י), וְכֵן ״מְסָעֵף פֹּארָה״ (ישעיהו י:לג):


**on its branches** Heb. בִּסְעִפֶיהָ. Comp. infra (27:10) “And he shall finish its branches (סְעִיפֶיהָ).” Also (supra 10:33), “Lops off the branches (מְסָעֵף).”



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:7:1)


**יִשְׁעֶה.** יִפְנֶה אֶל עוֹשֵׂהוּ, כְּמוֹ ״וַיִּשַׁע אֶל הֶבֶל״ (בראשית ד:ד):


**shall turn** Heb. יִשְׁעֶה, shall turn to his Maker. Comp. (Gen. 4:4) “And the Lord turned (וַיִּשַׁע) to Abel.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:7:2)


**הָאָדָם.** צַדִּיקִים שֶׁנִּשְׁאֲרוּ בָּם:


**man** the righteous men remaining among them.



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:8:1)


**לֹא יִרְאֶה.** לֹא יֵחָשְׁבוּ בְּעֵינָיו:


**he shall not regard** [lit. he shall not see.] They shall not be important in his eyes.



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:9:1)


**עָרֵי מָעֻזּוֹ.** שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל:


**the cities of his strength** [The antecedent is] Israel.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:9:2)


**כַּעֲזוּבַת הַחֹרֶשׁ וְהָאָמִיר.** עֲזוּבוֹת כְּיַעַר הַזֶּה, חֲרֵבוֹת מֵאֵין אָדָם:


**like the abandonment of the forest and the many branched trees** Forsaken like this forest, desolate without people.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:9:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:9:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:9:3)


**חֹרֶשׁ.** הוּא יַעַר, כְּדִמְתַרְגֵּם ״בַּיַּעַר״: ״בְּחוּרְשָׁא״ (דברים יט:ה):


**forest** Heb. הַחֹרֶשׁ. This is a forest, as [Onkelos] translates בְחוּרְשַָׁא בַיַעַר, in the forest (Deut. 19:8).


###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:9:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:9:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:9:4)


**וְהָאָמִיר.** אַף הוּא יַעַר, מְקוֹם אִילָנוֹת; **כַּעֲזוּבַת** עָרֵי הָאֱמוֹרִי, שֶׁהִנִּיחוּם חֲרֵבוֹת בִּימֵי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ כַּחֹרֶשׁ וְהָאָמִיר, וּבָרְחוּ לָהֶם **מִפְּנֵי בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל**, וְהָיְתָה אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל **שְׁמָמָה**:


**and the many branched trees** This, too, is a forest, a place of trees. Like the abandoned cities of the Amorites, which they left in desolation in the days of Joshua like the forest and the many branched trees and fled because of the children of Israel, and the land of Israel was desolate.



### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:10:1)


**עַל כֵּן תִּטְּעִי וְגוֹ׳.** עַל כֵּן כַּאֲשֶׁר נְטַעְתִּיךְ מִתְּחִלָּה נָטַעְתִּי נֶטַע נַעֲמָנִים, שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר בְּנֵי יַעֲקֹב, וּבְהַעֲלוֹת נְטָעַיִךְ לִזְמוֹרוֹת נָתְנוּ זֶרַע שֶׁאֵינוֹ הָגוּן, כִּזְמוֹרוֹת זָרוֹת שֶׁאֵינָם מִמִּין גֶּפֶן אֶלָּא דּוֹמִים לַגֶּפֶן:


**because I planted you** Because, when I planted you in the beginning, I planted a pleasant planting, twelve sons of Jacob, and when your saplings raised branches, they gave forth improper seed, like strange branches which are not of the species of the vine but resemble the vine.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:10:2)


**תִּזְרָעֶנּוּ.** תִּתְּנִי זַרְעֵךְ בְּאוֹתוֹ נֶטַע. וְעוֹד יֵשׁ לוֹמַר: **וּזְמוֹרַת זָר תִּזְרָעֶנּוּ** – הִתְחַתַּנְתְּ בַּכּוּתִים וְנִתְעָרְבוּ בָּכֶם:


**you sow it** You give your seed into that sapling. [It is also possible to say that “and with the branch of a stranger you sow it,” means that you intermarry with the nations and they mingled with you.]



### Verse 11

###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:11:1)


**בְּיוֹם נִטְעֵךְ תְּשַׂגְשֵׂגִי.** לְשׁוֹן סִכְסוּךְ: נִשְׁתַּגְשְׁגוּ זְמוֹרוֹתַיִךְ בְּמִינֵי דְשָׁאִים וְעִרְבּוּבִים הַמְקַלְקְלִים עַנְפֵי הַגֶּפֶן, כְּלוֹמַר: בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁנְּטַעְתִּיךְ לִי לְכֶרֶם, שָׁם קִלְקַלְתְּ בְּמַעֲשַׂיִךְ. הוּא שֶׁאָמַר לָהֶם (יחזקאל כ:ה) ״בְּיוֹם בָּחֳרִי בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וָאֶשָּׂא יָדִי לְזֶרַע בֵּית יַעֲקֹב וָאִוָּדַע לָהֶם בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם״, וְנֶאֱמַר (יחזקאל כ:ח) ״וַיַּמְרוּ בִי וְלֹא אָבוּ לִשְׁמֹעַ וְגוֹ׳״. וְאַף כָּאן תְּשַׂגְשֵׂגִי – נִתְעָרַבְתְּ בְּתוֹעֲבוֹת הַמִּצְרִיִּים:


**On the day of your planting you mingled** Heb. תְּשַׂגְשֵׂנִי, an expression of mingling. Your branches became mingled with sorts of grasses and mixtures that spoil the branches of the vine. That is to say that in the place where I planted you for Me as a vineyard, there you corrupted your deeds. That is what Ezekiel said to them (20:5): “On the day I chose Israel, and I lifted My hand to the seed of the house of Jacob, and I became known to them in the land of Egypt.” And it says further (verse 8): “And they rebelled against Me and they refused to obey...” Here, too, תְּשַׂגְשֵׂנִי, you became mingled with the abominations of Egypt.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:11:2)


**וּבַבֹּקֶר זַרְעֵךְ תַּפְרִיחִי.** וּלְיוֹם הַמָּחֳרָת, כְּשֶׁהוֹצֵאתִיךְ מִשָּׁם וְהִכְנַסְתִּיךְ לָאָרֶץ, גַּם שָׁם זַרְעֵךְ הָרַע הִפְרַחְתְּ:


**and in the morning you cause your seed to blossom** And on the morrow, when I took you out of there, and I brought you into the land, there, too, your evil seed you caused to blossom.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:11:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:11:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:11:3)


**נֵד קָצִיר בְּיוֹם נַחֲלָה.** גָּדִישׁ שֶׁל קָצִיר רַע, אֲשֶׁר הוֹכִיחַ בְּיוֹם נַחֲלָה, אוֹתוֹ קָצִיר הִגִּיעַ לְיוֹם צָרָה:


**a heap of harvest on a day of sickness** a heap of bad harvest that lies by day and by night, that harvest is stricken ill, it has reached a day of distress. [Rashi in printed editions.] [Since it is difficult to make sense of this comment of Rashi, Parshandatha prefers the reading of most mss.:] **a heap of harvest on a day of sickness** a heap of bad harvest, as “on a day of sickness” proves, that harvest reached a day of distress.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:11:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:11:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:11:4)


**נֵד.** הוּא לְשׁוֹן גֹּבַהּ, וְכֵן ״נִצְּבוּ כְמוֹ נֵד נוֹזְלִים״ (שמות טו:ח), וְכֵן ״כֹּנֵס כַּנֵּד״ (תהלים לג:ז), וְאֵין נֵד וְנֹאד שָׁוִים:


**a heap** Heb. נֵד. This is an expression of a tall heap. Comp. (Exodus 15:8) “Running water stood erect like a heap (נֵד).” Also (Ps. 33:3), “He gathers like a heap (כַּנֵּד).” [The words:] נֵד and נוֹד are not the same [i.e., נֵד is a heap or a stack, and נוֹד is a flask.]


###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:11:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:11:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:11:5)


**וּכְאֵב אָנוּשׁ.** שֶׁנִּשְׁלַמְתְּ שְׂכָרֵךְ:


**and mortal pain** that you were paid your reward.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:11:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:11:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:11:6)


**אָנוּשׁ.** נֶעְכַּר בְּחֹלִי רַע, וְכֵן ״וַיֵּאָנַשׁ״ (שמואל ב יב:טו), וְכֵן ״כִּי אֲנוּשָׁה מַכּוֹתֶיהָ״ (מיכה א:ט). דָּבָר אַחֵר: **וּבַבֹּקֶר זַרְעֵךְ תַּפְרִיחִי** עַד שֶׁלֹּא בָּא הַשָּׁרָב הִפְרַחְתֶּם, וְדֶרֶךְ הַכֶּרֶם לִפְרוֹחַ בְּבֹא הַשָּׁרָב, וְהַמַּפְרִיחַ בַּבֹּקֶר אֵינוֹ הָגוּן; זֶה בְּמִדְרַשׁ רַבִּי תַּנְחוּמָא (תנחומא שלח יב):


**mortal** Heb. אָנוּשׁ, distressed by severe illness. Comp. (II Sam. 12: 15) “And he became mortally ill (וַיֵּאָנַשׁ),” also (Micah 1:9), “For her wounds are mortal (אֲנוּשָׁה) .” Alternatively **and in the morning you cause your seed to blossom** Before the heat comes, you have blossomed, and it is customary for the vineyard to blossom when the heat comes, and the one that blossoms in the morning does not thrive. This is in the Midrash of Rabbi Tanhuma (Sh’lach 12).



### Verse 12

###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:12:1)


**הוֹי הֲמוֹן עַמִּים רַבִּים.** מִדָּה מְהַלֶּכֶת עַל פְּנֵי כָּל הַדּוֹרוֹת: שׁוֹט שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל לוֹקִים בּוֹ סוֹפוֹ לִלְקוֹת (מכילתא בשלח עמלק ב); לְפִיכָךְ הַנְּבִיאִים הַנִּבָּאִים פֻּרְעָנוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל יְדֵי הָאֻמּוֹת, סוֹמְכִין אַחֲרָיו פֻּרְעָנוּת הָאֻמָּה שֶׁלָּקָה יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל יָדָהּ:


**Woe to a multitude of many peoples** This is a principle followed throughout all generations; the scourge by which Israel is punished, shall eventually suffer. Therefore, the prophets who prophesy Israel’s retribution through the nations, juxtapose after it the retribution of the nation by which Israel was punished.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:12:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:12:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:12:2)


**הֲמוֹן עַמִּים.** אֻכְלוּסֵי סַנְחֵרִיב:


**a multitude of many peoples** The armies of Sennacherib.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:12:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:12:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:12:3)


**יִשָּׁאוּן.** לְשׁוֹן ׳תְּשׁוּאָה׳ וְ׳הוֹמֶה׳ (ישעיהו כב:ב):


**they rush** an expression of rushing and roaring.



### Verse 13

###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:13:1)


**וְגָעַר בּוֹ.** הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּאוֹתוֹ שָׁאוֹן:


**and He shall rebuke them** [lit.] him i.e., the Holy One, blessed be He, [shall rebuke] that rushing [or throng].


###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:13:2)


**כְּמֹץ הָרִים.** מָשַׁל אֶת הָרְשָׁעִים בַּמְקֻלְקָל שֶׁבַּמִּינִים וּבַמְקֻלְקָל שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ הַמִּין. מוֹץ הָרִים יָבֵשׁ מִשֶּׁל עֲמָקִים:


**like the chaff of the mountains** He likens the wicked to the most inferior of all species and the most inferior of that species. The chaff of the mountains is drier than that of the valleys.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:13:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:13:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:13:3)


**וּכְגַלְגַּל.** הוּא מַפְרִיחַ שֶׁל קוֹצִים שֶׁקּוֹרִין קרדונ״ש, הַדּוֹמִים לְאוֹתוֹ שֶׁגּוֹרְרִין בָּהֶן בִּגְדֵי צֶמֶר וְאֵינָן קָשִׁין, וּבְהַגִּיעַ סָמוּךְ לְסוֹף הַקַּיִץ הֵם מִתְנַפְּצִין מֵאֲלֵיהֶן וְהָרוּחַ מְפַזְּרָן, וְאוֹתוֹ הַנִּפּוּץ עָשׂוּי כְּמִין גַּלְגַּל עֲגוּלָה, כְּמִין הָעֵץ (ספרים אחרים: הָעַיִן) בָּאֶמְצַע וְחָמֵשׁ זְרוֹעוֹתָיו סָבִיב לָהּ:


**and like the thistle blossoms** Heb. וּכְגַלְגַל. That is from the blossom of the thistles called kardouns in O.F. [chardons in modern French] similar to those with which they pull woolen garments, and they are not hard. When the end of the summer arrives, they burst open by themselves and the wind scatters them. Now that bursting is made like a round wheel (גַלְגַּל) [var. like a wagon wheel], like a sort of eye in the center with five spokes around it.



### Verse 14

###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:14:1)


**וְהִנֵּה בַלָּהָה.** שֵׁדִים בָּאִים עַל הָאוֹיֵב וּמְבַהֲלִין אוֹתוֹ:


**and behold there is fright** Demons come upon the enemy and frighten him.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:14:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:14:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:14:2)


**בְּטֶרֶם בֹּקֶר אֵינֶנּוּ.** וְהָאוֹיֵב אֵין בָּעוֹלָם:


**before morning he is no more** The enemy is not in the world.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 17:14:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:14:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/17:14:3)


**זֶה חֵלֶק שׁוֹסֵינוּ.** חֵלֶק סַנְחֵרִיב וְחֵלֶק גּוֹג וּמָגוֹג, כְּשֶׁיָּבֹאוּ **לְבֹזְזֵינוּ**:


**this is the portion of our plunderers** The portion of Sennacherib and the portion of Gog and Magog, when they come to plunder us.



## Chapter 18


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Isaiah 18:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:1:1)


**הוֹי אֶרֶץ צִלְצַל כְּנָפָיִם.** תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״דְּאָתָן לַהּ בִּסְפִינוֹן מֵאַרְעָא רְחִיקָא וְקַלְעֵיהוֹן פְּרִיסָן כְּנִשְׁרָא דְּטָאִיס בִּכְנָפוֹהִי״. אֲנִי אוֹמֵר: לְפִי שֶׁהֵן שְׁרוּיִין בַּמִּזְרָח וְהָאָרֶץ חַמָּה, הָעוֹפוֹת נֶאֱסָפִים שָׁם וְהִיא מְצֻלְצֶלֶת בְּכַנְפֵי עוֹפוֹת. וּנְבוּאָה זוֹ עַל אֻכְלוּסֵי גּוֹג וּמָגוֹג, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (יחזקאל לח:ה) ״פָּרַס כּוּשׁ וּפוּט אִתָּם״:


**Woe to the land shaded by wings** Jonathan renders: to which they come in ships from a distant land, and their sails are spread out like an eagle that flies with its wings. I say, however, that because they live in the east, and the land is hot, birds assemble there, and it is shaded by the birds’ wings. Now this prophecy concerns the armies of Gog and Magog, as the matter is stated in Ezekiel (38: 5) “Persia, Cush, and Put with them.”



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Isaiah 18:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:2:1)


**לְכוּ מַלְאָכִים קַלִּים.** לִרְאוֹת אִם אֱמֶת הוּא שֶׁחָזְרוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לִמְקוֹמָם, אֲשֶׁר הוּא **גּוֹי מְמֻשָּׁךְ וּמְמֹרָט אֶל עַם** אֲשֶׁר הוּא הָיָה נוֹרָא בְּחֶזְקָתוֹ:


**Go swift messengers** to see whether it is true that the Israelites have returned to their place, a nation which is pulled and torn, to a people that is awesome from its inception.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 18:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:2:2)


**מִן הוּא וָהָלְאָה.** מִן הַיּוֹם אֲשֶׁר נִבְחַר לְעָם וָהָלְאָה:


**from their beginning and onward** From the day it was chosen as a people and onward.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 18:2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:2:3)


**גּוֹי קַו קָו.** שֶׁנִּפְרַע בּוֹ בַּעֲוֹנוֹ מִדָּה בְּמִדָּה וְנִתַּן לִמְבוּסָה. דָּבָר אַחֵר: **קַו קָו** – לְשׁוֹן קִיא ״סְחִי וּמָאוֹס״ (איכה ג:מה):


**a nation punished in kind** Heb. קַו-קָו [lit. a line for a line, i.e.,] when he is punished for his sin, he is punished in kind and given to be trampled. Alternatively, קַו-קָו is an expression of vomit (קִיא) (Lam. 3:45): “Loathsome and rejected.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 18:2:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:2:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:2:4)


**נְהָרִים.** מוֹשְׁלֵי כּוּשׁ וְנוֹף:


**river** [figurative for] kings.



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Isaiah 18:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:3:1)


**כָּל יֹשְׁבֵי תֵבֵל וְגוֹ׳.** אֵינְכֶם צְרִיכִים לִשְׁלוֹחַ צִירִים עַל כָּךְ, כִּי **כִּנְשֹׂא נֵס הָרִים תִּרְאוּ** בְּהִקָּבֵץ הַגָּלֻיּוֹת, **וְכִתְקוֹעַ שׁוֹפָר תִּשְׁמָעוּ**:


**All inhabitants of the world, etc.** You need not send messengers for this, for when a standard of the mountains is raised, you shall see the ingathering of the exiles, and when a shofar is sounded you shall hear.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Isaiah 18:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:4:1)


**אֶשְׁקֳטָה.** מִתַּשְׁלוּם שְׂכָרוֹ שֶׁל גּוֹג, אֶפָּנֶה מִכָּל עֲסָקַי **וְאַבִּיטָה בִמְכוֹנִי** לְהֵיטִיב לוֹ:


**I will rest** from paying Esau his just deserts; I will turn away from all My affairs and I will look down upon My dwelling-place to do good to it.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 18:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:4:2)


**כְּחֹם צַח עֲלֵי אוֹר.** יָאִיר וְיַבְהִיק לוֹ כְּחֹם הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ צַח עַל יָרָק, כְּמוֹ ״לְלַקֵּט אֹרֹת״ (מלכים ב ד:לט):


**like a clear heat upon herbs** It will illuminate it and cause to shine like the clear heat of the sun on herbs. Comp. (II Kings 4:39) “To gather herbs (אוֹרוֹת) .”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 18:4:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:4:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:4:3)


**כְּעָב טַל.** שֶׁהַקּוֹצְרִים מִתְאַוִּים לוֹ לְהָשִׁיב נֶפֶשׁ בְּחֹם קָצִיר:


**like a cloud of dew** for which the reapers long, to refresh themselves during the heat of the harvest.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Isaiah 18:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:5:1)


**כִּי לִפְנֵי.** בִּשּׁוּל קְצִירוֹ שֶׁל עֲמָלֵק וְשֶׁל גּוֹג, טֶרֶם תִּמָּלֵא תַּאֲוָתוֹ וּסְבָרוֹ שֶׁהוּא זוֹמֵם לְכַלּוֹת אֶת אֶחָיו:


**For before** the ripening of the harvest of Amalek and of Gog, when he has not yet filled his desire and his hope, that he plans to destroy his brothers.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 18:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:5:2)


**כְּתָם פֶּרַח.** שֶׁלּוֹ, וְיִקְרַב לְהִתְבַּשֵּׁל תְּבוּאָה בִּמְלִילוֹתֶיהָ, וְלִהְיוֹת פַּגֵּי נִצָּה שֶׁל גַּפְנָהּ בֹּסֶר וְגוֹמֵל, נִגְמָל לִהְיוֹת גַּסִּים כְּפוֹל הַלָּבָן (ברכות לו ב), הוּא בֹּסֶר הוּא גֵּרוּעַ:


**when the blossom is past** i.e., when its blossom is past and the grain is close to becoming ripe in its ears and before the buds of his vine become ripening grapes, ripened to the extent of being בֹּסֶר, i.e., when the grapes become as big as a white bean. This is called בֹּסֶר and also גֵּרוּעַ.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 18:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:5:3)


**וְכָרַת.** הַכּוֹרֵת אֶת זַלְזַלֵּי הַגֶּפֶן, הֵם הַזְּמוֹרוֹת וְהַשָּׂרִיגִים:


**and he shall cut off** i.e., the cutter shall cut off the tendrils; these are the branches and the boughs.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 18:5:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:5:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:5:4)


**בַּמַּזְמֵרוֹת.** שרפ״ש בלע״ז:


**with pruning hooks** sarpes in O.F. [serpes in Modern French].


###### Rashi on Isaiah 18:5:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:5:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:5:5)


**וְאֶת הַנְּטִישׁוֹת.** הֵם עִקְּרֵי הַגְּפָנִים שֶׁקּוֹרִין ציפ״ש בלע״ז:


**and the roots** These are the roots of the vines, called ceps in O.F.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 18:5:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:5:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:5:6)


**הֵתַז.** כָּרַת וְקִצֵּץ, כְּלוֹמַר: יַהֲרֹג הַשָּׂרִים וְהַשַּׁלִּיטִים שֶׁל גּוֹג וַחֲיָלוֹתָיו וְעוֹזְרָיו:


**he cut [them] off** Heb. הֵתַּז. i.e., to say that He shall slay the officers and the rulers of Esau and of Gog and his armies and his allies.



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Isaiah 18:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:6:1)


**יֵעָזְבוּ יַחְדָּו.** פִּגְרֵיהֶם:


**They shall be left** [i.e.,] their corpses.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 18:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:6:2)


**לְעֵיט הָרִים.** לְעוֹף הָרִים:


**to the birds of the mountains** Heb. לְעֵיט הָרִים, to the birds of the mountains.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 18:6:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:6:3)


**וְקָץ עָלָיו.** כָּל יְמוֹת הַקַּיִץ:


**shall spend the summer upon them** All the days of the summer.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 18:6:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:6:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/18:6:4)


**תֶּחֱרָף.** כָּל יְמוֹת הַחֹרֶף. מִכָּאן אָמְרוּ: מִשְׁפַּט גּוֹג לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ (סדר עולם רבה ג):


**shall spend the winter** All the days of the winter. From there they deduced that the judgment of Gog in the future shall be twelve months.



## Chapter 19


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:1:1)


**רֹכֵב עַל עָב קַל.** מְהֵרָה לִשְׁלֹחַ קַל מְהֵרָה גְּזֵרַת דְּבָרוֹ לִפָּרַע מִמִּצְרַיִם:


**is riding on a light cloud** quickly to send easily and quickly the decree of His word to punish Egypt.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:1:2)


**וְנָעוּ אֱלִילֵי מִצְרַיִם מִפָּנָיו.** לֹא יִהְיֶה לָהֶם כֹּחַ לְהַצִּיל אֶת עַמָּם מִיַּד שְׁלוּחָיו שֶׁל אַשּׁוּר. וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר הַנָּבִיא פֻּרְעָנוּת מִצְרַיִם בַּלָּשׁוֹן הַזֶּה, מַה שֶׁלֹּא אָמַר בַּלָּשׁוֹן הַזֶּה לִשְׁאָר אֻמּוֹת, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵם לְמוּדִים לִלְקוֹת בַּמִּדָּה הַזֹּאת: ״וְעָבַרְתִּי בְאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם״ (שמות יב:יב), ״וּבְכָל אֱלֹהֵי מִצְרַיִם״ (שם), וְדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ מְיָרְאִין אֶת הָאָדָם בְּמַכָּה שֶׁכְּבָר לָקָה בָּהּ:


**and the idols of Egypt shall quake from before Him** They will have no power to save their people from the messengers of the king of Assyria. The prophet presented the retribution of Egypt in this manner, unlike the way he presented it to other nations, because they are accustomed to being punished in this manner. (Exodus 12:12) “And I will pass through the land of Egypt...and upon all the gods of Egypt [will I execute punishment],” and it is customary to frighten a person with a misfortune from which he has already suffered.



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:2:1)


**וְסִכְסַכְתִּי מִצְרַיִם בְּמִצְרַיִם.** סוֹפוֹ מְפָרֵשׁ אֶת תְּחִלָּתוֹ: **וְנִלְחֲמוּ אִישׁ בְּאָחִיו**:


**And I will stir up Egyptians against Egyptians** The end of the verse explains its beginning: And they shall war one man against his brother.



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:3:1)


**וְנָבְקָה רוּחַ.** תִּתְרוֹקֵן חָכְמָתוֹ, כְּמוֹ ״בּוֹקֵק הָאָרֶץ״ (ישעיהו כד:א):


**And the spirit of Egypt shall empty out** Heb. וְנָבְקָה. His wisdom shall be emptied out. Comp. (infra 24:1) “Empties out (בּוֹקֵק) the land.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:3:2)


**הָאִטִּים.** אֶחָד מִן הַשֵּׁמוֹת שֶׁל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה:


**sorcerers** Heb. הָאִטִּים, one of the names of the idols.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:4:1)


**וְסִכַּרְתִּי.** כְּמוֹ ׳וְסָגַרְתִּי׳; וְיֵשׁ עוֹד לְפָרֵשׁ לְשׁוֹן ״וַיִּסָּכְרוּ מַעְיְנוֹת תְּהוֹם״ (בראשית ח:), אֶסְתְּמֶנּוּ וְאֶחְבְּשֶׁנּוּ:


**And I will deliver** וְסִכַּרְתִּי, And I will deliver. Alternatively, it can be interpreted as an expression like (Gen. 8:2): “And the fountains of the deep were stopped up (וַיִּסָּכְרוּ).” I will stop him up and bind him.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:4:2)


**בְּיַד אֲדֹנִים קָשֶׁה.** כָּל לְשׁוֹן אַדְנוּת קָרוּי בִּלְשׁוֹן רַבִּים, וַאֲפִלּוּ יָחִיד, כְּמוֹ ״אֲדֹנֵי יוֹסֵף״ (בראשית לט:), ״עַד בֹּא אֲדֹנָיו״ (בראשית לט:ז):


**into the hands of a harsh master** Heb. אֲדֹנִים קָשֶׁה. Any expression of lordship is used in the plural, even for a singular. Comp. (ibid. 39:20) “Joseph’s master (אֲדֹנֵי)”; (ibid. 16) “Until his master (אֲדֹנָיו) came.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:4:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:4:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:4:3)


**וּמֶלֶךְ עַז.** מֶלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר:


**and a mighty king** The king of Assyria.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:5:1)


**וְנִשְּׁתוּ מַיִם מֵהַיָּם.** וְנֶחְרְבוּ מַיִם מִן הַיָּם:


**And water from the sea shall dry up**


###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:5:2)


**וְנִשְּׁתוּ.** לְשׁוֹן ״הַשְּׁאֵת וְהַשֶּׁבֶר״ (איכה ג:מז). לְפִי שֶׁכָּל שֶׁבַח אֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם עַל יְדֵי נִילוּס הוּא, שֶׁאֵין גְּשָׁמִים יוֹרְדִים שָׁם, אֶלָּא נִילוּס עוֹלֶה וּמַשְׁקֶה אוֹתָהּ דֶּרֶךְ יְאוֹרִים הָעֲשׂוּיִים בִּידֵי אָדָם, לְפִיכָךְ הוּא מְדַמֶּה פֻּרְעָנוּת שֶׁלָּהּ לְיֹבֶשׁ יְאוֹרִים:


Heb. וְנִשְּׁתוּ, an expression like (Lam. 3:47): “The desolation (הַשְׁאֵת) and the breach.” Since the entire productivity of Egypt is due to the Nile, since no rain falls there, but the Nile rises and waters it through its man made canals, he, therefore, compares its retribution to the drying up of canals. [Some manuscripts read:] Rivers and canals.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:5:3)


**וְנִשְּׁתוּ מַיִם מֵהַיָּם.** וְלֹא יַחֲזִיר הַיָּם אֶת נִילוּס לַאֲחוֹרָיו, וְיֵרֵד נִילוּס לְתוֹכוֹ וְלֹא יַעֲלֶה וְיַשְׁקֶה אֶת מִצְרַיִם:


**And water from the sea shall dry up** And the sea shall not return the Nile to its source, but the Nile will descend into it and will not ascend to water Egypt.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:5:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:5:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:5:4)


**וְנָהָר.** זֶה נִילוּס:


**and the river** This is the Nile.



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:6:1)


**וְהֶאֶזְנִיחוּ.** כְּשֶׁהַמַּיִם מִתְמַעֲטִין, הַטִּיט נִכָּר בָּהֶם, וְנַעֲשִׂין רֶפֶשׁ וְנִזְנָחִין:


**And they shall abandon** When the water decreases, the mud is noticeable in it, and it becomes a mire and is abandoned.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:6:2)


**דָּלֲלוּ.** בְּמַחְבֶּרֶת ״אִם דַּל הוּא״ (ויקרא יד:כא):


###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:6:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:6:3)


**יְאֹרֵי מָצוֹר.** יְאוֹרִים עֲמֻקִּים בַּחֲרִיצֵי מְצוֹרֵי עֲיָרוֹת:


**the deep canals** Heb. יְאֹרֵי מָצוֹר. The deep canals, like the ditches of the sieges of cities. [Rashi according to Parshandatha. Printed editions read:] In the ditches of the sieges of cities.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:6:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:6:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:6:4)


**קָנֶה וָסוּף**, שֶׁהָיוּ גְּדֵלִים שָׁם מֵרֹב מֵימֵיהֶם:


**reeds and rushes** that grew there because of their abundant water.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:6:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:6:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:6:5)


**קָמֵלוּ.** כְּשֶׁיָּבְשׁוּ הַיְאוֹרִים, עָמְדוּ הַקָּנִים מִלִּגְדּוֹל עוֹד, וְהֵם מִתְיַבְּשִׁים וְנוֹפְלִים. תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן קָמֵלוּ: ״לָא יִסְקוּן״, וּבְמָקוֹם אַחֵר תִּרְגֵּם ״הֶחְפִּיר לְבָנוֹן קָמַל״ (ישעיהו לג:ט): ״נְתַר״. וְאוֹמֵר אֲנִי, שֶׁהוּא לְשׁוֹן ׳קְצִיצָה׳, שֶׁנִּקְצָצִים מֵאֲלֵיהֶן מֵחֲמַת יוֹבְשָׁן וְנוֹפְלִין:


**shall be cut off** When the canals dry up, the reeds stop growing, and they dry up and fall. Jonathan renders: Shall not come up. Elsewhere (infra 33:9), he renders: “The Lebanon was dried up, cut off (קָמַל),” as ‘fell.’ I say, however, that it is an expression of cutting off, that they are cut off by themselves because of their dryness, and they fall.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:7:1)


**עָרוֹת עַל יְאוֹר עַל פִּי יְאוֹר, וְכָל מִזְרַע יְאוֹר וגו׳. עָרוֹת** – לְשׁוֹן דָּבָר הַמְעוֹרֶה וְנִשְׁרָשׁ יָפֶה יָפֶה, וְדוֹמֶה לוֹ (תהלים לז:לה) ״רָשָׁע עָרִיץ וּמִתְעָרֶה כְּאֶזְרָח רַעֲנָן״, וְכֵן חִבְּרוֹ מְנַחֵם בְּמַחְבַּרְתּוֹ. זְרָעִים הַנִּשְׁרָשִׁים עַל נִילוּס, וַאֲפִלּוּ עַל פִּי שְׂפָתוֹ, וְכָל הַנִּזְרָעִים עָלָיו הַכֹּל **יָבֵשׁ וְנִדָּף**:


**The well-rooted plants by the stream, by the brink of the stream** Heb. עָרוֹת, an expression denoting something rooted very well. Comp. (Psalms 37:35) “The wicked, terrible in power, striking roots (מִתְעָרֶה) like a green tree in its native soil.” Menachem, too, equated it in this manner in his lexicon. [Menachem, however, explains both terms as an expression of growing and of freshness.] Seeds, well-rooted by the Nile, and even on its brink, and all those planted thereby, everything shall dry up and be driven away.



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:8:1)


**וְאָנוּ.** לְשׁוֹן אוֹנִי וָאֵבֶל:


**And...shall lament** Heb. וְאָנוּ, an expression of lamentation and mourning.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:8:2)


**הַדַּיָּגִים.** הֵם מִצְרַיִם, שֶׁצָּדִין דָּגִים מִנִּילוּס, שֶׁהוּא מִתְפַּשֵּׁט וְעוֹלֶה בִּיאוֹרִים רַבִּים הָעֲשׂוּיִין עַל שְׂפָתוֹ עַל פְּנֵי אֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם כֻּלָּהּ, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּכָל הַנְּהָרוֹת:


**the fishermen** They are the Egyptians who catch fish from the Nile, which spreads and goes up into many canals made on its banks over the surface of all the land of Egypt, unlike other rivers.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:8:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:8:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:8:3)


**חַכָּה.** אמ״ו בלע״ז:


**fishhooks** ajjm in O.F.



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:9:1)


**עֹבְדֵי פִשְׁתִּים.** זוֹרְעֵי פִּשְׁתִּים עַל הַנָּהָר:


**Those who work at flax** Who sow flax by the river.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:9:2)


**שְׂרִיקוֹת.** פִּשְׁתִּים שֶׁסּוֹרְקִין אוֹתָן, וְאוֹרְגִין מֵהֶם מְצוּדוֹת דָּגִים, שֶׁהֵן עֲשׂוּיוֹת חוֹרִין חוֹרִין:


**to be combed** Flax that they comb and from which they weave fish nets, which are made with many holes.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:9:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:9:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:9:3)


**חוֹרָי.** כְּמוֹ ״בַּהֲמוֹת שָׂדָי״ (תהלים ח:ח), ״וְקָרַע לוֹ חַלּוֹנָי״ (ירמיהו כב:יד):


**nets** [lit. holes.] Since the suffix is irregular, ordinarily חוֹרִים Rashi enumerates similar instances e.g.,] (Psalms 8:5) “The beasts of the field (שָׂדָי)”; (Jer. 22:14) “And he will cut out for himself windows (חַלּוֹנָי).”



### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:10:1)


**וְהָיוּ שָׁתֹתֶיהָ מְדֻכָּאִים כָּל עֹשֵׂי שֶׂכֶר.** אישקלוש״א בלע״ז, כְּמוֹ (בראשית ח:ב) ״וַיִּסָּכְרוּ מַעַיְנוֹת תְּהוֹם״, שֶׁסּוֹכְרִים הַמַּיִם הַיּוֹצְאִין חוּץ לִשְׂפַת הַנָּהָר וּמִתְפַּשְּׁטִים, וְנַעֲשִׂים אֲגַם מַיִם הַנִּקְוִים וְעוֹמְדִין בִּמְקוֹמָן, וְרָבִים שָׁם דָּגִים. וְאָמַר הַנָּבִיא שֶׁיִּהְיוּ יְסוֹדוֹת חֲפִירוֹתֵיהֶן מְדֻכָּאִים, וְיִפְּלוּ אַגְמֵי הַשֶּׂכֶר שֶׁעָשׂוּ:


**And its foundations shall be crushed, all who make dams** Eklusa in O.F., a sluice. Comp. (Gen. 8:2) “And the fountains of the deep were stopped up (וַיִּסָּכְרוּ),” for they would stop up the water that went out of the banks of the river and spread out, forming a pond of still water, standing in its place, where fish would spawn. The prophet says that the foundations of their diggings shall be crushed, and the dammed up pools that they made.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:10:2)


**אַגְמֵי נָפֶשׁ.** אַגְמֵי שֶׁבֶת לָשׁוֹן ״שָׁבַת וַיִּנָּפַשׁ״ (שמות לא:יז), שֶׁמֵּי הָאֲגַמִּים נוֹחִים וְעוֹמְדִים בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד. וְיוֹנָתָן תִּרְגֵּם: ״דַּהֲווֹ עָבְדִין סוּכְרָא וְכָנְשִׁין מַיָּא, גְּבַר לְנַפְשֵׁיהּ״:


**still ponds** An expression like (Ex. 31:17): “He rested and was refreshed (וַיִּנָּפַשׁ),” for the water of the ponds rests and stands in one place. Jonathan, however, renders: Who would make the dams and gather the water, each one for himself.



### Verse 11

###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:11:1)


**אֵיךְ תֹּאמְרוּ** מֵעַתָּה לְפַרְעֹה, כָּל אִישׁ מִכֶּם עַל עַצְמוֹ ״בֶּן חֲכָמִים אֲנִי״, וּמֵאַחַר שֶׁיִּכָּשֵׁל בַּעֲצַתְכֶם, אֵיךְ תִּתְהַלְּלוּ לְפָנָיו לֵאמֹר בְּנֵי חֲכָמִים אֲנַחְנוּ, אַתָּה בֶּן מַלְכֵי קֶדֶם:


**How will you say** from now on to Pharaoh, each one of you about himself, I am a son of the wise? Since he will fail because of your counsel, how will you boast before him to say, We are sons of the wise, O you who are a son of the kings of old.



### Verse 13

###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:13:1)


**נוֹאֲלוּ.** לְשׁוֹן אֱוִילִים:


**have become foolish** Heb. נוֹאֲלוּ, an expression related to אֱלִילִים, fools.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:13:2)


**נִשְּׁאוּ.** כְּמוֹ ״הַנָּחָשׁ הִשִּׁיאַנִי״ (בראשית ג:יג):


**have been misled** Heb. נָשְּׁאוּ, have been misled. Comp. (Gen. 3:13) “The snake misled me (הִשִּׁיאַנִּי) and I ate.”



### Verse 14

###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:14:1)


**מָסַךְ בְּקִרְבָּהּ.** מַשְׁקֶה מָזַג לָהֶם בְּתוֹכָהּ, שֶׁעִוָּה אֶת רוּחָם. לְשׁוֹן ״מָסְכָה יֵינָהּ״ (משלי ט:ב). עֵרוּב מַשְׁקֶה בְּחָבִית עַד שֶׁמַּעֲמִידוֹ בְּטַעְמוֹ קָרוּי מֶסֶךְ:


**The Lord has poured into its midst** He mixed a drink for them in its midst, which perverted their spirit, an expression similar to (Prov. 9:2), “She mixed (מָסְכָה) her wine.” Mixing a beverage in a cask until he blends it to its proper flavor is called מֶסֶךְ.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:14:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:14:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:14:2)


**עִוְעִים.** שֵׁם חֹלִי שֶׁל טֵרוּף הַדַּעַת:


**perverseness** Heb. עִוְעִים, the name of a malady of confusion.



### Verse 15

###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:15:1)


**אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה רֹאשׁ וְזָנָב כִּפָּה וְאַגְמוֹן.** הֵם הַחַרְטוּמִים וְאִצְטַגְנִינִים הַחוֹזִים בַּכּוֹכָבִים, שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּרָקִיעַ מַזָּלוֹת וְכוֹכָבִים הַמְכֻנִּים כֵּן וַעֲשׂוּיִין דֻּגְמַת רֹאשׁ וְזָנָב, וְהֵם נְתוּנִים בִּתְלִי (ספרים אחרים: בְּטָלֶה). וְיֵשׁ לְפָרֵשׁ כְּתַרְגּוּמוֹ: ״רֹאשׁ וְהֶגְמוֹן, שִׁלְטוֹן וְאַטְרוֹן״:


**that either the head or the tail, the branch or the reed shall do** These are the sorcerers and the astrologers who see in the stars that in the sky are heavenly bodies called by these names, formed in the pattern of a head and a tail, and they are placed in Aries. [Other editions read:] In Draco. Alternatively, it can be interpreted like the Targum: a head and a lower dignitary, a prince and a governor.



### Verse 17

###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:17:1)


**וְהָיְתָה אַדְמַת יְהוּדָה לְמִצְרַיִם לְחָגָּא.** כְּשֶׁיִּשְׁמְעוּ הַנּוֹתָרִים בְּמִצְרַיִם מִשְּׁבִי סַנְחֵרִיב אֶת מַפַּלְתּוֹ, שֶׁיִּפּוֹל בְּאֶרֶץ יְהוּדָה בְּלֹא שׁוּם מִלְחֲמוֹת זְרוֹעַ בָּשָׂר, יֵדְעוּ כִּי יֵשׁ שְׁכִינָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וּמוֹשִׁיעָם חָזָק, וְיִירָאוּ וְיִפְחֲדוּ מִפְּנֵי אַדְמַת יְהוּדָה:


**And the land of Judah shall be to Egypt for a dread** When those remaining in Egypt from the captivity of Sennacherib hear of his downfall, that he will fall in the land of Judah without any physical warfare, they will know that the Divine Presence is manifest in Israel and that their Savior is mighty, and they will fear and be frightened of the land of Judah.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:17:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:17:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:17:2)


**חָגָּא.** לְשׁוֹן שֶׁבֶר, וְאֵימָה וָפַחַד, לְשׁוֹן ״יָחוֹגּוּ וְיָנוּעוּ כַּשִּׁכּוֹר״ (תהלים קז:כז), וְכֵן ״חַגְוֵי הַסֶּלַע״ (שיר השירים ב:יד):


**a dread** Heb. לְחָגָּא, an expression of a breach and fear and fright, similar to (Psalms 107:27): “They were frightened (יָחוֹגוּ) and wander like a drunkard,” similarly (Song 2:14), “In the cracks of (בְּחַגְוֵי) the rock.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:17:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:17:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:17:3)


**מִפְּנֵי עֲצַת ה׳ צְבָאוֹת אֲשֶׁר הוּא יוֹעֵץ עָלָיו.** לְהַפִּילוֹ בְּיַד סַנְחֵרִיב, וִיהוּדָה יִמָּלֵט מִיָּדוֹ:


**because of the plan of the Lord of Hosts which he planned against him** to cause him to fall into the hands of Sennacherib, and Judah will escape from his hand.



### Verse 18

###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:18:1)


**בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא יִהְיוּ חָמֵשׁ עָרִים וְגוֹ׳.** שָׁנִינוּ בְּסֵדֶר עוֹלָם (סדר עולם רבה כג): אַחַר מַפַּלְתּוֹ שֶׁל סַנְחֵרִיב עָמַד חִזְקִיָּהוּ וּפָטַר אֶת הָאֻכְלוֹסִין שֶׁהֵבִיא עִמּוֹ מִמִּצְרַיִם וּמִכּוּשׁ בְּקוֹלָרִין לִפְנֵי יְרוּשָׁלַיִם, וְקִבְּלוּ עֲלֵיהֶם מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם, וְחָזְרוּ לִמְקוֹמָן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: **בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא יִהְיוּ חָמֵשׁ עָרִים וְגוֹ׳**. וְהָלְכוּ וּבָנוּ מִזְבֵּחַ לַה׳ בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם, וּמַקְרִיבִין עָלָיו קָרְבָּן לַשָּׁמַיִם, לְקַיֵּם מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: **בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא יִהְיֶה מִזְבֵּחַ לַה׳ בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם**. וְיֵשׁ מֵרַבּוֹתֵינוּ שֶׁדְּרָשׁוּהוּ בְּמַסֶּכֶת מְנָחוֹת (מנחות קט ב) עַל מִזְבַּח בֵּית חוֹנְיוֹ, בְּנוֹ שֶׁל שִׁמְעוֹן הַצַּדִּיק, שֶׁבָּרַח לוֹ לְמִצְרַיִם וְעָשָׂה שָׁם מִזְבֵּחַ:


**On that day there shall be five cities, etc.** We learned in Seder Olam (ch. 23): Following Sennacherib’s defeat, Hezekiah stood up and released the armies he had brought with him from Egypt and from Cush in chains before Jerusalem, and they imposed upon themselves the kingdom of heaven, and returned to their place, and it is said: “On that day there shall be five cities, etc.” They went and built an altar to the Lord in the land of Egypt and they would sacrifice on it to heaven, to fulfill what was said: On that day there shall be an altar to the Lord in the land of Egypt. Some of our Sages expounded it in the tractate Menahoth (109b) as referring to the altar of the temple of Onias the son of Simon the Just, who fled to Egypt and built an altar there.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:18:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:18:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:18:2)


**מְדַבְּרוֹת שְׂפַת כְּנַעַן.** כְּיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבְּאֶרֶץ כְּנַעַן:


**speaking the language of Canaan** like the Israelites in the land of Canaan.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:18:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:18:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:18:3)


**עִיר הַהֶרֶס יֵאָמֵר לְאֶחָת.** תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״קַרְתָּא דְבֵית שֶׁמֶשׁ דַּעֲתִידָא לְמֵיחֱרַב יִתְאַמַּר הִיא חֲדָא מִנְּהוֹן״. הַהֶרֶס תִּרְגְּמוֹ יוֹנָתָן לִשְׁנֵי פָנִים: לְשׁוֹן ״הָאֹמֵר לַחֶרֶס וְלֹא יִזְרָח״ (איוב ט:ז), וּלְשׁוֹן הֲרִיסָה וְחֻרְבָּן. וּמֵהֵיכָן לְמָדָהּ יוֹנָתָן? מִנְּבוּאָתוֹ שֶׁל יִרְמְיָה שֶׁנִּבָּא בְּתַחְפַּנְחֵס: ״וְשִׁבַּר אֶת מַצְּבוֹת בֵּית שֶׁמֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם״ (ירמיהו מג:יג). לָמַדְנוּ שֶׁבֵּית שֶׁמֶשׁ שֶׁבְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם וּמַצֵּבָה עֲתִידָה לֵחָרֵב, וּמַצֵּבוֹת הָאֲמוּרוֹת שָׁם הִיא מַצֵּבָה אֵצֶל גְּבוּלָהּ לַה׳ הָאֲמוּרָה כָּאן. וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר שֶׁהָיְתָה בֵּית שֶׁמֶשׁ יוֹשֶׁבֶת בִּגְבוּל מִצְרַיִם עַל הַסְּפָר, לְכָךְ נֶאֱמַר אֵצְלָהּ גְּבוּלָהּ:


**one of which will be called “the city of Heres.”** Jonathan paraphrases: The city of Beth-shemesh which is destined to be destroyed will be said to be one of them. Jonathan renders “Heres” in two ways: an expression related to (Job 9:7) “Who says to the sun (לַחֶרֶס) and it will not shine,” [הֶרֶס and חֶרֶס being interchangeable since ‘heh’ and ‘heth’ are both gutterals,] and an expression of demolition and destruction. (Some editions add:) And whence did Jonathan derive this? From Jeremiah’s prophecy, which he prophesied in Tahpanhes (43:13): “He shall also break the monuments of Beth shemesh which is in the land of Egypt.” We learn from here that Beth-shemesh that was in the land of Egypt [and the monument] was destined to be destroyed, and the monuments mentioned there are identical with “the monument beside its border, to the Lord,” mentioned here, and it may be said that Beth-shemesh was situated in the border of Egypt on the boundary. Therefore it is stated: Beside its border.

**וְהָיָה.** הַמִּזְבֵּחַ לְאוֹת וּלְעֵד בֵּינָם וּבֵין הַמָּקוֹם:

###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:21:1

**וְנוֹדַע ה׳.** יִהְיֶה כֹּחַ גְּבוּרָתוֹ נִכָּר לָהֶם:

**נָגֹף וְרָפוֹא.** וְאַחַר הַמַּכָּה יָבִיא לָהֶם רְפוּאָה:

**תִּהְיֶה מְסִלָּה.** תִּהְיֶה דֶּרֶךְ כְּבוּשָׁה שֶׁיֵּלְכוּ בָּהּ תָּמִיד **מִמִּצְרַיִם** לְאַשּׁוּר:

**וּבָא אַשּׁוּר בְּמִצְרַיִם.** תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״וְיִגִיחוּן אֲתוּרָאֵי לְמִצְרָאֵי״:

### Verse 24

###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:24:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:24:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:24:1)


**יִהְיֶה יִשְׂרָאֵל שְׁלִישִׁיָּה לְמִצְרַיִם וּלְאַשּׁוּר.** לְשָׁלוֹם וְלִבְרָכָה, לְפִי שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה אֻמָּה חֲשׁוּבָה בָּעוֹלָם בְּאוֹתוֹ הַזְּמַן כְּמִצְרַיִם וּכְאַשּׁוּר, וְיִשְׂרָאֵל הָיוּ שְׁפָלִים בִּימֵי אָחָז וּבִימֵי הוֹשֵׁעַ בֶּן אֵלָה, וְאָמַר הַנָּבִיא: עַל יְדֵי הַנֵּס שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה לְחִזְקִיָּהוּ יִגְדַּל שֵׁם שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל לְמַעְלָה וְיִהְיוּ חֲשׁוּבִים כְּאַחַת מֵאֵלּוּ הַמַּמְלָכוֹת לִבְרָכָה וְלִגְדֻלָּה:


**Israel shall be a third to Egypt and to Assyria** for a blessing, since there was no prominent nation in the world at that time like Egypt and like Assyria, and the Jews were humble in the days of Ahaz and in the days of Hoshea the son of Elah. And the prophet states that, through the miracle that will be performed for Hezekiah, Israel’s name will be greatly magnified, and they will be as prominent as one of these kingdoms in regards to blessing and greatness.



### Verse 25

###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:25:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:25:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:25:1)


**אֲשֶׁר בֵּרֲכוֹ.** לְיִשְׂרָאֵל:


**Which...blessed them** [lit. him,] i.e., Israel.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:25:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:25:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:25:2)


**בָּרוּךְ עַמִּי.** יִשְׂרָאֵל, אֲשֶׁר בָּחַרְתִּי לִי לְעָם בִּהְיוֹתָם בְּמִצְרָיִם:


**Blessed is My people** Israel, whom I chose for Myself as a people when they were in Egypt.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 19:25:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:25:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/19:25:3)


**וּמַעֲשֵׂה יָדַי** הֶרְאֵיתִי לָהֶם בִּגְבוּרוֹת שֶׁהִפְלֵאתִי בְּאַשּׁוּר, וְעַל יְדֵי אוֹתָם נִסִּים יָשׁוּבוּ אֵלַי וְיִהְיוּ כְּאִלּוּ עַתָּה עֲשִׂיתִים מֵחָדָשׁ, וְהֵם יִהְיוּ **נַחֲלָתִי יִשְׂרָאֵל**, וְדֻגְמָא זוֹ תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן:


**and the work of My hands** I showed them with the mighty deeds I performed wondrously against Assyria, and through those miracles they will repent and be as though I just made them anew, and they will be My heritage, Israel. Jonathan paraphrased this in a similar manner.



## Chapter 20


### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Isaiah 20:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/20:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/20:2:1)


**וּפִתַּחְתָּ הַשַּׂק מֵעַל מָתְנֶיךָ.** תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״וְתֵיסַר סַקָּא בְּחַרְצָךְ״, וְהַדְּבָרִים מוֹכִיחִים, שֶׁהֲרֵי עַד עַכְשָׁיו לֹא צִוָּהוּ לַחֲגוֹר שַׂק שֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר לוֹ לְהַתִּירָהּ. וְעוֹד: שֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר **וְנַעַלְךָ תַּחֲלֹץ**, וְהוּא סִימָן לַאֲבֵלוּת. וּפֵירוּשׁ **וּפִתַּחְתָּ** כְּמוֹ ״מְפֻתָּחוֹת פִּתּוּחֵי חוֹתָם״ (שמות לט:ו), לַחֲגוֹר שַׂק בְּדֹחַק עַל בְּשָׂרוֹ, כְּדֵי שֶׁתֵּרָאֶה חֲקוּקָה בִּבְשָׂרוֹ:


**and you shall gird sackcloth over your loins** (וּפִתַּחְתָּ) Jonathan renders: “And you shall gird the sackcloth over your loins.” And his interpretation is evidenced by the fact that until now, He had not commanded him to gird himself with sackcloth, that He should tell him to remove it. Moreover, when He tells him, “And you shall remove your shoes from upon your feet,” this is a sign of mourning. (It is, therefore, likely that He commanded him to gird himself with sackcloth, also a sign of mourning.) And the meaning of וּפִתַּחְתָּ is like: (Exodus 39:6) “Engraved like the engravings of a seal (מְפֻתָּחוֹת פִּתּוּחֵי חוֹתָם),” to gird himself with sackcloth tightly on his flesh, so that it appears to be engraved in his flesh.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 20:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/20:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/20:2:2)


**מֵעַל מָתְנֶיךָ.** לְמַעְלָה מִמָּתְנֶיךָ:


**over your loins** above your loins.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 20:2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/20:2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/20:2:3)


**עָרוֹם.** תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״פְּחִיחַ״, בִּבְגָדִים קְרוּעִים וּבְלוּאִים, וְלֹא עָרֹם מַמָּשׁ:


**naked** (עָרוֹם). Jonathan renders: פְּחֵיחַ, with torn and worn out clothing, but not actually naked.



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Isaiah 20:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/20:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/20:3:1)


**שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים.** יֵלֵךְ כֵּן לְאוֹת וּלְמוֹפֵת לְמִצְרַיִם וּלְכוּשׁ, שֶׁלְּסוֹף שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים ״יִנְהַג מֶלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר אֶת שְׁבִי מִצְרַיִם וְגוֹ׳״ (ישעיה כ:ד). לָמַדְנוּ שֶׁכָּבַשׁ תַּרְתָּן אֶת אַשְׁדּוֹד שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים לִפְנֵי מַפַּלְתּוֹ שֶׁל סַנְחֵרִיב, שֶׁהֲרֵי מַפַּלְתּוֹ הָיְתָה כְּשֶׁהֵבִיא אֶת שְׁבִי מִצְרַיִם וְתִרְהָקָה מֶלֶךְ כּוּשׁ לִפְנֵי יְרוּשָׁלַיִם בְּקוֹלָרִין, כְּשֶׁבָּא לָצוּר עַל חִזְקִיָּהוּ:


**three years** shall he go in this manner as a sign and a symbol for Egypt and for Cush, that, at the end of three years the king of Assyria shall lead the captivity of Egypt... We learn that Tartan conquered Ashdod three years prior to the downfall of Sennacherib, for his downfall was when he brought the captives of Egypt and Tirhakah the king of Cush before Jerusalem in chains, when he came to besiege Hezekiah.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Isaiah 20:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/20:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/20:4:1)


**וַחֲשׂוּפַי שֵׁת.** כְּמוֹ ׳חֲשׂוּף שֵׁת׳, וְהַיּוֹ״ד יְתֵרָה כְּיוֹ״ד ״חַלּוֹנָי״ (ירמיהו כב:יד) וְ״חוֹרָי״ (ישעיהו יט:ט) וְ״שָׂדָי״ (תהלים ח:ח):


**with bare buttocks** (וַחֲשׂוּפַי), like חֲשׂוּף, and the yud is superfluous, like the yud of חַלּוֹנָי (the window), חוֹרָי, (nets), שָׂדָי (the field).


###### Rashi on Isaiah 20:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/20:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/20:4:2)


**שֵׁת.** בֵּית מוֹצָא הָרְעִי, וְכֵן (שמואל ב י:ד): ״וַיִּכְרֹת אֶת מַדְוֵיהֶם עַד שְׁתוֹתֵיהֶם״. וּגְמוּל זֶה הָיָה לָהֶם תַּחַת חָם אֲבִיהֶם, אֲשֶׁר רָאָה עֶרְוַת אָבִיו וְלֹא כִּסָּה אוֹתָהּ, מִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה:


**buttocks** Near the anus. Comp. (II Sam. 10:4): “And he cut off their garments in half, up to their buttocks (שְׁתוֹתֵיהֶם).” This retribution was due them because of Ham their ancestor, who saw his father’s nakedness and did not cover it, payment in kind.

## Chapter 21


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:1:1)


**מַשָּׂא מִדְבַּר יָם.** הַנְּבוּאָה הַזֹּאת עַל בָּבֶל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּפֹרָשׁ בָּהּ. וְאִם תֹּאמַר: הֲרֵי כְּבָר נִבָּא עָלֶיהָ (ישעיהו יג:ב) ״עַל הַר נִשְׁפֶּה שְׂאוּ נֵס״ וְכָל הַפָּרָשָׁה כֻּלָּהּ? פְּעָמִים שֶׁהַנְּבוּאָה בָּאָה בְּפִיו הַיּוֹם בְּסִגְנוֹן אֶחָד וּלְאַחַר זְמַן בְּסִגְנוֹן אַחֵר:


**The harsh prophecy of the western desert** This prophecy refers to Babylonia, as is delineated therein. If you ask, Did he not already prophesy about it (supra 13): “On a tranquil mountain raise a banner,” and the entire chapter? sometimes the prophecy comes into his mouth today in one manner, and later in another manner.

**to pass** So will many camps pass to come upon Babylon.

**from an awesome land** Jonathan renders: From a land where mighty deeds have been performed. It is also possible to explain that it is a place of snakes and scorpions, as it is said (Deut. 8: 15): “The great and awesome desert.”



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:2:1)


**חָזוּת קָשָׁה.** הַנָּבִיא אוֹמֵר: נְבוּאָה זוֹ קָשָׁה עַל בָּבֶל **הֻגַּד לִי**:


**A harsh prophecy** The prophet says, “This harsh prophecy concerning Babylon was told to me.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:2:2)


**הַבּוֹגֵד בּוֹגֵד** תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״אֲנִיסַיָּא מִתְאַנְסִין וּבָזְזַיָּא מִתְבַּזְּזִין״. וְלָשׁוֹן הָעִבְרִית לְפִי הַתַּרְגּוּם כָּךְ פֵּרוּשׁוֹ: אֶת הַבּוֹגֵד בָּא אַחֵר וּבוֹגֵד אוֹתוֹ (ספרים אחרים: אוֹתְךָ), וְאֶת **הַשּׁוֹדֵד** בָּא אַחֵר **וְשׁוֹדֵד** אוֹתוֹ (ספרים אחרים: אוֹתְךָ). אֵלּוּ פָּרַס וּמָדַי שֶׁבּוֹזְזִין וְשׁוֹדְדִין אֶת בָּבֶל, שֶׁשָּׁדְדָה וּבָזְזָה עַד עַתָּה אֶת כָּל הַמְּדִינוֹת:


**the traitor shall be betrayed** Jonathan renders: The robbers are robbed and the plunderers are plundered. The Hebrew wording, according to the Targum, is to be explained thus: The traitor another will come and betray him; and the plunderer another will come and plunder him. These are Persia and Media, who rob and plunder Babylon, who, until now plundered and robbed all the countries.

**עֲלִי עֵילָם.** וּבוֹאִי עָלֶיהָ:


**march, Elam** and come upon them (lit., her).


###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:2:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:2:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:2:4)


**צוּרִי מָדַי.** עַל בָּבֶל בְּמָצוֹר. ״אֱלֹהִי צוּרִי״ (שמואל ב כב:ג) הַטַּעַם לְמַטָּה בָּרֵי״שׁ, וְזֶה טַעֲמוֹ לְמַעְלָה בַּצָּדִ״י, כְּמוֹ ׳שׁוּבִי׳:


**besiege, O Media** (צוּרִי). I.e., besiege Babylon with a siege. Comp. (II Sam. 22:3) “God is my rock (צוּרִי).” The accent is on the latter syllable, on the “resh,” whereas, in this case, the accent is on the first syllable, like “rise (קוּמִי),” “return (שׁוּבִי).”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:2:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:2:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:2:5)


**כָּל אַנְחָתָה הִשְׁבַּתִּי.** לֹא מַפִּיק הֵ״א, לְפִי שֶׁהוּא כְּמוֹ כָּל אֲנָחוֹת שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם, וְהוּא לְשׁוֹן אֲנָחָה מְרֻבָּה שֶׁל אֲנָשִׁים רַבִּים, שושפיר״ש בלע״ז. כָּל אֲנָחוֹת הִשְׁבַּתִּי, שֶׁהָיָה הָעוֹלָם נֶאֱנָח מִפְּנֵי עֻלָּהּ שֶׁל מַלְכוּת בָּבֶל, עַתָּה הִשְׁבַּתִּי אוֹתָהּ:


**all sighs have I brought to an end** (אַנְחָתָה). (This is) not (spelled with a) “Mappiq heh,” (which would mean “her sigh”) for this is like “all sighs in the world,” and it is an expression denoting a great sigh of many people (sospiradic in O.F.). All sighs have I brought to an end, for the world was sighing because of the yoke of the kingdom of Babylon; now I have brought it to an end.



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:3:1)


**מָלְאוּ מָתְנַי חַלְחָלָה.** הַנָּבִיא הוּא רַחֲמָנִי וּמִתְאַנֵּחַ עַל פֻּרְעָנוּת הָאֻמּוֹת; זוֹ מִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה (תנחומא בלק א). וּלְפִי פְּשׁוּטוֹ, הַנָּבִיא אוֹמֵר הַקִּינָה וְהָאֲנִינוּת, כְּאִלּוּ זוֹ בָּבֶל מִתְאוֹנֶנֶת:


**my loins are filled with trembling** The prophet is merciful and sighs over the retribution meted out to the nations. This is the Midrash Aggadah (Tan., beginning of Balak). According to its simple meaning, however, the prophet is reciting the lamentation and the mourning as though this were Babylonia lamenting.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:3:2)


**צִירִים.** לְשׁוֹן חִיל וַחֲבָלִים. רַבּוֹתֵינוּ אָמְרוּ (בכורות מה א; ויקרא רבה יד ד): יֵשׁ דְּלָתוֹת וְצִירִים לָאִשָּׁה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁיֵּשׁ צִירִים לְדַלְתוֹת הַבַּיִת:


**pangs (צִירִים),** an expression denoting trembling and pains. And our Rabbis said: A woman has doors and hinges (צִירִים) on her womb just as the doors of a house have hinges (Bechoroth 45a).


###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:3:3)


**נַעֲוֵיתִי.** חֹלִי הוּא הַקָּרוּי עֲוִית בִּלְשׁוֹן חֲכָמִים:


**I became confused** This is a malady known as עֲוִית, convulsions, in the language of the Sages.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:4:1)


**פַּלָּצוּת.** בֶּהָלָה:


**fright** (פַּלָּצוּת). fright.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:4:2)


**אֵת נֶשֶׁף חִשְׁקִי.** לַיְלָה שֶׁהָיִיתִי חוֹשֵׁק בָּהּ לְשִׂמְחָה וּלְמִשְׁתֶּה. בְּסֵפֶר יוֹסִיפוֹן מָצִינוּ שֶׁהָיָה שָׂמֵחַ עַל שֶׁנָּצְחוּ גְּדוּדָיו אֶת חֵיל פָּרַס. אוֹתוֹ לַיְלָה **שָׂם לִי לַחֲרָדָה**, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דניאל ה:א) ״בֵּלְשַׁאצַּר מַלְכָּא עֲבַד לְחֶם רַב וְגוֹ׳״, ״אִשְׁתִּיו חַמְרָא וְגוֹ׳״, ״בֵּהּ בְּלֵילְיָא קְטִיל וְגוֹ׳״, ״וְדָרְיָוֶשׁ מָדָאָה קַבִּיל מַלְכוּתָא״ (דניאל ו:א):


**the evening of my desire** The night that I longed for, for rejoicing and for a banquet. In the Book of Josipon we find that he was happy since his troops had defeated the army of Persia. (Book 1, ch. 5) That night He made for me into trembling, as it is said (Dan. 5:1): “King Belshazzar made a great feast...They drank wine...(verse 4). On that very night, King Belshazzar was slain...(verse 30).” (6:1) “And Darius the Mede received the kingdom.”



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:5:1)


**צָפֹה הַצָּפִית.** זְקוֹף הַמְּנוֹרָה, בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (סג יד) צָוְוחִין לִמְנַרְתָּא צָפִיתָא:


**setting up the lamp** (הַצָּפִית), Set up the lamp. In Gen. Rabbah (63:14) we learn that people call a lamp צָפִיתָא.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:5:2)


**אָכוֹל שָׁתֹה.** וּמִתּוֹךְ הָאֲכִילָה וְהַשְּׁתִיָּה צָעֲקוּ: **קוּמוּ הַשָּׂרִים**:


**eating, drinking** And in the midst of the eating and the drinking, they cried, “Arise, princes!”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:5:3)


**מָשְׁחוּ מָגֵן.** מָגִנֵּי עוֹר שָׁלוּק הֵן, וּמוֹשְׁחִין אוֹתָן בְּשֶׁמֶן כְּדֵי שֶׁיַּחֲלִיק אֶת הַזַּיִן. וְכָךְ נֶאֱמַר בְּשָׁאוּל (שמואל ב א:כא): ״כִּי שָׁם נִגְעַל מָגֵן גִּבּוֹרִים״, פָּלַט אֶת מְשִׁיחָתוֹ וְלֹא קִבְּלָה, וְנַעֲשָׂה מָגֵן שָׁאוּל כְּאִלּוּ לֹא נִמְשַׁח בְּשֶׁמֶן:


**anoint a shield** They were shields of boiled leather, and they would anoint them with oil so that the weapons would glide off. The same is mentioned concerning Saul (II Sam. 1:21): “For there the shield of the mighty was rejected.” It rejected its anointing and did not absorb it, and Saul’s shield became as though it was not anointed with oil.



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:6:1)


**לֵךְ הַעֲמֵד הַמְצַפֶּה.** עָתִיד אֶחָד מִתַּלְמִידֶיךָ לִקְרֹא תִּגָּר עַל מִדּוֹתַי, עַל אֹרֶךְ שַׁלְוָתָהּ שֶׁל בָּבֶל, וְהוּא חֲבַקּוּק, שֶׁעָג עוּגָה וְעָמַד בְּתוֹכָהּ וְאָמַר (חבקוק ב:א) ״עַל מִשְׁמַרְתִּי אֶעֱמֹדָה וּמְצַפֶּה לִרְאוֹת מַה יְדַבֵּר בִּי״. אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִישַׁעְיָה: הַעֲמִידֵהוּ לְאוֹתוֹ מְצַפֶּה, וְהַבְטִיחֵהוּ מֵאִתִּי שֶׁיַּעֲמֹד עַל מִצְפֵּהוּ, וַ**אֲשֶׁר יִרְאֶה** בְּמַפַּלְתָּהּ שֶׁל בָּבֶל **יַגִּיד**:


**Go set up the lookout** One of your disciples is destined to complain about My attribute, concerning the long prosperity of Babylon, and that was Habakkuk who made a circle and stood inside it, and said (Habakkuk 2:1), “On my watch will I stand, and I will look out to see what He will speak within me.” Said the Holy One, blessed be He, “Put up that lookout and promise him in My Name that he will stand on his watch and what he sees in the downfall of Babylon he will tell.”



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:7:1)


**וְרָאָה רֶכֶב.** וַאֲנִי אַרְאֶנּוּ שָׁם כְּמִין **רֶכֶב צֶמֶד פָּרָשִׁים**, אֶחָד רוֹכֵב **חֲמוֹר** וְאֶחָד רוֹכֵב **גָּמָל**, וְסִימָן הוּא לְפָרַס וּמָדַי:


**And he shall see a chariot** and I will show him there a sort of chariot with a pair of riders, one riding a donkey and one riding a camel, and that is a sign of Persia and Media.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:7:2)


**וְהִקְשִׁיב קֶשֶׁב** וְשָׁם יִשְׁמַע בִּנְבוּאָתוֹ כְּמִין רֹב הוֹמִיּוֹת תְּשׁוּאוֹת חֲיָלוֹת:


**and he shall listen attentively** And there he shall hear in his prophecy a representation of the mighty rumbling and stirring of armies.



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:8:1)


**וַיִּקְרָא אַרְיֵה.** הוּא חֲבַקּוּק, ׳אַרְיֵה׳ בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא כְּמִנְיַן ׳חֲבַקּוּק׳; יְשַׁעְיָה נִתְנַבֵּא שֶׁעָתִיד חֲבַקּוּק לְהִתְפַּלֵּל עַל זֹאת וְלוֹמַר כֵּן:


**And the lion called** That is Habakkuk. אַרְיֵה (lion) has the same numerical value as Habakkuk. Isaiah prophesied that Habakkuk was destined to pray for this and say the following.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:8:2)


**עַל מִצְפֶּה אֲדֹנָי.** ה׳ אֱלֹהַי, עַל מִצְפֶּה **אָנֹכִי עוֹמֵד תָּמִיד יוֹמָם** לְהוֹדִיעֵנִי עַל זֹאת:


**on the watchtower, O Lord** O Lord, my God, I always stand on the watchtower to inform me about this.



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:9:1)


**וְהִנֵּה זֶה בָא.** כְּשֶׁיִּתְפַּלֵּל עַל כָּךְ, יִרְאֶה כְּמִין **רֶכֶב** אָדָם וְגוֹ׳:


**And behold this is coming** When he prays concerning this, he will see sort of a chariot of men, etc.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:9:2)


**נָפְלָה נָפְלָה בָּבֶל.** תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״נָפְלַת וְאַף עֲתִידָה לְמִיפַּל״, שְׁתֵּי נְפִילוֹת שָׁנָה אַחַר שָׁנָה: תְּחִלָּה עַל יְדֵי מָדַי וּפָרַס, וּבַשָּׁנָה הַשְּׁנִיָּה עַל יְדֵי שָׁמַיִם, וְהָיְתָה בָּבֶל צְבִי מַמְלָכוֹת כְּמַהְפֵּכַת סְדוֹם. וְכֵן מָצִינוּ בְּסֵדֶר עוֹלָם (סדר עולם רבה כח): וּבָא בַשָּׁנָה הַשְּׁמוּעָה זוֹ שֶׁל דָּרְיָוֶשׁ, וְאַחֲרָיו בַּשָּׁנָה הַשְּׁמוּעָה ״וְהָיְתָה בָּבֶל צְבִי מַמְלָכוֹת כְּמַהְפֵּכַת וְגוֹ׳״ (ישעיהו יג:יט):


**Babylon has fallen, yea, it has fallen** Jonathan renders: Has fallen and is also destined to fall. This denotes two downfalls in two consecutive years, first through Media and Persia, and in the second year, through Heaven, as it is stated (supra 13:19): “And Babylon, the beauty of the kingdoms, the glory of the pride of the Chaldees, shall be like God’s overturning of Sodom...” And so we find in Seder Olam (ch. 28): And in that year the news came concerning Darius, and after him, in the year, the news, “And Babylon, the beauty of the kingdoms...shall be like the overturning, etc.” (supra 13:19).



### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:10:1)


**מְדֻשָׁתִי וּבֶן גָּרְנִי** תְּבוּאַת קֹדֶשׁ שֶׁלִּי, עֲרֵמַת חִטִּי, אֲשֶׁר נִצְטַוֵּיתִי מִפִּי רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ לְתַקֵּן אֶתְכֶם בְּדֶרֶךְ הַיְשָׁרָה, כְּאָדָם הַדָּשׁ וְזוֹרֶה תְּבוּאָתוֹ בַּגֹּרֶן:


**My threshed grain and the product of my threshing floor** My hallowed grain, the stack of wheat which I was commanded by the Holy Spirit to rectify you and lead you on the straight path, like a man who threshes and winnows his grain on the threshing floor.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:10:2)


**אֲשֶׁר שָׁמַעְתִּי.** מֵאִתּוֹ **הִגַּדְתִּי לָכֶם**:


**What I heard** from Him I have related to you.



### Verse 11

###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:11:1)


**דּוּמָה.** הוּא אֱדוֹם, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר ״מִי כְצוֹר כְּדוּמָה בְּתוֹךְ הַיָּם״ (יחזקאל כז:לב):


**The harsh prophecy of Dumah** That is Edom, and so does Scripture say (Ezekiel 27:32): “Who is like Tyre, like Dumah in the midst of the sea?”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:11:2)


**אֵלַי קֹרֵא מִשֵּׂעִיר.** אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: ״אֵלַי קוֹרֵא הַנָּבִיא, אוֹ הַמַּלְאָךְ, מֵעוֹל מַלְכוּת שֵׂעִיר״:


**To Me one calls from Seir** Said the Holy One, blessed be He: “To Me the prophet or the angel calls from the yoke of the kingdom of Seir.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:11:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:11:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:11:3)


**שׁוֹמֵר מַה מִלַּיְלָה.** שׁוֹמֵר יִשְׂרָאֵל, מַה תְּהֵא מִן הַלַּיְלָה וְהַחֲשֵׁכָה הַזֹּאת?


**Watchman, what will be of the night?** Watcher of Israel, what will be of this night and this darkness?

###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:12:3

### Verse 13

###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:13:1)


**מַשָּׂא בַּעְרָב.** עַל עַרְבִיִּים:


**The harsh prophecy concerning Arabia** About the Arabs.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:13:2)


**בַּיַּעַר בַּעְרַב תָּלִינוּ.** רָאִיתִי מַה עֲשִׂיתֶם בְּהַגְלוֹת אַשּׁוּר אֶת עַמִּי, וְהָיוּ מְבַקְשִׁים לְשַׁבָּאִים שֶׁלָּהֶם לְהוֹלִיכָם דֶּרֶךְ עֲלֵיכֶם, לְפִי שֶׁאַתֶּם בְּנֵי דוֹדֵיהֶם, אוּלַי תְּרַחֲמוּ עֲלֵיהֶם, וְאַתֶּם הֱיִיתֶם יוֹצְאִים וְלָנִים בַּיַּעַר דֶּרֶךְ הַעֲבָרַת שַׁיָּרוֹת:


**In the forest in Arabia did you lodge** I saw what you did when Assyria exiled my people, and they begged their captors to lead them through your land, since you are the descendants of their uncles, perhaps you would have mercy on them, and you were going out and lodging in the forest, the road where the caravans pass.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:13:3
