**אֹרְחוֹת דְּדָנִים.** בְּנֵי דוֹדְכֶן:


**the roads of your cousins** the children of your uncle.



### Verse 14

###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:14:1)


**לִקְרַאת צָמֵא** דֶּרֶךְ לְהָבִיא מַיִם, וְאַתֶּם **יוֹשְׁבֵי אֶרֶץ תֵּימָא** לֹא עֲשִׂיתֶם כֵּן, אֶלָּא **בְּלַחְמוֹ קִדְּמוּ נֹדֵד**, הֵבִיאוּ לָהֶם מִינֵי מַאֲכָלִים מְלוּחִים וְנוֹדוֹת נְפוּחִים מְלֵאֵי רוּחַ, וְהָיָה אוֹכֵל וּמְבַקֵּשׁ לִשְׁתּוֹת, וְנוֹתֵן פִּי הַנּוֹד לְתוֹךְ פִּיו, וְהָרוּחַ נִכְנָס בְּמֵעָיו וְהוּא מֵת. דָּבָר אַחֵר: **לִקְרַאת צָמֵא הֵתָיוּ מָיִם** – לֹא כֵּן עָשִׂיתִי לַאֲבִיכֶם, כְּשֶׁהָיָה צָמֵא גִּלִּיתִי לוֹ בְּאֵר מַיִם (בראשית כא:יט):


**Toward the thirsty** it is customary to bring water, but you, the inhabitants of the land of Tema, did not do so, but with his bread they came before the wanderer; they brought them sorts of salty foods and blown up flasks full of air, and he would eat and ask to drink, and he would put the opening of the flask into his mouth, and the air would go into his innards, and he would die. Another explanation of “Toward the thirsty they bring water,” is as follows: I did not do so to your forefather, Ishmael; when he was thirsty, I revealed to him a well of water.



### Verse 15

###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:15:1)


**כִּי מִפְּנֵי חֲרָבוֹת נָדָדוּ.** עַמִּי:


**Since because of the swords they wandered** (I.e.,) my people (wandered).


###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:15:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:15:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:15:2)


**חֶרֶב נְטוּשָׁה.** פְּשׁוּטָה עַל פְּנֵי הָאָרֶץ, כְּמוֹ (שמואל א ל:טז) ״וְהִנָּם נְטוּשִׁים עַל פְּנֵי כָל הָאָרֶץ״, (שמואל ב ה:יח) ״וַיִּנָּטְשׁוּ בְּעֵמֶק רְפָאִים״. דָּבָר אַחֵר: **נְטוּשָׁה** כְּמוֹ ׳לְטוּשָׁה׳, כָּל אוֹתִיּוֹת אֲשֶׁר מוֹצָאֵיהֶם קְרוֹבִים לִהְיוֹת מִמָּקוֹם אֶחָד מִתְחַלְּפוֹת זוֹ בָּזוֹ, נוּ״ן בְּלָמֶ״ד, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (נחמיה יג:ז) ״לַעֲשׂוֹת לוֹ נִשְׁכָּה״ כְּמוֹ לִשְׁכָּה:


**the outstretched sword** (נְטוּשָׁה), spread over the surface of the earth, as (I Sam. 30:16) “And behold, they were scattered (נְטוּשִׁים) over the entire landscape,” (II Sam. 5: 18) “And spread out (וַיִּנָּטְשׁוּ) in the Valley of Rephaim.” Another explanation is that נְטוּשָׁה is like לְטוּשָׁה, sharp. All letters whose sources are close to being from one place, (i.e., from one speech organ,) are interchangeable with one another, the ‘nun’ with the ‘lamed,’ as in the case stated (in Nehemiah 13: 7): “To make him a chamber (נִשְׁכָּה),” like לִשְׁכָּה.



### Verse 16

###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:16:1)


**כִּשְׁנֵי שָׂכִיר.** אֲדַקְדֵּק בָּהּ לְצַמְצֵם הַמּוֹעֵד, כְּשָׂכִיר הַנִּשְׂכָּר לְשָׁנִים, שֶׁמְּדַקְדֵּק בְּמוֹעֵד תַּשְׁלוּם שְׁנָתוֹ:


**like the year of a hireling** I will be exact with them to limit the time like a hireling, hired by years, who is exact with the time of the completion of his year.



### Verse 17

###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:17:1)


**וּשְׁאָר.** שְׁאֵרִית:


**And the rest** the remnant.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 21:17:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:17:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/21:17:2)


**קֶשֶׁת גִּבּוֹרֵי בְנֵי קֵדָר.** בַּעֲלֵי רוֹבֵי קֶשֶׁת, שֶׁהֵם כַּאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ (בראשית כא:כ) ״וַיְהִי רֹבֶה קָשֶׁת״:


**the bows of the heroes of the children of Kedar** Archers, for they are like their forefather, (Ishmael,) about whom it is stated (Gen. 21:2): “And he was an archer.”



## Chapter 22


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:1:1)


**גֵּיא חִזָּיוֹן.** הִיא יְרוּשָׁלַיִם, גֵּיא שֶׁנִּתְנַבְּאוּ עָלֶיהָ רֹב נְבוּאוֹת:


**the Valley of Vision** This is Jerusalem, the valley concerning which most prophecies were prophesied.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:1:2)


**כִּי עָלִית כֻּלָּךְ לַגַּגּוֹת.** כְּשֶׁבָּא עֲלֵיהֶם חַיִל, עוֹלִים עַל גַּגּוֹתֵיהֶם לִרְאוֹת הַחַיִל וּלְהִלָּחֵם. וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ פֵּרְשׁוּ עַל כֹּהֲנִים, שֶׁעָלוּ עַל גַּגּוֹ שֶׁל הֵיכָל וּמַפְתְּחוֹת הָעֲזָרָה בְּיָדָם, כִּדְאִיתָא בְּמַסֶּכֶת תַּעֲנִית (תענית כט א). וּמִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה אוֹמֵר שֶׁהָיוּ גַּסֵּי הָרוּחַ, בְּאֵיכָה רַבָּתִי (פתיחתא כד):


**that all of you have gone up to the rooftops** When an army comes upon them, they go up to their roofs to see the army and to fight. Our Rabbis, however, explained this concerning the priests who went up to the roof of the Temple with the keys of the forecourt in their hands, as is stated in the Tractate Taanith (29a). The Midrash Aggadah, however, states that they, (the people of Jerusalem,) were haughty. (This is found) in Lamentations Rabbah (Int. 24).



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:2:1)


**תְּשֻׁאוֹת מְלֵאָה.** עִיר שֶׁהָיְתָה מְלֵאָה תְּשׁוּאוֹת, קוֹל רֹב אָדָם, **הוֹמִיָּה וְעַלִּיזָה**, עַכְשָׁיו מַה לָּךְ מִתְאַבֶּלֶת?


**full of clamor** A city that was full of clamor, the voice of many people, tumultuous and happy, now, what ails you that you mourn?


###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:2:2)


**חֲלָלַיִךְ לֹא חַלְלֵי חֶרֶב.** טוֹבִים הָיוּ אִלּוּ חַלְלֵי חֶרֶב הָיוּ, מֵעַכְשָׁיו שֶׁהֵם חַלְלֵי רָעָב (איכה ד:ט):


**your fallen have not fallen by the sword** It would have been better had they fallen by the sword than now that they have perished by hunger.



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:3:1)


**כָּל קְצִינַיִךְ נָדְדוּ יַחַד.** צִדְקִיָּהוּ וְשָׂרָיו שֶׁיָּצְאוּ לִבְרוֹחַ בַּלַּיְלָה (מלכים ב כה:ד):


**All your officers wandered together** Zedekiah and his officers, who went out to flee at night (II Kings 25:4).


###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:3:2)


**מִקֶּשֶׁת אֻסָּרוּ.** אֲשֶׁר מֵאֵימַת הַמּוֹרִים חִצִּים בַּקֶּשֶׁת, הָיוּ נֶאֱסָרִים לְהִסָּגֵר בְּתוֹךְ הָעִיר, וְכָל הַנִּמְצָאִים בּוֹ אֻסְּרוּ יַחַד בְּזִיקִים, וְרֻבָּן **מֵרָחוֹק בָּרָחוּ** קֹדֶם לָכֵן:


**because of the bow they were bound** who, because of fear of the archers, were bound to be confined within the city, and all those found therein were bound together with chains, and the majority of them fled from afar prior to this.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:4:1)


**שְׁעוּ מִנִּי.** חִדְלוּ מִמֶּנִּי! כָּךְ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אוֹמֵר לְמַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת (איכה רבה פתיחתא כד):


**Leave Me alone** (שְׁעוּ מִנִּי). Leave Me alone. So says the Holy One, blessed be He, to the ministering angels.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:5:1)


**וּמְבוּסָה.** מִרְמָס, כְּמוֹ ״בּוֹסְסוּ אֶת חֶלְקָתִי״ (ירמיה יב:י), וּכְמוֹ ״כְּגִבּוֹרִים בּוֹסִים בְּטִיט חוּצוֹת״ (זכריה י:ה):


**trampling** (מְבוּסָה), trampling. Comp. (Jer. 12:10) “They trampled (בּוֹסְסוּ) My heritage.” Comp. also (Zech. 10:5): “And they shall be like heroes, trampling (בּוֹסִים) in the mire of the streets.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:5:2

**מְקַרְקַר קִר.** יוֹם קִרְקוּר קִיר הַחוֹמָה:


**destroying the wall** a day of destroying the wall.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:5:3)


**וְשׁוֹעַ אֶל הָהָר.** וְקוֹל שַׁוְעָה לָנוּס אֶל הֶהָרִים, לְהִמָּלֵט:


**and shouting, “To the mountain!”** (וְשׁוֹעַ). And the voice of a shout to flee to the mountains to escape.



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:6:1)


**נָשָׂא אַשְׁפָּה.** אַשְׁפּוֹת חִצִּים, קויבר״ץ בלע״ז:


**carried a quiver** a quiver of arrows.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:6:2)


**וְקִיר עֵרָה מָגֵן.** תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״וְעַל שׁוּר דְּבָקוּ תְּרִיסִין״, וְהוּא כְּמוֹ ״עָרוֹת עַל יְאוֹר״ (ישעיהו יט:ז), ״וּמִתְעָרֶה כְּאֶזְרָח רַעֲנָן״ (תהלים לז:לה). וְיֵשׁ לְפָרֵשׁ **וְקִיר עֵרָה מָגֵן**: ׳קִיר׳ שֵׁם הָעִיר, כְּמוֹ ״וַיַּגְלֶה קִירָה״ (מלכים ב טז:ט), בְּנֵי אוֹתָהּ מְדִינָה גִּלּוּ מָגִנֵּיהֶם עַל יְרוּשָׁלַיִם:


**and to the wall they attached their shields** (עֵרָה). Comp. (above 19:7) “The well rooted plants (עָרוֹת) by the stream,” (Psalms 37:35) “Striking roots (מִתְעָרֶה) like a green tree in its native soil.” It is also possible to explain: וְקִיר עֵרָה מָגֵן as follows: Kir is the name of the city. Comp. (II Kings 16:9) “And exiled [its inhabitants] to Kir.” The people of that province exposed their shields toward Jerusalem.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:7:1)


**שֹׁת שָׁתוּ הַשָּׁעְרָה.** שָׂמוּ מָצוֹר עַל הַשְּׁעָרִים, וְדֻגְמָתוֹ יֵשׁ בִּמְלָכִים בְּמִלְחֶמֶת בֶּן הֲדַד ״שִׂימוּ עַל הָעִיר״ (מלכים א כ:יב):


**laid [siege] to the gate** (Lit., laid to the gate.) They laid siege to the gates. There is a similar expression in Kings (II 20:12) in the war with Ben Hadad, “Lay on!” And they laid siege to the city.



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:8:1)


**וַיְגַל.** לְשׁוֹן גִּלּוּי:


**And he bared** (וַיְגַל), an expression of uncovering.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:8:2)


**מָסַךְ יְהוּדָה.** הוּא בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, שֶׁהָיָה מֵגִין וּמֵיסַךְ וּמְסַכֵּךְ עֲלֵיהֶם:


**the covert of Judah** That is the Temple, which shielded, protected, and covered them.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:8:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:8:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:8:3)


**וַתַּבֵּט בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא.** תַּחְבּוּלוֹת לְהִלָּחֵם בָּם:


**and you looked on that day** for means of waging war.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:8:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:8:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:8:4)


**אֶל נֶשֶׁק בֵּית הַיָּעַר.** הֵם הַמָּגִנִּים, שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת וּמָאתַיִם צִנָּה שֶׁעָשָׂה שְׁלֹמֹה, ״וַיִּתְּנֵם הַמֶּלֶךְ בֵּית יַעַר הַלְּבָנוֹן״ (מלכים א י:טז):


**to the weapons of the house of the forest** They are the three hundred shields and two hundred body shields that Solomon made, and the king placed them in the house of the forest of Lebanon (I Kings 10:16).



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:9:1)


**בְּקִיעֵי עִיר דָּוִד.** בִּקְעֵי הַחוֹמָה **רְאִיתֶם כִּי רָבּוּ**:


**the cracks of the city of David** The cracks of the wall you saw that they had increased.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:9:2)


**וַתְּקַבְּצוּ אֶת מֵי הַבְּרֵכָה.** יוֹנָתָן תִּרְגֵּם: ״וּכְנִישְׁתּוּן יָת עַמָּא לְמֵי בְּרִיכְתָא אַרְעִיתָא״, שֶׁהוּא אֵצֶל בְּקִיעֵי עִיר דָּוִד לְהִלָּחֵם שָׁם, לְפִי שֶׁרְאִיתֶם שֶׁיֵּשׁ שָׁם תָּרְפָּה לִירוּשָׁלַיִם וְנוֹחָה לִכָּבֵּשׁ מִשָּׁם:


**and you gathered the water of the lower pool** Jonathan renders: And you gathered the people to the waters of the lower pool, which is near the cracks of the city of David, to fight there, because you saw that Jerusalem had a weak spot there and was vulnerable to conquest from there.



### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:10:1)


**וְאֶת בָּתֵּי יְרוּשָׁלִַם סְפַרְתֶּם.** כַּמָּה בָּתִּים יֵשׁ לְכָל אֶחָד, שֶׁיִּתְּנוּ מֵהֶם לְפִי חֶשְׁבּוֹן, כְּדֵי לָקַחַת הָאֲבָנִים וְהָעֵצִים לְבַצֵּר אֶת הַחוֹמָה:


**And the houses of Jerusalem you counted** how many houses each one had, that they give of them proportionally, to take the stones and the wood to fortify the wall.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:10:2)


**לְבַצֵּר.** לְחַזֵּק, לְשׁוֹן ״עָרִים בְּצוּרוֹת״ (במדבר יג:כח):


**to fortify** (לְבַצֵּר), to strengthen, an expression similar to “fortified cities” (בְּצוּרוֹת) (Num. 13:28).



### Verse 11

###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:11:1)


**וּמִקְוָה עֲשִׂיתֶם.** אֲגַם מַיִם לִהְיוֹת חֹזֶק לָעִיר:


**And a ditch you made** A pool of water, to be a defense (lit., strength) for the city.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:11:2)


**בֵּין הַחֹמֹתַיִם.** הַחוֹמוֹת כְּפוּלוֹת: חַיִל וְחוֹמָה, וּבֵין **מֵי הַבְּרֵכָה הַיְשָׁנָה**:


**between the two walls** the double walls, the low wall and the high wall, and the water of the old pool.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:11:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:11:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:11:3)


**וְלֹא הִבַּטְתֶּם אֶל עֹשֶׂיהָ.** וְאִם תֹּאמְרוּ: אַף חִזְקִיָּה עָשָׂה כֵּן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דברי הימים ב לב:ה) ״וַיִּתְחַזֵּק וַיִּבֶן אֶת כָּל הַחוֹמָה הַפְּרוּצָה וַיַּעַל עַל הַמִּגְדָּלִים וְלַחוּצָה הַחוֹמָה הָאַחֶרֶת וַיְחַזֵּק אֶת הַמִּלֹּא עִיר דָּוִד״? חִזְקִיָּהוּ ״בַּה׳ אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּטַח וְגוֹ׳״ (מלכים ב יח:ה), אֲבָל אַתֶּם, בִּימֵי יְהוֹיָקִים וְצִדְקִיָּה, לֹא הִבַּטְתֶּם אֶל עוֹשֶׂיהָ:


**but you did not look to its Maker** Now, if you ask, Hezekiah, too, did so, as it is stated (in II Chron. 32:5) “And he strengthened himself, and he built up all the broken down wall, and he went up on the towers and outside the other wall, and he strengthened the Millo of the city of David,” the answer is that Hezekiah “trusted in the Lord God of Israel, etc.” (II Kings 18:5), but you, in the days of Jehoiakim and Zedekiah did not look to its Maker.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:11:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:11:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:11:4)


**וְיֹצְרָהּ מֵרָחוֹק.** מֵאָז שֶׁבָּרָא אֶת הָעוֹלָם, עָלְתָה יְרוּשָׁלַיִם וּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ בַּמַּחֲשָׁבָה:


**and Him Who fashioned it from afar** From the time He created the world, Jerusalem and the Temple were His intention.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:11:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:11:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:11:5)


**לֹא רְאִיתֶם.** לֹא חֲשַׁבְתֶּם:


**you did not see** You did not think of Him.



### Verse 13

###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:13:1)


**וְהִנֵּה שָׂשׂוֹן וְשִׂמְחָה.** הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא כִּבְיָכוֹל אָבֵל לְפָנָיו, וְאַתֶּם אוֹכְלִים וּשְׂמֵחִים:


**And behold, joy and happiness** The Holy One, blessed be He, so to speak, is mourning, and you are eating and rejoicing.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:13:2)


**כִּי מָחָר נָמוּת.** בָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא, הַנְּבִיאִים אוֹמְרִים לָנוּ מֵאֵת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה לָנוּ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, נַעֲשֶׂה לָנוּ הֲנָאָה בְּחַיֵּינוּ:


**for tomorrow we will die** in the World to Come. The prophets tell us in the name of the Holy One, blessed be He, that we will have no share in the World to Come. Let us, therefore, enjoy ourselves during our lifetime.



### Verse 14

###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:14:1)


**עַד תְּמֻתוּן.** תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״מוֹתָא תִּנְיָינָא לְעוֹלָם הַבָּא״:


**until you die** Jonathan paraphrases a second death in the World to Come.



### Verse 15

###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:15:1)


**הַסֹּכֵן.** בַּעַל הֲנָאוֹת הָיָה, וְכֵן (מלכים א א:ב) ״וַתְּהִי לוֹ סֹכֶנֶת״. וּמִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה אוֹמֵר: מִן סִכְנִי הָיָה וּבָא לוֹ לִירוּשָׁלַיִם (ויקרא רבה ה ה):


**voluptuary** (סוֹכֵן), he was lustful of pleasures. Comp. (I Kings 1:2): “And she shall be to him a warmer (סוֹכֶנֶת),” (San. 26b, where Rashi cites exegetes who claim that Shebna had homosexual tendencies.) Midrash Aggadah states: He was from Sichni, and he came to Jerusalem. This is in Lev. Rabbah (5:5).


###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:15:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:15:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:15:2)


**אֲשֶׁר עַל הַבָּיִת.** מְמֻנֶּה הָיָה עַל בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, יֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל, וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: אֲמַרְכָּל:


**appointed over the Temple** (lit., the house.) He was appointed over the entire Temple. Some say he was the High Priest and some say he was a Temple trustee.



### Verse 16

###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:16:1)


**מַה לְּךָ פֹה** הַכָּתוּב מְגַנֵּהוּ, לְפִי שֶׁרָצָה לְהַסְגִּיר אֶת חִזְקִיָּהוּ לְמֶלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר, כְּדְאָמְרִינַן בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (סנהדרין כו א), כָּתַב פִּיתְקָא וְשַׁדָּא בְּגִירָא: ״שֶׁבְנָא וְסִיעָתוֹ הִשְׁלִימוּ, חִזְקִיָּה וְסִיעָתוֹ לֹא הִשְׁלִימוּ״:


**What have you here** Scripture denigrates him because he wished to surrender Hezekiah to the king of Assyria, as is stated in San. (26a): He wrote a note and shot it on an arrow, “Shebna and his company wish to make peace; Hezekiah and his company do not wish to make peace.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:16:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:16:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:16:2)


**וּמִי לְךָ פֹה.** מִי מִמִּשְׁפַּחְתְּךָ קָבוּר כָּאן?


**and whom do you have here** Who of your family is buried here?


###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:16:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:16:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:16:3)


**חֹצְבִי מָרוֹם קִבְרוֹ.** שֶׁחָצַב לוֹ קֶבֶר בְּקִבְרֵי בֵּית דָּוִד לִקָּבֵר בֵּין הַמְּלָכִים, לְכָךְ הוּא אוֹמֵר לוֹ: ״**מַה** יְרֻשָּׁה **לְךָ** בַּקְּבָרוֹת הַלָּלוּ?״


**he hews his grave on high** For he hewed a grave for himself among the graves of the House of David, to be buried among the kings. Therefore, he says to him, “What right of heritage do you have in these graves?”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:16:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:16:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:16:4)


**חֹצְבִי** חֹקְקִי. יוּ״ד יְתֵירָה, כְּמוֹ ״שֹׁכְנִי סְנֶה״ (דברים לג:טז), ״מְקִימִי מֵעָפָר דָּל״ (תהלים קיג:ז):


**he hews** (חֹצְבִי). The ‘yud’ is superfluous. Comp. (Deut. 33:16): “Who dwells (שׁוֹכְנִי) in the thornbush”; (Psalms 113:7) “He raises up (מְקִימִי) the poor man from the dust.”



### Verse 17

###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:17:1)


**טַלְטֵלָה גָּבֶר.** כְּהָדֵין תַּרְנְגוֹלָא דְּמִטַּלְטֵל מֵאֲתַר לַאֲתַר (ויקרא רבה שם), וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ אָמְרוּ (סנהדרין כו א): טִלְטוּלָא דְּגַבְרָא קָשֶׁה מְדְאִיתְּתָא:


**Shall cast you about with a mighty toss** (גָבֶר) like a rooster that wanders from place to place (Lev. Rabbah ibid.) The Midrash explains גֶבֶר as a rooster. Our Rabbis, however, stated that the wandering of a man is more trying than that of a woman (San. 26a).


###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:17:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:17:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:17:2)


**וְעֹטְךָ עָטֹה.** כְּמוֹ ״וַיָּעַט בָּהֶם״ (שמואל א כה:יד), לְשׁוֹן ׳עַיִט׳ – יַפְרִיחֲךָ כְּעוֹף בַּגָּלוּת. וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ אָמְרוּ (ויקרא רבה ה ה): צָרַעַת פָּרְחָה בּוֹ, כְּמָה דְאַתְּ אָמֵר ״עַל שָׂפָם יַעְטֶה״ (ויקרא יג:מה):


**and cause you to fly.** Heb. (וְעֹטְךָ עָטֹה). Comp. (I Sam. 25:14) “And he drove them away (וַיָּעַט),” an expression of עַיִּט, a bird. He will make you fly away like a bird, in exile. Our Rabbis, however, stated that ‘zaraath’ broke out upon him, as is stated: (Leviticus 13:45) “And on his upper lip he shall enwrap himself (יַעְטֶה).”



### Verse 18

###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:18:1)


**צָנוֹף יִצְנָפְךָ.** כְּמִצְנֶפֶת הַמַּקֶּפֶת אֶת הָרֹאשׁ, יַקִּיפוּךָ אוֹיְבִים וּמְצִיקִים:


**He shall wind you around** like a turban that surrounds the head, the enemies and oppressors shall surround you.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:18:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:18:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:18:2)


**כַּדּוּר.** כְּשׁוּר מֻקָּף, וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ פֵּרְשׁוּ (ויקרא רבה ה ה) לְשׁוֹן ׳כַּדּוּר׳, שֶׁקּוֹרִין פלוט״א בלע״ז, שֶׁזּוֹרְקִין אוֹתוֹ וּמְקַבְּלִין מִיָּד לְיָד:


**like a surrounding wall.** (כַּדּוּר). Our Rabbis, however, explained it as an expression of a ball, which they call ‘pelote’ in French, which is tossed and caught from hand to hand.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:18:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:18:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:18:3)


**אֶל אֶרֶץ רַחֲבַת יָדָיִם.** ״בְּכָסִפְיָא״, שֵׁם הַמָּקוֹם (עזרא ח:יז):


**to a land of ample space** in Casiphia, the name of a place.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:18:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:18:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:18:4)


**שָׁמָּה תָמוּת.** וְלֹא תִּקָּבֵר בְּקִבְרֵי בֵּית דָּוִד, וְ**שָׁמָּה** יִהְיוּ **מַרְכְּבוֹת כְּבוֹדֶךָ** נֶהְפָּכִים לְ**קָלוֹן בֵּית אֲדוֹנֶיךָ** שֶׁבִּקַּשְׁתָּ:


**there you shall die** And you shall not be buried in the sepulchre of the House of David, and there the chariots of your glory shall be converted into the shame of the house of your master which you sought.



### Verse 19

###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:19:1)


**וּמִמַּעֲמָדְךָ.** וּמִשִּׁמּוּשְׁךָ בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ **יֶהֶרְסֶךָ**:


**and from your station** (Lit., your stand. The Temple service was performed in a standing position.) And from your service in the Temple, He shall tear you down.



### Verse 20

###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:20:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:20:1)


**לְאֶלְיָקִים.** הוּא הָיָה עַל הַבַּיִת כְּשֶׁנָּפַל סַנְחֵרִיב (ישעיהו לו:ג), כְּמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ כְּשֶׁיָּצְאוּ אֶל רַבְשָׁקֵה, וְגִלָּה לוֹ שֶׁבְנָא וְסִיעָתוֹ וּגְרָרוּהוּ בִּזְנָבוֹת סוּסֵיהֶם, כִּדְאִיתָא בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (סנהדרין כו ב). כְּשֶׁהָלַךְ סַנְחֵרִיב אֶל תִּרְהָקָא מֶלֶךְ כּוּשׁ שָׁטַף שֶׁבְנָא וְסִיעָתוֹ וְהָלַךְ לוֹ, כָּךְ שָׁנִינוּ בְּסֵדֶר עוֹלָם (סדר עולם רבה כג):


**to Eliakim** He was appointed over the house when Sennacherib took him, (i.e., Shebna,) as we find, when they went out to Rabshakeh, and he revealed to him Shebna and his company, and they dragged him with their horses’ tails, as is related in San. (26b). When Sennacherib went to Tirhakah, king of Cush, he swept away Shebna and his company and went away. We learned this in Seder Olam (ch. 23).



### Verse 22

###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:22:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:22:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:22:1)


**מַפְתֵּחַ בֵּית דָּוִד.** תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״מַפְתֵּחַ בֵּית מַקְדְּשָׁא וְשֻׁלְטָן בֵּית דָּוִד״:


**the key of the House of David** Jonathan paraphrases: The key of the Temple and the government of the House of David.



### Verse 23

###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:23:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:23:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:23:1)


**וּתְקַעְתִּיו יָתֵד בְּמָקוֹם נֶאֱמָן.** ״וַאֲמַנִּינִיהּ אֲמַרְכַּל מְהֵימָן מְשַׁמֵּשׁ בַּאֲתַר קַיָּם״ תַּרְגּוּם יוֹנָתָן. **נֶאֱמָן** לְשׁוֹן ׳קִיּוּם׳, מָקוֹם שֶׁהוּא נֶאֱמָן לַנִּשְׁעָנִים עָלָיו כִּי לֹא יִמּוֹט. סָרֵס אֶת הַמִּקְרָא: ״וּתְקַעְתִּיו יָתֵד נֶאֱמָן בְּמָקוֹם״:


**And I will thrust him like a peg in a sure place** (Jonathan renders:) And I will appoint him a faithful trustee, serving in a sure place. Jonathan renders נֶאֱמָן as sure, i.e., a place that is faithful to those who lean on it, for it shall not move. Another explanation is to reverse the word order of the verse: And I will thrust him a sure peg in a place.



### Verse 24

###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:24:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:24:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:24:1)


**הַצֶּאֱצָאִים וְהַצְּפִיעוֹת.** תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״בְּנַיָּא וּבְנֵי בְּנַיָּא״. וּמְנַחֵם חִבְּרוֹ עִם ״צְפִיעֵי הַבָּקָר״ (יחזקאל ד:טו), לִמֵּד שֶׁהוּא לְשׁוֹן עוֹלָלִים דַּקִּים הַיּוֹצְאִים מִמְּעֵי אִמָּן, וְיִהְיֶה צְפִיעֵי לְשׁוֹן ׳יְצִיאָה׳, דָּבָר הַיּוֹצֵא:


**the children and the grandchildren** (צֶאֱצָאִים וּצְפִיעוֹת). Jonathan renders: the children and the children’s children. Menachem (Machbereth p. 151) associates it with, (Ezekiel 4:15) “Cattle dung (צְפִיעֵי).” This teaches us that it is an expression of tiny infants that issue forth from their mother’s womb. making צְפִיעוֹת an expression of coming out, i.e., a thing that comes out.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:24:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:24:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:24:2)


**כָּל כְּלֵי הַקָּטָן.** הַקְּטַנִּים שֶׁבְּמִשְׁפְּחוֹתָם יִהְיוּ מִתְפָּאֲרִין בּוֹ וְנִסְמָכִין עָלָיו:


**all the small vessels** the smallest of their families shall take pride in him and rely on him.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:24:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:24:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:24:3)


**מִכְּלֵי הָאַגָּנוֹת וְעַד כָּל כְּלֵי הַנְּבָלִים.** תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״מִכָּהֲנַיָּא לְבִישֵׁי אֵפוֹדָא וְעַד בְּנֵי לֵוִי אַחֲדֵי נִבְלַיָּא״, וְיִהְיֶה אַגָּנוֹת לְשׁוֹן ׳כְּלֵי שָׁרֵת׳, שֶׁמְּשָׁרְתִין בָּהֶם הַכֹּהֲנִים בְּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ:


**from the vessels of basins to the vessels of the lyres** Jonathan paraphrases: From the priests who wear the ephod to the Levites who hold the lyres. Accordingly, it is an expression of the ministration vessels with which the priests perform the service in the Temple.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:24:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:24:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:24:4)


**הַנְּבָלִים.** שֶׁאוֹמְרִים בְּנֵי לֵוִי בָּהֶן הַשִּׁיר:


**the lyres** with which the Levites recite the song during the offering of the sacrifices.



### Verse 25

###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:25:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:25:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:25:1)


**תָּמוּשׁ הַיָּתֵד.** גְּדֻלָּתוֹ שֶׁל שֶׁבְנָא:


**shall the peg...move** (This alludes to) the greatness of Shebna.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 22:25:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:25:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:25:2)


**וְנִכְרַת הַמַּשָּׂא אֲשֶׁר עָלֶיהָ.** בְּנֵי מִשְׁפַּחְתּוֹ וְסִיעָתוֹ הַנִּסְמָכִים עָלָיו וְהַתּוֹלִים בּוֹ כְּלֵי תִפְאַרְתָּם. וּלְפִי שֶׁדִּמָּהוּ לְיָתֵד, דִּמָּה הַמִּתְפָּאֲרִים בּוֹ וְנִשְׁעָנִים עָלָיו לְמַשָּׂא שֶׁמַּטְעִינִים עַל הַיָּתֵד. וְיֵשׁ פּוֹתְרִים אוֹתוֹ: וְתִתְקַיֵּם הַנְּבוּאָה שֶׁנִּתְנַבְּאָה עָלָיו:


**and the burden which is upon it shall be cut off** His family members and his company who depend on him and who hang upon him the vessels of their glory. And since he likened him to a peg, he likened those who boast about him and rely on him, to a burden loaded on the peg. Some interpret it: And the prophecy prophesied about him shall be fulfilled.



## Chapter 23


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:1:1)


**הֵילִילוּ אֳנִיּוֹת תַּרְשִׁישׁ.** שֶׁהָיוּ מִתְעַשְּׁרִים עַל יְדֵי סוֹחֲרֵי צוֹר, שֶׁהָיוּ מְבִיאִים אֳנִיּוֹת תַּרְשִׁישׁ סְחוֹרָה לְצוֹר. **תַּרְשִׁישׁ** שֵׁם הַיָּם:


**Wail, ye ships of Tarshish** who became wealthy through the merchants of Tyre, for the ships of Tarshish would bring merchandise to Tyre. Tarshish is the name of the sea.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:1:2)


**כִּי שֻׁדַּד מִבַּיִת מִבּוֹא.** כִּי שֻׁדַּד מִבִּפְנִים, מָקוֹם שֶׁהֱיִיתֶם רְגִילִין לְפֻנְדָּק, מִלָּבוֹא עוֹד לְתוֹכוֹ, וְלֹא יִהְיוּ עוֹד לָכֶם מָקוֹם בְּצוֹר לָלוּן שָׁם:


**for it has been pillaged from within** For it has been pillaged from within, the place you were wont to lodge, from coming anymore into his midst, and you will no longer have a place in Tyre to lodge there.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:1:3)


**מֵאֶרֶץ כִּתִּים.** הֵם הָרוֹמִיִּים:


**from the land of Kittim** They are the Romans.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:1:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:1:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:1:4)


**נִגְלָה לָמוֹ.** הַשּׁוֹדֵד לְאַנְשֵׁי צוֹר. דָּבָר אַחֵר: **מֵאֶרֶץ כִּתִּים נִגְלָה** לְאַנְשֵׁי תַרְשִׁישׁ שׁוֹד שֶׁל צוֹר, שֶׁבָּרְחוּ בְּנֵי צוֹר אֵצֶל כִּתִּים וּמִשָּׁם נִשְׁמְעָה הַשְּׁמוּעָה:


**he appeared to them** The marauder appeared to the people of Tyre. Another explanation is that from the land of Kittim, the plunder of Tyre was revealed to the people of Tarshish, for the people of Tyre fled to Kittim and from there the news was heard.



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:2:1)


**דֹּמּוּ יֹשְׁבֵי אִי.** הִתְאַבְּלוּ וְשְׁבוּ דוֹמִים, יוֹשְׁבֵי אִי הַיָּם; לָמָּה? סוֹחֲרֵי צִידוֹן, עוֹבְרֵי יַמִּים, הָיוּ רְגִילִים לְמַלְּאוֹתֵךְ כָּל סְחוֹרָה; עַכְשָׁיו כְּשֶׁתִּפּוֹל צוֹר תִּפּוֹל צִידוֹן עִמָּהּ, שֶׁסְּמוּכוֹת הָיוּ זוֹ לָזוֹ בְּתוֹךְ מַהֲלַךְ יוֹם:


**Be silent, ye island dwellers** Mourn and sit silently, you dwellers of the island of the sea. Why? The seafaring merchants of Zidon were wont to replenish you with all merchandise. Now, when Tyre falls, Zidon will fall with it, for they were within a day’s journey from one another.



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:3:1)


**וּבְמַיִם רַבִּים.** הָיָה בָּא **זֶרַע** מִמִּצְרַיִם, הַיּוֹשֶׁבֶת עַל נְהַר **שִׁחוֹר**, אֶל צוֹר:


**And on great waters** the seed would come from Egypt, that is situated on the river Shihor, to Tyre.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:3:2)


**קְצִיר יְאוֹר.** מִצְרַיִם הָיָה תְּבוּאָה שֶׁל צוֹר:


**the harvest of the Nile** Egypt was the revenue of Tyre.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:3:3)


**שִׁיחוֹר.** הוּא נִילוּס, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (יהושע יג:ג): ״מִן הַשִּׁיחוֹר אֲשֶׁר עַל פְּנֵי מִצְרָיִם״, וְהָיוּ מְבִיאִים הַתְּבוּאָה לְצוֹר בָּאֳנִיּוֹת מִצְרָיִם:


**Shihor** This is the Nile, as it is said (Jos. 13: 3): “From the Shihor, which is before Egypt.” And they would bring the produce to Tyre in Egyptian ships.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:3:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:3:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:3:4)


**וַתְּהִי.** צוֹר:


**and she became** (I.e.,) Tyre.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:3:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:3:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:3:5)


**סְחַר גּוֹיִם.** מֵעַם רַב שֶׁהָיָה בָּהּ, כָּל הַגּוֹיִם מְבִיאִין לָהּ סְחוֹרָה:


**the mart of the nations** from the multitude of people that were therein. All the nations brought merchandise to her. ([Some editions read:] All the strangers.)



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:4:1)


**בּוֹשִׁי צִידוֹן.** שֶׁטְּפֵלָה לְצוֹר:


**Be ashamed, Zidon** which was secondary to Tyre.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:4:2)


**כִּי אָמַר יָם.** כִּי אָמְרָה צוֹר, הַיּוֹשֶׁבֶת בְּמָעוֹז הַיָּם שֶׁהוּא עִקַּר רֹאשׁ הַמַּלְכוּת, הֲרֵינִי כְּמוֹ שֶׁ**לֹּא חַלְתִּי וְלֹא יָלַדְתִּי** בַּחוּרִים, כִּי כֻּלָּם נֶהֶרְגוּ, וַהֲרֵי כְּמוֹ שֶׁלֹּא **רוֹמַמְתִּי בְתוּלוֹת**. וְכֵן תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן. וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ אָמְרוּ בָּאַגָּדָה (ספרי במדבר מב): **בּוֹשִׁי צִידוֹן כִּי אָמַר יָם** – מָה אֲנִי שֶׁאֵין לִי בָּנִים וּבָנוֹת לִדְאוֹג עֲלֵיהֶם, שֶׁלֹּא יִתָּפְשׂוּ בַּעֲוֹנִי, אֵינִי מְשַׁנֶּה מִצְווֹת קוֹנִי לַעֲבוֹר גְּבוּל חוֹל אֲשֶׁר שָׂם לִי, עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה **בּוֹשִׁי צִידוֹן** שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָךְ לִדְאוֹג בְּכָל אֵלֶּה:


**for the sea said** For Tyre, that was situated in the stronghold of the sea, who was the main head of the kingdom, said, “I am as though I have not travailed, nor have I borne young men, for they all were slain, and I am as though I have not raised virgins.” And so did Jonathan render it. And our Sages said in the Aggadah: Be ashamed, Zidon, for the sea has spoken, “If I, who have no sons and daughters about whom to worry that they not be seized for my iniquity, do not deviate from the commandment of my Maker, by crossing the boundary of sand which He placed for me, how much more should you be ashamed, Zidon, since you have to worry about all these!”



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:5:1)


**כַּאֲשֶׁר שֵׁמַע לְמִצְרָיִם.** אֲשֶׁר שָׁמְעוּ עַל מִצְרַיִם שֶׁהֵבֵאתִי עֲלֵיהֶם עֶשֶׂר מַכּוֹת, וְסוֹף טָבְעוּ בַּיָּם:


**Like the report concerning Egypt** which they heard about the Egyptians, that I had brought ten plagues upon them, and that they finally drowned in the sea.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:5:2)


**יָחִילוּ.** יִבָּהֲלוּ:


**shall they quake** They shall be frightened.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:5:3)


**כְּשֵׁמַע.** הַשּׁוֹמְעִים כְּשֶׁיָּצָא **שֵׁמַע צוֹר**, כִּי גַם מַכּוֹתֶיהָ שֶׁל צוֹר יִהְיוּ דֻּגְמַת אוֹתָן מַכּוֹת: ״דָּם וָאֵשׁ״ (יואל ג:ג) דֻּגְמַת מַכַּת דָּם, ״קוֹל שָׁאוֹן מֵעִיר״ (ישעיהו סו:ו) זוֹ קִרְקוּר הַצְפַרְדְּעִים, ״וְנֶהֶפְכוּ נְחָלֶיהָ לְזֶפֶת״ (ישעיהו לד:ט) וְכוּ׳:


**at the report** When the listeners hear that the report concerning Tyre has been announced, for also the plagues of Tyre shall be in the same pattern as those plagues: “Blood and fire” (Joel 3:3); (Isaiah 66:6) “A voice of tumult from the city,” like the croaking of the frogs, (Infra 34:9) “And its brooks shall be turned to pitch and its dust into sulphur,” on the pattern of the plague of lice. (Ibid. 11) “But the pelican and hedgehog shall take possession of it,” after the pattern of the plague of a mixture of noxious beasts. (Ezekiel 38:22) “And I will hold judgment over him with pestilence and with blood,” a pattern of the plague of murrain. (Zechariah 14:12) “His flesh shall consume away,” after the pattern of the plague of boils. (Supra 18:5) “And he shall cut off the tendrils,” after the pattern of the hail and locusts; (infra 34:6) “And a great massacre in the land of Edom,” corresponding to the plague of the first born. This system is true if his צוֹר is another city (Edom, Rome[Parshandatha]). If it is actually Tyre, because the sea inundated it, the prophet says about it, “Like the report concerning Egypt,” and I say that the entire section, indeed, is talking about Tyre, because Zidon is near it. ([Other editions read:] And I say that the entire section is, indeed, talking about Tyre. Because Zidon is near it, he juxtaposes Zidon to it [Parshandatha].)

**Proceed** you inhabitants of Tyre, to flee to Tarshish.

###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:7:1

**הֲזֹאת לָכֶם עַלִּיזָה** הֲרֵי נָפְלָה לִפְנֵיכֶם, וְיֹאמַר לָכֶם: ״**הֲזֹאת** הָעִיר שֶׁהָיְתָה **עַלִּיזָה** בְּעֵינֵיכֶם, אֲשֶׁר **מִימֵי קֶדֶם קַדְמָתָהּ** הָיְתָה עַלִּיזָה? עַכְשָׁיו **יוֹבִלוּהָ רַגְלֶיהָ מֵרָחוֹק** לְבַקֵּשׁ לָהּ מָנוֹחַ״:


**Is this your joyful [city]** It has fallen before you, and he will say to you, “Is this the city that was joyful in your eyes, that from ancient times was joyful; whose feet now carry her afar to seek for herself a resting place?”



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:8:1)


**כִּנְעָנֶיהָ.** תַּגָּרֶיהָ, כְּמוֹ ״כְּנַעַן בְּיָדוֹ מֹאזְנֵי מִרְמָה״ (הושע יב:ח), ״וְלֹא יִהְיֶה כְנַעֲנִי עוֹד״ (זכריה יד:כא):


**whose traffickers** (כִּנְעָנֶיהָ) traffickers. Comp. (Hosea 12:8) “As for the trafficker (כְּנַעַן) in his hand are the balances of deceit”; (Zech. 14:21) “And there shall no longer be a trafficker (כְּנַעֲנִי).”

###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:10:2)


**כַּיְאֹר.** כַּיְאוֹר הַזֶּה שֶׁעוֹלֶה וּמִתְפַּשֵּׁט:


**like a river** Like this river that rises and spreads out.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:10:3

**בַּת תַּרְשִׁישׁ.** צוֹר הַיּוֹשֶׁבֶת בְּיָם תַּרְשִׁישׁ:


**O daughter of Tarshish** Tyre, which is situated on the Sea of Tarshish.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:10:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:10:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:10:4)


**אֵין מֵזַח.** אֵין לְךָ **עוֹד** חֹזֶק וְאֵזוֹר לְשַׁנֵּס מָתְנַיִם, **מֵזַח** לְשׁוֹן ׳אֵזוֹר׳, כְּמוֹ (תהלים קט:יט) ״וּלְמֵזַח תָּמִיד יַחְגְּרֶהָ״, וְכָל ׳אֵזוֹר׳ לְשׁוֹן ׳חֹזֶק׳:


**there is no more strength** (אֵין מֵזַח עוֹד). You have no more strength or girdle to gird your loins. מֵזַח is an expression of a girdle. Comp. (Psalms 109: 19) “And for a girdle (וּלְמֵֵזַח) he shall always gird himself with it.” And every ‘girdle’ is an expression of strength.

###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:11:1

**יָדוֹ נָטָה.** הַנּוֹטֶה:

###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:11:2

**ה׳ צִוָּה אֶל כְּנַעַן.** צִוָּה אֶת קוֹרְאָיו עַל כְּנַעַן:


**the Lord commanded upon Canaan** He commanded His summoned ones upon Canaan.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:11:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:11:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:11:3)


**לַשְׁמִד.** כְּמוֹ ׳לְהַשְׁמִיד׳, וְכֵן ״לָלֶכֶת לַגִּיד בְּיִזְרְעֶאל״ (מלכים ב ט:טו) כְּמוֹ ׳לְהַגִּיד׳, וְכֵן ״לַשְׁמִיעַ קוֹל תּוֹדָה״ (תהלים כו:ז) כְּמוֹ ׳לְהַשְׁמִיעַ׳:

**its strongholds** Tyre and Zidon were of Canaan, as it is stated (Gen. 10:15): “Zidon his first born.”



### Verse 12

###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:12:1)


**כִּתִּים.** אֶל אֶרֶץ **כִּתִּים קוּמִי עֲבוֹרִי, גַּם שָׁם לֹא יָנוּחַ לָךְ**. לָמָּה אֲנִי אוֹמֵר **קוּמִי עֲבוֹרִי**?


**to Kittim** to the land of Kittim, arise and cross; even there you shall have no rest. Why do I say, “Arise and cross over?” ([According to our reading, that of the printed editions, we find no answer to this question. According to some manuscripts, however, the reading is as follows:] **to Kittim** to the land of Kittim, arise and cross, even there you shall have no rest. Why? **Behold the land of the Chaldees** They shall exile you from there.



### Verse 13

###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:13:1)


**הֵן אֶרֶץ כַּשְׂדִּים זֶה הָעָם לֹא הָיָה.** אֲשֶׁר לֹא כְּדַאי הוּא לִהְיוֹת עָם, שֶׁהֲרֵי נִקְרְאוּ ״הַגּוֹי הַמַּר וְהַנִּמְהָר״ (חבקוק א:ו). עַם שׁוֹטֶה הוּא, מִן הַבְּרִיּוֹת שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִתְחָרֵט עֲלֵיהֶן עַל שֶׁבְּרָאָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁנִינוּ: שְׁלֹשָׁה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִתְחָרֵט עֲלֵיהֶם בְּמַסֶּכֶת סֻכָּה (סוכה נב ב):


**Behold the land of the Chaldees, this people has never been** It was not to be a people, for they are called, (Habakkuk 1:6) “bitter, impetuous nation.” They are a foolish nation, of the creatures that the Holy One, blessed be He, (so to speak,) regrets (creating) them. [Tractate Sukkah (52b)].


###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:13:2)


**אַשּׁוּר יְסָדָהּ.** לְהַשְׁכִּין בָּהּ צִיִּים שֶׁלּוֹ, סְפִינוֹתָיו, בִּרְנִיּוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת, כְּמוֹ ״צִי אַדִּיר״ (ישעיהו לג:כא):


**Assyria established it** to station his fleets therein, his ships, huge battle ships, as (infra 33:21): “A mighty fleet (צִי).”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:13:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:13:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:13:3)


**הֵקִימוּ בַחוּנָיו.** הֵם יָקִימוּ מְצוּדוֹתֵיהֶם עַל צוֹר. **בַחוּנָיו** – לְשׁוֹן ״עֹפֶל וָבַחַן״ (ישעיהו לב:יד), בורפריי״ץ בלע״ז שֶׁעוֹשִׂין לְמָצוֹר עַל הַכְּרַכִּים:


**they erected its towers** They shall erect their fortifications (var., their siege towers) upon Tyre. (Heb.) בַּחוּנָיו, an expression similar to (infra 32:14): “tower and bastion (בֹּחַן),” bajjpred in O.F., which they erect for a siege against walled cities.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:13:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:13:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:13:4)


**עוֹרְרוּ אַרְמְנוֹתֶיהָ.** יַחֲרִיבוּ, לְשׁוֹן ״עָרוּ עָרוּ״ (תהילים קלז:ז), לְשׁוֹן ׳נְתִיצָה׳ עַד הַיְסוֹד:


**destroyed its palaces** (עוֹרְרוּ). They shall destroy. (This is) an expression like (Psalms 137:7): “Raze it, raze it (עָרוּ עָרוּ),” an expression of demolition until the very foundation.



### Verse 15

###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:15:1)


**וְנִשְׁכַּחַת צֹר.** לְפִי שֶׁמַּזְכִּירָהּ בִּלְשׁוֹן גְּנַאי, לְשׁוֹן ׳זוֹנָה׳, אָמַר ״וְנִשְׁכַּחַת״ כְּזוֹנָה שֶׁשְּׁכָחוּהָ אוֹהֲבֶיהָ, אַף הִיא תִּשָּׁכַח מֵאֵין סוֹחֲרִים וְתַגָּרִים פּוֹנִים אֵלֶיהָ, לְפִי שֶׁתִּהְיֶה חֲרֵבָה:


**that Tyre shall be forgotten** Since the prophet refers to her with an expression of degradation, with an expression comparing her to a harlot, he says, “shall be forgotten,” like a harlot whose lovers have forgotten her. She, too, shall be forgotten for want of merchants and traffickers turning to her, because she shall be destroyed.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:15:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:15:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:15:2)


**כִּימֵי מֶלֶךְ אֶחָד.** יְמֵי דָוִד שִׁבְעִים שָׁנָה הָיוּ; וְאֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מַהוּ הַסִּימָן הַזֶּה הַנִּתָּן כָּאן:


**like the days of one king** The days of David were seventy years, but I do not know why this sign is given here.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:15:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:15:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:15:3)


**יִהְיֶה לְצֹר** זִכָּרוֹן מְעַט, שֶׁתִּתְנַעֵר מִשִּׁפְלוּתָהּ וְתַחֲזוֹר לְאוֹתָן שֶׁהָיוּ רְגִילִין אֶצְלָהּ, לַחֲזוֹר אֵלֶיהָ לָשׁוּב לְקַדְמוּתָהּ:


**it shall fare with Tyre** a slight remembrance, that she shall shake herself from her humble state and appeal to those who were wont to trade with her, to return to her so that she return to her original state.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:15:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:15:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:15:4)


**כְּשִׁירַת הַזּוֹנָה.** שֶׁרוֹאָה שֶׁאֵין פּוֹנֶה אֵלֶיהָ, וְנוֹשֵׂאת קוֹל עָרֵב וְנָעִים בְּשִׁיר, אוּלַי תֶּעֱרַב עַל מְאַהֲבֶיהָ:


**like the song of the harlot** who sees that no one turns to her and raises a sweet and melodious voice in song, perhaps she will please her lovers.



### Verse 16

###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:16:1)


**הַרְבִּי שִׁיר.** כְּלוֹמַר, אַף הַרְבִּי תַּחֲנוּנִים וְהַשְׁפִּילִי גַּאֲוָתֵךְ:


**sing many songs** That is to say, also make many supplications and humble your haughtiness.



### Verse 17

###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:17:1)


**לְאֶתְנַנָּה.** לְקַדְמוּתָהּ וּלְעָשְׁרָהּ עַל יְדֵי סְחוֹרָתָהּ, וּמְכַנֶּה אוֹתָהּ בִּלְשׁוֹן גְּנַאי:


**to her hire** To her original state and to her wealth through her commerce. He denigrates her with a degrading expression.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:17:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:17:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:17:2)


**וְזָנְתָה.** וּתְסַפֵּק סְחוֹרָה, אַךְ בְּלָשׁוֹן גְּנַאי כִּנָּה אוֹתָהּ:


**and she shall have commerce** (Lit., and she shall prostitute.) She shall supply merchandise. But he denigrates her with a shameful expression.



### Verse 18

###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:18:1)


**קֹדֶשׁ לַה׳.** עֲתִידִים צַדִּיקִים לָבוֹז אוֹתָהּ כְּשֶׁיָּבֹא מֶלֶךְ הַמָּשִׁיחַ:


**holy to the Lord** The righteous are destined to plunder her when the king Messiah comes.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:18:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:18:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:18:2)


**לֹא יֵאָצֵר.** לִהְיוֹת אוֹצָר:


**it shall not be stored** to be a treasure for her kings.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:18:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:18:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:18:3)


**וְלֹא יֵחָסֵן.** לֹא יַנְחִילֶנָּה לִבְנֵיהֶם:


**and it shall not be inherited** They will not leave it over as an inheritance to their children.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 23:18:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:18:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:18:4)


**וְלִמְכַסֶּה עָתִיק.** לְמַלְבּוּשֵׁי נוֹי, **עָתִיק** מְשֻׁבָּח, כְּמוֹ ״יְדַבְּרוּ עָתָק״ (תהלים צד:ד):


**and for stately clothing** (וְלִמְכַסֶּה עָתִיק) for beautiful clothing means laudable, as (Psalms 94:4): “They speak with haughtiness (עָתָק).”



## Chapter 24


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Isaiah 24:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:1:1)


**הִנֵּה ה׳ בּוֹקֵק הָאָרֶץ וּבוֹלְקָהּ.** הֲרֵי נְבוּאָה זוֹ פֻּרְעָנוּת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, לְפִי שֶׁנִּבָּא לָהֶם נֶחָמָה זוֹ, וְהֵם עֲתִידִים לִרְאוֹת לְפָנֶיהָ צָרָה רַבָּה, לְכָךְ אָמַר לָהֶם: ״לֹא לָכֶם אֲנִי אוֹמֵר שֶׁתִּירָשׁוּהָ, כִּי הִנֵּה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בּוֹקֵק וּבוֹלֵק אֶתְכֶם, וְהַנּוֹתָרִים מִכֶּם לְיוֹם הַגְּאוּלָּה ״הֵמָּה יִשְׂאוּ קוֹלָם יָרֹנּוּ״״ (ישעיהו כד:יד), זֶהוּ סוֹף הָעִנְיָן, וְלָהֶם נִבֵּאתִי הַנְּבוּאָה הַטּוֹבָה:


**Behold the Lord empties the land and lays it waste** This prophecy represents retribution for Israel. Since he prophesied for them this consolation, and they are destined to see great distress before it, he, therefore, said to them, “Not to you do I say that you will inherit it, for, behold, the Holy One, blessed be He, empties you out and lays you waste, but those of you who survive until the day of redemption, they shall raise their voice and sing;” this is the end of the passage (v. 14), and for them have I prophesied the favorable prophecy.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 24:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:1:2)


**בּוֹקֵק.** מְרוֹקֵן:


**empties** (בּוֹקֵק) empties.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 24:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:1:3)


**וּבוֹלְקָהּ.** מַחֲרִיבָהּ:


**and lays it waste** (וּבוֹלְקָה) and lays is waste.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 24:1:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:1:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:1:4)


**וְעִוָּה פָנֶיהָ.** וְהִבְהִיל חֲשׁוּבֶיהָ. **עִוָּה** לְשׁוֹן ״נַעֲוֵיתִי מִשְּׁמוֹעַ״ (ישעיהו כא:ג):


**and He shall turn over its face** And He shall confuse its esteemed men. עִוָּה is an expression related to (supra 21:3): “I have become confused (נַעֲוֵיתִי) from hearing.”



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Isaiah 24:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:2:1)


**תוספת: וְהָיָה כָעָם כַּכֹּהֵן.** לֹא כִּשְׁאָר הוֹלְכֵי דְרָכִים, שֶׁהָאָדוֹן מוֹלִיכוֹ עַבְדּוֹ וְהַגְּבִירָה מוֹלִיכָה שִׁפְחָתָהּ, הָאָדוֹן נִכְבָּד וְהָעֶבֶד נִקְלֶה, הַגְּבִירָה נִכְבֶּדֶת וְהַשִּׁפְחָה נִקְלֵית, אֲבָל כְּשֶׁהַשַּׁבַּאי מוֹלִיךְ הַשְּׁבוּיִים, הַכֹּל שָׁוִין לְפָנָיו:


**(Addendum) And it shall be, as with the people, so with the priest** Not like other travelers, that the master is led by his slave, and the mistress is led by her maidservant; the master is esteemed and the slave is held in low esteem, the mistress is esteemed and the maidservant is held in low esteem, but when the captor leads the captives, all are equal before him. [Addendum to Rashi]


###### Rashi on Isaiah 24:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:2:2)


**כַּקּוֹנֶה כַּמּוֹכֵר.** בִּזְמַן שֶׁהָעָם יוֹשֵׁב עַל נַחֲלָתוֹ לָבֶטַח, הַקּוֹנֶה שָׂמֵחַ וְהַמּוֹכֵר עָצֵב שֶׁלֹּא יָשׁוּב מִמְכָּרוֹ, אֲבָל כְּשֶׁהַשַּׁבַּאי מוֹלִיכָם, הַקּוֹנֶה אַל יִשְׂמַח וְהַמּוֹכֵר אַל יִתְאַבֵּל. וְכֵן כַּמַּלְוֶה כַּלֹּוֶה שְׁנֵיהֶם שָׁוִים, שֶׁהַלֹּוֶה אֵין לוֹ לִפְרוֹעַ, וְהַמַּלְוֶה אִם לֹא הִלְוָה לָזֶה הָיָה הַשַּׁבַּאי נוֹטְלוֹ כְּמוֹ כֵן. **כַּנֹּשֶׁה כַּאֲשֶׁר נוֹשֶׁה בּוֹ** – לוֹה נוֹפֵל בְּכֶסֶף, וְנוֹשֶׁה נוֹפֵל בְּכָל שְׁאָר דְּבָרִים, כְּגוֹן: יַיִן וְשֶׁמֶן וּתְבוּאָה וּדְבַשׁ, כְּדִכְתִיב (דברים כד:י): ״כִּי תַשֶּׁה בְרֵעֲךָ מַשַּׁאת מְאוּמָה״. עד כאן:


**as with the buyer, so with the seller** When the people lives in its land securely, the buyer is happy and the seller is unhappy, since he will not return to the land he sold, but when the captor leads them, the buyer will not rejoice and the seller will not mourn, and so, as with the lender, so with the borrower, both are equal, for the borrower has nothing to pay, and the lender, had he not lent to this one, the captor would have taken it. Likewise, as with the creditor, so with the one who owes him. The word לֹֹוֶה applies to money and נֹשֶה applies to other commodities, such as wine, oil, grain, and honey, as it is written (Deut. 24:10): “When you lend your brother anything as a loan.” [Addendum to Rashi]



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Isaiah 24:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:3:1)


**הִבּוֹק תִּבּוֹק.** תִּתְרוֹקֵן:


**shall be emptied** (וְהִבּוֹק תִּבּוֹק) shall be emptied.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 24:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:3:2)


**הִבּוֹז תִּבּוֹז.** לְשׁוֹן בִּזָּה וְשָׁלָל:


**and it shall be pillaged** (וְהִבּוֹז תִּבּוֹז) an expression of pillage and spoils.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Isaiah 24:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:4:1)


**נָבְלָה.** כְּמוֹ ״וְהֶעָלֶה נָבֵל״ (ירמיהו ח:יג), לְשׁוֹן ׳כָּמַשׁ׳ וְתַשּׁוּת כֹּחַ:


**it has withered** (נָבְלָה) Comp. (Jeremiah 8:13) “And the leaf has withered (נָבֵל).” An expression of withering and languishing.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 24:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:4:2)


**אֻמְלְלָה.** לְשׁוֹן ׳שִׁפְלוּת׳, כְּמוֹ ״הַיְּהוּדִים הָאֻמְלָלִים״ (נחמיה ג:לד):


**has been humbled** (אֻמְלְלָה), an expression of humility. Comp. (Neh. 3: 34) “humble Jews (אֻמְלָלִים).”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 24:4:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:4:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:4:3)


**תֵּבֵל.** הִיא אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהִיא מְתֻבֶּלֶת בְּמִצְוֹת הַרְבֵּה:


**The land** (תֵּבֵל) This is the land of Israel, which is spiced (מְתֻבֶּלֶת) with many commandments.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 24:4:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:4:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:4:4)


**מְרוֹם עַם הָאָרֶץ.** גָּאוֹן עַם הָאָרֶץ:


**the highest of the people of the land** the pride of the people of the land.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Isaiah 24:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:5:1)


**וְהָאָרֶץ חָנְפָה.** כְּמִין חֲנִיפוּת: עוֹשָׂה עֵשֶׂב וְאֵינוֹ עוֹשֶׂה קָמָה, מַרְאָה קָמָה וְאֵין חִטִּין בְּקַשֶּׁיהָ:


**And the land has deceived** This is a sort of deceit; it produces grass but does not produce growing grain; it shows growing grain, but there are no wheat kernels in its stalks (lit., in its straws).


###### Rashi on Isaiah 24:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:5:2)


**תַּחַת יוֹשְׁבֶיהָ.** בִּשְׁבִיל יוֹשְׁבֶיהָ:


**because of its inhabitants** (תַּחַת יוֹשְׁבֶיהָ) lit., under its inhabitants; because of its inhabitants.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 24:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:5:3)


**בְּרִית עוֹלָם.** הִיא הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁקִּבְּלוּ בִּבְרִית:


**the everlasting covenant** That is the Torah that they received with a covenant.



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Isaiah 24:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:6:1)


**עַל כֵּן אָלָה.** בַּעֲוֹן שְׁבוּעַת שָׁוְא:


**Therefore, an oath** For the sin of vain oaths. ([Manuscripts read:] Because of the sin of false oaths.)


###### Rashi on Isaiah 24:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:6:2)


**חָרוּ.** לְשׁוֹן יָבֵשׁ וְצָמָא בְּחוֹם חֹרֶב, כְּמוֹ ״נִחַר מַפֻּחַ״ (ירמיה ו:כט):


**were dried up** (חָרוּ) an expression of dryness and thirst through the heat of dryness. Comp. (Jer. 6: 29) “The bellows are dried (נִחַר).”



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Isaiah 24:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:8:1)

**The joy of the drums** that you said (supra 22:13), “And behold, joy and happiness.”

**וּשְׁאִיָּה יֻכַּת שָׁעַר.** עַל יְדֵי שְׁאִיַּת גַּלְמוּד, שֶׁיִּהְיוּ הַבָּתִּים שׁוֹאִים מֵאֵין יוֹשֵׁב, יֻכְּתוּ הַשְּׁעָרִים עַל יְדֵי מַזִּיקִין:

**like the cutting of the olive tree** that leaves over berries at the tip of the uppermost bough.



### Verse 14

###### Rashi on Isaiah 24:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:14:1)

###### Rashi on Isaiah 24:14:2

**they shall shout for joy more than [by the] sea** (Lit., they shall shout for joy from the sea.) More than they shouted for joy by the sea during the redemption from Egypt.



### Verse 15

###### Rashi on Isaiah 24:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:15:1)


**עַל כֵּן בָּאֻרִים.** תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״בְּמֵיתֵי נְהוֹרָא לְצַדִּיקַיָּא״, עַל שְׁתֵּי (ספרים אחרים: מְאוֹרוֹת) שֶׁל גָּאוּלַת בָּבֶל וְשֶׁל אֱדוֹם. וּמְנַחֵם אָמַר (מחברת: אר) ׳אוּרִים׳ לְשׁוֹן ׳נְקִיעִים וּסְעִיפִים׳ שֶׁהָיוּ בּוֹרְחִים שָׁם, וְכֵן ״אוּר כַּשְׂדִּים״ (בראשית יא:כח) בִּקְעַת כַּשְׂדִּים, וְכֵן ״מְאוּרַת צִפְעוֹנִי״ (ישעיהו יא:ח) נֶקַע חוֹר מְעוֹנָתוֹ:


**Therefore, for the lights** (בָּאֻרִים). Jonathan paraphrases: When lights come to the righteous, concerning the two good tidings, both that of the redemption from Babylon and that of Edom. ([Most manuscripts read:] Jonathan paraphrases: When lights come to the righteous, concerning the two lights, etc.) And Menachem stated (Machbereth, p. 32) that אֻרִים is an expression of holes and crevices where they were fleeing, and so (Gen. 11:28): “אוּר, the valley of the Chaldees,” and so (supra 11: 8): “And on the hole (מְאוּרַת) of an adder,” the hole of its dwelling.



### Verse 16

###### Rashi on Isaiah 24:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:16:1)


**מִכְּנַף הָאָרֶץ.** תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״מִבֵּית מַקְדְּשָׁא״, שֶׁהוּא בְּסוֹף אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּמִזְרָחָהּ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁנִינוּ (מעשר שני ה ב): לוֹד מִן הַמַּעֲרָב וְיַרְדֵּן מִן הַמִּזְרָח, נִמְצָא מִירוּשָׁלַיִם לְיַרְדֵּן מַהֲלַךְ יוֹם. וַאֲנִי אוֹמֵר לְפִי פְּשׁוּטוֹ: שָׁמַעְנוּ מֵאֲחוֹרֵי הַפַּרְגּוֹד שֶׁעֲתִידִין לְהַעֲלוֹת זְמִירוֹת מִכְּנַף הָאָרֶץ, וּמָה הֵן הַזְּמִירוֹת? **צְבִי לַצַּדִּיק** – עָתִיד לִהְיוֹת מַצָּב וּתְקוּמָה לַצַּדִּיקִים:


**From the end of the earth** Jonathan paraphrases: From the Temple, which is at the edge of the land of Israel in the east, as we learned: (Maaser Sheni 5:2) [According to Lev. 19:23 25, the produce of the vineyards produced during the first three years of its growth may neither be eaten nor may any benefit be derived therefrom. The produce of the fourth year must be taken to Jerusalem and eaten there. If this is inconvenient, the owner may redeem the produce and take the redemption money to Jerusalem, where he must buy food to eat with the sanctity of כֶּרֶם רְבָעִי, the fourth year vineyard. The Rabbis decreed, however, that within a day’s journey from Jerusalem, all produce must be brought to Jerusalem, and the owner has no option to redeem it. The following Mishnah delineates the boundaries of this area.] Lod from the west, and the Jordan from the east. It is found that from Jerusalem to the Jordan is a day’s journey. But I say according to the simple meaning, that we heard from behind the heavenly Curtain that they are destined to raise their voices in song from the edge of the earth. Now what are the songs? “The righteous shall be upraised.” There shall be a position and an upraising for the righteous.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 24:16:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:16:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:16:2)


**וָאֹמַר רָזִי לִי וגו׳.** אוֹי לִי שֶׁנִּגְלוּ לִי שְׁנֵי רָזִים: רָז פֻּרְעָנוּת וְרָז יְשׁוּעָה, וַהֲרֵי תִּרְחַק הַיְשׁוּעָה עַד שֶׁיָּבֹאוּ אוֹיְבִים, בּוֹזְזִים אַחַר בּוֹזְזִים אֲחֵרִים וְשׁוֹדְדִים אַחֲרֵי שׁוֹדְדִים (סנהדרין צד א). חָמֵשׁ בְּגִידוֹת אֲמוּרוֹת כָּאן:


**And I said, I have my secret; I have my secret; woe is to me!** Woe is to me that these two secrets have been revealed to me, the secret of retribution and the secret of salvation, for the salvation will be far off until enemies come, plunderers after plunderers, and marauders after marauders (San. 94a). Five instances of treachery are stated here, corresponding to Babylon, Media, Persia, Greece, and Edom, who will enslave Israel before their redemption, and after these plunderings.

**Fright and a pit and a trap [shall come] upon you** upon the peoples dwelling in the land.

**פַּחַת.** גֻּמָּא לִפּוֹל בָּהּ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּפָרֵשׁ וְאוֹמֵר:


**a pit** a hole in which to fall, as he goes on to state.



### Verse 18

###### Rashi on Isaiah 24:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:18:1)


**הַנָּס (מפני) [מִקּוֹל] הַפַּחַד יִפֹּל אֶל הַפַּחַת וְגוֹ׳** – הַנִּמְלָט מֵחֶרֶב מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף יִפּוֹל אֶל חֶרֶב מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד, וְהַנִּמְלָט מִשָּׁם **יִלָּכֵד בַּפַּח** בְּמִלְחֶמֶת גּוֹג:


**he who flees from the sound of the fright shall fall into the pit. etc.** Whoever escapes the sword of the Messiah the son of Joseph shall fall into the sword of the Messiah the son of David, and whoever escapes from there shall be snared in the trap of the wars of Gog.



### Verse 19

###### Rashi on Isaiah 24:19:1

**רֹעָה הִתְרֹעֲעָה.** לְשׁוֹן שֶׁבֶר, כְּמוֹ (תהלים ב:ט) ״תְּרֹעֵם בְּשֵׁבֶט בַּרְזֶל״:


**The earth has broken** (רֹעָה הִתְרֹעֲעָה) an expression of breaking. Comp. (Ps. 2:9): “You shall break them (תְּרֹעֵם) with an iron rod.”

###### Rashi on Isaiah 24:20:1

**כַּמְּלוּנָה.** סֻכַּת נוֹצְרִים שֶׁבְּרֹאשׁ הָאִילָן:


**like a lodge** a booth of the watchmen at the top of a tree.

###### Rashi on Isaiah 24:21:1
