**צְבָא הַמָּרוֹם.** יַפִּיל שָׂרֵי הָאֻמּוֹת תְּחִלָּה (מכילתא בשלח שירה ב):


**the host of heaven** He shall cast down the heavenly princes of the nations first.



### Verse 22

###### Rashi on Isaiah 24:22:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:22:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:22:1)


**וְאֻסְּפוּ.** הָעַכּוּ״ם **אֲסֵפָה,** שֶׁהוּא לְרָעָתָם, לְהַכְנִיס **אַסִּיר** אֶל **בּוֹר** הַמּוּכָן לוֹ, מְחֻיָּבֵי גֵּיהִנֹּם לַגֵּיהִנֹּם:


**And they shall be gathered** a gathering that is to their detriment, i.e., to bring a prisoner into a dungeon prepared for him, those sentenced to Gehinnom to be brought into Gehinnom.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 24:22:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:22:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:22:2)


**וְסֻגְּרוּ עַל מַסְגֵּר.** הֵם שִׁבְעָה מְדוֹרֵי גֵּיהִנֹּם:


**and they shall be shut up in the prison** They are the seven compartments of Gehinnom.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 24:22:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:22:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:22:3)


**וּמֵרֹב יָמִים יִפָּקֵדוּ.** עֲוֹנוֹת יָמִים רַבִּים יִפָּקְדוּ עֲלֵיהֶם, וְזֶהוּ שֶׁיִּסֵּד הַקָּלִירִי (בסלוק של יוצר דפרשת זכור): ״לְרֹב יָמִים לְהִמָּנוֹת, לַחְשׁוֹב לָהֶם חֶשְׁבּוֹנוֹת״:


**and [sins] of many days shall be visited [upon them]** Sins of many days shall be visited upon them. This is what the Kalir (R. Eleazar son of R. Kalir in his final liturgical poem for Parshath Zachor) established: “From many days to be counted, to reckon their reckonings.”



### Verse 23

###### Rashi on Isaiah 24:23:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:23:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:23:1)


**וְחָפְרָה הַלְּבָנָה וגו׳.** תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״וְיִבְהֲתוּן דְּפָלְחִין לְסִיהֲרָא וְיִתְכַּנְעוּן דְּסָגְדִין לְשִׁמְשָׁא״:


**And the moon shall be ashamed, etc.** Jonathan paraphrases: And the worshippers of the moon shall be ashamed, and the worshippers of the sun shall be humbled.



## Chapter 25


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Isaiah 25:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:1:1)


**עֵצוֹת מֵרָחוֹק אֱמוּנָה אֹמֶן.** עֵצוֹת שֶׁיָּעַצְתָּ מֵרָחוֹק לְאַבְרָהָם בִּבְרִית בֵּין הַבְּתָרִים:


**counsels from long ago in true faith** Counsels that You advised from long ago to Abraham in the Covenant between the Parts.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 25:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:1:2)


**אֱמוּנָה אֹמֶן.** אֱמוּנָה נֶאֱמֶנֶת. **אֹמֶן** כְּמוֹ ׳אֹהֶל׳, ׳אֹכֶל׳, וְאֵינוֹ לְשׁוֹן פּוֹעֵל אֶלָּא לְשׁוֹן מִפְעָל, אבוירמנ״ט בלע״ז:


**true faith** (אֱמוּנָה אֹמֶן). אֹמֶן is like אֹהֶל, tent, אֹכֶל, food, and it is not a verb in present tense but an expression of a noun, obrement (truth) in O.F.



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Isaiah 25:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:2:1)


**כִּי שַׂמְתָּ.** הַר שֵׂעִיר **מֵעִיר לְגָל**:


**For You have made** Mount Seir from a city into a heap.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 25:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:2:2)


**אַרְמוֹן זָרִים מֵעִיר.** מָעוֹן שֶׁעָשׂוּ בְּעִירְךָ, שֶׁהֶחֱרִיבוּהָ, תִּתֵּן אַרְמְנוֹתֶיהָ חֻרְבָּן, אֲשֶׁר **לְעוֹלָם לֹא יִבָּנֶה**:


**a palace of strangers, because of the city** Because of the iniquity they committed in Your city, that they destroyed it, You shall make its palaces a ruin, which shall never be rebuilt.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Isaiah 25:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:4:1)


**מַחְסֶה מִזֶּרֶם.** כִּסּוּי אֹהֶל לְהַצִּיל מִזֶּרֶם, וְ**צֵל** לְהָגֵן **מֵחֹרֶב**. וּמַהוּ אוֹתוֹ זֶרֶם? הוּא **רוּחַ עָרִיצִים**, כִּי רוּחָם דִּמָּה לְזֶרֶם הַשּׁוֹטֵף בְּקִיר וּמַפִּילוֹ:


**a shelter from pouring rain** a covering of a tent to save from pouring rain and a shade to protect from heat. Now, what is that pouring rain? A spirit of tyrants, for their spirit is like a stream that floods the wall and causes it to fall.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Isaiah 25:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:5:1)


**כְּחֹרֶב בְּצָיוֹן.** בְּעֵת יֹבֶשׁ, שֶׁמְיַבֵּשׁ הַזְּרָעִים לְהִתְמוֹלֵל, כֵּן **תַּכְנִיעַ שְׁאוֹן זָרִים**:


**Like heat in the dry season** In the dry season, when the seeds dry out to be cut off, so shall You humble the multitude of the strangers.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 25:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:5:2)


**חֹרֶב בְּצֵל עָב.** כְּשֶׁהַמַּיִם מִתְקַשְּׁרִים בְּעָנָן **עָב** בִּימֵי הַשָּׁרָב, שֶׁהַכֹּל שְׂמֵחִים בּוֹ, כֵּן **יַעֲנֶה** שִׁיר הַצַּדִּיקִים עַל **זְמִיר עָרִיצִים** וּמַפַּלְתָּן:


**like heat with a thick cloud** When the heavens thicken with thick clouds in the hot season, with which everyone rejoices, so will the song of the righteous be sung concerning the cutting down of the tyrants and their downfall.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 25:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:5:3)


**זְמִיר.** לשון ״לא תִזְמֹר״ (ויקרא כה:ד):


**the downfall of** (lit., the cutting down of. זְמִיר). An expression related to (Lev. 25:4): “You shall not prune (תִזְמֹר).”



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Isaiah 25:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:6:1)


**וְעָשָׂה ה׳ צְבָאוֹת לְכָל הָעַמִּים.** כְּשֶׁיָּבֹאוּ לִצְבֹּא עַל יְרוּשָׁלַיִם:


**And the Lord of Hosts shall make for all the peoples** when they come to mobilize against Jerusalem.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 25:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:6:2)


**מִשְׁתֵּה שְׁמָנִים.** שֶׁהֵם סְבוּרִים שֶׁיְּהֵא נוֹחַ לָהֶם כְּשֶׁמֶן, יֵהָפֵךְ לְ**מִשְׁתֵּה שְׁמָרִים**:


**a feast of fat things** which they think that it will be easy for them like fat, which is smooth and soft, will be converted for them to a feast of dregs.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 25:6:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:6:3)


**שְׁמָנִים מְמֻחָיִם.** נוֹחִים וְשְׁמֵנִים כְּמוֹחַ עֲצָמוֹת, יִהְיֶה **שְׁמָרִים מְזֻקָּקִים** מִכָּל מַשְׁקֶה שֶׁמֶן וְיַיִן, שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא שָׁם אֶלָּא שְׁמָרִים לְבַדָּם; וְכָל זֶה בְּמִלְחֲמוֹת גּוֹג וּמָגוֹג:


**fat things full of marrow** soft and fat like the marrow of bones, will be dregs well refined from any liquid of wine or oil, for there will be there only the dregs. All this will be in the war of Gog and Magog.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Isaiah 25:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:7:1)


**הַלּוֹט.** הַכִּסּוּי. **הַלּוֹט עַל [כָּל] הָעַמִּים.** הַמְכַסֶּה אֶת כָּל הָעַמִּים, **הַלּוֹט** כְּמוֹ ״וַיָּלֶט פָּנָיו״ (מלכים א יט:יג), ״הִנֵּה הִיא לוּטָה בַשִּׂמְלָה״ (שמואל א כא:י):


**the covering** The covering that covers all the people. Heb. הלוט, similar to “he wrapped his face” (I Kings 19:13), and to “behold, it is wrapped in a garment” (I Samuel 21:10).


###### Rashi on Isaiah 25:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:7:2)


**וְהַמַּסֵּכָה.** לְשׁוֹן נְסִיכוּת וְשָׂרָרָה:


**and the kingdom** (Heb. וְהַמַּסֵּכָה.) An expression of kingdom and ruling.



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Isaiah 25:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:8:1)


**בִּלַּע הַמָּוֶת.** יְכַסֶּנּוּ וְיַעֲלִימֶנּוּ עוֹלָמִית מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל (פסחים סח א):


**He has concealed death** He will cover it and hide it forever from Israel.



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Isaiah 25:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:9:1)


**וְאָמַר.** עַמּוֹ **בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא ״הִנֵּה וְגוֹ׳״**:


**And they shall say** (Lit., and he shall say, i.e.,) His people (shall say) on that day, “Behold, etc.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 25:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:9:2)


**קִוִּינוּ לוֹ וְיוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ.** הָיִינוּ מְקַוִּים לוֹ שֶׁיּוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ:


**we hoped for Him that he would save us** We were hoping for Him that He would save us.



### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Isaiah 25:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:10:1)


**כִּי תָנוּחַ יַד ה׳.** גְּבוּרָתוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם:


**For the hand of the Lord shall rest** The might of the Omnipresent.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 25:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:10:2)


**וְנָדוֹשׁ.** יְהֵא נָדוֹשׁ:


**shall be trampled** וְנָדוֹשׁ, shall be trampled.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 25:10:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:10:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:10:3)


**תַּחְתָּיו.** בִּמְקוֹמוֹ. **וְנָדוֹשׁ** כְּמוֹ ״וְנָרוֹץ הַגַּלְגַּל״ (קהלת יב:ו):


**in its place** (תַּחְתָּיו, lit., under him,) in its place. וְנָדוֹשׁ is of the same structure as (Eccl. 12: 6) “And the wheel is crushed (וְנָרוֹץ),” the “nun” indicating the passive voice.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 25:10:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:10:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:10:4)


**מַתְבֵּן.** תֶּבֶן:


**straw** (מַתְבֵּן) derived from תֶּבֶן.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 25:10:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:10:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:10:5)


**מַדְמֵנָה.** טִיט, וְכֵן ״לְדֹמֶן עַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה״ (ירמיה ח:ב):


**mire** (מַדְמֵנָה) mire. Comp. (Jer. 8:2) “For dung (לְדֹמֶן) on the face of the earth.”



### Verse 11

###### Rashi on Isaiah 25:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:11:1)


**וּפֵרַשׂ יָדָיו.** וְשָׁבַר יָדוֹן וּזְרוֹעוֹתָיו בְּסִפּוּק כַּפַּיִם בִּבְכִי:


**And he shall spread out his hands** (וּפֵרַשׂ) He shall break his hands and his arms by clapping his hands in weeping.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 25:11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:11:2)


**הַשֹּׂחֶה.** הַשָּׁט בַּמַּיִם:


**the swimmer** (הַשׂחֶה) the one who floats upon the water.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 25:11:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:11:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:11:3)


**לִשְׂחוֹת.** לָשׁוּט, וְכֵן ״מֵי שָׂחוּ״ (יחזקאל מז:ה):


**to swim** (לִשְׂחוֹת) to float, as: (Ezekiel 47:5) “Water fit to swim in (מֵי שָׂחוּ).”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 25:11:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:11:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:11:4)


**וְהִשְׁפִּיל.** הַמַּשְׁפִּיל אֶת **גַּאֲוָתוֹ**:


**and He shall humble** the One Who humbles his haughtiness.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 25:11:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:11:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:11:5)


**עִם אָרְבּוֹת יָדָיו.** לָשׁוֹן ״וְאָרַב לוֹ״ (דברים יט:יא), תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״אַשְׁוַת יְדוֹהִי״ – מָקוֹם שֶׁהוּא שָׂם לוֹ יָדַיִם לֶאֱרוֹב, וְהֵם מִגְדָּלִים גְּבוֹהִים. אַשְׁוַת – חוֹמוֹת וּמִגְדָּלִים, כְּמוֹ ״נָפְלוּ אָשְׁיוֹתֶיהָ״ (ירמיהו נ:טו):


**with the cunning of His hands** (אָרְבוֹת,) an expression similar to (Deut. 19:11): “And he lay in wait for him (וְאָרַב).” Jonathan renders: The layings of His hands. The place where He lays His hands to lie in wait. These are the high towers. אַשְׁוַת is an expression of walls and towers, as: (Jer. 50: 15) “Her walls fell (אָשְׁיוֹתֶיהָ).”



### Verse 12

###### Rashi on Isaiah 25:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/25:12:1)


**מִשְׂגַּב חוֹמֹתֶיךָ.** לְמוֹאָב הוּא אוֹמֵר:


**the strength of your walls** He addresses Moab.



## Chapter 26


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:1:1)


**עִיר עָז לָנוּ יְשׁוּעָה יָשִׁית.** הָעִיר יְרוּשָׁלַיִם, שֶׁהָיָה מֵאָז תָּמִיד לָנוּ לְעוֹז, יְשׁוּעָה יָשִׁית הַמּוֹשִׁיעַ אֶת חוֹמוֹתֶיהָ וְאֶת חֵילָה:


**The city that was our strength, salvation shall He place** The city of Jerusalem, which was always our strength from time immemorial, the Savior shall place salvation for its walls and its bulwark.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:1:2)


**וָחֵל.** חוֹמָה נְמוּכָה שֶׁלִּפְנֵי הַחוֹמָה הַגְבוֹהַּ:


**and a bulwark** a low wall before the high wall.



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:2:1)


**פִּתְחוּ שְׁעָרִים.** שֶׁלָּהּ, **וְיָבֹא** לְתוֹכָהּ **גּוֹי צַדִּיק**:


**Open the gates** I.e., open her gates, and let a righteous nation,


###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:2:2)


**שֹׁמֵר.** שֶׁשָּׁמַר וְצִפָּה בְּגָלוּתוֹ יָמִים רַבִּים לֶאֱמוּנָתוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, שֶׁיְּקַיֵּם הַבְטָחָתוֹ שֶׁהִבְטִיחַ עַל פִּי נְבִיאָיו לְגָאֳלָם:


**awaiting**, that waited and longed in its exile many days for the faith of the Holy One, blessed be He, that He fulfill His promise through His prophets, to redeem them.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:2:3)


**שֹׁמֵר.** מַמְתִּין, וְכֵן (בראשית לז:יא) ״וְאָבִיו שָׁמַר אֶת הַדָּבָר״, וְכֵן (דברים ז:יב) ״וְשָׁמַר ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְךָ״:


**awaiting** (שֹׁמֵר) waiting. Comp. (Gen. 37:11) “And his father awaited (שָׁמַר) the matter.” Similarly (Deut. 7:12), “And the Lord, your God, shall await (וְשָׁמַר) the covenant for you.”



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:3:1)


**יֵצֶר.** שֶׁהָיָה **סָמוּךְ** עַל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְנִשְׁעָן עָלָיו בְּחָזְקָה, שֶׁלֹּא זָז מֵאֱמוּנָתוֹ בִּשְׁבִיל שׁוּם אֵימָה וְיִסּוּרִין:


**The creature** that relied on the Holy One, blessed be He, and depended on Him steadfastly, that did not deviate from his faith because of any fear or torture.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:3:2)


**תִּצֹּר.** שֶׁיְּהֵא **שָׁלוֹם, כִּי בְךָ** הָיָה **בָּטוּחַ**, לְפִיכָךְ הָגוּן לְךָ לְנָצְרוֹ:


**You shall guard** that there be peace, for he trusted in You. It is, therefore, fitting for You to guard him.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:4:1)


**כִּי בְּיָהּ ה׳.** כִּי יֵשׁ לִסְמֹךְ עָלָיו, שֶׁהוּא ״דְּחִילָא ה׳״, סֶלַע וְ**צוּר** מַחֲסֶה **עוֹלָמִים**:


**for in Yah, the Lord** For we must rely on Him for He is the fear of God, the rock and everlasting shelter.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:5:1)


**יֹשְׁבֵי מָרוֹם.** צוֹר וְשָׁאָר אֲרָצוֹת:


**the inhabitants of the high places** Tyre and other lands. ([Manuscripts yield:] Tyre and Rome and Italy. [Parshandatha])



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:6:1)


**רַגְלֵי עָנִי.** מֶלֶךְ הַמָּשִׁיחַ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ: ״עָנִי וְרֹכֵב עַל הַחֲמוֹר״ (זכריה ט:ט):


**the feet of a poor man** The King Messiah, who is referred to as a poor man riding on a donkey (Zech. 9:9).


###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:6:2)


**פַּעֲמֵי דַלִּים.** יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהָיוּ דַלִּים עַד הֵנָּה:


**the soles of the impoverished** Israel, who were heretofore impoverished.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:7:1)


**אֹרַח לַצַּדִּיק מֵישָׁרִים.** אֹרַח שֶׁתְּהֵא מִישׁוֹר לְקִבּוּל שְׂכָרוֹ שֶׁל צַדִּיק, אַתָּה ה׳ שֶׁאַתָּה אֵל **יָשָׁר תְּפַלֵּס מַעְגַּל צַדִּיק**, לְהוֹלִיכוֹ בְּאוֹתוֹ אוֹרַח שֶׁיְּקַבֵּל שְׂכָרוֹ. וְהַצַּדִּיק הוּא יַעֲקֹב וְזַרְעוֹ, וְכֹה פִּתְרוֹנוֹ: אֹרַח לַצַּדִּיק לִטּוֹל שָׂכָר מֵישָׁרִים שֶׁנּוֹהֵג בָּהֶן:


**The way of the righteous that is straight** A way that is straight for the reception of the reward of the righteous You, O God, Who are an upright God, shall weigh the path of the righteous man, to lead him in that way, that he receive his reward. The righteous man is Jacob and his descendants. We must render in this manner: the straight way for the righteous man. ([Printed editions read:] The way for the righteous man to receive the reward for the upright deeds he performed.)


###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:7:2)


**יָשָׁר.** אַתָּה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא **מַעְגַּל** רַגְלֵי הַ**צַּדִּיק תְּפַלֵּס** לוֹ לְאוֹתוֹ אֹרַח. פִּלּוּס זֶה לְשׁוֹן קונטרפיי״ש בלע״ז, כְּמֶלֶךְ הַיּוֹשֵׁב וּמְחַשֵּׁב וּמְשַׁקֵּל בְּלִבּוֹ אֵיזֶה יִכְשַׁר, הַזֶּה אוֹ זֶה, כָּךְ הַיָּשָׁר בְּלִבּוֹ לְהוֹלִיכוֹ בְּדֶרֶךְ קִבּוּל שָׂכָר עַל כָּל אֲשֶׁר הִנְהִיג מַעֲשָׂיו לְפָנֶיךָ בְּכִשְׁרוֹן:


**O Upright One** You, the Holy One, blessed be He, the path of the feet of the righteous man, You shall weigh that way for him. This weighing is an expression of kontrepajjs in O.F., You counterbalance, equalize. Like a king who sits and thinks and weighs in his mind, which way is better, this one or that one. So, judge with equity to lead him in the way of receiving the reward for performing his deeds before You with propriety.

**Even [for] the way of Your judgments, O Lord, have we hoped for You** When we looked forward to receiving benefit from You, likewise we hoped that You would show us the way of the judgments of Your revenge upon the wicked. ([Manuscripts read:] Upon the wicked Esau.)

###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:10:1)


**יֻחַן רָשָׁע בַּל לָמַד צֶדֶק.** וְכִי יֵשׁ לְךָ לָחוֹן אֶת עֵשָׂו הָרָשָׁע אֲשֶׁר דָּר בֵּין שְׁנֵי צַדִּיקִים וְלֹא לָמַד צֶדֶק (סנהדרין לט ב):


**Shall the wicked be favored who did not learn righteousness** Should you favor the wicked Esau, who lived between two righteous men and did not learn righteousness?


###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:10:2

**בְּאֶרֶץ נְכֹחוֹת.** יְרוּשָׁלַיִם וּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, **יְעַוֵּל** לִשְׁלוֹל וְלָבֹז וּלְהַשְׁחִית:


**in the land of uprightness** Jerusalem and the Temple, he will deal unjustly, to pillage and spoil and to destroy.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:10:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:10:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:10:3)


**וּבַל יִרְאֶה גֵּאוּת ה׳.** לֹא חָשַׁב בְּעֵינָיו גָּדְלְךָ וְגַאֲוָתְךָ, **וּבַל יִרְאֶה** לְשׁוֹן ׳רְגִילוּת וּתְמִידוּת׳: לֹא רָאָה, לֹא חָשַׁב, כְּמוֹ ״כָּכָה יַעֲשֶׂה אִיּוֹב״ (איוב א:ה):


**and he does not see the pride of the Lord** He did not regard Your pride and greatness. The expression, וּבַל יִרְאֶה, (lit., he shall not see,) is an expression of a habitual act, meaning: he did not see, he did not regard. Comp. (Job 1:5) “In this manner, Job was wont to do (יַעֲשֶׂה).”



### Verse 11

###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:11:1)


**ה׳ רָמָה יָדְךָ וגו׳.** רָאִיתִי מִדְרְשֵׁי אַגָּדָה רַבִּים לַמִּקְרָאוֹת שֶׁל פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ, עֶלְיוֹנָה וְתַחְתּוֹנָה, וְאֵינָם מְיֻשָּׁבִים אוֹ עַל דִּקְדּוּק הַלָּשׁוֹן אוֹ עַל סֵדֶר הַמִּקְרָאוֹת, וְהֻצְרַכְתִּי לְבָאֵר אוֹתָהּ עַל אָפְנֵי סִדְרָהּ. וּמִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה יֵשׁ שֶׁמְּבַקֵּשׁ הַנָּבִיא וְכוּ׳, אָמַר לוֹ: מוּטָב שֶׁיֶּחֱזוּ וְיֵבוֹשׁוּ (אליהו זוטא כא). וְאֵין זֶה אַחַר הַלָּשׁוֹן, שֶׁאֵין כָּתוּב כָּאן ׳הָרִימָה יָדְךָ׳. וְעוֹד, שֶׁאַף הַתֵּיבָה חֲלוּקָה מִתֵּיבָה כַּיּוֹצֵא בָּהּ; כָּל ׳יָד רָמָה׳ שֶׁבַּמִּקְרָא טַעֲמוֹ לְמַטָּה וְזֶה טַעֲמוֹ לְמַעְלָה, כְּמוֹ (בראשית לז:ז) ״הִנֵּה קָמָה אֲלֻמָּתִי״, וּכְמוֹ (רות א:טו) ״הִנֵּה שָׁבָה יְבִמְתֵּךְ״, שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ לְשׁוֹן עָבָר. אַף זֶה – **ה׳**, נִסְתַּלְּקָה יַד גְּבוּרָתְךָ מֵעַל צָרֶיךָ, **בַּל** יִרְאוּ גְּבוּרָתְךָ כִּי רָאוּ דַּרְכָּם צָלְחָה. בְּבַקָּשָׁה מִמְּךָ, יֶחֱזוּ וְיֵבוֹשׁוּ:


**O Lord, Your hand has been taken away** I have seen many Aggadic Midrashim on the verses of the above section and the following, but they are not appropriate, either because of the grammatical forms of the language or because of the context of the verses. I had to explain it according to its order. There is an Aggadic Midrash that states that the prophet begs that the nations not see the bounty of the Holy One, blessed be He, when He lavishes good upon Israel. The Holy One, blessed be He, replied, “It is better that they see and be ashamed,” (Eliyahu Zuta ch. 21). (The Midrash explains the verse as follows: O Lord, take away Your hand, so that they see not. I.e., the prophet begs that God conceal His might from the nations that they see it not. Thereupon, God replies, “Let them see and be ashamed...”) This does not fit with the language, however, since it does not say, “Raise Your hand.” Moreover, this word differs from all similar words. Every יָד רָמָה is accented on the final syllable, whereas this one is accented on the first syllable. Comp. (Gen. 37:7) “Behold, my sheaf rose (קָמָה).” Comp. also (Ruth 1:9) “Behold your sister in law has returned (שָׁבָה).” All of these are in the past tense. This too is to be explained: The hand of Your might has been taken away from upon Your enemies so that they see not Your might for they have seen that their way has prospered. I beg of You, let them see and be ashamed.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:11:2)


**קִנְאַת עָם** בַּטּוֹבָה שֶׁתֵּיטִיב לְעַמְּךָ, **אַף** בְּעַצְמָן יִרְאוּ מִשְׁפַּט נִקְמָתְךָ שֶׁ**תֹּאכְלֵם** הָ**אֵשׁ**:


**the envy of a people** Let them see the bounty that You shall lavish upon Your people, Even they themselves shall see the judgment of Your vengeance, that the fire (of envy) shall consume them.

###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:12:1

**תִּשְׁפֹּת.** תָּכִין, וְכֵן ״שְׁפֹת הַסִּיר״ (מלכים ב ד:לח), וְכֵן ״לַעֲפַר מָוֶת תִּשְׁפְּתֵנִי״ (תהלים כב:טז), וְיֵשׁ לִפְתּוֹר אֶת כֻּלָּן לְשׁוֹן ׳שִׂימָה׳ – תָּשִׁית שָׁלוֹם לָנוּ:

You shall establish peace for us.

###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:13:2

**זוּלָתֶךָ.** בְּדָבָר שֶׁלֹּא כִּרְצוֹנְךָ, דָּרוֹשׁ לֵאלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים, לַעֲבוֹר עַל תּוֹרָתֶךָ, וַאֲנַחְנוּ **לְבַד בְּךָ** הִזְכַּרְנוּ, וְלֹא **נַזְכִּיר** שֵׁם אֱלֹהוּתוֹ בְּאֵל אַחֵר אֶלָּא בּוֹ לְבַדּוֹ:

### Verse 14

###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:14:1

**מֵתִים בַּל יִחְיוּ.** יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ שֶׁלֹּא יִחְיוּ הָרְשָׁעִים הָאֵלֶּה לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, וְהָ**רְפָאִים** הָאֵלֶּה שֶׁרִפּוּ יְדֵיהֶם מִמִּצְווֹתֶיךָ **בַּל** תְּהִי לָהֶם תְּקוּמָה:

###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:14:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:14:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:14:2)


**לָכֵן פָּקַדְתָּ וַתַּשְׁמִידֵם.** הֲלֹא פָּקַדְתָּ עֲלֵיהֶם כְּבָר וְתַשְׁמִידֵם בְּאִמְרֵי פִיךָ, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״כִּי מָחֹה אֶמְחֶה אֶת זֵכֶר עֲמָלֵק״ (שמות יז:יד):


**therefore, You visited [upon them] and You destroyed them** Have You not already visited upon them and destroyed them with the words of Your mouth, like the matter that is stated (Exodus 17:14): “For I will surely erase the memory of Amalek.”



### Verse 15

###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:15:1)


**יָסַפְתָּ לַגּוֹי.** לְיִשְׂרָאֵל יָסַפְתָּ לָהֶם תּוֹרָה וּגְדֻלָּה וְכָבוֹד, וְכָל כַּמָּה שֶׁיָּסַפְתָּ לָהֶם נִכְבַּדְתָּ, שֶׁהֵם מוֹדִים וּמְשַׁבְּחִים לְפָנֶיךָ עַל כָּל הַטּוֹבָה (תנחומא פנחס טז). הֲרֵי בְּטוֹבָתָם כָּךְ עוֹשִׂים יִשְׂרָאֵל לְפָנֶיךָ קִלּוּס וְכָבוֹד, וּבְצַר לָהֶם:


**You have added to the nation** to Israel (Tan. Pinchas 16) You added to them Torah and greatness and honor, and the more that You added to them, the more You were honored, for they thank You and praise You for all the bounty, unlike the custom of the heathens (var. of Esau). Therefore, You rejected from before You all other ends of the earth, i.e., all distant nations. Behold, in their bounty, in this manner the Israelites bestow praise and honor upon You, and in their straits.



### Verse 16

###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:16:1)


**ה׳ בַּצַּר פְּקָדוּךָ.** אֵינָם מְהַרְהֲרִים אַחַר מִדּוֹתֶיךָ:


**O Lord, in their straits they remembered You** They do not question Your retributions.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:16:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:16:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:16:2)


**צָקוּן לַחַשׁ.** שֶׁפֶךְ שִׂיחַ וּתְפִלָּה:


**they pour out prayer** the pouring of speech and prayer.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:16:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:16:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:16:3)


**מוּסָרְךָ לָמוֹ.** בִּהְיוֹת מוּסַר יִסּוּרֶיךָ בָּאִין עֲלֵיהֶם, וְכָךְ הִיא תְּפִלָּתָם:


**when Your chastening is upon them** When they are chastened, when Your chastening comes upon them; and so is their prayer.



### Verse 17

###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:17:1)


**כְּמוֹ הָרָה תַּקְרִיב לָלֶדֶת וְגוֹ׳ כֵּן הָיִינוּ מִפָּנֶיךָ**. רוֹאִים אָנוּ צָרוֹת מִתְחַדְּשׁוֹת וּסְבוּרִים אָנוּ שֶׁהֵם מִינֵי סִימָנֵי יְשׁוּעָה וּגְאֻלָּה, לְפִי שֶׁאָנוּ מֻבְטָחִים לִגָּאֵל מִתּוֹךְ צוּקָה וְצָרָה כְּיוֹלֵדָה זוֹ שֶׁהֵם מִינֵי סִימָנֵי יְשׁוּעָה וּגְאֻלָּה:


**As a pregnant woman comes near to give birth, etc.** So were we because of You; we see troubles being renewed, and we think that they are sorts of indications of salvation and redemption, for we are promised to be redeemed out of straits, as a woman giving birth.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:17:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:17:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:17:2)


**מִפָּנֶיךָ.** מִפְּנֵי גְזֵרוֹתֶיךָ:


**because of You** Because of Your decrees.



### Verse 18

###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:18:1)


**הָרִינוּ חַלְנוּ.** חִיל כְּיוֹלֵדָה, כְּאִלּוּ **יָלַדְנוּ**, כְּאִלּוּ קְרוֹבִים אָנוּ לְהִגָּאֵל, וְהוּא **רוּחַ** וְאֵין יְשׁוּעָה:


**We conceived, we shuddered** a shudder like a woman giving birth, as though we had given birth, as though we were close to being redeemed, yet it was wind and no salvation.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:18:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:18:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:18:2)


**יְשׁוּעֹת בַּל נַעֲשֶׂה אֶרֶץ.** בְּכָל סִבְלֵינוּ וְצָרָתֵינוּ אֵין אָנוּ מְכִינִים לָנוּ יְשׁוּעָה:


**we wreak no salvation [in] the land** We have suffered everything, and our troubles (sic) we do not understand for ourselves a salvation.[Rashi in Nach Lublin] ([Warsaw edition reads:] With all our suffering and our trouble, we do not prepare salvation for ourselves.) ([K’li Paz reads:] with all our pains and our troubles, we do not bring salvation for ourselves.) ([Some manuscripts read:] Throughout our troubles we do not see any salvation.) ([Others read:] We do not recognize any salvation.) ([Others read:] We cannot prepare for ourselves any salvation.)


###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:18:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:18:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:18:3)


**וּבַל יִפְּלוּ.** וְאֵין נוֹפְלִין הָעַמִּים, שֶׁהֵם **יוֹשְׁבֵי תֵבֵל**, שֶׁכָּבְשׁוּ וּמָלְאוּ אֶת הָאָרֶץ. וְיוֹנָתָן תִּרְגֵּם **בַּל יִפְּלוּ** לְשׁוֹן ״וְנִפְלִינוּ אֲנִי וְעַמְּךָ״ (שמות לג:טז), אֵין **יוֹשְׁבֵי תֵבֵל** יְכוֹלִין לַעֲשׂוֹת פֶּלֶא:


**neither do the inhabitants of the world fall** The nations (var. the children of Esau), who are the inhabitants of the world, since they conquered and filled the earth, do not fall. And Jonathan rendered יִפְּלוּ as an expression related to (Ex. 33:16): “And wonders shall be wrought (וְנִפְלִינוּ) for me and Your people.” The inhabitants of the world cannot perform a wonder.



### Verse 19

###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:19:1)


**יִחְיוּ מֵתֶיךָ.** כָּאן הִתְפַּלֵּל שֶׁיִּחְיוּ הַצַּדִּיקִים, בְּבַקָּשָׁה מִמְּךָ יִחְיוּ אוֹתָן שֶׁמּוּמָתִין עָלֶיךָ. יֵצֵא דְּבַר מַלְכוּת מִלְּפָנֶיךָ לוֹמַר **נְבֵלָתִי יְקוּמוּן**, נְבֵלוֹת עַמִּי שֶׁנִּבְּלוּ עַצְמָן עָלַי, לָהֶם תְּהִי תְּקוּמָה זוֹ. חִלּוּף לְמַה שֶׁכָּתוּב לְמַעְלָה (ישעיהו כו:יד) ״רְפָאִים בַּל יָקוּמוּ״, אֲבָל אֵלּוּ **יְקוּמוּן**:


**May Your dead live** Above (v. 14) he prayed that the wicked should not live, and here he prayed that the righteous should live. I beseech You that those who were slain for Your sake come to life. May a royal edict emanate from You saying, “My corpses shall rise.” The corpses of My people who made themselves corpses for My sake, they shall be raised up. This is the opposite of what is written above (v. 14): “Slackers shall not rise.” These, however, shall rise.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:19:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:19:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:19:2)


**הָקִיצוּ וְרַנְּנוּ.** כָּל זֶה יֹאמַר לָהֶם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, ״הָקִיצוּ וְרַנְּנוּ״ לְשׁוֹן צִוּוּי הוּא זֶה:


**awaken and sing** All this the Holy One, blessed be He, shall say to them. “Awaken and sing,” is an imperative form.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:19:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:19:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:19:3)


**כִּי טַל אוֹרֹת טַלֶּךָ.** כִּי נָאֶה לְךָ לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן, שֶׁיְּהֵא טַל תּוֹרָתְךָ וּמִצְווֹתֶיךָ לָהֶם טַל שֶׁל אוֹר:


**for a dew of lights is Your dew** For it is fitting for You to do so, that the dew of Your Torah and Your commandments shall be to them dew of light.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:19:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:19:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:19:4)


**וָאָרֶץ רְפָאִים תַּפִּיל.** וְלָאָרֶץ וְלֶעָפָר תַּפִּיל אֶת אֶרֶץ רְפָאִים, שֶׁרִפּוּ יְדֵיהֶם מִתּוֹרָתֶךָ (כתובות קיא ב):


**and [to the] earth You shall cast the slackers** And to the earth and to the dust You shall cast the land of (sic) the slackers who slackened their hands from Your Torah.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:19:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:19:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:19:5)


**רְפָאִים תַּפִּיל.** לְפִי שֶׁאָמַר ״וּבַל יִפְּלוּ יוֹשְׁבֵי תֵבֵל״ (ישעיהו כו:יח), חוֹזֵר וְאוֹמֵר: אַתָּה הַפִּילֵם, כִּי אֵין בְּצִדְקוֹתֵינוּ כְּדֵי לְהַפִּילָם:


**You shall cast the slackers** Since he stated (v. 18) “Neither do the inhabitants of the world fall,” he repeats, “You cast them down, for our merits do not suffice to cast them down.”



### Verse 20

###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:20:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:20:1)


**לֵךְ עַמִּי בֹּא בַחֲדָרֶיךָ.** תְּשׁוּבָה זוֹ הֵשִׁיבוּהוּ לַנָּבִיא: **לֵךְ עַמִּי בֹּא בַחֲדָרֶיךָ** – בְּבָתֵּי כְנֵסִיּוֹת וּבְבָתֵּי מִדְרָשׁוֹת. דָּבָר אַחֵר: הִתְבּוֹנֵן עַל מַעֲשֶׂיךָ בְּחַדְרֵי לִבְּךָ. כָּךְ דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי תַּנְחוּמָא (תנחומא ויצא ה):


**Go, My people, come into your chambers** This reply they replied to the prophet, “Go, My people, come into your chambers,” into the synagogues and the study houses. Alternatively, think about your deeds, in the chambers of your heart. In this manner Rabbi Tanhuma expounded it.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:20:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:20:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:20:2)


**וּסְגֹר דַּלְתָּךְ בַּעֲדֶךָ** תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״עֲבִיד לָךְ עוֹבְדִין טָבִין דְּיָגִנּוּן עֲלָךְ״, וְרַבִּי תַּנְחוּמָא דָּרַשׁ: סְגוֹר דַּלְתֵי פִּיךָ, שֶׁלֹּא תְהַרְהֵר אַחַר מִדַּת הַדִּין:


**close your door about you** Jonathan renders: Do good deeds that will protect you. Rabbi Tanhuma, however, expounded: Close the doors of your mouth so as not to question the divine standard of justice.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:20:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:20:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:20:3)


**חֲבִי.** הִתְחַבְּאִי מְעַט **עַד יַעֲבָר זָעַם**, כִּי אֱמֶת אֶפְקֹד עַל שׂוֹנְאֶיךָ:


**hide** Hide a little until the wrath passes, for indeed I will visit upon your enemies.



### Verse 21

###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:21:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:21:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:21:1)


**כִּי הִנֵּה ה׳ יוֹצֵא וְגוֹ׳.** מִמִּדַּת הָרַחֲמִים לְמִדַּת הַדִּין (ירושלמי תענית ב א):


**For behold the Lord comes forth** from the divine standard of mercy to the divine standard of justice.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:21:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:21:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:21:2)


**יוֹשֵׁב הָאָרֶץ.** הוּא הַר שֵׂעִיר:


**the dweller of the land** That is Mount Seir. ([Some manuscripts read:] That is Esau and Mount Seir.) ([Others read:] That is Esau on Mount Seir.)


###### Rashi on Isaiah 26:21:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:21:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:21:3)


**עַל הֲרוּגֶיהָ.** שֶׁהָרְגוּ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל:

## Chapter 27


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:1:1)


**עַל לִוְיָתָן נָחָשׁ בָּרִחַ וְגוֹ׳.** תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״עַל מַלְכָּא דְּאִתְרַבְּרַב כְּפַרְעֹה מַלְכָּא קַדְמָאָה וְעַל מַלְכָּא דְּאִתְגָּאֵי כְּסַנְחֵרִב מַלְכָּא תְּנִינָא״. ׳בָּרִחַ׳ לְשׁוֹן ׳פָּשׁוּט׳ כַּבְּרִיחַ הַזֶּה, לְפִי שֶׁהוּא רִאשׁוֹן:


**on leviathan the barlike serpent** Jonathan renders: On the king who aggrandized himself like Pharaoh the first king, and upon a king who was as haughty as Sennacherib the second king. בָּרִיחַ is an expression of ‘straight’ like a bar, since he is the first. (The matter of simplicity is related to oneness. Since Pharaoh was the first great king, he is referred to as ‘the barlike serpent,’ a straight, penetrating serpent, that does not coil.)


###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:1:2)


**עֲקַלָּתוֹן.** לְשׁוֹן כָּפוּל, לְפִי שֶׁהוּא שֵׁנִי. וְאוֹמֵר אֲנִי: לְפִי שֶׁאֵלּוּ שָׁלֹשׁ אֻמּוֹת חֲשׁוּבוֹת, מִצְרַיִם וְאַשּׁוּר וֶאֱדוֹם, לְכָךְ אָמַר עַל אֵלּוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר בְּסוֹף הָעִנְיָן ״וּבָאוּ הָאֹבְדִים בְּאֶרֶץ אַשּׁוּר וְהַנִּדָּחִים בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם״ (ישעיהו כז:יג):


**crooked** An expression of ‘double,’ since he is the second one. (I.e. the bend in the serpent indicates duality, thus the number two.) And I say that these are three important nations: Egypt, Assyria, and Edom. He, therefore, stated concerning these as he said at the end of the section (v. 13), “And those lost in the land of Assyria shall come, as well as those lost in the land of Egypt,” and since the nations are likened to serpents that bite.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:1:3)


**לִוְיָתָן נָחָשׁ בָּרִחַ.** הוּא מִצְרָיִם:


**leviathan the barlike serpent** That is Egypt.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:1:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:1:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:1:4)


**לִוְיָתָן נָחָשׁ עֲקַלָּתוֹן.** הוּא אַשּׁוּר:


**leviathan the crooked serpent** That is Assyria.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:1:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:1:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:1:5)


**וְהָרַג אֶת הַתַּנִּין אֲשֶׁר בַּיָּם.** הִיא יוֹשֶׁבֶת בְּלֵב יַמִּים, וְכֵן כִּתִּיִּים קְרוּיִים אִיֵּי הַיָּם:


**and He shall slay the dragon that is in the sea** That is Tzor that is the head of the children of Esau, and it is situated in the heart of the seas, and so Kittim are called the islands of the sea, and they are the Romans [according to certain manuscripts]. ([Some editions read:] They are the Greeks.)



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:2:1)


**בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא.** בְּעֵת הַגְּאֻלָּה יָשִׁירוּ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל: ״זוֹ הִיא **כֶּרֶם חֶמֶר**, הוֹצִיאָה יֵינָהּ הַטּוֹב״. **חֶמֶר** – וינו״ש בלע״ז:


**On that day** At the time of the redemption, they shall sing to Israel, “This is a wine producing vineyard. It has yielded its good wine.” חֶמֶר vinos in O.F., winish.



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:3:1)


**אֲנִי יְהוָה נֹצְרָהּ.** בְּעֵת הַגָּלוּת:


**I, the Lord, guard it** in the time of exile.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:3:2)


**לִרְגָעִים אַשְׁקֶנָּה.** מְעַט מְעַט אֲנִי מַשְׁקֶה אוֹתָהּ כּוֹס פֻּרְעָנוּת הַבָּאָה עָלֶיהָ, **פֶּן אֶפְקֹד עָלֶיהָ** בְּבַת אַחַת וַאֲכַלֶּנָּה, לְכָךְ **לַיְלָה וָיוֹם** אֲנִי מִתְבּוֹנֵן בָּהּ. וְיוֹנָתָן תִּרְגֵּם: אִם לֹא שֶׁאֲנִי פּוֹקֵד עֲלֵיהֶם עֲווֹנוֹת שֶׁהֵם מַרְגִּילִים לְפָנַי, **לַיְלָה וָיוֹם** הָיִיתִי מֵגִין עֲלֵיהֶם:


**every moment I water it** Little by little I water it with the cup of retribution that comes upon it, lest I visit upon it at once and I destroy it. Therefore, night and day I ponder about it. Jonathan renders: Were it not that I visit upon them the iniquities that they are accustomed to commit before Me, I would guard it day and night.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:4:1)


**חֵמָה אֵין לִי.** אֵין לִי פֶּה לְהַגְבִּיר חֲמָתִי עַל הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמָזָלוֹת, לְפִי שֶׁאַף יִשְׂרָאֵל חוֹטְאִים, וּמִדַּת הַדִּין מְקַטְרֶגֶת:


**I have no wrath** I have no mouth (var. excuse) to arouse My wrath on the nations, for Israel sins as well, and the standard of justice accuses.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:4:2)


**מִי יִתְּנֵנִי שָׁמִיר שַׁיִת בַּמִּלְחָמָה.** בִּבְנֵי מִלְחַמְתִּי וְהוּא יִשְׁמָעֵאל, מִי יִתְּנֵנִי וְאוּכַל לִפְקוֹד עֲלֵיהֶם, וְלֹא תוּכַל מִדַּת הַדִּין לִמְחוֹת שֶׁיָּשׁוּבוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּתְשׁוּבָה, וְהִיא נוֹתֶנֶת אוֹתִי שָׁמִיר וָשַׁיִת בִּבְנֵי מִלְחָמָה. אֶפְסַע פְּסִיעָה עַל מִדַּת הַדִּין וְאֶפְקוֹד עֲלֵיהֶם אַף יִתְרוֹן וְנוֹסָפוֹת עַל עֲוֹנָם, וַאֲצִיתֵם **יָחַד**. כֵּן תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן עַל הָאֻמּוֹת, וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה פֵּרְשׁוּ (עבודה זרה ד א) עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְהוּא מוּסָב עַל הַכֶּרֶם. **חֵמָה אֵין לִי.** בְּכָל הַכְּעָסִים שֶׁהִכְעִיסָנִי הַכֶּרֶם הַזֹּאת, לֹא אוּכַל לִשְׁפּוֹךְ חֲמָתִי לְבַעֲרָהּ מִפְּנֵי הַשְּׁבוּעָה שֶׁנִּשְׁבַּעְתִּי לַאֲבוֹתֵיהֶם. מִי יִתְּנֵנִי כְּיָמִים שֶׁעָבְרוּ, לוּלֵי הַשְּׁבוּעָה הָיִיתִי שָׁמִיר וָשַׁיִת וּפוֹשֵׁעַ בַּכֶּרֶם וַאֲצִיתֶנָּה יָחַד:


**would that I were thorns and briers against [the objects of My] war** Against those with whom I wage war, namely Ishmael (ms. Esau). Would that I could visit upon them and the standard of justice would not be able to protest, i.e., that Israel would repent, and that would give Me thorns and briers against the enemies! I would tread upon the standard of justice and I would visit upon them even more and additional punishment over their iniquity, and I would ignite them together. Jonathan rendered it in this manner, as referring to the nations. Our Sages of blessed memory explained it concerning Israel, and it refers back to the vineyard, as follows: **I have no wrath** Despite all the angers with which this vineyard has provoked Me, I cannot pour out My wrath to destroy it because of the oath I swore to their forefathers. If only it were like days long past! Were it not for the oath, I would be thorns and briers and I would tread upon the vineyard, and I would ignite it together.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:5:1)


**אוֹ יַחֲזֵק בְּמָעוּזִּי.** ׳אוֹ׳ לְשׁוֹן ׳אִם׳, כְּמוֹ ״אוֹ נוֹדַע כִּי שׁוֹר נַגָּח הוּא״ (שמות כא:לו). אוֹ יַחֲזִיק עַמִּי בְּמָעֻזִּי שֶׁלֹּא יְבַקֵּשׁ מָעֹז אֶלָּא מָעֻזִּי, אָז **יַעֲשֶׂה שָׁלוֹם לִי** לְהָנִיחַ דַּעְתִּי וְאַפִּי, שֶׁמִּתְקַשְׁקֶשֶׁת בִּי עַל שֶׁאֵינִי נוֹקֵם בְּצָרַי, וְאֶנָּקֵם בָּהֶם:


**If they would grasp My fortress** (אוֹ), lit., or they would grasp My fortress,) an expression of ‘if.’ Comp. “(Ex. 21:36) If (אוֹ) it was known that he was a goring ox.” If My people grasp My fortress, i.e., My Torah, that they seek no other fortress but My fortress, then they shall grant Me peace, to calm My thoughts and My ire which trouble Me because I do not avenge Myself upon My adversaries, and I will, indeed, take revenge from them.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:5:2)


**שָׁלוֹם יַעֲשֶׂה לִּי.** מִמִּדַּת הַדִּין, שֶׁלֹּא יוּכַל לְקַטְרֵג וְלוֹמַר: ״מַה נִּשְׁתַּנּוּ אֵלּוּ מֵאֵלּוּ?״


**they would make peace for Me** from the standard of justice, so that it will be unable to accuse and to say, “Why are these different from those?” (I.e., Why are the Jews different from the other nations?)



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:6:1)


**הַבָּאִים יַשְׁרֵשׁ יַעֲקֹב.** הֲלֹא יְדַעְתֶּם מַה עָשִׂיתִי בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה? הַבָּאִים לְמִצְרַיִם אֲשֶׁר הִשְׁרִישׁ יַעֲקֹב, צָצוּ וּפָרְחוּ שָׁם עַד (אֲשֶׁר) **מָלְאוּ פְנֵי תֵבֵל תְּנוּבָה**:


**Those who came, whom Jacob caused to take root** Do you not know what I did at first? Those who came to Egypt which Jacob caused to take root, flourished and blossomed there until they filled the face of the world with fruitage.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:7:1)


**הַכְּמַכַּת מַכֵּהוּ הִכָּהוּ** הַרְּאִיתֶם בִּגְבוּרָתִי, שֶׁכְּמַכַּת הַמַּכֶּה יַעֲקֹב הִכִּיתִיו? הֵם טִבְּעוּם בַּמַּיִם וַאֲנִי טִבַּעְתִּים בַּמַּיִם. יֵשׁ תְּמִיהוֹת שֶׁהֵם מִתְקַיְּמוֹת, כְּגוֹן זוֹ, וּכְגוֹן (שמואל א ב:כז) ״הֲנִגְלֹה נִגְלֵיתִי אֶל בֵּית אָבִיךָ״, (יחזקאל ח:ו) ״הֲרוֹאֶה אַתָּה מָה הֵמָּה עוֹשִׂים״:


**Like the smiting of him who smote him did He smite him** Have you seen My might, that like the smiting of the one who smote Jacob, I smote him. They drowned them in the water, and I drowned them in the water. There are some other rhetorical questions that warrant an affirmative answer, e.g. (I Sam. 2:27), “Did I appear to the house of your father?” Also (Ezek. 8:6), “Do you see what they are doing?”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:7:2)


**אִם כְּהֶרֶג** יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהָיוּ הֲרוּגִין שֶׁל פַּרְעֹה, הוֹרֵג פַּרְעֹה וְעַמּוֹ?


**like the slaying of** Israel, who were the slain ones of Pharaoh, were Pharaoh and his people slain?



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:8:1)


**בְּסַאסְּאָה.** בְּאוֹתָהּ מִדָּה:


**In that measure** (בְּסַאסְּאָה) in that measure.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:8:2)


**בְּשַׁלְחָהּ תְּרִיבֶנָּה.** כְּשֶׁשִּׁלְּחָה מִצְרַיִם אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, תְּרִיבֶנָּה הַמִּדָּה בִּסְאָה שֶׁלָּהּ:


**when they sent them out, it strove with it** When Egypt sent Israel out, it strove with it, the seah of the measure with its seah.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:8:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:8:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:8:3)


**הָגָה בְּרוּחוֹ הַקָּשָׁה.** ׳הָגָה׳ דִּבֵּר בְּדִבּוּרוֹ הַקָּשֶׁה:


**He spoke with His harsh wind** (הָגָה) He spoke with His harsh speech.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:8:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:8:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:8:4)


**בְּיוֹם קָדִים.** בְּיוֹם ״וַיּוֹלֶךְ ה׳ אֶת הַיָּם בְּרוּחַ קָדִים עַזָּה״ (שמות יד:כא):


**on the day of the east wind** On the day (concerning which Scripture states) (Ex. 14:21): “And the Lord led the sea with a strong east wind.”



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:9:1)


**לָכֵן.** גַּם עַתָּה **בְּזֹאת** הָיָה מִתְכַּפֵּר **עֲוֹן יַעֲקֹב** לִזְכּוֹת לְהִגָּאֵל כְּמֵאָז:


**Therefore** Now, too, with this, Jacob’s iniquity would be atoned for, to merit to be redeemed as then.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:9:2)


**וְזֶה כָּל פְּרִי** הַטּוֹב לוֹ לְ**הָסִיר חַטָּאתוֹ**, אִם יָשִׂים **כָּל אַבְנֵי** מִזְבְּחוֹת בָּמוֹתָיו **כְּאַבְנֵי גִיר מְנֻפָּצוֹת** מְדֻקָּרוֹת. וְכֵן (תהלים קלז:ט) ״וְנִפֵּץ אֶת עוֹלָלַיִךְ״, וְכֵן (ירמיהו יג:יד) ״וְנִפַּצְתִּים אִיש אֶל אָחִיו״. **גִּיר** מִין צֶבַע הוּא:


**and this is all the fruit** that is best for Me to remove his sin, if he makes all the altar stones of his high places, like crushed chalk-stones. מְנֻפָּצוֹת means crushed. Comp. (Ps. 137:9) “And crushes (וְנִפֵּץ) your babies.” Comp. (Jer. 13:14) “And I will crush them (וְנִפַּצְתִּים) one against the other.” גִּיר is a kind of dye.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:9:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:9:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:9:3)


**לֹא יָקֻמוּ אֲשֵׁרִים וְחַמָּנִים.** לְמַעַן לֹא יָקִימוּ לָהֶם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה:


**asherim and sun images shall not rise** So that they shall not retain their idolatry.



### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:10:1)


**כִּי עִיר בְּצוּרָה בָּדָד.** כִּי בַּעֲשׂוֹתָם זֹאת, עִיר בְּצוּרָה שֶׁל יִשְׁמָעֵאל תִּהְיֶה **בָּדָד**, וְהַ**נָּוֶה** יִהְיֶה **מְשֻׁלָּח וְנֶעֱזָב כַּמִּדְבָּר**:


**For a fortified city is solitary** For, when they do this, a fortified city of Ishmael (ms. Esau) will be solitary and the dwelling will be forsaken by its inhabitants and abandoned like a pasture.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:10:2)


**שָׁם יִרְעֶה עֵגֶל.** אֶפְרַיִם יִירָשֶׁנּוּ, שֶׁקָּרוּי ׳עֵגֶל׳, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ירמיהו לא:יח) ״כְּעֵגֶל לֹא לֻמָּד״:


**there a calf shall graze** Ephraim shall inherit it, for he is called a calf, as it is said (Jer. 31:17): “Like an untamed calf.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:10:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:10:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:10:3)


**וְכִלָּה סְעִפֶיהָ.** עֲנָפֶיהָ:


**and shall consume its branches** (סְעִיפֶיהָ) its branches.



### Verse 11

###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:11:1)


**בִּיבֹשׁ קְצִירָהּ.** קְצִירֵי שָׁרָשֶׁיהָ, כְּמוֹ ״תְּשַׁלַּח קְצִירֶיהָ״ (תהלים פ:יב), ״וְעָשָׂה קָצִיר״ (איוב יד:ט). כְּלוֹמַר: כְּשֶׁתִּכְלֶה זְכוּת מְעַט שֶׁכִּבֵּד אֶת אָבִיו, אָז **תִּשָּׁבַרְנָה סְעִפֶיהָ**:


**When its branches dry out** The branches of its roots. Comp. (Ps. 80:12) “It sent forth its branches (קְצִירֶיהָ).” Also (Job 14:9): “And produce branches (קָצִיר).” I.e., when the little merit that Edom has for honoring his father, is depleted, then its branches shall be broken.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:11:2)


**נָשִׁים בָּאוֹת מְאִירוֹת אוֹתָהּ.** עַם חַלָּשׁ כְּנָשִׁים יַדְלִיקוּם, כָּךְ תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן. **מְאִירוֹת** כְּמוֹ (מלאכי א:י) ״וְלֹא תָאִירוּ מִזְבְּחִי חִנָּם״, וְכֵן פָּתַר דּוּנָשׁ: מֵחֲמַת שֶׁהָעֵצִים יִהְיוּ יְבֵשִׁים יִהְיוּ נוֹחִים לְהַדְלִיק. אֲבָל מְנַחֵם (מחברת: אר) פָּתַר: ׳מְלַקְּטוֹת׳, כְּמוֹ (שיר השירים ה:א) ״אָרִיתִי מוֹרִי״, (תהלים פ:יג) ״וְאָרוּהָ כָּל עֹבְרֵי דָרֶךְ״. הֵשִׁיב לוֹ דּוּנָשׁ: וַהֲלֹא כְּתִיב ״בִּיבֹשׁ קְצִירָהּ״, וּבַעֲנָפִים יְבֵשִׁים אֵין מְלַקְּטִין פְּרִי. וְכֵן רַבּוֹתֵינוּ, שֶׁאָסְרוּ לְקַבֵּל מֵהֶן צְדָקָה מִפְּנֵי הַטַּעַם הַזֶּה, שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא פֶּרֶק קַמָּא (בבא בתרא י ב): לֵית לֵיהּ ״בִּיבֹשׁ קְצִירָהּ תִּשָּׁבַרְנָה״:


**women shall come and ignite it** A people weak as women shall ignite them. Jonathan renders in this manner. מְאִירוֹת means ‘ignite.’ Comp. (Mal. 1:10) “And you shall not light (תָּאִירוּ) My altar in vain.” Dunash too interpreted it in this manner, for since the wood will be dry, it will be easy to ignite. Menahem, however, interpreted it to mean ‘gather.’ Comp. (Song 5:1) “I gathered (אָרִיתִי) my myrrh.” Also (Ps. 80:13): “All passersby gathered from it (וְאָרוּהָ).” (Machbereth Menahem p. 32) Dunash replied, “Does it not say, ‘When its branches dry out’? And with dry grapes, no one gathers fruit.” (Teshuvoth Dunash p. 45)] Likewise, our Sages, who prohibited accepting charity from them because of this reason, for they stated in Baba Bathra ch. 1, (10b,) “Does he not believe, ‘When its branches dry out, they shall be broken?’”



### Verse 12

###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:12:1)


**יַחְבֹּט ה׳.** תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״יִתְרְמוֹן קְטִילִין״. וַאֲנִי אוֹמֵר: שְׁתֵּי לְשׁוֹנוֹת הַלָּלוּ, ׳חִבּוּט׳ וּ׳לְקִיטָה׳, נוֹפְלִין זֶה עַל זֶה, כְּחוֹבֵט זֵיתָיו וְחוֹזֵר וּמְלַקְּטָן, וַאֲחֵרִים מְלַקְּטִין אוֹתוֹ מִן הָאָרֶץ. כָּךְ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יַתְחִיל הָאֲסִיפָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: **יִתָּקַע בְּשׁוֹפָר גָּדוֹל**:


**that the Lord shall gather** יַחְבֹּט, lit., shall beat. Jonathan renders: shall fall dead. I.e., the nations from the banks of the Euphrates to the stream of Egypt. I say, however, that these two expressions, (viz.) beating and gathering, coincide with one another, like one who bears his olive trees and goes back and gathers them and (ms. or) others gather them from the ground, so will the Holy One, blessed be He, commence the gathering, as it is said: A great shofar shall be sounded.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:12:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:12:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:12:2)


**מִשִּׁבֹּלֶת הַנָּהָר.** הֵם **הָאֹבְדִים בְּאֶרֶץ אַשּׁוּר**:


**from the flood of the river** These are those lost in the land of Assyria.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:12:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:12:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:12:3)


**עַד נַחַל מִצְרָיִם.** הֵם **הַנִּדָּחִים בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם**:


**to the stream of Egypt** Those are the ones exiled in the land of Egypt.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:12:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:12:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:12:4)


**הַנָּהָר.** פְּרָת, הֵם בְּנֵי אַשּׁוּר הַיּוֹשְׁבִים עַל פְּרָת:


**the river** Euphrates. They are those in Assyria who live by the Euphrates.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:12:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:12:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:12:5)


**עַד נַחַל מִצְרָיִם.** הֵם יוֹשְׁבֵי מִצְרַיִם, **יַחְבֹּט** אוֹתָם כְּחוֹבֵט זֵיתִים:


**to the stream of Egypt** These are those who live in Egypt, He shall gather them like one who gathers olives.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:12:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:12:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:12:6)


**וְאַתֶּם תְּלֻקְּטוּ.** מִן הַגָּלֻיּוֹת:


**and you shall be gathered** from the exiles.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:12:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:12:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:12:7)


**לְאַחַד אֶחָד.** הַמּוֹצֵא אֶחָד מִכֶּם יְבִיאֵהוּ מִנְחָה:


**one and one** Whoever finds one of you will bring him as an offering.



### Verse 13

###### Rashi on Isaiah 27:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:13:1)


**הָאֹבְדִים בְּאֶרֶץ אַשּׁוּר.** לְפִי שֶׁנָּפוֹצוּ בְּאֶרֶץ רְחוֹקָה, לִפְנִים מִן הַנָּהָר סַמְבַּטְיוֹן קְרָאָם ׳אוֹבְדִים׳ (בראשית רבה עג ה):


**those lost in the land of Assyria** Since they were scattered in a distant land, within the Sambatyon River, he calls them, ‘lost.’



## Chapter 28


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:1:1)


**שִׁכּוֹרֵי אֶפְרַיִם.** שֶׁהָיוּ מִשְׁתַּכְּרִין בְּיַיִן טוֹב שֶׁל מְדִינַת פְּרוּגִיתָא, כִּדְאָמַר (שבת קמז ב): מַיָּא דְּדוֹרְמַסְקִית וְחַמְרָא דִּפְרוּגִיתָא קִפְּחוּ עֲשֶׂרֶת הַשְּׁבָטִים:


**the drunkards of Ephraim** who would become intoxicated with the wine of the state of Prugitha, as (the Rabbis) stated (Shabbath 147b): The water of Damascus and the wine of Prugitha robbed away the ten tribes.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:1:2)


**וְצִיץ נֹבֵל צְבִי תִפְאַרְתּוֹ.** וּמַצַּב מַטַּע תִּפְאַרְתּוֹ יִהְיֶה צִיץ הַפֶּרַח שֶׁלּוֹ **נוֹבֵל.** הֵם תְּאֵנִים הַמְקֻלְקָלוֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁנִינוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (ברכות מ ב) עַל הַנּוֹבְלוֹת, וּפֵרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ: בְּשׁוּלֵי כַּמְרָא, וְ**צִיץ** נֵץ, כְּדִמְתַרְגְּמִינָן (במדבר יז:כג) ״וַיָּצֵץ צִיץ״ – ״וְאָנֵץ נֵץ״:


**and the young fruit of an inferior fig is the position of his glory** And the position of the planting of his glory - the young fruit of his blossom shall be **inferior figs** (נֹבֵל) They are the spoiled figs, as we learned in Berachoth (40b): For noveloth. And our Sages explained: Burned by the heat. **young fruit** (צִיץ) synonymous with נֵץ, as the Targum renders: (Num. 27:13) וַיָּצֵץ צִיץ, “and it produced young fruit,” as וְאָנֵץ נֵץ.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:1:3)


**אֲשֶׁר** נְטוּעִים **עַל רֹאשׁ גֵּיא שְׁמָנִים.** הִיא כִּנֶּרֶת, שֶׁפֵּרוֹתֶיהָ מְתוּקִים, וְשָׁם הֵם הוֹלְמִים עַצְמָן בְּ**יָיִן**:


**which is** planted **at the head of a valley of fatness** That is Kinnereth, whose fruits are sweet, and there they crush themselves with wine.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:1:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:1:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:1:4)


**הֲלוּמֵי יָיִן.** ״כְּתוּשֵׁי חֲמַר״. וְיֵשׁ עוֹד לִפְתּוֹר **צְבִי תִפְאַרְתּוֹ אֲשֶׁר עַל וְגוֹ׳**: צְבִי הַתִּפְאֶרֶת שֶׁעַל רֹאשׁ עֲשֶׂרֶת הַשְּׁבָטִים, הַמְּשׁוּחִין בְּגֵאוּת רָאשֵׁי שְׁמָנִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (עמוס ו:ו) ״רֵאשִׁית שְׁמָנִים יִמְשָׁחוּ״. **גֵּיא** לְשׁוֹן ׳גַּאֲוָה׳, כְּמוֹ (ישעיהו טז:ו) ״מוֹאָב גֵּיא מְאֹד״ (וְאוֹתוֹ הַצִּיץ כְּצִיצַת נוֹבֵל תִּהְיֶה). **הֲלוּמֵי יָיִן.** כָּךְ קוֹרְאָן עַל שֵׁם שִׁכְרוּתָן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בָּהֶם (עמוס ו:ו) ״הַשּׁוֹתִים בְּמִזְרְקֵי יָיִן״:


**crushed with wine** הֲלוּמֵי יַיִן. This may also be interpreted as follows: צבי תפארתו אשר על ראש וכו', (his glorious beauty, which is, etc.): His glorious beauty, which is on the head of the ten tribes, anointed with pride with the best oils, as it is said (Amos 6:6): “With the best oils they anoint themselves.” גֵּיא is an expression of pride, as (supra 16:6): “Moab, they have become very proud.” (And that blossom will be like a wilting blossom) crushed by wine. So he calls them because of their drunkenness, and it is said concerning them (Amos 6:6): “Those who drink with basins of wine.”



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:2:1)


**הִנֵּה** יֵשׁ רוּחַ **חָזָק וְאַמִּץ לַה׳**, שֶׁהוּא **כְּזֶרֶם בָּרָד** וְ**שַׂעַר קֶטֶב** מְרִירִי:


**Behold** The Lord has a strong and powerful wind, which is like a downpour of hail and a storm of קֶטֶב מְרִירִי, bitter destruction.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:2:2)


**הִנִּיחַ לָאָרֶץ בְּיָד.** יַנִּיחֵהוּ עַל אַרְצָם בְּיָדוֹ הַחֲזָקָה, וְיַפִּיל הַנּוֹבְלוֹת מִן הַתְּאֵנִים:


**He lays it on the land with [His] hand** He shall place it on their land with His strong hand and cast down the inferior figs from fig trees.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:4:1)


**כְּבִכּוּרָהּ בְּטֶרֶם קַיִץ.** כְּבִשּׁוּלָהּ שֶׁל תְּאֵנַת **צִיץ נֹבֵל**:


**as a fig that ripens before the summer** like the ripening of the young fruits of an inferior fig.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:4:2)


**בְּטֶרֶם קַיִץ.** עֵת בִִּשּׁוּל שְׁאָר הַתְּאֵנִים, אֲשֶׁר מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁהִיא בְּכוּרָה קוֹפֵץ עָלֶיהָ וּבוֹלְעָהּ בְּעוֹדָהּ בְּכַפּוֹ, כָּךְ ״וַיִּשְׁקֹד עַל הָרָעָה וַיְבִיאֶהָ עָלֵינוּ״ (דניאל ט:יד):


**before the summer** the time of the ripening of other figs, which, because of its early ripening, he pounces on it and swallows it while it is still in his hand. So (Dan. 9:14), “He hastened the evil and brought it upon us.”



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:5:1)


**בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא.** כְּהִתָּם הַפּוֹשְׁעִים:


**On that day** When the transgressors are destroyed.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:5:2

**for a crown of beauty** for the remaining righteous men among them.



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:6:1)


**וּלְרוּחַ מִשְׁפָּט.** יִהְיֶה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהוֹרוֹת מִשְׁפָּט:


**And for a spirit of justice** will the Holy One, blessed be He, be, i.e., to teach justice, to him who sits in judgment.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:6:2)


**לַיּוֹשֵׁב עַל הַמִּשְׁפָּט וְלִגְבוּרָה.** יִהְיֶה לְאוֹתָן שֶׁהֵם **מְשִׁיבֵי מִלְחָמָה**, מִלְחַמְתָּהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה (מגילה טו ב):


**and for might** will He be for those who bring back the war, the war of Torah.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:7:1)


**וְגַם אֵלֶּה.** יוֹשְׁבֵי **מִשְׁפָּט** וּ**מְשִׁיבֵי מִלְחָמָה** שֶׁבַּדּוֹר הַזֶּה, כְּלוֹמַר: טוֹבִים וַחֲשׁוּבִים שֶׁבָּהֶן, **בַּיַּיִן שָׁגוּ**, כִּי עַתָּה אֵין טוֹב בָּהֶם:


**These too** who sit in judgment and return the war in this generation, i.e., the best and most esteemed among them, erred because of wine, for now there is no good in them.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:7:2)


**שָׁגוּ בָּרֹאֶה.** הִלְעִיגוּ בְּדִבְרֵי הַנְּבִיאִים, וְיוֹנָתָן תִּרְגֵּם בְּמַאֲכַל מַעֲדַנִּים, שֶׁרָאוּהוּ עֹנֶג לָהֶם:


**they erred against the seer** They mocked the words of the prophets. Jonathan renders: with eating delicacies, which they saw as a pleasure to them.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:7:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:7:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:7:3)


**פָּקוּ פְּלִילִיָּה.** הִכְשִׁילוּ הַמִּשְׁפָּט:


**they caused justice to stumble** (פָּקוּ פְּלִילֶיהָ), they caused justice to stumble.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:7:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:7:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:7:4)


**פָּקוּ.** לְשׁוֹן ״פִּיק בִּרְכַּיִם״ (נחום ב:יא), ״פּוּקָה״ (שמואל א כה:לא):


פָּקוּ is an expression similar to (Nahum 2:11), “The stumbling (פִּיק) of knees”; (I Sam. 25:31) “A stumbling block (פּוּקָה).”



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:8:1)


**כִּי כָּל שֻׁלְחָנוֹת.** שֶׁלָּהֶם, שֶׁל זִבְחֵי מֵתִים הֵם, שֶׁהֵם כְּ**קִיא צוֹאָה**:


**For all tables** I.e., all their tables are of sacrifices for the dead, i.e., the pagan deities, which are like vomit and ordure.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:8:2)


**בְּלִי מָקוֹם.** אֵין הַדַּעַת סוֹבַלְתָּן:


**without a place** (I.e.) the mind cannot tolerate them.



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:9:1)


**אֶת מִי יוֹרֶה דֵעָה.** שֶׁמָּא לְתִינוֹקוֹת שֶׁאֵין יוֹדְעִין לְהָבִין, כִּי הַגְּדוֹלִים פָּנוּ לְדֶרֶךְ רָעָה?


**Whom shall he teach knowledge** Perhaps to babes who know not to understand, since the adults have turned to an evil way?


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:9:2)


**גְּמוּלֵי מֵחָלָב.** בְּדוּלֵי מֵחָלָב:


**those weaned from milk** separated from milk.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:9:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:9:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:9:3)


**עַתִּיקֵי מִשָּׁדָיִם.** לְשׁוֹן ״וַיַּעְתֵּק מִשָּׁם״ (בראשית יב:ח). דָּבָר אַחֵר: בְּדוּלִים מִן הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּקְרֵאת חָלָב, וְ**עַתִּיקֵי מִשָּׁדָיִם** מוּסָרִים מִלִּפְנֵי תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים:


**removed from breasts** (עַתִּיקֵי) an expression similar to (Gen. 12:8), “And he removed (וַיַּעְתֵּק) from there.” Alternatively, separated from the Torah, which is called milk, and removed from breasts, removed from before Torah scholars.



### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:10:1)


**כִּי צַו לָצָו צַו לָצָו.** נָבִיא מְצַוֶּה לָהֶם מֵאֵת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, וְהֵם יֵשׁ לָהֶם צַו שֶׁל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כְּנֶגֶד צַו זֶה; וְחוֹזֵר הַנָּבִיא וּמוֹכִיחָם, וְהֵם תָּמִיד אוֹמְרִים: ״יֵשׁ לָנוּ צַו לְצַו שֶׁלָּנוּ חָשׁוּב מִשֶּׁלְּךָ״:


**For a precept for a precept, a precept for a precept** The prophet commands them from the Holy One, blessed be He, but they - they have a precept of the idols, equal to this precept, and the prophet repeatedly admonishes them, and they always say, “We have a precept for the precept.” Ours is superior to yours.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:10:2)


**קַו לָקָו.** יֵשׁ לָהֶם קַו מִשְׁקוֹלֶת מִשְׁפְּטֵי רֶשַׁע כְּנֶגֶד קַו הַצֶּדֶק:


**a line for a line** They have a plumb-line of wicked judgments equal to the plumb- line of justice.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:10:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:10:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:10:3)


**זְעֵיר שָׁם.** הַנָּבִיא אוֹמֵר לָהֶם: עוֹד מְעַט תָּבוֹא עֲלֵיכֶם רָעָה, וְהֵם אוֹמְרִים: ״זְעֵיר שָׁם, יְמַהֵר יָחִישָׁה מַעֲשֵׂהוּ״ (ישעיהו ה:יט) לְיָמִים מוּעָטִין:


**a little there, a little there** The prophet says to them, “In a short time evil will come upon you,” and they say, “A little there, let Him hurry, let Him hasten His deeds in a short time.”



### Verse 11

###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:11:1)


**בְּלַעֲגֵי שָׂפָה.** וְכֵן כָּל לְשׁוֹן לְעָגִים, וְכֵן (ישעיהו לב:ד) ״עִלְּגִים״, שְׁנֵיהֶם לְשׁוֹן הָפוּךְ שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְיֻשָּׁר לְהִשָּׁמַע:


**With distorted speech** (בְּלַעֲגֵי שָׂפָה) Similarly, לְעָגִים and (infra 32:4), עִלְּגִים, are both expressions of distorted speech, which is not readily grasped.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:11:2)


**יְדַבֵּר אֶל הָעָם הַזֶּה.** כָּל הַמְדַבֵּר אֲלֵיהֶם דְּבַר נְבוּאָה וְתוֹכָחָה, דּוֹמֶה לָהֶם לְלָשׁוֹן נִלְעָג, שֶׁאֵין יְכוֹלִין לְהָבִין בּוֹ:


**he speaks to this people** Everyone who speaks to them words of prophecy or admonition is to them like a distorted language, which they cannot understand.



### Verse 12

###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:12:1)


**אֲשֶׁר אָמַר** הַנָּבִיא לָהֶם **זֹאת הַמְּנוּחָה** – לִהְיוֹתְכֶם בְּשַׁלְוָה, **הָנִיחוּ לֶעָיֵף** – שֶׁלֹּא תִגְזְלוּהוּ, **זֹאת** תִּהְיֶה לָכֶם **הַמַּרְגֵּעָה**:


**For he said** The prophet said to them, “This is the rest,” that you should have rest, “give rest to the weary,” that you shall not rob him, “and this” shall be “tranquility” for them (var. for you).



### Verse 13

###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:13:1)


**וְהָיָה לָהֶם דְּבַר ה׳ וגו׳.** כְּמִדָּתָם יִמְדּוֹד לָהֶם, יִגְזוֹר שֶׁדְּבָרוֹ עֲלֵיהֶם **צַו** שֶׁל אֻמּוֹת הַמִּשְׁתַּעְבְּדִים בָּם עַל **צַו**, פְּקוּדָה עַל פְּקוּדָה, עֲבוֹדָה עַל עֲבוֹדָה,**קַו** שֶׁל פֻּרְעָנוּת כְּנֶגֶד **קַו** שֶׁל עֲבֵירוֹת שֶׁבְּיָדָם, **קַו לָקָו** תִּקְוָה חִלּוּף תִּקְוָה, יְקַוּוּ לְאוֹר וְהִנֵּה חֹשֶׁךְ (איוב ג:ט):


**And the word of the Lord shall be, etc.** According to their measure, He shall mete out to them; He shall decree upon them with His word upon them, a precept of the nations that enslave them, upon a precept, a command upon a command, labor upon labor; a line of retribution commensurate with the line of sins that they committed (lit., in their hand); קַו לָקָו, derived from קוה, a hope instead of a hope; they will hope for light, and behold, there will be darkness.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:13:2)


**זְעֵיר שָׁם זְעֵיר שָׁם.** לְיָמִים מוּעָטִים תָּבֹא עֲלֵיהֶם, וְהֵם יִתְמַעֲטוּ שָׁם בְּאֶרֶץ אוֹיְבֵיהֶם:


**a little there, a little there** In a short time, it shall come upon them, and they shall become few there in the land of their enemies.

###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:14:1

**מֹשְׁלֵי הָעָם הַזֶּה.** הָאוֹמְרִים **לָצוֹן** בְּלָשׁוֹן מָשָׁל, כְּגוֹן:


**the allegorists of this people** who express their scorn as an allegory, such as:



### Verse 15

###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:15:1)


**כָּרַתְנוּ בְרִית אֶת מָוֶת.** שֶׁלֹּא יָבֹא עָלֵינוּ:


**We made a treaty with death** that it come not upon us.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:15:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:15:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:15:2)


**עָשִׂינוּ חֹזֶה.** גְּבוּל שֶׁלֹּא יַעַבְרֶנְהוּ, וְכֵן ״מְחוֹז חֶפְצָם״ (תהלים קז:ל), וְכֵן ״מֶחֱזָה אֶל מֶחֱזָה״ (מלכים א ז:ה), כֻּלָּם לְשׁוֹן ׳גְּבוּל׳ הֵם וְחִיצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל דָּבָר, אשומיי״ר בלע״ז:


**we have made a limit** a boundary that it should not cross. Comp. (Ps. 117:30) “the boundary (מְחוֹז) of their desire,” similarly (I Kings 7:4), “An edge opposite an edge (מֶחֱזָה אֶל מֶחֱזָה). They are all an expression of a boundary and an extremity of a thing, asomajjl in O.F.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:15:3

**שִׁיט שׁוֹטֵף.** מַכָּה הַמִּתְהַלֶּכֶת בָּאָרֶץ:


**an overflowing scourge** a scourge that travels throughout the land.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:15:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:15:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:15:4)


**לֹא יְבוֹאֵנוּ.** לֹא יָבֹא עָלֵינוּ:


**it shall not come upon us** (יְבוֹאֵנוּ), the usual form for a transitive verb with a direct object. It shall not come upon us.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:15:5

**שַׂמְנוּ כָזָב.** שַׂמְנוּ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה:

###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:15:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:15:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:15:6)


**מַחְסֵנוּ.** מַחֲסֶה שֶׁלָּנוּ:
