**וּבַשֶּׁקֶר נִסְתָּרְנוּ.** בְּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בָּטַחְנוּ לְהַסְתִּירֵנוּ:


**and in falsehood have we hidden ourselves** We have hoped in idols to conceal us.



### Verse 16

###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:16:1)


**הִנְנִי יִסַּד** לְשׁוֹן עָבָר הוּא, כְּמוֹ (אסתר א:ח) ״יִסַּד הַמֶּלֶךְ״, וְכֵן צָרִיךְ לְפוֹתְרוֹ: הִנְנִי הוּא אֲשֶׁר יִסַּד כְּבָר. (**בְּצִיּוֹן אֶבֶן** כְּבָר) נִגְזְרָה הַגְּזֵרָה לְפָנַי, וְהֶעֱמַדְתִּי מֶלֶךְ מָשִׁיחַ, שֶׁיְּהֵא בְּצִיּוֹן לְ**אֶבֶן בֹּחַן**, לְשׁוֹן מִבְצָר וְחֹזֶק, כְּמוֹ (ישעיהו לב:יד) ״עֹפֶל וָבַחַן״, וּכְמוֹ ״הֵקִימוּ בְחוּנָיו״ (ישעיהו כג:יג):


**Behold, I have laid a foundation** This is the past tense. Comp. (Esther 1:8) “For so had the king established (יִסַּד).” And so must it be interpreted: Behold, I am He Who has already laid [a stone in Zion. Already] a decree has been decreed before Me, and I have set up the King Messiah, who shall be in Zion as an אֶבֶן בּוֹחֵן, a fortress stone, an expression of a fortress and strength. Comp. (infra 32:14) “A tower and a fortress (וּבֹחֵן).” Comp. also (supra 23:13) “They erected its towers (בַּחוּנָיו).”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:16:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:16:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:16:2)


**מוּסָד מוּסָּד.** הָרִאשׁוֹן פַּתַּח לְפִי שֶׁהוּא דָבוּק, מוּסָד שֶׁל מוּסָד, שֶׁהוּא מוּסָד גָּמוּר:


**a foundation well founded** (מוּסַד מוּסָּד). The first one is voweled with a pattah because it is in the construct state, a foundation of a foundation, which is a solid foundation.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:16:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:16:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:16:3)


**הַמַּאֲמִין לֹא יָחִישׁ.** הַמַּאֲמִין דָּבָר זֶה לֹא יְמַהֲרֶנָּה, לֹא יֹאמַר: ״אִם אֱמֶת הוּא, יְמַהֵר לָבֹא״:


**the believer shall not hasten** Whoever believes this word shall not hasten it. He shall not say, “If it is true, let it come quickly.”



### Verse 17

###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:17:1)


**וְשַׂמְתִּי מִשְׁפָּט לְקָו.** לִפְנֵי בֹּא אוֹתוֹ מֶלֶךְ אָבִיא עֲלֵיכֶם גְּזֵרוֹת לְהָתֵם הַפּוֹשְׁעִים שֶׁבָּכֶם, וְשַׂמְתִּי מִשְׁפָּט יִסּוּרִין לִהְיוֹת לְקָו, כְּלוֹמַר: אָשִׂים קַו מִדַּת יִסּוּרִין לְהָבִיא עֲלֵיכֶם, וְאֶת **צְדָקָה** אָשִׂים שֶׁתְּהֵא **מִשְׁקֹלֶת** הַמְיַשֶּׁרֶת בִּנְיַן הַבּוֹנִין בַּחוֹמוֹת, כְּלוֹמַר: שֶׁתְּהֵא צְדָקָה מְהַלֶּכֶת לִפְנֵיהֶם וּמְיַשֶּׁרֶת דַּרְכֵיהֶם, שֶׁיִּכְלוּ הַפּוֹשְׁעִים וְנוֹתְרוּ הַצַּדִּיקִים:


**And I will make justice the line** Before the advent of that king, I will bring decrees upon you to end the transgressors among you, and I will make the judgment of chastening to the line; i.e., I will make the line the standard of chastening (var. the line of My standard, chastening), to bring upon you, and righteousness I will make that it should be the plummet that straightens the building of walls, i.e. that righteousness shall go before them and straighten their ways, that the transgressors shall be destroyed and the righteous shall remain.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:17:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:17:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:17:2)


**וְיָעָה בָרָד מַחְסֵה כָזָב.** אוֹתוֹ כִּסּוּי שֶׁאֲמַרְתֶּם **כִּי שַׂמְנוּ כָזָב מַחְסֵנוּ**, יָבֹא בָרָד וִיטַאטְאֵנוּ. **וְיָעָה** לְשׁוֹן ׳טִאוּט׳, כְּמוֹ ״אֶת הַיָּעִים״ (מלכים א ז:מ) שֶׁגּוֹרְפִין בָּהֶן אֵפֶר הַכִּירוֹת:


**and hail shall sweep away the shelter of lies** That covering that you said, “For we have made lies our shelter,” I will bring hail and it shall sweep it away. (וְיָעָה) is an expression of sweeping. Comp. (I Kings 7:40) “the shovels (הַיָּעִים)” with which they scoop up the ashes from the stoves.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:17:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:17:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:17:3)


**וְסֵתֶר**, שֶׁאֲמַרְתֶּם עָלָיו **וּבַשֶּׁקֶר נִסְתָּרְנוּ** הַמַּיִם יִשְׁטְפוּהוּ, כְּלוֹמַר: אָבִיא הֲמוֹן אֻמּוֹת שֶׁיִּשְׁבְּרוּ מַצֵּבוֹתֵיכֶם וּפְסִילֵיכֶם. וְלָשׁוֹן **מִשְׁפָּט** הָאָמוּר כָּאן יושטיצ״א בלע״ז:


**the hiding place** concerning which you said, “And in falsehood have we hidden ourselves,” the water shall flood it, i.e. I will bring a multitude of nations that will break your monuments and your graven images. The expression of מִשְׁפָּט mentioned here is jostise (justice) in O.F.



### Verse 18

###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:18:1)


**וְכֻפַּר בְּרִיתְכֶם אֶת מָוֶת.** וְיִתְבַּטֵּל הַבְּרִית אֲשֶׁר אֲמַרְתֶּם **כָּרַתְנוּ בְרִית אֶת מָוֶת**. כָּל ׳כַּפָּרָה׳ לְשׁוֹן ׳קִנּוּחַ׳ וְ׳סִלּוּק דָּבָר׳, וְכֵן ״אֲכַפְּרָה פָנָיו״ (בראשית לב:כא):


**And your treaty with death shall be nullified** The treaty about which you said, “We have made a treaty with death,” shall be nullified. Every expression of כַּפָּרָה, atonement, is really an expression of wiping or removing something. Compare (Gen. 32:21): “I shall appease (אֲכַפְּרָה) his anger,” (lit., I will wipe away his anger.)


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:18:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:18:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:18:2)


**וְחָזוּתְכֶם**, אֲשֶׁר אֲמַרְתֶּם: **עִם שְׁאוֹל עָשִׂינוּ חֹזֶה**:


**and your limit** which you said, “With the grave we set a limit.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:18:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:18:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:18:3)


**שׁוֹט שׁוֹטֵף.** אֲשֶׁר אֲמַרְתֶּם **לֹא יְבוֹאֶנּוּ, וִהְיִיתֶם לוֹ לְמִרְמָס**:


**an overflowing scourge** which you said, “will not come upon us,” you shall be trampled by it.



### Verse 19

###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:19:1)


**בַּבֹּקֶר בַּבֹּקֶר.** כְּלוֹמַר, תָּדִיר תָּדִיר אָבִיא עֲלֵיכֶם גְּזֵרוֹת:


**every morning** I.e., I will always bring decrees upon you.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:19:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:19:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:19:2)


**וְהָיָה רַק זְוָעָה הָבִין שְׁמוּעָה.** זְוָעָה לְכָל הַשּׁוֹמְעִים לְהָבִין שְׁמוּעוֹת פֻּרְעָנוּת הַקָּשׁוֹת שֶׁאָבִיא עֲלֵיכֶם, כָּל הַשּׁוֹמְעִים יָזוּעוּ:


**and it shall be sheer terror to understand the message** Terror for all those who hear, to understand the messages of the harsh retributions that I will bring upon you. All who hear shall quake.



### Verse 20

###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:20:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:20:1)


**כִּי קָצַר הַמַּצָּע מֵהִשְׂתָּרֵעַ.** כִּי אָבִיא עֲלֵיכֶם שׂוֹנֵא דּוֹחֵק אֶתְכֶם, אֲשֶׁר לֹא תוּכְלוּ לְהַסְפִּיק עֲבוֹדָתוֹ, כְּשֶׁיַּצִּיעַ מַצָּעוֹ עֲלֵיכֶם יִקְצַר לוֹ **מֵהִשְׂתָּרֵעַ** הַשּׁוֹכֵב עָלָיו:


**For the bed is too short for one to stretch** When I bring the enemy upon you, he shall press you so that you will not be able to supply his work. When he spreads out his bed upon you, it will be too short for the one who lies on it to stretch.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:20:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:20:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:20:2)


**מֵהִשְׂתָּרֵעַ.** מִהִשְׁתַּטֵּחַ לְהַאֲרִיךְ אֵיבָרָיו, אישטנדליי״ר בלע״ז:


**to stretch** (מֵהִשְׂתָּרֵעַ) to lengthen one’s limbs, estandejlejjr in O.F.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:20:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:20:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:20:3)


**וְהַמַּסֵּכָה צָרָה.** הַנָּסִיךְ שֶׁיִּמְשׁוֹל עֲלֵיכֶם יִהְיֶה מְקוֹמְכֶם דָּחוּק לוֹ בְּהִתְכַּנְּסוֹ לְתוֹכוֹ. וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ דְּרָשׁוּהוּ (יומא טב) עַל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁהִכְנִיס מְנַשֶּׁה לַהֵיכָל (דברי הימים ב לג:ז): **קָצַר הַמַּצָּע** הַזֶּה **מֵהִשְׂתָּרֵעַ**, מֵהִשְׂתָּרֵר עָלָיו שְׁנֵי רֵעִים. וַאֲנִי פֵּרַשְׁתִּיו לְפִי פְּשׁוּטוֹ, וּבְדֶרֶךְ זֶה תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן. וְאַף מִדְרַשׁ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ יֵשׁ לְיַשְּׁבוֹ עַל אֹפֶן הַדִּבּוּר, כְּלוֹמַר: לָמָּה אֲנִי מֵבִיא עֲלֵיכֶם פֻּרְעָנוּת זוֹ? לְפִי שֶׁ**קָּצַר הַמַּצָּע מֵהִשְׂתָּרֵעַ** אֲנִי לְבַדִּי עָלָיו, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (מלכים א ח:כז) ״הִנֵּה הַשָּׁמַיִם לֹא יְכַלְכְּלוּךָ״, וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן בְּהַכְנִיסְכֶם מַסֵּכָה עִמִּי, כִּבְיָכוֹל צַר לָנוּ הַמָּקוֹם:


**and the ruler it shall be narrow** (וְהַמַּסֵּכָה) The prince who will rule over you - your place will be cramped for him when he enters it. Our Rabbis, however, expounded it as referring to the idol that Manasseh brought into the heichal, (the Temple proper) (II Chron. 33:7). This bed is too short מֵהִשְׂתָּרֵעַ, for two friends to rule over it. I explained it according to its simple meaning, and in this manner Jonathan rendered it. The Midrashic interpretation of our Rabbis, however, can be reconciled with the context. I.e., why do I bring this retribution upon you? Because the bed is too narrow for Me alone to stretch out on it, as it is said (I Kings 8:27): “Behold the heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain You.” Surely, when you bring in a molten image with Me, so to speak, the place is too narrow for us.



### Verse 21

###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:21:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:21:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:21:1)


**כִּי כְהַר פְּרָצִים.** תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״אֲרֵי כְּמָא דְזָעוּ טוּרַיָּא כַּד אִתְגְּלִי יְקָרָא דַה׳ בְּיוֹמֵי עֻזִּיָּה מַלְכָּא (ישעיהו ו:ד), וּכְנִיסִין דַּעֲבִיד לִיהוֹשֻׁעַ בְּמֵישַׁר גִּבְעוֹן (יהושע י:יב) וְכוּ׳, כֵּן יִתְגְּלֵי לְאִתְפָּרְעָא מִדְּעַבְדִין וְכוּ׳״:


**For like the mountain of breaches** Jonathan paraphrases: For, just as the mountains quaked when the glory of the Lord was revealed on the day of King Uzziah, (supra. 6:4,) and as the miracles He performed for Joshua in the valley of Gibeon (Jos. 10:12f) (to punish the wicked who transgressed His word,) so shall He be revealed to punish those who perform (strange deeds, strange are their deeds, and those who worship pagan deities, strange is their worship).


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:21:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:21:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:21:2)


**זָר מַעֲשֵׂהוּ.** יִדְמֶה לָכֶם לְזָר, כִּי יָבוֹא עֲלֵיכֶם פֻּרְעָנוּת קָשָׁה:


**strange is His deed** He will seem to you as a stranger, for He will bring upon them ([all other editions:] upon you) harsh retribution.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:21:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:21:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:21:3)


**וְלַעֲבֹד עֲבֹדָתוֹ.** לַעֲשׂוֹת מְלַאכְתּוֹ, כְּמוֹ ׳עֲבוֹדַת הָאֲדָמָה׳, לבורי״ר בלע״ז:


**and to perform His work** (וְלַעֲבֹד עֲבֹדָתוֹ) like work of the soil, ‘laborer’ in O.F.



### Verse 22

###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:22:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:22:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:22:1)


**וְעַתָּה אַל תִּתְלוֹצָצוּ.** לֵאמֹר ״כָּרַתְנוּ בְרִית אֶת מָוֶת״ (ישעיהו כח:טו):


**And now, do not scorn** saying, “We have made a treaty with death.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:22:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:22:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:22:2)


**מוֹסְרֵיכֶם.** יִסּוּרִין:


**your pains** (מוֹסְרֵיכֶם) your pains.



### Verse 24

###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:24:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:24:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:24:1)


**הֲכֹל הַיּוֹם** לְשׁוֹן תְּמִיהָה הוּא, לְכָךְ נָקוּד חֲטַף פַּתַּח:


**all day** This is the interrogative. Therefore, it is voweled with a hataf pattah.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:24:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:24:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:24:2)


**יַחֲרֹשׁ.** מִי שֶׁחוֹרֵשׁ לִזְרוֹעַ, וְכִי הַחוֹרֵשׁ כְּדֵי לִזְרֹעַ לְעוֹלָמִים חוֹרֵשׁ? אִם כֵּן, מַה יּוֹעִיל? אַף הַנְּבִיאִים מוֹכִיחִים אֶתְכֶם לְהַחֲזִירְכֶם לְמוּטָב, הַלְּעוֹלָמִים יוֹכִיחוּ וְלֹא יוֹעִילוּ?


**shall...plow** One who plows to sow - does the one who plows to sow plow forever? If so, what does he accomplish? Similarly, the prophets admonish you to bring you back to do good deeds. Shall they admonish forever and not accomplish?


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:24:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:24:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:24:3)


**יִפְתַּח וִישַׂדֵּד אַדְמָתוֹ.** וְכִי לְעוֹלָם לֹא יִזְרַע, אֶלָּא תָּמִיד יִפְתַּח אֶת הָאֲדָמָה בְּאִתִּים וּבִכְלֵי מַחֲרֵשָׁה? **וִישַׂדֵּד** לְשׁוֹן עֲבוֹדַת שָׂדֶה. **יִפְתַּח וִישַׂדֵּד** – בִּתְחִלָּה הוּא עוֹשֶׂה תְּלָמִים רְחָבִים וְסוֹף הוּא עוֹשֶׂה תְּלָמִים קְטַנִּים בְּמִדְרַשׁ רַבִּי תַּנְחוּמָא:


**Shall he open and harrow his soil?** Shall he never sow but always open the soil with plowshares and plowing implements? יְשַׂדֵּד is an expression of work of the field. Shall he open and harrow? First he makes wide furrows and later he makes small furrows. This we learned in the Midrash of Rabbi Tanhuma.



### Verse 25

###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:25:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:25:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:25:1)


**הֲלוֹא** כֵּן דֶּרֶךְ הַחוֹרֵשׁ: כֵּיוָן שֶׁחוֹרֵשׁ, מַשְׁוֶה פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה וְאַחַר כָּךְ זוֹרֵעַ:


**Is it not** so that the plowman, as soon as he plows, smooths the surface of the soil and afterwards sows.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:25:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:25:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:25:2)


**וְהֵפִיץ קֶצַח.** אִם קֶצַח בָּא לִזְרוֹעַ, זוֹרְעָהּ בִּתְפוּצָה, וְאִם **כַמֹּן** בָּא לִזְרוֹעַ, זוֹרְעוֹ בִּזְרִיקָה. **קֶצַח** מִין אֹכֶל הוּא:


**he scatters the black cumin** If he comes to sow black cumin, he sows it by scattering it, and if he comes to sow cumin, he sows it by casting it. קצח is a kind of food.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:25:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:25:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:25:3)


**וְשָׂם חִטָּה שׂוֹרָה וּשְׂעֹרָה נִסְמָן וְכֻסֶּמֶת גְּבֻלָתוֹ.** וְאִם תְּבוּאָה בָּא לִזְרֹעַ, כָּךְ הוּא מִנְהָגוֹ: זוֹרֵעַ הַחִטִּין בְּאֶמְצַע הַחֲרִישָׁה, וְהַשְּׂעוֹרָה זוֹרֵעַ סָבִיב לָהֶם לָהֶם, וְהַכּוּסְמִין זוֹרְעָהּ עַל גְּבוּלֵי הַשָּׂדֶה וּמְצָרָיו. **שׂוֹרָה** לְשׁוֹן ׳שְׂרָרָה׳, זוֹרֵעַ בָּאֶמְצַע, וְנִמְצָאָה שׂוֹרָה עַל הַשְּׂעוֹרִין וְהַכּוּסְמִין:


**and he places the prominent wheat, and the barley for a sign, and the spelt on its borders** And if he comes to sow grain, this is his custom. He sows the wheat in the middle of the furrow, and the barley he sows around it for a sign, and the spelt he sows on the borders of the field [and its boundaries]. שׂוֹרָה is an expression of ruling (שְׂרָרָה). He sows it in the center, and it appears ([printed editions] is found) to rule over the barley and the spelt.



### Verse 26

###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:26:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:26:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:26:1)


**וְיִסְּרוֹ לַמִּשְׁפָּט וְגוֹ׳.** אַף מִי שֶׁ**אֱלֹהָיו יוֹרֶנּוּ**, לֹא לָנֶצַח יִשְׁלַח נְבִיאִים לְהוֹכִיחוֹ. אַחֲרֵי שֶׁאֵינוֹ שׁוֹמֵעַ לַתּוֹכָחָה, הוּא יְיַסְּרֶנּוּ בְּמִשְׁפְּטֵי יִסּוּרִין כְּדֵי שֶׁתּוֹעִיל עֲמַל תּוֹכַחְתּוֹ שֶׁהוֹכִיחַ, כָּזֶה שֶׁמַשְׁוֶה פְּנֵי הָאָרֶץ לִזְרוֹעַ כְּדֵי שֶׁתִּצְלַח עֲמַל חֲרִישָׁתוֹ שֶׁחָרַשׁ:


**And He shall chasten him justly** Likewise, he whose God directs him, He shall not send prophets forever to admonish him. Since he does not heed admonition, He shall chasten him with judgments of chastening in order that the toil of His admonition will help, like the one who smoothes the surface of the earth to sow, in order that the toil of his plowing that he plowed shall succeed.



### Verse 27

###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:27:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:27:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:27:1)


**בֶחָרוּץ.** הוּא עֵץ עָשׂוּי חֲרִיצִים חֲרִיצִים, וּשְׁמוֹ ״מוֹרַג״ (ישעיהו מא:טו), וּמְחַתֵּךְ בּוֹ הַקַּשִּׁין לִהְיוֹת תֶּבֶן:


**with a grooved [implement]** That is a wooden implement, made with grooves, and its name is מוֹרַג, a threshing-board, and one cuts the straw with it to be straw fodder.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:27:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:27:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:27:2)


**כִּי לֹא בֶחָרוּץ יוּדַשׁ קֶצַח.** לְפִי שֶׁזַּרְעוֹ נוֹחַ לָצֵאת מִתּוֹךְ קַשִּׁין שֶׁלּוֹ, וְכֵן עַל **כַּמֹּן** לֹא יָסִבּוּ **אוֹפַן עֲגָלָה** לְדוּשׁוֹ, לְפִי כִּי קַל הַקֶּצַח לְחוֹבְטָהּ **בַּמַטֶּה** וְהַ**כַּמֹּן בַּשָּׁבֶט**:


**For not with a grooved [implement]** do they thresh the black cumin, for its seed is easily extracted from within its straw, and, likewise, on cumin they do not turn the wheel of a wagon to thresh it, because the black cumin is easily beaten with a staff and the cumin with a rod.



### Verse 28

###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:28:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:28:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:28:1)


**לֶחֶם יוּדָק.** וְאֶת מִי דָּקִים בִּדְבָרִים קָשִׁין? אֶת הַלֶּחֶם שֶׁל תְּבוּאָה, לְפִי שֶׁאֵינָהּ נוֹחָה לֵחָבֵט:


**Bread grain is crushed** And whom (sic) do they crush with harsh implements? The bread of grain (sic), because it is not easily beaten.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:28:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:28:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:28:2)


**כִּי לֹא לָנֶצַח אָדוֹשׁ יְדוּשֶׁנּוּ.** הֲרֵי ׳כִּי׳ זֶה מְשַׁמֵּשׁ בִּלְשׁוֹן ׳אֶלָּא׳: לֹא לָנֶצַח כּוֹתְשִׁין עָלָיו, לְפִי שֶׁלְּעוֹלָם לֹא יִכְתְּשׁוּ גַּרְעִינֵי הַזֶּרַע לִהְיוֹת נִדָּשִׁין לִכָּתֵת עַל יְדֵי הֶחָרוּץ וְאוֹפַן הָעֲגָלָה:


**but it is not threshed forever** This כִּי is used in the sense of ‘but.’ But they do not crush it forever, [because they will not crush the seed kernels forever for them to be threshed to be crushed through the threshing-board and the wagon wheel].


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:28:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:28:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:28:3)


**וְהָמַם גִּלְגַּל עֶגְלָתוֹ וּפָרָשָׁיו.** וּכְשֶׁמְּסַבְּבִין עָלָיו אוֹפַנֵּי עֲגָלָה לְדֻקּוֹ וּלְדוּשׁוֹ, אֲפִלּוּ הַגִּלְגַּל הוּמַם וּמִשְׁתַּבֵּר, וְכֵן שְׁאָר כְּלֵי הָעֲגָלָה עִמּוֹ הַמַּפְרִישִׁים אֶת הַתְּבוּאָה מִקַּשֶּׁיהָ **לֹא יְדֻקֶּנּוּ**, וְהַחִטִּים אֵינָם נִדֹּקִּין לִהְיוֹת נִטְחָנִין. אָדוֹשׁ יְדוּשֶׁנּוּ – כְּמוֹ ״עָשֹׂה יַעֲשֶׂה״ (יחזקאל לא:יא), ״צָנוֹף יִצְנֹף״ (ישעיהו כב:יח), וְאָלֶ״ף זוֹ בָּאָה בִּמְקוֹם הֵ״א, כְּמוֹ ״וְאַחֲרֵי כֵן אֶתְחַבַּר יְהוֹשָׁפָט״ (דברי הימים ב כ:לה) כְּמוֹ הִתְחַבֵּר, אַף כָּאן הָדוֹשׁ יְדוּשֶׁנּוּ, וְכֵן חִבְּרוֹ מְנַחֵם:


**and the wheel of his wagon shall break and its separators** And when they turn the wagon wheels over to crush it and thresh it, even the wheel breaks, and the remaining implements of the wagon with it, that separate the grain from its straw, he will not crush it, and the wheat is not crushed to be ground. be threshed (אָדוֹשׁ יְדוּשֶׁנּוּ. The repetition is peculiar.) Comp. (Ezekiel 31:11) “He will deal (עָשׂה יַעֲשֶׂה),” also (supra 22:18): “He shall wind you around (צָנוֹף יִצְנָפְךָ).” And this ‘alef’ comes instead of a ‘heh’. Comp. (II Chron. 20:35) “And afterwards Jehoshaphat joined (אִתְחַבֵּר),” like הִתְחַבֵּר. Here too, אָדוֹשׁ[is like] הִדּוֹשׁ, and Menahem classified it in this manner (Machbereth p. 68).



### Verse 29

###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:29:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:29:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:29:1)


**גַּם זֹאת מֵעִם וגו׳.** גַּם זֹאת, כְּדֶרֶךְ דָּשֵׁי תְּבוּאָה וְחוֹבְטֵי קֶצַח וְכַמֹּן, **מֵעִם** הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יָצָא:


**This too, etc.** This too, like the custom of threshers of grain and those who flail black cumin and cumin, comes forth from the Holy One, blessed be He.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 28:29:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:29:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:29:2)


**הִפְלִיא עֵצָה.** לְהַרְאוֹתְכֶם רְמָזִים בְּדֶרֶךְ חִדּוּשׁ מָשָׁל נִפְלָא וּמְכֻסֶּה, כִּי כַּאֲשֶׁר הַכַּמּוֹן וְהַקֶּצַח אֵינָם מַכְבִּידִין עֲלֵיהֶם בִּמְדוּשָׁה רַבָּה, לְפִי שֶׁהֵם נֶחְבָּטִין בְּקַל, כָּךְ אִלּוּ הֱיִיתֶם מְמַהֲרִין לְקַבֵּל מוּסָר, לֹא הָיָה מַכְבִּיד עֲלֵיכֶם גְּזֵרוֹת; וְאַתֶּם קָשִׁים לְקַבֵּל תּוֹכָחוֹת כַּתְּבוּאָה הַקָּשָׁה לָדוּשׁ, לְכָךְ יַכְבִּיד עֲלֵיכֶם הַרְבֵּה, וְלֹא לָנֶצַח לְכִלָּיָה יָרִיב וִידַקֶּה, כַּאֲשֶׁר ״לֹא לָנֶצַח אָדוֹשׁ יְדוּשֶׁנּוּ״ (ישעיהו כח:כח), וְיִכְלוּ חִצֵּי מַכּוֹתָיו וְאַתֶּם לֹא תִכְלוּ, דֻּגְמַת הֲמִימַת הַגַּלְגַּל וְהָעֲגָלָה וְהַחִטִּין לֹא יִדֹּקּוּ; וְאִלּוּ הֱיִיתֶם נוֹחִים לִכְלוֹת, לֹא הָיָה בּוֹדֵק אֶתְכֶם בְּיִסּוּרִין קָשִׁין, כַּפִּשְׁתָּנִי הַזֶּה, כְּשֶׁהוּא יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁפִּשְׁתָּנוֹ יָפֶה, הוּא מְנַקֵּשׁ עָלֶיהָ (בראשית רבה לד ב):


**He gave marvelous counsel** to show you hints in the manner of riddles and with an allegory, marvelous and obscure, for, just as with the cumin and the black cumin, with which they do not deal harshly by overthreshing them because they are easily flailed, so, if you would hasten to accept reproof, He would not bear heavily upon you with decrees, but since you are hard to accept reproof, like the grain that is hard to thresh, therefore, He will mete out heavy punishment upon you ([printed editions] - He will make it very heavy for you), but He will not strive and smite forever, ([certain editions]He will not strive and crush forever to destroy) just as one does not thresh forever, and His arrows and His blows shall terminate but you shall not terminate, in the manner that the wagon wheel breaks, but the wheat is not crushed. [If, however, you were easily destroyed, he would not test you with harsh afflictions, like the flax merchant, when he knows that his flax is of high quality, he beats it.]



## Chapter 29


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:1:1)


**הוֹי אֲרִיאֵל.** תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״מַדְבְּחָא דַה׳״, וְאַף יְחֶזְקֵאל קְרָאוֹ כֵּן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (יחזקאל מג:טז): ״וְהָאֲרִיאֵל שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה״, עַל שֵׁם אֵשׁ שֶׁל מַעְלָה שֶׁהָיְתָה רוֹבֶצֶת כַּאֲרִי עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁנִינוּ בְּסֵדֶר יוֹמָא (כא ב). וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ פֵּרְשׁוּ עַל הַהֵיכָל, שֶׁהָיָה צַר מֵאַחֲרָיו וְרָחָב מִלְּפָנָיו:


**Woe, Ariel** Jonathan renders: Altar of the Lord. Ezekiel, too, called it that, as it is said (43: 16): “And the altar (וְהָאֲרִיאֵל) twelve [cubits] in length,” [because of the heavenly fire that lay like a lion atop the altar, as we learned in Tractate Yoma (21b)]. Our Sages, however, explained it in reference to the heichal (the Temple proper), which was narrow from the rear and wide in the front.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:1:2)


**קִרְיַת חָנָה דָוִד.** ״דְּאִתְבְּנֵי בְּקַרְתָּא דִּשְׁרָא בַּהּ דָּוִד״ (תרגום יונתן):


**the city wherein David encamped** The altar that was built in the city wherein David encamped [from Jonathan].


###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:1:3)


**סְפוּ שָׁנָה עַל שָׁנָה.** וְתָמִיד עֲוֹנוֹתֵיכֶם הוֹלְכִים וַחֲזָקִים, עַד שֶׁ**חַגִּים** שֶׁלָּכֶם **יִנְקֹפוּ** וְיִכָּרְתוּ, לְשׁוֹן ״נוֹקֵף זַיִת״ (ישעיהו יז:ו):


**add year to year** And always your sins are continuously increasing until your sacrifices are cut off (יִנְקֹפוּ), an expression similar to (supra 17:6): “like the cutting (כְּנֹקֶּף) of an olive tree.”



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:2:1)


**וְהָיְתָה לִּי כַּאֲרִיאֵל** תְּהֵא מֻקֶּפֶת חַלְלֵי חֶרֶב, כְּמִזְבֵּחַ הַמֻּקָּף זִבְחֵי בְּהֵמָה:


**and it shall be to Me like Ariel** It shall be surrounded by those slain by the sword, like the altar, which is surrounded by animal sacrifices.



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:3:1)


**כַדּוּר.** כְּשׁוּרָה שֶׁל גְּיָסוֹת מַקִּיפוֹת:


**in a circle** like a row of surrounding troops. ([Other editions read:] In a row of surrounding troops.) ([Some manuscripts read:] An expression of the encampment of surrounding troops.)


###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:3:2)


**מֻצָּב.** לְשׁוֹן ׳כַּרְקוֹם׳, הַ**מֻּצָּב** עַל הָעֲיָרוֹת (גיטין כח ב):


**a camp of siege** (מֻצַּב, lit. stationed,) an expression of a camp of siege stationed against the towns.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:3:3)


**מְצֻרוֹת.** לְשׁוֹן ׳מָצוֹר׳:

### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:4:1)


**מֵאֶרֶץ תְּדַבֵּרִי.** יְהֵא נִרְאֶה כְּאִלּוּ דִּבּוּר הַיּוֹצֵא מִפִּיךְ יוֹצֵא מִתַּחַת הַקַּרְקַע:


**from the earth shall you speak** It shall appear as though the speech that comes out of your mouth comes from below the ground.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:4:2)


**אִמְרָתֵךְ תְּצַפְצֵף.** לְהִתְחַנֵּן אֵלַי, וּמִתּוֹךְ תְּחִנָּתֵךְ יִכָּמְרוּ רַחֲמַי:


**shall your speech chirp** to supplicate to Me, and because of your supplication, My mercies shall be aroused.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:4:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:4:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:4:3)


**צִפְצוּף.** הוּא לְשׁוֹן קוֹל לַחַשׁ כְּקוֹל עוֹפוֹת דַּקִּים:


צִפְצוּף is an expression of a whispering (var. weak) voice like the voice of small birds.

**And the multitude of your foreigners shall be like fine dust** The army of Sennacherib, which will be consumed by fire and will become dust.

**and it shall be** this thing.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:5:3

### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:7:1)


**וְהָיָה כַּחֲלוֹם.** שֶׁדּוֹמֶה שֶׁרוֹאֶה וְלֹא רָאָה, כָּךְ יִהְיֶה **הֲמוֹן כָּל הַגּוֹיִם** יִדְמוּ לִכְבּוֹשׁ וְלֹא תַעֲלֶה בְּיָדָם:


**And shall be like a dream** that one imagines that he saw, yet he did not see, so will this multitude of all the nations contemplate to conquer, but they will not succeed.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:7:2)


**וְכָל צֹבֶיהָ.** הַמַּצִּיבִים עָלֶיהָ מַצָּב וּמַשְׁחִית, שֶׁקּוֹרִין צנבי״ל בלע״ז, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּשָׁאוּל (שמואל א יד:טו): ״הַמַּצָּב וְהַמַּשְׁחִית חָרָדוּ״:


**those stationed around her** who set up against her a garrison and raiders called cenbel in O.F., as it is stated regarding Saul (I Sam. 14: 15): “The garrison and the raiders trembled.”

**yearns** (שׁוֹקֵקָה) desires. Comp. (Gen. 3:16) “And to your husband shall be your yearning (תְּשׁוּקָתֵךְ) .”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:8:2

**So shall be, etc.** They shall not achieve their desire which they planned to do.

###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:9:1

**stop** Be patient to reflect [to think] about your deeds.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:9:2

**and wonder** And wonder about your corruption.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:9:3

**הִשְׁתַּעַשְׁעוּ.** לְשׁוֹן ״עֵינָיו הָשַׁע״ (ישעיהו ו:י), הָיוּ עִוְּרִים מֵרְאוֹת:


**they became blind** (הִשְׁתַּעַשְׁעוּ) an expression related to (supra 6:10) “And his eyes are becoming sealed (הָשַׁע),” they were blind, not being able to see [lit., from seeing].

**שָׁכְרוּ.** עַצְמְכֶם **וְלֹא** מִ**יַּיִן**, לָמָּה?


**They were intoxicated** yourselves (sic) but not from wine. Why? ([Parshandatha claims that this reading is erroneous. The correct reading, according to all manuscripts is:] their wise men, but not from wine.)



### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:10:1)


**כִּי נָסַךְ עֲלֵיכֶם ה׳ וגו׳** – לְשׁוֹן ״מֶזֶג״, כְּמוֹ ״מָסְכָה יֵינָהּ״ (משלי ט:ב), אוֹ לְשׁוֹן ׳נְסִיכוּת׳: הִשְׁלִיט בָּכֶם רוּחַ תַּרְדֵּמָה. עַל פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיָה נִבָּא, שֶׁהָיוּ חוֹזִים בַּכּוֹכָבִים:


**For the Lord has poured upon you, etc.** (נָסַךְ) an expression of mixing wine. Comp. (Prov. 9: 2) “She mixed (מָסְכָה) her wine.” It may also be an expression of princedom (נְסִיכוּת). He caused a spirit of deep sleep to overcome you, (lit., to rule over you). Concerning the transgressors of Israel he was prophesying, for they were stargazers and were experts in adjuring the heavenly princes, each one with the proper name for adjuring him. Therefore, they say, “Who will encamp upon us (Jer. 21:13)? If the enemy comes upon us, we can make for it a wall of fire around, ([Most manuscripts read:] If the enemy comes upon the city, we can make for it a wall of fire around,) or surround it with the Great Sea.” Said the Holy One, blessed be He, “I will change the heavenly princes; the one appointed over fire, is appointed over water. When he adjures the prince of fire to bring him fire, he will reply, “This is not mine,” And, likewise, the prince of water. And even the name by which you adjure him, he does not recognize. This is the closing of the eyes and the covering of the heads of the stargazers.



### Verse 11

###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:11:1)


**חֲזוּת הַכֹּל.** כָּל מַה שֶׁהֱיִיתֶם חוֹזִים בַּמַּזָּלוֹת, יִהְיֶה מְכֻסֶּה מִכֶּם כְּדִבְרֵי אִגֶּרֶת הַחֲתוּמָה בְּשַׁעֲוָה, אֲשֶׁר יִתְּנוּהָ לִקְרוֹתָהּ לְיוֹדֵעַ לִקְרוֹת אִגֶּרֶת, **וְאָמַר: ״לֹא אוּכַל״**, שֶׁהֲרֵי אֵין אֲנִי רוֹאֶה בְּתוֹכָהּ לְפִי שֶׁהִיא חֲתוּמָה:


**the vision of everything** All that you used to see in the constellations shall be concealed from you like the words of a letter sealed with wax, which, if they give to read one able to read a letter, he will say, “I cannot, for I see not what is inside, for it is sealed.”



### Verse 12

###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:12:1)


**וְנִתַּן הַסֵּפֶר עַל אֲשֶׁר לֹא יָדַע סֵפֶר.** וּכְשֶׁנּוֹטְלִין מִמֶּנּוּ וּפוֹתְחִין חוֹתָמָהּ וְנוֹתְנִין אוֹתָהּ לְמִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַכִּיר לְשׁוֹן אִגֶּרֶת, וְאוֹמְרִין לוֹ **״קְרָא נָא זֶה״, וְאָמַר ״לֹא יָדַעְתִּי סֵפֶר״**. כָּךְ כְּשֶׁתַּשְׁבִּיעַ שַׂר הָאֵשׁ יֹאמַר **״לֹא אוּכַל כִּי חָתוּם** הַדָּבָר מִמֶּנִּי״, וּכְשֶׁתַּשְׁבִּיעַ אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ יֹאמַר ״אֵינִי מַכִּיר אֶת הַשֵּׁם הַזֶּה שֶׁאַתָּה מַשְׁבִּיעֵנִי בּוֹ, שֶׁאֵין זֶה שְׁמִי״. וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמַר יִרְמְיָה ״הִנְנִי מֵסֵב אֶת כְּלֵי הַמִּלְחָמָה אֲשֶׁר בְּיֶדְכֶם״ (ירמיהו כא:ד), זֶה הַשֵּׁם הַמְפֹרָשׁ. בְּמִדְרַשׁ תְּהִלִּים (מדרש תהלים לו ה):


**And if the book is given** And when they take it from him and open its seal and give it to one who does not understand the language of the letter, and they say to him, “now read this,” he will say, “I cannot read.” Similarly, when you adjure the prince of fire, he will say, “I cannot, for the matter is sealed from me,” and when you adjure his colleague, he will say, “I do not recognize this name, by which you adjure me, for this is not my name.” This is what Jeremiah said (Jer. 21:4): “Behold I will turn around my implements of war that are in your hands.” This refers to the Explicit Name. In Midrash Tehillim (36:5).



### Verse 13

###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:13:1)


**יַעַן כִּי נִגַּשׁ הָעָם הַזֶּה.** יוֹנָתָן תִּרְגֵּם: ״חֲלַף דְּאִתְרַבְרַב עַמָּא הָדֵין״, כְּלוֹמַר: נִגְּשׁוּ לְהַגְבִּיהַּ עַצְמָן עַד לַשָּׁמַיִם, הֵם מַרְאִין עַצְמָן כִּמְכַבְּדִין אוֹתִי בְּפֶה וְשָׂפָה, וְאֶת לִבָּם הִרְחִיקוּ **מִמֶּנִּי**:


**Because this people has come near** Jonathan renders: Because this people has aggrandized itself. I.e., they have come near to raise themselves up to the heavens. They show themselves as though honoring Me with mouth and lip, but their heart they have drawn far away from Me.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:13:2)


**וַתְּהִי יִרְאָתָם אֹתִי.** לֹא בְּלֵב שָׁלֵם, כִּי אִם בְּ**מִצְוַת** הָ**אֲנָשִׁים** הַמְּלַמְּדִים אוֹתָם. הִתְרָאוּ כְּנִכְנָעִים מִלְּפָנָיו כְּדֵי לְפַתּוֹתוֹ בְּפִיכֶם:


**and their fear of Me has become** not wholehearted, but by the command of the people who teach them, they show themselves as humbled before Him in order to entice Him with your mouth.



### Verse 14

###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:14:1)


**לָכֵן הִנְנִי.** הוּא אֲשֶׁר יוֹסִיף **לְהַפְלִיא** פֶּלֶא נוֹסָף עַל פֶּלֶא, כִּסּוּי עַל כִּסּוּי, אֹטֶם עַל אֹטֶם. וּמַהוּ **הַפְּלֵא וָפֶלֶא? וְאָבְדָה חָכְמַת חֲכָמָיו** – קָשֶׁה סִלּוּקָם שֶׁל חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כִּפְלַיִם כְּחֻרְבַּן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ וְכָל קְלָלוֹת שֶׁבְּמִשְׁנֵה תוֹרָה, שֶׁכֻּלָּן אֵינָן אֶלָּא הַפְלָאָה אַחַת, ״וְהִפְלָא ה׳ אֶת מַכּוֹתְךָ״ (דברים כח:נט), וְכָאן שְׁתֵּי הַפְלָאוֹת (איכה רבה א לז):


**Therefore, I will continue** I am He Who will continue to perform additional obscurity upon obscurity, concealment upon concealment, sealing upon sealing. And what is this obscurity upon obscurity? And the wisdom of their wise men shall be lost. The taking away of the sages of Israel is twice as hard as the destruction of the Temple and all the curses in Deuteronomy, for all of them are only one obscurity, as it is said (Deut. 28:59): “And the Lord shall make your plagues obscure (וְהִפְלָא),” whereas here are two obscurities.



### Verse 15

###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:15:1)


**לַסְתִּר עֵצָה.** כְּמוֹ ׳לְהַסְתִּיר עֵצָה׳:


**to hide counsel** (לַסְתִּיר) equivalent to לְהַסְתִּיר.



### Verse 16

###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:16:1)


**הַפְכְּכֶם אִם כְּחֹמֶר הַיֹּצֵר יֵחָשֵׁב.** תַּהְפּוּכוֹת שֶׁלָּכֶם, הֲזֹאת אַתֶּם יוֹדְעִים שֶׁהוּא **כְּחֹמֶר הַיֹּצֵר**? שֶׁאֵין הַחֹמֶר יָכוֹל לוֹמַר **לְעֹשֵׂהוּ לֹא עֲשָׂנִי**, כָּךְ אֵינְכֶם יְכוֹלִין לוֹמַר שֶׁאֵינִי מֵבִין מַעֲשֵׂיכֶם:


**Shall your perversion be regarded like the potter’s clay** (Heb. הָפְכְּכֶם) Your perversions. Do you know this, that it is like the potter’s clay? Just as the clay cannot say of its maker, “He did not make me,” so you cannot say that I do not understand your deeds.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:16:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:16:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:16:2)


**כְּחֹמֶר וגו׳.** לָשׁוֹן תְּמִיהָה הוּא, וְיֵשׁ תְּמִיהוֹת הַמִּתְקַיְּמוֹת:


**Shall...like the potter’s clay, etc.** This is an expression of a question, but there are questions to be answered in the affirmative.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:16:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:16:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:16:3)


**לְעֹשֵׂהוּ.** כְּמוֹ ׳עַל עוֹשֵׂהוּ׳, וְדֻגְמָתוֹ: ״וְאָמַר פַּרְעֹה לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״ (שמות יד:ג), ״פֶּן יֹאמְרוּ לִי אִשָּׁה הֲרָגָתְהוּ״ (שופטים ט:נד):


**of him who made it** (לְעֹשֵׂהוּ, lit. to him who made it.) Like עַל עֹשֵׂהוּ. Comp. (Ex. 14:3) “And Pharaoh shall say of the children of Israel (וְלִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל).” (Jud. 9:54) “Lest they say of me (לִי), ‘A woman killed him.’”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:16:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:16:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:16:4)


**וְיֵצֶר אָמַר לְיוֹצְרוֹ לֹא הֵבִין.** אָמַר עַל יוֹצְרוֹ ״לֹא הֵבִין מַה בְּיִצְרוֹ״? וַהֲלֹא הוּא בָּנָה אֶת הַמַּטְמוֹנִיּוֹת וְהַחֲדָרִים וְהַמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת!


**and the impulse say concerning the One Who formed it, “He does not understand”?** Did he say concerning the One Who formed it, “He does not understand what is in my impulse”? Did He not build the hidden recesses, the inner chambers, and the thoughts?



### Verse 17

###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:17:1)


**הֲלוֹא עוֹד מְעַט** בְּיָמִים מוּעָטִין נָקֵל בְּעֵינַי אִם תָּשׁוּבוּ אֵלַי:


**Indeed, in a short time** In a few days, it is easy in My eyes, if you return to Me


###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:17:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:17:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:17:2)


**וְשָׁב לְבָנוֹן.** שֶׁהוּא יַעַר עֵצִים, לִהְיוֹת כַּרְמֶל, וְיִשּׁוּב שָׂדוֹת וּכְרָמִים:


**the Lebanon shall be turned** The Lebanon, which is a forest of trees, shall be turned into a ‘karmel,’ a settlement of fields and vineyards.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:17:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:17:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:17:3)


**וְהַכַּרְמֶל לַיַּעַר יֵחָשֵׁב.** תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״קִירְוִין סַגִּיאִין יֵיתִיב״. וְאַגָּדָה בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (בראשית רבה כד א): חוּרְשִׁין דְּבַר אִינָשׁ, יִשּׁוּב עָרִים וּבְנֵי אָדָם רָצוּף וּמָלֵא כַּיַּעַר הַזֶּה, שֶׁהוּא מָלֵא עֵצִים:


**and the fruitful field shall be regarded as a forest** Jonathan renders: It shall be populated by large cities. And the Aggadah in Gen. Rabbah (24:1) explains it as forests of people, a settlement of cities and people, crowded and full, like this forest, which is full of trees.



### Verse 18

###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:18:1)


**וְשָׁמְעוּ בַיּוֹם הַהוּא וגו׳.** וְתִבָּטֵל הַקְּלָלָה הָאֲמוּרָה לְמַעְלָה, ״כִּי נָסַךְ ה׳ עֲלֵיכֶם וגו׳ וַתְּהִי לָכֶם חֲזוּת הַכֹּל וגו׳ וְאָבְדָה חָכְמַת חֲכָמָיו״ (ישעיהו כט:י):


**And on that day...shall hear, etc.** And the curse stated above (v. 10 14): “For the Lord has poured upon you, etc....And the vision of everything has been to you, etc....And the wisdom of his wise men shall be lost,” shall be repealed.



### Verse 19

###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:19:1)


**עֲנָוִים.** סַבְלָנִים, שֶׁסָּבְלוּ עֻלּוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וּגְזֵרוֹתָיו:


**And those who suffered** The suffering ones, who bore the yoke of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His decrees.



### Verse 20

###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:20:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:20:1)


**כָּל שֹׁקְדֵי אָוֶן.** הַשּׁוֹקְדִים וּמִתְבּוֹנְנִים הֵיאַךְ יִפְעֲלוּ אָוֶן:


**those eager to commit violence** Those who hurry and give thought how they will commit violence.



### Verse 21

###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:21:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:21:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:21:1)


**מַחֲטִיאֵי אָדָם בְּדָבָר.** הֵם נְבִיאֵי הַשֶּׁקֶר:


**Those who cause man to sin by a word** They are the false prophets.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:21:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:21:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:21:2)


**וְלַמּוֹכִיחַ בַּשַּׁעַר יְקֹשׁוּן.** ״וּלְדְמוֹכַח לְהוֹן בָּעַן לֵיהּ תַּקְלָא״ (תרגום יונתן). לְשׁוֹן ׳מוֹקֵשׁ׳:


**and him who reproves in the gate they trap** (יְקשׁוּן. Jonathan renders:) And for the one who reproves them, they seek for him a stumblingblock. (יְקשׁוּן is) an expression related to מוֹקֵשׁ, a trap.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:21:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:21:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:21:3)


**וַיַּטּוּ בַתֹּהוּ צַדִּיק.** ״וְאַסְטִיאוּ בְּשֶׁקֶר דִּין זַכָּאִין״ (תרגום יונתן):


**and they mislead the righteous through fraud** And they pervert with fraud the cause of the just [from Jonathan].



### Verse 22

###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:22:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:22:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:22:1)


**אֲשֶׁר פָּדָה אֶת אַבְרָהָם.** מֵאוּר כַּשְׂדִּים:


**Who redeemed Abraham** from Ur of the Chaldees.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:22:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:22:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:22:2)


**לֹא עַתָּה יֵבוֹשׁ יַעֲקֹב** מֵאָבִיו:


**Now Jacob shall not be ashamed** of his father.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:22:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:22:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:22:3)


**וְלֹא עַתָּה פָּנָיו יֶחֱוָרוּ.** מֵאֲבִי אָבִיו, שֶׁאֵין נִמְצָא פְּסוּל בְּמִטָּתוֹ, וּמִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵמָה:


**and now his face shall not pale** because of his father’s father, for no imperfection has been found in his bed, and his bed is perfect.



### Verse 23

###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:23:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:23:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:23:1)


**כִּי בִרְאֹתוֹ יְלָדָיו.** אֲשֶׁר יִהְיוּ מַעֲשֵׂי יָדַי, כְּלוֹמַר: צַדִּיקִים **בְּקִרְבּוֹ, כִּי בִרְאֹתוֹ בְּקִרְבּוֹ** אֲשֶׁר **יְלָדָיו מַעֲשֵׂה יָדַי יַקְדִּישׁוּ שְׁמִי**, כְּגוֹן חֲנַנְיָה מִישָׁאֵל וַעֲזַרְיָה (דניאל ג), לְכָךְ לֹא **יֶחֱוָרוּ פָּנָיו**:


**For, when he sees his children** who will be the work of My hands, i.e., righteous men, in his midst, for when he sees in his midst that his children, the work of My hands, shall hallow My name, e. g., Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah (see Dan. 3), therefore, his face shall not pale.



### Verse 24

###### Rashi on Isaiah 29:24:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:24:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/29:24:1)


**וְרוֹגְנִים יִלְמְדוּ לֶקַח.** לָשׁוֹן ״וַתֵּרָגְנוּ בְאָהֳלֵיכֶם״ (דברים א:כז), אוֹתָם שֶׁהָיוּ מִתְלוֹנְנִים וְנִרְגָּנִים עַל דִּבְרֵי הַנְּבִיאִים יִלְמְדוּ לֶקַח:


**and grumblers shall learn instruction** (וְרוֹגְנִים) an expression similar to (Deut. 1:27) “And you grumbled (וַתְּרָגְנוּ) in your tents.” Those who were complaining and grumbling about the words of the prophets shall learn instruction.



## Chapter 30


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Isaiah 30:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/30:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/30:1:1)


**סוֹרְרִים.** סָרִים מִן הַדֶּרֶךְ:


**rebellious** (סוֹרְרִים) who turn away from the way of God.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 30:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/30:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/30:1:2)


**לִנְסֹךְ מַסֵּכָה.** לְהַמְשִׁיל עֲלֵיהֶם מוֹשֵׁל, **וְלֹא רוּחִי** וְדַעְתִּי בַּדָּבָר; וּמַהוּ הַנִּסּוּךְ? הוּא פַּרְעֹה:


**and to appoint a ruler** (וְלִנְסֹךְ מַסֵּכָה) to appoint a ruler to rule over them, with neither My spirit nor My will in the matter, and what is this appointing? This is Pharaoh.



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Isaiah 30:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/30:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/30:2:1)


**הַהֹלְכִים לָרֶדֶת מִצְרַיִם.** עַל הוֹשֵׁעַ בֶּן אֵלָה, ״אֲשֶׁר שָׁלַח מַלְאָכִים אֶל סוֹא מֶלֶךְ מִצְרַיִם״ (מלכים ב יז:ד):


**Those who go to descend to Egypt** This alludes to Hoshea, son of Elah, who sent emissaries to So, king of Egypt (II Kings 17:4).


###### Rashi on Isaiah 30:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/30:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/30:2:2)


**לָרֶדֶת מִצְרַיִם.** אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל גְּבוֹהָה מִכָּל הָאֲרָצוֹת (קידושין סט א). דָּבָר אַחֵר: יְרִידָה הִיא לָהֶם:


**to descend to Egypt** The land of Israel is higher than all the other lands. Alternatively, this is a degradation for them.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 30:2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/30:2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/30:2:3)


**וְלַחְסוֹת.** לְהִתְכַּסּוֹת, אבריאי״ר בלע״ז:


**and to take shelter** (lit.) to cover themselves, abrier in O. F. (This is the equivalent of sabriter in Modern French, to take shelter.)



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Isaiah 30:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/30:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/30:4:1)


**כִּי הָיוּ בְצֹעַן שָׂרָיו.** שֶׁל מֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּשְׁלִיחוּת לְמֶלֶךְ מִצְרָיִם:


**For his princes were in Zoan** The princes of the king of Israel in their errand to the king of Egypt.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 30:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/30:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/30:4:2)


**חָנֵס.** הִיא תַּחְפַּנְחֵס:


**Hanes** That is Tahpanhes.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Isaiah 30:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/30:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/30:5:1)


**כֹּל הוֹבִאישׁ.** כֻּלָּם בִּיְּשׁוּ אֶת עַצְמָן לִקְנוֹת לָהֶם אֲדוֹנִים חִנָּם, וְעַם הָאָרֶץ **לֹא יוֹעִילוּ לָמוֹ**:


**They all disgraced themselves** They all disgraced themselves to acquire a master for nothing, and the people of the land will not avail them.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 30:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/30:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/30:5:2)


**עַל עַם.** בִּשְׁבִיל **עַם לֹא יוֹעִילוּ לָמוֹ**:


**because of a people** (Lit., on a people.) Because of a people that will not avail them.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 30:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/30:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/30:5:3)


**לְחֶרְפָּה.** גִּדּוּף, דישטרב״ר בלע״ז:


**for disgrace** For insult, distraber in O.F., to insult.



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Isaiah 30:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/30:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/30:6:1)


**מַשָּׂא בַּהֲמוֹת נֶגֶב.** ״מַטְלִין עַל בְּעִירְהוֹן בְּאוֹרַח דָּרוֹמָא״ (תרגום יונתן), לְפִי שֶׁאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם בִּדְרוֹמָהּ שֶׁל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְזֶהוּ הַגִּדּוּף וְהַחֶרְפָּה שֶׁמְּחָרְפִין אוֹתָן: רְאוּ אֶת אֵלּוּ שֶׁטּוֹעֲנִין מַשָּׂאוֹת מָמוֹנָם עַל בַּהֲמְתָּם לְהוֹלִיךְ שֹׁחַד לְמִצְרַיִם חִנָּם, וּמְסַכְּנִין עַצְמָן בַּמִּדְבָּרוֹת **אֶרֶץ צָרָה וְצוּקָה וְכוּ׳**:


**The burden of the beasts of the southland** The burdens on their beasts on the way to the southland (Jonathan), for Egypt is in the south of Eretz Israel, and this is the insult and the derision that they would insult them: See these people, whose burdens of money are laden on their beasts to transport bribes to Egypt for nothing, and they imperil themselves in the deserts, in a land of trouble and anguish, etc.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 30:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/30:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/30:6:2)


**אֶפְעֶה.** מִין נָחָשׁ רַע הוּא, וְאֵין בָּעוֹלָם כִּי אִם שְׁנַיִם זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה, וְהֵם יוֹלְדִים לְשִׁבְעִים שָׁנָה (בכורות ח א), וְאַף **שָׂרָף מְעוֹפֵף** מִין נָחָשׁ הוּא, וְלֹא שֶׁיִּהְיוּ לוֹ כְּנָפַיִם לָעוּף, אֶלָּא קוֹפֵץ וּמְדַלֵּג רָחוֹק מְאֹד וְזוֹרֵק לַהַב מִפִּיו:


**viper** It is a species of deadly snakes, and there are only two of them in the world, a male and a female, which reproduce after seventy years, (i.e. its gestation period is seventy years) (Bechoroth 8a). The flying serpent, too, is a species of snake, not that it has wings with which to fly, but it jumps and springs long distances and throws a flame from its mouth.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 30:6:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/30:6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/30:6:3)


**חֵילֵיהֶם.** מָמוֹנָם:


**their wealth** (חֵילֵיהֶם) their money.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 30:6:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/30:6:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/30:6:4)


**דַּבֶּשֶׁת.** חֲטוֹטְרָא, חלדרוב״א בלע״ז, יֵשׁ לוֹ לַגָּמָל בִּמְקוֹם טְעִינַת הַמַּשָּׂא, וְעַל שֵׁם שֶׁמִּתְרַקֶּבֶת תָּמִיד וְסָכִין שָׁם דְּבַשׁ לִרְפוּאָה קְרוּיָה דַּבֶּשֶׁת, כְּדְאָמְרִינַן בְּבָבָא מְצִיעָא (בבא מציעא לח ב): דְּבַשׁ וְהִדְבִּישׁ חָזֵי לִכְתִישָׁא דְּגַמְלֵי:


**the humps** (דַּבֶּשֶׁת) hidroba in O.F. A camel has this in the place the burden is laden, and since it always becomes sore, and they smear honey there to heal it, it is called דַּבֶּשֶׁת, (from דְּבַשׁ, honey,) as we say in Baba Mezia 38b: Honey that lost its sweetness is fit for the sores of the camels.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Isaiah 30:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/30:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/30:7:1)


**לָזֹאת.** לְמִצְרַיִם:


**this** to Egypt.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 30:7:2

**רַהַב הֵם.** גַּסֵּי הָרוּחַ:


**They are haughty** (רַהַב) of proud spirit.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 30:7:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/30:7:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/30:7:3)


**שָׁבֶת.** עַם בָּטֵל וּמִתְגָּאִים חִנָּם. דָּבָר אַחֵר: **שָׁבֶת** – רַהְבָּם וְגַסּוּתָם שֶׁלָּהֶם רָאוּי הוּא לִשְׁבּוֹת:


**idlers** (שָׁבֶת) A people who are idle and are proud for no reason. Alternatively, שָׁבֶת means that their pride and haughtiness is fit to be curtailed.
