**נֹעֵר כַּפָּיו.** אשקו״ט בלע״ז:


**who shakes his hands** (eskot in O.F.).


###### Rashi on Isaiah 33:15:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:15:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:15:3)


**אֹטֵם.** סוֹתֵם, וְכֵן ״שְׁקוּפִים אֲטֻמִים״ (מלכים א ו:ד):


**closes his ear** (אֹטֵם) Comp. (I Kings 6:4) “transparent but closed (אֲטֻמִים).”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 33:15:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:15:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:15:4)


**עֹצֵם.** סוֹגֵר, וְכֵן ״וַיְעַצֵּם אֶת עֵינֵיכֶם״ (ישעיהו כט:י):


**and closes** (וְעֹצֵם) Comp. (supra 29:10) “And He has closed (וַיְעַצֵּם) your eyes.”



### Verse 16

###### Rashi on Isaiah 33:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:16:1)


**לַחְמוֹ נִתָּן.** לֹא יְהֵא ״מְבַקֵּשׁ לֶחֶם״ (תהלים לז:כה), כִּי מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם יַסְפִּיקוּ לוֹ מָזוֹן:


**his bread shall be given** He will not seek bread, for it will be supplied to him from heaven.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 33:16:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:16:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:16:2)


**מֵימָיו נֶאֱמָנִים.** מְקוֹר מֵימָיו לֹא יְכַזֵּב, כְּלוֹמַר: זַרְעוֹ יִגְדַּל וְכָל צְרָכָיו יְסֻפָּקוּ:


**his water sure** The source of his water will not fail. I.e., his seed will become great, and all his wants will be supplied.



### Verse 17

###### Rashi on Isaiah 33:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:17:1)


**מֶלֶךְ בְּיָפְיוֹ תֶּחֱזֶינָה עֵינֶיךָ.** פֵּרוּשׁ: תִּזְכֶּה לִרְאוֹת מֵ**אֶרֶץ מֶרְחַקִּים** מַלְכְּךָ בַּהֲדַר גְּאוֹנוֹ, אוֹ פֵּרוּשׁ: (הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁהוּא מֶלֶךְ, אוֹתוֹ תֶּחֱזֶה מֵ**אֶרֶץ מֶרְחַקִּים** שֶׁאַתָּה עוֹמֵד, תִּרְאֶה הַנִּסִּים וְהַגְּדֻלָּה שֶׁאֶעֱשֶׂה לְךָ, וְ**עַם נוֹעָז עִמְקֵי שָׂפָה** לֹא יִרְאֶה שְׁכִינַת הַמֶּלֶךְ בְּיָפְיוֹ עד כאן, כל זה בסא"א):


**The King in His beauty shall your eyes behold** (The Holy One, blessed be He, Who is a King, Him you shall see from a distant land where you are standing. You shall see the miracles and the greatness that I will perform for you, and a people of a strange tongue, of obscure speech, shall not see the Shechinah of the King in His beauty. [This does not appear in many editions.])


###### Rashi on Isaiah 33:17:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:17:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:17:2)


**מֶלֶךְ בְּיָפְיוֹ תֶּחֱזֶינָה עֵינֶיךָ.** לְךָ הַצַּדִּיק אֲנִי אוֹמֵר שֶׁתִּזְכֶּה לִרְאוֹת זִיו שְׁכִינָתוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם:


**The King in His beauty shall your eyes behold.** To you, O righteous man, I say that you shall merit to see the splendor of the Shechinah of the Omnipresent.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 33:17:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:17:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:17:3)


**תִּרְאֶינָה אֶרֶץ מַרְחַקִּים.** תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״תִּסְתַּכֵּל וְתֶחֱזֵי בְּנַחֲתֵי אַרְע גֵּיהִנָּם״:


**they shall see [from] a distant land** Jonathan renders: You shall look and see those who go down to the land of Gehinnom.



### Verse 18

###### Rashi on Isaiah 33:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:18:1)


**לִבְּךָ יֶהְגֶּה אֵימָה.** כְּשֶׁתִּרְאֶה הַשָּׂרִים וְהַחֲכָמִים שֶׁל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, שֶׁהָיוּ שַׁלִּיטִים בְּחַיֵּיהֶן, וַהֲרֵי הֵם נִדּוֹנִים בַּגֵּיהִנֹּם, יֶהְגֶּה לִבְּךָ אֵימָה וְתֹאמַר: ״אַיֵּה חָכְמָתָן וּגְדֻלָּתָן שֶׁל אֵלּוּ? **אַיֵּה** שֶׁהָיָה **סוֹפֵר** בְּחַיָּיו וְ**שׁוֹקֵל** כָּל דְּבַר חָכְמָה, שֶׁהָיוּ שׁוֹאֲלִין מִמֶּנּוּ כָּל עֲצַת מַלְכוּת?״


**Your heart shall meditate [in] fear** When you see the princes and the savants of the heathens, who ruled during their lifetime, and who are now being judged in Gehinnom, your heart will meditate in terror, and you will say, “Where is the wisdom and the greatness of these men? Where is the one who, during his lifetime, would count and weigh every word of wisdom, for they would ask him every counsel of the kingdom?


###### Rashi on Isaiah 33:18:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:18:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:18:2)


**אַיֵּה סֹפֵר אֶת הַמִּגְדָּלִים.** פֵּרוּשׁ, שֶׁהָיָה סוֹפֵר הַמִּגְדָּלִים אֲשֶׁר בְּעִיר וָעִיר; כִּי אוֹתָם הַבָּתִּים הַגְּבוֹהִים הָיוּ חֲשׁוּבִים, וְנוֹתְנִים יוֹתֵר בְּמַס. וְכָל אוֹתָהּ הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה וְהַפַּחַד לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ עוֹד:


**Where is he who counts the towers** This too is a matter of the kingdom. He is appointed over the houses of the kingdom, how many they are, and how many towers a certain city requires. Comp. (Ps. 48:13) “Encircle Zion and surround it, count its towers,” how many towers it requires.



### Verse 19

###### Rashi on Isaiah 33:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:19:1)


**אֶת עַם נוֹעָז.** כְּמוֹ ״לוֹעֵז״ (תהלים קיד:א), אֵלּוּ אַשּׁוּר וּבָבֶל שֶׁאֵין לְשׁוֹנָם לְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ:


**A people of a strange tongue** (נוֹעָז) like לוֹעֵז. These are all the heathens, whose language is not the holy tongue. ([Other editions read:] These are Assyria and Babylon, whose language is not the holy tongue.) ([Manuscripts read:] These are all the nations whose language is not the holy tongue.)


###### Rashi on Isaiah 33:19:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:19:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:19:2)


**לֹא תִרְאֶה.** לֹא תַחְשֹׁב בְּלִבְּךָ, כִּי כֻּלָּם יִהְיוּ חֲשֵׁכִים וּשְׁפָלִים:


**you shall not see** You shall not esteem in your heart, for they shall all be dark and humble.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 33:19:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:19:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:19:3)


**עִמְקֵי שָׂפָה.** כְּמוֹ ״וַיְהִי כָל הָאָרֶץ שָׂפָה אֶחָת״ (בראשית יא:א):


**speech... obscure** (שָׂפָה, lit. lip.) Comp. (Gen. 11:1) “And all the land was one speech (שָׂפָה).”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 33:19:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:19:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:19:4)


**נִלְעַג לָשׁוֹן.** ״עִגְּלִים״ (ישעיהו לב:ד), וְ**עִמְקֵי שָׂפָה** – כָּל זֶה לָשׁוֹן נָכְרִית שֶׁאֵינָן מַכִּירִין בִּלְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ:


**of stammering tongue** (נִלְעָג לָשׁוֹן). Comp. (32:4) “The tongue of the stammerers (לְשׁוֹן עִלְּגִים),” (and of obscure speech. All this is a foreign language, for they do not understand the holy tongue.)



### Verse 20

###### Rashi on Isaiah 33:20:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:20:1)


**חֲזֵה צִיּוֹן.** וְאֶת מִי תִּרְאֶה בְּלִבְּךָ לְהֵחָשֵׁב מְלוּכָה וּשְׂרָרָה? אֶת צִיּוֹן אֲשֶׁר הִיא **קִרְיַת** בֵּית וַעַד לָנוּ:


**See Zion** But whom will you see in your heart to be regarded as a kingdom and a ruling power? Zion, which is the city of our meeting place.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 33:20:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:20:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:20:2)


**בַּל יִצְעָן.** בַּל יִסַּח, וְדוֹמֶה לוֹ ״אֵלוֹן בְּצַעֲנַנִּים״ (שופטים ד:יא), וּמְתַרְגְּמִינָן: ״מִישַׁר אַגְנַיָּא״, וְהֵם נְקָעִים שֶׁבַּשָּׂדוֹת, שֶׁקּוֹרִין קומבי״ש בלע״ז, כְּמוֹ ״אַגְנֵי דְאַרְעָא מִקְרֵי״ (בבא קמא סא א) שֶׁהַמַּיִם נֶאֱסָפִים שָׁם מִן הֶהָרִים וְהַגִּבְשׁוּשִׁיּוֹת, וּבֵי״ת שֶׁל ׳בְּצַעֲנַנִּים׳ אוֹמֵר אֲנִי שֶׁאֵינָהּ נִשְׁרֶשֶׁת בַּתֵּיבָה אֶלָּא מְשַׁמֶּשֶׁת הִיא:


**that shall not fall** (יִצְעָן) shall not be lowered. Comp. (Jud. 4:11) “Elon-bezaanannim (אֵלוֹן בְּצַעֲנַנִּים),” which is rendered as: the plain of pits (מִישׁוֹר אַגְנַיָּא), which are pits in the fields, called kombes in O.F. Comp. (Baba Kamma 61b) “The pits of the earth (אַגְנֵי דְאַרְעָא) they are considered,” where water gathers from the mountains and the hills. I believe that the ‘beth’ of the word בְּצַעֲנַנִּים is not radical, but is a prefix.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 33:20:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:20:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:20:3)


**בַּל יִסַּע יְתֵדֹתָיו.** הַיְתֵדוֹת שֶׁקּוֹשְׁרִין בּוֹ מֵיתְרֵי הָאֹהֶל, בַּל יִסַּע אוֹתָם מִן הָאָרֶץ מִמְּקוֹם תְּקִיעָתָם, כְּמוֹ ״וַיַּסִּעוּ אֲבָנִים גְּדוֹלוֹת״ (מלכים א ה:לא), וְכֵן ״וַיִּסָּעֵם עִם הַבְּרִיחַ״ (שופטים טז:ג), לְשׁוֹן ׳תְּלִישָׁה׳:


**whose pegs shall never be moved** (יִסַּע) The pegs with which they tie the ropes of the tent he shall not move them from the earth, from the place into which they are thrust. Comp. (I Kings 5:31) “And they quarried (וַיַּסִּעוּ) great stones.” Also (Jud. 16:3), “And he plucked them (וַיִּסּעֵם) together with the bolt,” an expression of uprooting.



### Verse 21

###### Rashi on Isaiah 33:21:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:21:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:21:1)


**כִּי אִם שָׁם.** כִּי אִם מוּסָב עַל **בַּל יִסַּע יְתֵדוֹתָיו** וְעַל **בַּל יִנָּתֵקוּ**, הָרָעָה לֹא תִהְיֶה, כִּי אִם הַטּוֹבָה. **ה׳** יִהְיֶה **שָׁם אַדִּיר לָנוּ**, וְהָעִיר תִּהְיֶה **מְקוֹם נְהָרִים יְאוֹרִים**, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (יחזקאל מז:ד): ״וַיָּמָד אֶלֶף וַיַּעֲבִירֵנִי נַחַל אֲשֶׁר לֹא אוּכַל לַעֲבוֹר״, וְכֵן נִבָּא יוֹאֵל ״וּמַעְיָן מִבֵּית ה׳ יֵצֵא״ (יואל ד:יח), וְהוּא הַנַּחַל שֶׁיְּהֵא מִתְגַּבֵּר וְהוֹלֵךְ:


**But there** ‘But’ refers back to ‘whose pegs shall never be moved,’ and ‘shall not be torn.’ The evil shall not be, only the good. There the Lord shall be mighty for us, and the city shall be a place of rivers and streams, in the manner it is said in Ezekiel (47:4f.): “And He measured a thousand (cubits), and He led me...a stream that I could not cross.” And so did Joel prophesy (4:18) “And a spring shall emanate from the house of the Lord,” that it shall become progressively stronger.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 33:21:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:21:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:21:2)


**אֳנִי שַׁיִט.** אֳנִיָּה הַשָּׁטָה בַּמַּיִם:


**a galley with oars** a ship that floats on the water.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 33:21:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:21:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:21:3)


**וְצִי אַדִּיר.** ״וּבוּרְנִי רַבְּתָא״ (תרגום יונתן)׃


**and a great ship** (וְצִי אַדִּיר) and a great ship [from Jonathan].

###### Rashi on Isaiah 33:23:7

### Verse 24

###### Rashi on Isaiah 33:24:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:24:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:24:1)


**וּבַל יֹאמַר שָׁכֵן.** שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל:


**And the neighbor shall not say** (I.e., the neighbor of) Israel.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 33:24:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:24:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/33:24:2)


**חָלִיתִי.** בִּשְׁבִיל הָאֻמָּה הַזֹּאת בָּאַתְנִי הָרָעָה, כִּי **הָעָם.** יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ עָם, **הַיּוֹשֵׁב** בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם יִהְיֶה סְלוּחַ **עָוֹן**:


**“I am sick”** Because of this nation, this misfortune has befallen me, for **The people** Israel, who is called a people, that dwells in Jerusalem, shall be forgiven of sin.



## Chapter 34


### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:4:1)


**וְנָמַקּוּ כָּל צְבָא הַשָּׁמָיִם.** יִפְחֲדוּ כְּשֶׁאַשְׁלִיךְ אֶת שָׂרֵי אַשּׁוּר וּבָבֶל:


**And all the host of heaven shall melt** They shall be frightened when I cast down the princes of the heathens.([Mss. yield:] the princes of the nations.) ([Warsaw edition:] of Assyria and Babylon.)


###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:4:2)


**וְנָגֹלּוּ.** לְשׁוֹן ׳גּוֹלֵל׳, **וְנָגֹלּוּ כַסֵּפֶר הַשָּׁמָיִם** תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״וְיִתְמְחוֹן מִתְּחוֹת שְׁמַיָּא כְּמָא דְאָמַר עֲלֵיהֶן בְּסִיפְרָא״. וַאֲנִי מְפָרְשׁוֹ לְפִי הָעִנְיָן: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁעַכְשָׁיו הַטּוֹבָה וְהָאוֹרָה לָרְשָׁעִים, לִכְשֶׁיִּתְמַחוּ וְיֵחָרְבוּ יִהְיֶה דוֹמֵם הָעוֹלָם חֹשֶׁךְ עֲלֵיהֶם, כְּאִלּוּ נִגְלַל הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ וְהָאוֹר כִּגְלִילַת סֵפֶר:


**shall be rolled** (וְנָגֹלּוּ) an expression of rolling. And the heavens shall be rolled like a scroll. Jonathan renders: And they shall be erased from beneath the heavens, as it is stated about them in the Book. But I explain it according to the context, for now, the kingdoms of the Ishmaelites (the nations [ms.]) (the wicked [Warsaw ed.]) have fortune and light. When they are erased and destroyed, it will be as though the world has darkened for them, as though the sun and the light are rolled up like the rolling of a scroll.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:4:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:4:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:4:3)


**יִבּוֹל.** יִכְמוֹשׁ:


**withers** (יִבּוֹל) withers.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:4:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:4:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:4:4)


**וְכְנֹבֶלֶת מִתְּאֵנָה.** ׳כְּמֵשָׁה׳ בָּאִילָן קְרוּיָה ׳נוֹבֶלֶת׳, וְזֶהוּ שֶׁפֵּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ (ברכות מ ב): מַאי נוֹבְלוֹת? בּוֹשְׁלֵי כּוֹמְרָא, שֶׁנִּתְבַּשְּׁלוּ בַּכֹּמֶר; לְאַחַר לְקִיטָתָן צוֹבְרָן, וּמִתְחַמְּמוֹת וּמִתְבַּשְּׁלוֹת:


**and as a withered [fig] from a fig tree** The withered fruit of a tree is called נוֹבְלוֹת. This is what our Rabbis (Ber. 40b) explained: What are ‘noveloth’? Fruit ripened in the heater, that become ripe in the heater. After they are picked, he gathers them and they become heated and ripen.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:5:1)


**כִּי רִוְּתָה בַשָּׁמַיִם חַרְבִּי.** לַהֲרוֹג שָׂרִים שֶׁל מַעְלָה, וְאַחַר כָּךְ **תֵּרֵד** עַל עֲמָלֵק לְמַטָּה, שֶׁאֵין כָּל אֻמָּה לוֹקָה עַד שֶׁיִּלְקֶה שַׂר שֶׁלָּהּ בַּמָּרוֹם:


**For My sword has become sated in the heaven** To slay the heavenly princes, and afterward it shall descend on the nation Ishmael ([mss. and Kli Paz:] Edom) ([Warsaw ed.:] Babylonians) below, for no nation suffers until its prince suffers in heaven.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:5:2)


**עַם חֶרְמִי.** עַם מִלְחַמְתִּי, לְשׁוֹן מִשְׁנָה (כתובות יז ב): ״בִּשְׁעַת חֵירוּם שָׁנוּ״, וְכֵן (מלכים א כ:מב) ״אֶת אִישׁ חֶרְמִי״ דְּאַחְאָב:


**the nation with whom I contend** (עַם חֶרמִי), the nation with whom I battle. This is a Mishnaic expression: (Keth. 17b) They taught this in connection with time of strife (חֵרוּם). Comp. (I Kings 20:42) “The man with whom I contend (אִישׁ חֶרְמִי),” referring to Ahab.



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:6:1)


**כָּרִים עַתּוּדִים.** שָׂרִים וְשַׁלְטוֹנִים:


**lambs and goats** princes and governors.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:6:2)


**בְּבָצְרָה.** מֵאֶרֶץ מוֹאָב הִיא, אֲבָל לְפִי שֶׁהֶעֱמִידָה מֶלֶךְ לֶאֱדוֹם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וַיָּמָת חוּשָׁם וַיִּמְלֹךְ תַּחְתָּיו יוֹבָב בֶּן זֶרַח מִבָּצְרָה״ (בראשית לו:לג), לְפִיכָךְ תִּלְקֶה עִמָּהֶם; בפסיקתא:


**in Bozrah** It is from the land of Moab, but since it supplied a king for Edom, as it is stated (Gen. 36:33): “And Jobab son of Zerah of Bozrah reigned in his stead,” it will, therefore, suffer with them. This is found in Pesikta.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:7:1)


**רְאֵמִים עִמָּם.** עִם הָ**עַתּוּדִים** הַכְּתוּבִים לְמַעְלָה:


**wild oxen with them** Kings with governors, wild oxen with the goats mentioned above.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:7:2)


**אַבִּירִים.** פָּרִים בְּרִיאִים וּגְדוֹלִים, כְּמָה דְאַתְּ אָמַר ״עִם אַבִּירֵי בָשָׁן״ (תהלים כב:יג):


**fat bulls** (אַבִּירִים) fat and large bulls, as it is stated (Ps. 22:13): “Fat bulls (אַבִּירֵי) of Bashan surrounded me.”



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:8:1)


**שִׁלּוּמִים לְרִיב צִיּוֹן.** שֶׁיְּשַׁלֵּם גְּמוּל עַל עִסְקֵי רִיב צִיּוֹן, הַצּוֹעֶקֶת לְפָנָיו לְשָׁפְטָהּ מִן הַמְּרֵיעִים לָהּ:


**retribution for the plea of Zion** That He will mete out punishment (lit., pay a reward) for the plea of Zion, who cries before Him to judge her from those who harm her.



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:9:1)


**וְנֶהֶפְכוּ נְחָלֶיהָ.** שֶׁל בַּבְלִים:


**And its streams shall turn** (I.e., the streams) of the heathens. ([Mss. yield:] of Edom.)



### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:10:1)


**מִדּוֹר לָדוֹר.** מֵאוֹתוֹ דּוֹר עַד דּוֹר אַחֲרוֹן. דָּבָר אַחֵר: הִיא קִלְלַת מֹשֶׁה (שמות יז:טז) ״מִלְחָמָה לַה׳ בַּעֲמָלֵק מִדֹּר דֹּר״, מִדּוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה לְדוֹרוֹ שֶׁל שָׁאוּל, וּמִשָּׁם לְדוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מָרְדְּכַי, וּמִשָּׁם לְדוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מֶלֶךְ מְשִׁיחֵנוּ:


**from generation to generation** From that generation until the last generation. Another explanation is that this is Moses’ curse (Ex. 17:16): “The Lord has a war against Amalek from generation to generation.” From Moses’ generation to Saul’s generation, and from there to Mordecai’s generation, and from there to the generation of the King Messiah.



### Verse 11

###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:11:1)


**וְקִפּוֹד.** עוֹף הַפּוֹרֵחַ בַּלַּיְלָה, צואיט״א בלע״ז:


**owl** (קִפֹּד) a bird that flies at night (chouette in French), an owl.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:11:2)


**קַו תֹהוּ.** מִשְׁפָּט שֶׁל שְׁמָמָה:


**a line of waste** A judgment of desolation.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:11:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:11:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:11:3)


**וְאַבְנֵי בֹהוּ.** מִשְׁקָָָָָלוֹת שֶׁל דִּין חֻרְבָּן, כְּמוֹ (דברים כה:טו) ״אֶבֶן שְׁלֵמָה״:


**and weights of destruction** Weights of the judgment of destruction. (אַבְנֵי, lit., stones.) Comp. (Deut. 25:15) “a whole weight (אֶבֶן).”



### Verse 12

###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:12:1)


**חוֹרֶיהָ וְאֵין שָׁם מְלוּכָה יִקְרָאוּ.** שָׂרִים שֶׁלָּהּ עוֹמְדִים, וְאֵין אֶחָד מֵהֶם קוֹרֵא עַל עַצְמוֹ שֵׁם שְׂרָרָה וּמְלוּכָה:


**As for its nobles, there are none who proclaim the kingdom** Its princes stand, and none of them calls upon himself the name of ruling and kingdom.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:12:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:12:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:12:2)


**אָפֶס.** כִּלָּיָה:


**nothing** Destruction.



### Verse 13

###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:13:1)


**וְעָלְתָה אַרְמְנוֹתֶיהָ סִירִים.** כָּךְ דֶּרֶךְ חֳרָבוֹת לִצְמוֹחַ בָּהֶם קוֹצִים וּסְנָאִים, וְהוּא **קִמּוֹשׂ** וְהוּא **חוֹחַ**, כֻּלָּם מִינֵי קוֹצִים הֵם, כְּגוֹן אורטיא״ש וְכַיּוֹצֵא בָּהֶם:


**And its palaces shall grow thorns** So is the nature of ruins to grow thorns and briers, and that is ‘kimosh’ and that is ‘choach’; they are all types of thorns, e.g., ortias, (nettles,) and the like.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:13:2)


**נְוֵה תַנִּים.** הוּא מִדְבָּר, שֶׁהוּא דֶּרֶךְ לִהְיוֹת בּוֹ תַּנִּים, שֶׁהוּא מִין חַיָּה רָעָה:


**the habitat of jackals** (תַּנִּים) That is a desert, which is usually frequented by ‘tannim,’ which is a species of wild animal.



### Verse 14

###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:14:1)


**וּפָגְשׁוּ צִיִּים אֶת אִיִּים.** ״וְיַעֲרְעוּן תַּמְוָן בְּחֲתוּלִין״, כָּךְ תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן. ״תַּמְוָן״ – נְמִיּוֹת, מרטרינ״ש בלע״ז:


**And martens shall meet cats** And martens shall meet with cats. In this matter Jonathan rendered it. תַּמְוָן is נִמִּיּוֹת (martrines in O.F.), martens.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:14:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:14:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:14:2)


**וְשָׂעִיר.** שֵׁד:


**and a satyr** A demon.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:14:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:14:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:14:3)


**הִרְגִּיעָה.** לְשׁוֹן מַרְגּוֹעַ:


**rests** (הִרְגִּיעָה) an expression related to מַרְגּוֹעַ, rest.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:14:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:14:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:14:4)


**לִּילִית.** שֵׁם שֵׁדָה:


**lilith** The name of a female demon.



### Verse 15

###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:15:1)


**קִנְּנָה.** לְשׁוֹן ״קַן צִפּוֹר״ (דברים כב:ו):


**has made its nest** (קִנְּנָה) an expression related to ‘a bird’s nest’ (קַן) (Deut. 22:6).


###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:15:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:15:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:15:2)


**קִפּוֹז.** הוּא קִפּוֹד:


**owl** (קִפּוֹז) that is the owl (קִפֹּד).


###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:15:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:15:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:15:3)


**וַתְּמַלֵּט.** וְתֵלֵד בֵּיצָה:


**and she has laid** She laid eggs.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:15:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:15:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:15:4)


**וּבָקְעָה.** הִיא יְצִיאַת הָאֶפְרוֹחִים מִן הַבֵּיצָה, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר ״בֵּיצֵי צִפְעוֹנִי בָּקָעוּ״ (ישעיהו נט:ה):


**and hatched** This is the emerging of the chicks from the egg. Comp. (below 59:5) The eggs of the viper have hatched.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:15:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:15:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:15:5)


**וְדָגְרָה.** הִיא קְרִיאַת הָעוֹף שֶׁהָעוֹף קוֹרֵא בִּגְרוֹנוֹ לְהַמְשִׁיךְ אֶפְרוֹחִים אַחֲרָיו, גלוציי״ר בלע״ז, וְכֵן (ירמיה יז:יא) ״קוֹרֵא דָגָר״:


**and gathered** This is the call that the bird calls with its throat to draw the chicks after it, gloussera in French. Comp. (Jer. 17:11) “A cuckoo gathers (דָגָר) what it did not lay.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:15:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:15:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:15:6)


**דַיּוֹת.** ולטוייר״ש בלע״ז:


**vultures** (דַיּוֹת) voltojjrs in O.F.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:15:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:15:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:15:7)


**אִשָּׁה רְעוּתָהּ.** כְּמוֹ אֶל רְעוּתָהּ:


**each one to her friend** (lit., each one her friend,) like to her friend.



### Verse 16

###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:16:1)


**דִּרְשׁוּ מֵעַל סֵפֶר ה׳.** קִרְאוּ מֵעַל סֵפֶר בְּרֵאשִׁית, כְּשֶׁהֵבִיא הַמַּבּוּל גָּזַר שֶׁיִּתְקַבְּצוּ כָּל הַבְּרִיּוֹת לְהִסָּגֵר בַּתֵּיבָה זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה. **אַחַת מֵהֵנָּה לֹא נֶעְדָּרָה.** מִלָּבוֹא, עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה כְּשֶׁיִּגְזוֹר עֲלֵיהֶם זֹאת וּלְהִקָּבֵץ לִשְׁתּוֹת דָּם לֶאֱכוֹל בָּשָׂר וְחֵלֶב (יחזקאל לט:יז-יט):


**Seek out of the Book of the Lord** Read out of the Book of Genesis; when He brought the Flood, He decreed that all the creatures gather in the Ark, male and female, and none of them was missing. How much more will this be so when He decrees this upon them, to gather to drink blood and to eat flesh and fat!


###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:16:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:16:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:16:2)


**לֹא פָקָדוּ.** לֹא חָסְרוּ, כְּמוֹ (במדבר לא:מט) ״לֹא נִפְקַד מִמֶּנּוּ אִישׁ״:


**did not miss** (פָקָדוּ) Comp. (Num. 31:49) “Not a man was missing (נִפְקַד) of us.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:16:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:16:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:16:3)


**כִּי פִי הוּא צִוָּה.** שֶׁיָּבוֹאוּ:


**for My mouth it has commanded** that they come.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:16:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:16:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:16:4)


**וְרוּחוֹ.** שֶׁל פִּי. **הוּא קִבְּצָן.** רוּחוֹ מוּסָב עַל פִּי, כְּמוֹ (תהלים לג:ו) ״וּבְרוּחַ פִּיו כָּל צְבָאָם״, אַף כָּאן רוּחוֹ שֶׁל פִּי הוּא קִבְּצָן:


**and the breath** of My mouth **it gathered them.** The antecedent of ‘its breath’ is ‘My mouth.’ Comp. (Ps. 33:6) “And with the breath of His mouth all their host.” Here too, the breath of My mouth it gathered them.



### Verse 17

###### Rashi on Isaiah 34:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/34:17:1)


**וְהוּא הִפִּיל לָהֶן.** עַכְשָׁיו הַנָּבִיא אוֹמֵר עַל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, וְהוּא הִפִּיל לָהֶם לְאוֹתָן הַחַיּוֹת וְהָעוֹפוֹת **גּוֹרָל**, שֶׁיַּעֲלוּ אֵלּוּ לְחֶלְקָם:


**And He cast...for them** Now the prophet says concerning the Holy One, blessed be He, “And He cast lots for them,” for all those beasts and fowl, that these shall fall to their share.



## Chapter 35


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Isaiah 35:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:1:1)


**יְשֻׂשׂוּם.** יָשִׂישׂוּ עֲלֵיהֶם כְּמוֹ ׳יָשׂוּשׂוּ מֵהֶן׳, כְּמוֹ ״בָּנַי יְצָאֻנִי״ (ירמיהו י:כ) שֶׁפִּתְרוֹנוֹ ׳יָצְאוּ מִמֶּנִּי׳, וְכֵן ״בִּשְּׁלָם הַבָּשָׂר״ (מלכים א יט:כא) ׳בִּשֵּׁל לָהֶם הַבָּשָׂר׳:


**shall rejoice over them** (יְשֻׂשׂוּם) This is usually the sign of the direct object, inappropriate here in the case of an intransitive verb. (like יָשׂוּשׂוּ מֵהֶם, shall rejoice from them). Comp. (Jer. 10:20) “My sons have gone away from me (יְצָאֻנִי).” Also, (I Kings 19:21) “He cooked the meat for them (בִּשְּׁלָם),” equivalent to בִּשֵּׁל לָהֶם, “He cooked the meat for them.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 35:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:1:2)


**מִדְבָּר וְצִיָּה.** יְרוּשָׁלַיִם הַקְּרוּיָה צִיָּה, וְצִיּוֹן הַקְּרוּיָה מִדְבָּר (ישעיהו סד:ט), הֵן יָשׂוּשׂוּ עַל מַפַּלְתָּם שֶׁל גִּבּוֹרֵי שֵׂעִיר (וּבָצְרָה):


**Desert and wasteland** Jerusalem, called ‘wasteland,’ and Zion, called ‘desert,’ they shall rejoice over the downfall of the mighty of the heathens and Persia ([Manuscripts yield:] of Edom and Bozrah). ([The Warsaw edition reads:] the mighty of Seir (and Bozrah).)


###### Rashi on Isaiah 35:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:1:3)


**וְתָגֵל עֲרָבָה.** שֶׁל יְרוּשָׁלַיִם:


**and the plain shall rejoice** the plain of Jerusalem.



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Isaiah 35:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:2:1)


**וְרַנֵּן.** כְּמוֹ ׳וּלְרַנֵּן׳:


**and to sing** (lit., and sing,) like: and to sing.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 35:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:2:2)


**הַלְּבָנוֹן.** בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ (ספרי דברים כח):


**the Lebanon** The Temple.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 35:2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:2:3)


**הֲדַר.** כְּבוֹדוֹ לְצִיּוֹן:

### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Isaiah 35:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:3:1)


**חַזְּקוּ יָדַיִם רָפוֹת.** כָּל הַנְּבִיאִים, מְבַשְּׂרֵי יְשׁוּעָה, נִחֲמוּ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְחִזְּקוּ אֶת יְדֵיהֶם הָרָפוֹת. **חַזְּקוּ** לְשׁוֹן מִשְׁקָל כָּבֵד, וּפִתְרוֹנוֹ: חַזְּקוּ אֶת אֲחֵרִים. וְאִם הָיָה בָּא לוֹמַר חִזְקוּ אַתֶּם שֶׁיֶּדְכֶם רָפוֹת, הָיָה לִנָּקֵד ״חִזְקוּ וְאִמְצוּ״ (דברי הימים ב לב:ז). עַכְשָׁיו שֶׁאוֹמֵר לָהֶם לְחַזֵּק וּלְאַמֵּץ אֲחֵרִים, נָקוּד ׳חַזְּקוּ׳ ׳**אַמְּצוּ**׳. **חִזְקוּ אַל תִּירָאוּ** זֶה נָקוּד ׳חִזְקוּ׳ לְשׁוֹן ׳קַל׳: חִזְקוּ אַתֶּם מֵאֲלֵיכֶם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁיֹּאמַר לְיָחִיד ״חֲזַק וֶאֱמָץ״ (יהושע א:ו), וְלֹא יֹאמַר ׳חַזֵּק׳:


**Strengthen weak hands** (חַזְּקוּ) All the prophets who brought tidings of salvation consoled Israel and strengthened their weak hands. (The word) is in the intensive conjugation, and its meaning is (the causative, i.e.,) strengthen others. If he intended to say, “Be strong, you whose hands are weak,” it would be vowelized like (2 Chron. 32:7) “Be strong (חִזְקוּ) and be firm (וְאִמְצוּ).” Now that he says to them to strengthen others and to make others firm, it is vowelized, חַזְּקוּ, אַמְּצוּ. “Be strong (חִזְקוּ), do not fear” is vowelized חִזְקוּ, a form of the ‘kal’ conjugation, meaning ‘you be strong by yourselves,’ as one says to singular (Jos. 1:6), “Be strong and be firm (חֲזַק ֶמָץ),” and he does not say, חַזֵּק.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Isaiah 35:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:4:1)


**לְנִמְהֲרֵי לֵב.** שֶׁמְּמַהֲרִים אֶת הַגְּאֻלָּה וּמְצֵרִים עַל אִחוּרָהּ:


**to the hasty of heart** Who hurry the redemption and are troubled by its delay.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 35:4:2

**נָקָם יָבוֹא.** כְּמוֹ ׳בְּנָקָם יָבֹא׳:


**[with] vengeance He shall come** (lit., vengeance He shall come,) with vengeance He shall come.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 35:4:3

**גְּמוּל אֱלֹהִים.** עַל הָרְשָׁעִים **הוּא יָבוֹא** וְאֶתְכֶם יוֹשִׁיעַ:


**the recompense of God** Upon the wicked ([mss.] upon your enemies) He shall come and save you.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Isaiah 35:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:5:1)


**עֵינֵי עִוְרִים.** אוֹתָם שֶׁהָיוּ עַד הֵנָּה, עִוְרִים מְהַכִּיר אֶת מוֹרָא זוֹ עֲלֵיהֶם:


**the eyes of the blind shall be opened** Those who were blind, not to recognize (lit., from recognizing) their fear (sic) ([Warsaw:] this fear;) ([mss.] My fear) upon them.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 35:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:5:2)


**וְאָזְנֵי חֵרְשִׁים.** שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ שׁוֹמְעִים לְקוֹל נְבִיאִים עַד הֵנָּה, תִּפָּקַחְנָה **וְתִפָּתַחְנָה**, כִּי אֶתֵּן לָהֶם רוּחַ נָכוֹן לְיִרְאָה אוֹתִי; וְעַל יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא אוֹמֵר, שֶׁקְּרָאָם **עִוְּרִים** וְחֵרְשִׁים, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״הַחֵרְשִׁים שִׁמְעוּ וְגוֹ׳״ (ישעיהו מב:יח):


**and the ears of the deaf** Who did not hearken to the voice of the prophets until now, will be opened and unstopped, for I will give them a proper spirit to fear Me. He says this concerning Israel, whom he called blind and deaf, as the matter is stated (infra 42:18) “You deaf ones, hearken, etc.”



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Isaiah 35:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:6:1)


**אָז יְדַלֵּג כָּאַיָּל פִּסֵּחַ וְגוֹ׳.** יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהֵם עַכְשָׁיו פִּסְחִים וְחַלָּשִׁים. מָצִינוּ שֶׁקּוֹרְאָם פִּסְחִים חַלָּשִׁים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״פִּסְחִים בָּזְזוּ בַז״ (ישעיהו לג:כג):


**Then the lame shall skip like a hart, etc.** Israel, who are now lame and weak. We find that he calls the weak with an expression of ‘lame,’ as the matter is stated (above 33:23): “The lame take the prey.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 35:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:6:2)


**וְתָרֹן.** בִּישׁוּעָתִי:


**shall sing** in My salvation.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 35:6:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:6:3)


**לְשׁוֹן אִלֵּם.** לְשׁוֹנָם שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהָיוּ בֵּין הַכַּשְׂדִּים אִלְּמִים, שׁוֹמְעִים חֶרְפּוֹת וְאֵינָם מְשִׁיבִים (גיטין לו ב):


**the tongue of the mute** The tongue of Israel, who are among the nations as mutes, for they hear their scorn and do not respond.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 35:6:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:6:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:6:4)


**כִּי נִבְקְעוּ בַמִּדְבָּר מַיִם.** כִּי תְּשַׂמְּחֵם יְשׁוּעָתוֹ, וְיִפְרְחוּ כְּמִדְבַּר צִיָּה הַצְּמֵאָה לְמַיִם וּמַעְיָנוֹת נִבְקָעִים בְּתוֹכָהּ, כְּלוֹמַר, כִּי יִצְמַח יֶשַׁע לַנִּדְכָּאִים:


**for water has broken out in the desert** For My salvation shall cheer them up, and they shall blossom like a desert wasteland, which thirsts for water, and springs break out into it; i.e., for salvation shall sprout for the crushed ones.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Isaiah 35:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:7:1)


**וְהָיָה הַשָּׁרָב.** לָהֶם **לַאֲגַם**. הַתָּאֵב לִתְשׁוּעָה יְהֵא נוֹשַׁע, וְהַנָּבִיא דִּבֵּר בִּלְשׁוֹן מָשָׁל:


**And the dry place shall become a pool** He who longs for salvation shall be saved. The prophet spoke figuratively.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 35:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:7:2)


**בִּנְוֵה תַנִּים רִבְצָהּ וגו׳.** בִּנְוֵה מָקוֹם שֶׁהָיָה מִדְבָּר צִיָּה, שֶׁהוּא נְוֵה מִרְבַּץ תַּנִּין, יִהְיֶה לַח, מְקוֹם **חָצִיר** הַנַּעֲשֶׂה לְ**קָנֶה וָגֹמֶא**; וְאֵין דֶּרֶךְ **קָנֶה וָגֹמֶא** גְּדֵלִים אֶלָּא בִּמְקוֹם מַיִם, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הֲיִגְאֶה גֹמֶא בְּלִי בִצָּה״ (איוב ח:יא):


**in the habitat of jackals, a resting place, etc.** A place that was a desert wasteland, which is the habitat, the resting place of jackals, shall become moist, a place of grass, made for reeds and rushes, and it is not customary for reeds and rushes to grow except in a watery place, as the matter is stated (Job 8:11): “Can the rush shoot upwards without mire?”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 35:7:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:7:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:7:3)


**רִבְצָהּ.** שֵׁם דָּבָר הוּא, כְּמוֹ ״מַרְבֵּץ״ (צפניה ב:טו), שֶׁהֲרֵי אֵינוֹ מֵפִיק הֵ״א:


**a resting place** (רִבְצָה) This is a noun like מַרְבֵּץ, since it has no ‘mappiq hey.’



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Isaiah 35:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:8:1)


**וְהָיָה שָׁם מַסְלוּל.** לְעוֹבְרִים וְשָׁבִים:


**And there shall be a highway** for the travelers.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 35:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:8:2)


**לֹא יַעַבְרֶנּוּ.** לְאוֹתוֹ דֶּרֶךְ שׁוּם **טָמֵא**, כְּלוֹמַר: לֹא יִהְיֶה עוֹד לָאֻמּוֹת:


**no unclean one shall traverse it** No unclean one shall traverse that road; i.e., it will no longer belong to the heathens ([mss.:] nations).


###### Rashi on Isaiah 35:8:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:8:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:8:3)


**וְהוּא לָמוֹ.** וְהוּא הַדֶּרֶךְ שֶׁל אוֹתָן עִוְּרִים וְחֵרְשִׁים וּפִסְּחִים וְאִלְּמִים הַנִּזְכָּרִים לְמַעְלָה (ישעיהו לה:ה-ו), וְהָיָה הִלּוּךְ אוֹתוֹ **דֶּרֶךְ**, וַאֲפִלּוּ הֵם **אֱוִילִים לֹא יִתְעוּ**, כִּי אֲיַשְּׁרֶנּוּ לִפְנֵיהֶם:


**and it shall be for them** And that is the road of those blind, deaf, lame, and mute mentioned above. They shall travel on this road, and even if they are fools, they shall not go astray, for I will straighten it for them.



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Isaiah 35:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:9:1)


**וּפְרִיץ חַיּוֹת.** ״חֲזִיר מִיַּעַר״ (תהילים פ:יד), אֵין לְךָ פָּרִיץ בַּחַיּוֹת כַּחֲזִיר הַבַּר, וְגַם ״אַרְיֵה מִסֻּבְּכוֹ״ (ירמיהו ד:ז), הוּא נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר, לֹא יִמָּצֵא שָׁם:


**a profligate beast** The boar out of the forest (80:14). There is none as profligate among the beasts as the boar, and also “the lions from his thicket” (Jer. 4:7), i.e., Nebuchadnezzar, shall not be found there.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 35:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:9:2)


**בַּל יַעֲלֶנָּה** לְאוֹתָהּ הַדֶּרֶךְ. ׳דֶּרֶךְ׳ מְשַׁמֵּשׁ לְשׁוֹן זָכָר וּלְשׁוֹן נְקֵבָה, כְּדִכְתִיב ״אֶת הַדֶּרֶךְ אֲשֶׁר יֵלְכוּ בָהּ״ (שמות יח:כ) הֲרֵי נְקֵבָה, ״בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶחָד יֵצְאוּ אֵלֶיךָ״ (דברים כח:ז) הֲרֵי זָכָר:


**nor shall...ascend thereon** On that road (הַדֶּרֶךְ). The word דֶּרֶךְ is used both as masculine and feminine gender, as it is written (Ex. 18:20): “The way (הַדֶּרֶךְ) upon which (בָּהּ) they shall walk.” (Lit., on her.) Thus it is feminine. Comp. (Deut. 28:7) “In one road (בַּדֶּרֶךְ אֶחָד) they shall come out to you.” Thus it is masculine.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 35:9:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:9:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:9:3)


**לֹא תִמָּצֵא.** חַיָּה רָעָה שָׁם:


**it shall not be found** any wild beast there.



### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Isaiah 35:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:10:1)


**וְשִׂמְחַת עוֹלָם.** שִׂמְחָה אֲשֶׁר מֵעוֹלָם, שֶׁהָיְתָה לָהֶם כְּבָר בְּדֶרֶךְ יְצִיאָתָן מִמִּצְרַיִם, ״וַה׳ הוֹלֵךְ לִפְנֵיהֶם יוֹמָם״ (שמות יג:כא):


**with joy of days of yore** (Heb. שִׂמְחַתעוֹלָם, joy that is from days of yore, which they already experienced on the way of their Exodus from Egypt, “and the Lord was going before them by day” (Ex. 13:21).


###### Rashi on Isaiah 35:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/35:10:2)


**וְנָסוּ.** הַ**יָּגוֹן** וְהָ**אֲנָחָה** מֵהֶם:


**shall flee** The sadness and the sighing shall flee from them.



## Chapter 36


### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Isaiah 36:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:2:1)


**בִּתְעָלַת.** פושי״ר בלע״ז:


**near the conduit** fosed (fosse) in French, (a ditch, a trench, a moat.)


###### Rashi on Isaiah 36:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:2:2)


**בְּרֵכָה.** מְקוֹם כִּנּוּס מַיִם, חָפוּר בַּקַּרְקַע בִּידֵי אָדָם לָתֵת בּוֹ דָּגִים, אָרוֹךְ וְרָחָב:


**the pool** A place where water is gathered, dug in the ground by man, in which to put fish. It is long and wide.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 36:2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:2:3)


**בִּמְסִלַּת.** דֶּרֶךְ כְּבוּשָׁה, קמי״ן בלע״ז:


**on the road** A paved road. (chemin in French.)


###### Rashi on Isaiah 36:2:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:2:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:2:4)


**שְׂדֵה כוֹבֵס.** תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״חֲקַל מִשְׁטַח קַצְרַיָּא״, שֶׁשּׁוֹטְחִין שָׁם הַכּוֹבְסִים אֶת הַבְּגָדִים:


**the washer’s field** Jonathan renders: A field where the washers stretch out, i.e., where the washers stretch out the garments.



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Isaiah 36:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:3:1)


**הַמַּזְכִּיר.** כּוֹתֵב הַזִּכְרוֹנוֹת בְּסִפְרֵי דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים, (דבר אחר: **הַמַּזְכִּיר** אֵיזֶה דִּין בָּא לְפָנָיו רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁיִּפְסְקֶנּוּ רִאשׁוֹן):


**the recorder** The writer of the records in the annals. (Another explanation: He would record which judgment came before him first, that he adjudicate it first.)



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Isaiah 36:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:5:1)


**אָמַרְתִּי.** עַד הֵנָּה **אַךְ דִּבְרֵי שְׂפָתַיִם** הוּא בְּפִיו לֵאמֹר: ״לֹא אֶעֱבֹד לְמֶלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר״, וּמִשֶּׁיִּרְאֶה שֶׁאֶעֱלֶה עָלָיו לְצָבָא יַחֲזֹר בּוֹ; עַכְשָׁיו הֲרֵי עָלִיתִי, מֵעַתָּה אוֹ יַעַבְדֵנִי, אוֹ צָרִיךְ הוּא לְבַקֵּשׁ **עֵצָה וּגְבוּרָה לַמִּלְחָמָה**:


**I said** (until now), “It is but words of the lips, that he speaks (lit., in his mouth), saying, ‘I will not serve the king of Assyria.’ And when he sees that I will march against him with an army, he will recant. Now I have marched. From now on, either he will serve me, or he will need to seek counsel and might for war.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 36:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:5:2)


**עַתָּה.** שֶׁבָּא הָעֵת, אֱמוֹר נָא **עַל מִי בָטַחְתָּ** לִמְרוֹד בִּי:


**Now** that the time has come, tell me now on whom you have depended to rebel against me.



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Isaiah 36:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:6:1)


**אֲשֶׁר יִסָּמֵךְ אִישׁ** עַל **הַקָּנֶה הָרָצוּץ** הַנִּשְׁבָּר, וְהַקְּרוּמִיּוֹת בָּאִים **בְכַפּוֹ** וְנוֹקְבִין אוֹתָהּ, **כֵּן פַּרְעֹה** לַבּוֹטְחִים בּוֹ; סוֹפָן לִהְיוֹת עֶזְרָתוֹ לְרָעָתָן:


**upon which a man will lean** On the splintered and broken reed, and the scaly envelopes enter his palm and puncture it, so is Pharaoh to those who trust him. Eventually, their aid will be to their detriment.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Isaiah 36:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:7:1)


**אֲשֶׁר הֵסִיר חִזְקִיָּה אֶת בָּמֹתָיו.** בִּעֵר אֶת כָּל בָּתֵּי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וּמִזְבְּחוֹת וּבָמוֹת, וְהִזְקִיק אֶת כָּל יְהוּדָה לְהִשְׁתַּחֲווֹת לִפְנֵי מִזְבֵּחַ אֶחָד:


**Whose high places...has removed** He abolished all the pagan temples and the altars and the high places, and has coerced all Judah to prostrate themselves before one altar.



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Isaiah 36:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:8:1)


**הִתְעָרֶב נָא.** בְּדָבָר זֶה, אִם תּוּכַל לְקַיְּמָן. לְשׁוֹן ׳עֵרָבוֹן׳, שֶׁקּוֹרִין גי״ר בלע״ז:


**wager now** on this matter, if you will be able to accomplish it. This is an expression of a wager, which is called gajjer in O.F.



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Isaiah 36:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:9:1)


**וְאֵיךְ תָּשִׁיב.** אֲפִלּוּ **פְּנֵי פַחַת אַחַד** שֶׁהוּא מֵ**עַבְדֵי אֲדוֹנִי הַקְּטַנִּים**, שֶׁהַקָּטָן בְּרָאשֵׁי גְּיָסוֹת שֶׁלּוֹ מְמֻנֶּה עַל אֲלָפִים אִישׁ (מכילתא בשלח שירה ב):


**And how can you repulse** even a captain, who is one of my master’s smallest servants, for the smallest of the heads of his troops is in charge of two thousand men.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 36:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:9:2)


**אַחַד עַבְדֵי.** אֶחָד מֵעַבְדֵי, כְּמוֹ ״אַחַד הַשִּׂיחִם״ (בראשית כא:טו), ״אַחַד הָרֵיקִים״ (שמואל ב ו:כ):


**one of...servants** (אַחַד) one of the servants of. Comp. (Gen. 21:15) “One of (אַחַד) the bushes.” Also (II Sam. 6:20) “One of (אַחַד) the idlers.”



### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Isaiah 36:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:10:1)


**הֲמִבַּלְעֲדֵי ה׳.** שֶׁלֹּא מֵרְשׁוּתוֹ:


**is it [with] other than the Lord** Without His permission?


###### Rashi on Isaiah 36:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:10:2)


**ה׳ אָמַר אֵלַי.** כְּבָר נִבְּאוּ הַנְּבִיאִים: ״יִשָּׂא אֶת חֵיל דַּמֶּשֶׂק וְאֶת שְׁלַל שׁוֹמְרוֹן לִפְנֵי מֶלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר״ (ישעיהו ח:ד), וְהוּא טָעָה לוֹמַר: ״כַּאֲשֶׁר עָשִׂיתִי לְשׁוֹמְרוֹן כֵּן אֶעֱשֶׂה לִירוּשָׁלִָם״ (ישעיהו י:יא):


**The Lord said to me** The prophets have already prophesied (supra 8:4): “The wealth of Damascus and the plunder of Samaria shall be carried off before the king of Assyria.” But he erred, saying (supra 10:11), “Indeed, as I did to Samaria..., so will I do to Jerusalem...”



### Verse 11

###### Rashi on Isaiah 36:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:11:1)


**כִּי שֹׁמְעִים אֲנָחְנוּ.** מַכִּירִים אֲנַחְנוּ אוֹתוֹ לָשׁוֹן. **שׁוֹמְעִים** – איטנדנ״ט בלע״ז:


**for we understand it** (שֹׁמְעִים, lit. hear.) We understand that language, an expression of hearing (entendenc in O.F.).


###### Rashi on Isaiah 36:11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:11:2)


**וְאַל תְּדַבֵּר אֵלֵינוּ יְהוּדִית.** שֶׁכָּל הָעָם מַכִּירִים בְּלָשׁוֹן יְהוּדִית, וְהֵם מִתְפַּחֲדִים מִדְּבָרֶיךָ. (לְפִי שֶׁאָמַר לָהֶם ״אִמְרוּ נָא אֶל חִזְקִיָּה״ (ישעיהו לו:ד), (סָבְרוּ) שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לְהַפְחִיד הָעָם. וְרַבְשָׁקֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּמָר הָיָה, כִּסְבוּרִים הֵם אַף שֶׁמִּצְוַת רַבּוֹ עַל רַבְשָׁקֵה, אֲבָל לִבּוֹ נִמְשָׁךְ לְמִשְׁפַּחְתּוֹ וְיִכָּמְרוּ נִחוּמָיו):


**do not speak with us in Judean** for all the people understand the Judean language, and they are frightened by your words. (Since he said to them, “Say now to Hezekiah,” they thought that he did not come to frighten the people. Since Rabshakeh was an apostate Jew, they thought that even though his master’s orders were incumbent upon Rabshakeh to observe, his heart was attracted to his family and he would take pity upon them.)



### Verse 12

###### Rashi on Isaiah 36:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:12:1)


**הַאֶל אֲדֹנֶיךָ** תְּמִיהָה הוּא, לְכָךְ נָקוּד חֲטַף פַּתַּח. וְכִי אֶל שְׁנֵיכֶם לְבַדְּכֶם **שְׁלָחַנִי אֲדֹנִי**? הֲלוֹא אֶל כֻּלָּם שְׁלָחַנִי, וּלְכָךְ בָּאתִי, שֶׁכָּל הָעָם יִשְׁמְעוּ וְיִרְאוּ, וְאַל יְסִיתֵם חִזְקִיָּהוּ לִמְרוֹד:


**Did...to your master** (הַאֶל) This is the interrogative form. It is therefore vowelized with a ‘hataf pattah’ (not so in our editions). Did my master send me to you two alone? Indeed, he sent me to all of them, and for that reason I have come, so that all the people hear and see, and let not Hezekiah persuade them to rebel.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 36:12:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:12:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:12:2)


**לֶאֱכֹל אֶת צוֹאָתָם.** אַף הֵם בְּרָעָב הַמָּצוֹר:


**to eat their dung** They too (sic) would eat in the hunger of the siege.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 36:12:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:12:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:12:3)


**יֹאכְלוּ אֶת חֹרֵיהֶם.** רְעִי הַיּוֹצֵא דֶּרֶךְ הַנֶּקֶב שֶׁלָּהֶם, וְלָשׁוֹן נָאֶה תִּקְּנוּ סוֹפְרִים לִקְרוֹתוֹ צוֹאָתָם. כָּךְ שָׁנוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ (מגילה כה ב): מִקְרָאוֹת הַכְּתוּבִים לִגְנַאי קוֹרִין אוֹתוֹ לְשֶׁבַח, כְּמוֹ (דברים כח:כז) ״בַּעֲפוֹלִים״ – ״בַּטְּחוֹרִים״, (דברים כח:ל) ״יִשְׁגָּלֶנָּה״ – ״יִשְׁכָּבֶנָּה״, ״חוֹרֵיהֶם״ – ״צוֹאָתָם״:


**their dung** The kethib reads חֹרָאֵיהֶם, the dung that is excreted through their orifice. Our Sages instituted to euphemize and read it צוֹאָתָם, i.e., their dung. Thus did our Rabbis teach: Verses written in uncomplimentary words are to be read in a complimentary manner, e.g., (Deut. 28:27) עֲפֹלִים (is read) טְחֹרִים. (Both mean hemorrhoids. The former means ‘that which is in the dark holes,’ being more explicit than the latter. (ibid. v. 30) יִשְׁגָּלֶנָּה (is to be read) יִשְׁכָּבֶנָּה. (Both denoting intimacy, the former related as well to a dog.) חֹרָאֵיהֶם (is to be read) צוֹאָתָם, שִׁינֵיהֶם (is to be read) מֵימֵי רַגְלֵיהֶם.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 36:12:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:12:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:12:4)


**שִׁינֵיהֶם.** מֵימֵי רַגְלֵיהֶם, **שִׁינֵיהֶם** צוֹאָה לַחָה. שִׁינֵי דְכַרְכַּשְׁתָּא (שבת פב א) הִיא הַחַלְחֹלֶת (חולין נ א) שֶׁקּוֹרִין טבחי״א בלע״ז, עוֹמֶדֶת עַל יְדֵי שָׁלֹשׁ שִׁנַּיִם:


**their urine** The kethib is שִׁינֵיהֶם, loose excrement. The teeth of the large intestine. That is the intestine called tabahie in O.F. that stands on three teeth, (i.e. the glands of the rectum, which is held by three glands. They are called שִׁנַּיִּם because they are shaped like teeth).



### Verse 14

**יַשִּׁיא.** יַתְעֶה:


**deceive** (יַשִּׁיא) mislead.



### Verse 16

###### Rashi on Isaiah 36:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:16:1)


**עֲשׂוּ אִתִּי בְרָכָה. צְאוּ אֵלַי** לְשָׁלוֹם וּבָרְכוּנִי, וְהָבִיאוּ אֵלַי תְּשׁוּרַת שָׁלוֹם:


**Make peace with me** (בְרָכָה, lit., a blessing.) Come out to me for peace and greet me and bring me a gift of peace.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 36:16:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:16:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:16:2)


**בְּרָכָה.** שלו״ד בלע״ז, כמו: ״וַיְבָרֶךְ יַעֲקֹב אֶת פַּרְעֹה״ (בראשית מז:י):


בְּרָכָה is saloud in O.F., salutation. Comp. (Gen. 47:10) “And Jacob greeted Pharaoh.”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 36:16:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:16:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:16:3)


**וְאִכְלוּ אִישׁ גַּפְנוֹ.** וְאֵלֵךְ מֵעֲלֵיכֶם וְשְׁבוּ בְּשָׁלוֹם עַד שֶׁאֶמְצָא אֶרֶץ טוֹבָה כְּאַרְצְכֶם, וְאַגְלֶה אֶתְכֶם שָׁם; כִּי כֵּן דַּרְכּוֹ, לְהַעֲבִיר הָאֻמּוֹת מֵאֶרֶץ אֶל אֶרֶץ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ישעיהו י:יג) ״וְאָסִיר גְּבוּלוֹת עַמִּים״:


**and each man will eat of his vine** And I will leave you, and dwell in peace until I find a land as good as your land, and I will exile you there, for so is my wont, to transfer nations from land to land, as it is said (supra 10:13): “And I remove the boundaries of the peoples.”



### Verse 17

###### Rashi on Isaiah 36:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:17:1)


**אֶל אֶרֶץ כְּאַרְצְכֶם.** אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי: שׁוֹטֶה הָיָה זֶה, מָשָׁל לְמֶלֶךְ וְכוּ׳ בְּסִפְרֵי פָּרָשַׁת וְהָיָה עֵקֶב (דברים ז יב). הָיָה לוֹ לוֹמַר ״אֶל אֶרֶץ יָפָה מֵאַרְצְכֶם״, אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה יָכוֹל לְסַפֵּר בִּגְנוּתָהּ:


**to a land like your land** Said Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai: Was this one (Sennacherib) a fool? This is an example of a king, etc. in Sifre, parshath Ekev (Deut. 7:12). He should have said, “to a land better than your land,” but he could not denigrate it.



### Verse 19

###### Rashi on Isaiah 36:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:19:1)


**וְכִי הִצִּילוּ אֶת שֹׁמְרוֹן מִיָּדִי.** וּבְנֵי שׁוֹמְרוֹן הָיוּ עוֹבְדִים לֵאלֹהֵי אֲרָם שְׁכֵינֵיהֶם, וַ**חֲמָת** הִיא מֵאֲרָם:


**Now did they save Samaria from my hand?** and the inhabitants of Samaria worshipped the Gods of the Arameans, who were their neighbors, and Hamath is from Aram.



### Verse 22

###### Rashi on Isaiah 36:22:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:22:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/36:22:1)


**קְרוּעֵי בְגָדִים.** עַל שֶׁשָּׁמְעוּ גִּדּוּפֵי הַשֵּׁם (סנהדרין ס א), וְהִיא כְּמוֹ בִּרְכַּת הַשֵּׁם:


**with torn garments** Because they heard blasphemies of the Name of God, and that is tantamount to cursing the Name.



## Chapter 37


### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Isaiah 37:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/37:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/37:3:1)


**וְתוֹכֵחָה.** אשפרובמנ״ט בלע״ז, הָאוֹיְבִים מוֹכִיחִים בְּהַצְלָחָתָם לֵאמֹר: ״יָדֵינוּ רָמָה״ (דברים לב:כז) וְאֵין אֱלֹהִים כֵּאלֹהֵינוּ:


**proof** (Aprobement in O.F.) The enemies show evidence to praise themselves with their success, saying, “Our hand has overpowered (lit., has become high), and there is no God (like our God).”


###### Rashi on Isaiah 37:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/37:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/37:3:2)


**כִּי בָאוּ בָנִים.** בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, בָּנָיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:


**for the children have come** The children of Israel, children of the Holy One, blessed be He.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 37:3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/37:3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/37:3:3)


**עַד מַשְׁבֵּר וְכֹחַ אַיִן לְלֵדָה** עֵת צָרָה, הַדּוֹמָה לְאִשָּׁה הַיּוֹשֶׁבֶת עַל הַמַּשְׁבֵּר, וְאֵין כֹּחַ לַוָּלָד לָצֵאת:


**as far as the birthstool and there is no strength to give birth** It is a time of distress analogous to a woman sitting on the birthstool, and the fetus has no strength to come out.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Isaiah 37:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/37:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/37:4:1)


**וְהוֹכִיחַ בַּדְּבָרִים.** הִגִּיד כֹּחוֹ וְהֶרְאָה הַצְלָחָתוֹ, **וְהוֹכִיחַ** – אישפרובי״ר בלע״ז:


**and he brought proof with the words** (וְהוֹכִיחַ) He told his strength and showed his success. The word והוֹכִיחַ is eprober in O.F., to prove.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Isaiah 37:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/37:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/37:7:1)


**וְשָׁמַע שְׁמוּעָה.** מִיָּד, זוֹ שְׁמוּעַת תִּרְהָקָה מֶלֶךְ כּוּשׁ (ישעיהו לז:ט), וּמִתּוֹךְ כָּךְ יֵלֵךְ מֵעֲלֵיכֶם הַפַּעַם הַזֹּאת לְהִלָּחֵם עִם תִּרְהָקָה, וְאֵין זוֹ שִׁיבָה לְאַרְצוֹ; וְאַחַר כָּךְ יָשׁוּב הֲלוֹם, וַאֲנִי עָתִיד לַהֲשִׁיבוֹ לְאַרְצוֹ וּלְהַפִּילוֹ שָׁם **בַּחֶרֶב**:


**and he will hear a rumor** immediately. This is the rumor of Tirhakah, king of Cush, because of which he will leave you this time to battle with Tirhakah, but this is not the return to his land. Afterwards he will return here, and I am destined to return him to his land and to cause him to fall there by the sword.



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Isaiah 37:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/37:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/37:9:1)


**וַיִּשְׁמַע.** מֶלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר:


**And he heard** i.e., the king of Assyria.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 37:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/37:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/37:9:2)


**עַל תִּרְהָקָה.** לֵאמֹר יָצָא תִּרְהָקָה לְהִלָּחֵם אִתָּךְ:


**about Tirhakah...saying** Tirhakah went out to wage war against you.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 37:9:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/37:9:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/37:9:3)


**וַיִּשְׁמַע וַיִּשְׁלַח מַלְאָכִים.** אֵין ׳וַיִּשְׁמַע׳ הַשֵּׁנִי כְּמוֹ ׳וַיִּשְׁמַע׳ הָרִאשׁוֹן: הָרִאשׁוֹן לְשׁוֹן ׳שְׁמוּעָה׳, וְהַשֵּׁנִי לְשׁוֹן ׳קַבָּלָה׳. קִבֵּל דִּבְרֵי הַשְּׁלוּחִים וַיִּיטְבוּ בְּעֵינָיו לָתֵת לֵב לְהִסְתַּלֵּק מֵעַל יְרוּשָׁלַיִם, לְהִלָּחֵם תְּחִלָּה עִם כּוּשׁ:


**And he heard, and he sent emissaries** The second “and he heard” is not like the first “and he heard.” The first is an expression of hearing, and the second is an expression of accepting. He accepted the report of the messengers, and it appealed to him to give thought to withdraw from Jerusalem to fight first with Cush.


###### Rashi on Isaiah 37:9:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/37:9:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/37:9:4)


**וַיִּשְׁלַח מַלְאָכִים אֶל חִזְקִיָּהוּ.** לְהוֹדִיעוֹ שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִסְתַּלֵּק לְגַמְרֵי, אֶלָּא עַל מְנָת לָשׁוּב:


**and he sent emissaries to Hezekiah** to notify [him] that he was not withdrawing completely, but with the intention of returning.



### Verse 12

###### Rashi on Isaiah 37:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/37:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/37:12:1)


**עֶדֶן.** שֵׁם מַלְכוּת, כְּמָה דְאַתְּ אָמַר (יחזקאל כז:כג) ״חָרָן וְכַנֵּה וְעֶדֶן״:


**Eden** the name of a kingdom, as it is stated (Ezekiel 27:23): “Haran and Canneh and Eden.”



### Verse 13

###### Rashi on Isaiah 37:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/37:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/37:13:1)


**הֵנַע וְעִוָּה.** הֱנִיעֵהוּ וְעִוְּהוּ מֶלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר, הֶחֱרִיבָם וְטִלְטְלָם מִמְּקוֹמָם:


**He exiled [them] and twisted [them]** (וְעִוָּה הֵנַע) The king of Assyria exiled him and twisted him; he destroyed them and exiled them from their place.



### Verse 18

###### Rashi on Isaiah 37:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/37:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/37:18:1)


**אָמְנָם ה׳.** אֱמֶת הוּא כִּי **הֶחֱרִיבוּ מַלְכֵי אַשּׁוּר**:


**Indeed, O Lord** It is true that the kings of Assyria destroyed


###### Rashi on Isaiah 37:18:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/37:18:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/37:18:2)


**אֶת כָּל הָאֲרָצוֹת וְאֶת אַרְצָם. הָאֲרָצוֹת** – רָאשֵׁי הַמְּדִינוֹת, וְאֶת אֶרֶץ הַסְּמוּכָה לָהֶם. עָרֵי הַמַּמְלָכָה אֲשֶׁר הֵנָּם רֹאשׁ לַמְּדִינוֹת קוֹרֵא ׳אֲרָצוֹת׳, וּשְׁאָר הַמְּחוֹזוֹת אֲשֶׁר סְבִיבוֹתֵיהֶם קוֹרֵא ׳אַרְצָם׳. וּבְסֵפֶר מְלָכִים (מלכים ב יט:יז) כָּתוּב ״אֶת הַגּוֹיִם וְאֶת אַרְצָם״, וְלָשׁוֹן אֶחָד הוּא:


**all the countries and their land** “The countries” refers to the (capitals) of the provinces, and (“their land” refers to) the land near them, the royal cities, which are the heads of the provinces, he calls “countries” and the remaining regions surrounding them he calls “their land.” And in the Book of II Kings (19:7) it is written: “the nations and their land.” It has, however, one meaning.



### Verse 19

###### Rashi on Isaiah 37:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/37:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/37:19:1)


**וְנָתֹן.** כְּמוֹ ״וְנָתוֹן אוֹתוֹ עַל כָּל אֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם״ (בראשית מא:ג), לְשׁוֹן ׳פָּעוֹל׳, ׳שָׁמוֹר׳, ׳זָכוֹר׳, דוננ״ט בלע״ז:


**And committing** (Heb. וְנָתֹן). Comp. (Gen. 41:43) “And appointing (וְנָתוֹן) him over all the land of Egypt,” an expression of the infinitive. Comp. “saying” (אָמוֹר), “remembering” (זָכוֹר), (donnant in French, giving).


###### Rashi on Isaiah 37:19:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/37:19:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/37:19:2)


**עֵץ וָאֶבֶן** הֵם, לְפִיכָךְ לֹא הָיָה בָּהֶם כֹּחַ, **וַיְאַבְּדוּם** מֶלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר:


**wood and stone** are they; therefore, they had no power, and the king of Assyria destroyed them.



### Verse 24

###### Rashi on Isaiah 37:24:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/37:24:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Isaiah/r/37:24:1)


**מְרוֹם הָרִים.** הַר הַבַּיִת:
